Plumbing: shared code libraries, compatibility patches, and bugfixes. You’ll never open a menu for any of these — listed here purely for completeness.
Core libraries & APIs
Fabric API, Architectury, Cloth Config v11, Bookshelf, Fabric Language Kotlin, Iceberg, Necronomicon, OctoLib, Obscure API, Ash API, Athena, Cardinal Components API, CICADA, Collective, Common Network, CoroUtil, Dawn API, EpheroLib, fakerlib, FTB XMod Compat, Fzzy Config, Integrated API, JamLib, Konkrete, LibZ, MidnightLib, oωo (owo-lib), Player Animator, Puzzles Lib, Resourcefulconfig, Resourceful Lib, SuperMartijn642’s Config Lib, Thermoo, TxniLib, YetAnotherConfigLib, Balm, Cupboard, Melody, Cristel Lib, Lithostitched, Structure Pool API, Structure Essentials Mod, Moog’s Structure Lib, TerraBlender, Botarium, Reborn Core, BCLib, RecipeSplitter, recipeessentials Mod, CreativeCore. Mods/Building--and--Decoration-Mods.content:
Building & Decoration Mods
Chipped / Chipped-Express
Chipped adds a huge library of matching decorative block variants; Chipped-Express lets you autocraft those blocks through AE2 or Create instead of clicking a crafting table 200 times. See Tech & Automation Mods.
Supplementaries
A big grab-bag of functional, good-looking “vanilla+” blocks — signs, lanterns, benches, dozens of small useful pieces.
Handcrafted
A full furniture mod — tables, chairs, cabinets — for making builds feel lived-in.
Twigs / Stoneworks
Twigs adds new building materials and fresh vanilla-block takes; Stoneworks does the same specifically for stone types.
Decorative Blocks / Building Wands / Build Guide
Decorative Blocks (new decorative sets), Building Wands (place a whole shape at once), Build Guide (client-side shape projection — circles, spheres — works even without the mod on the server).
Convenient Decor / Macaw’s Holidays / Promenade
Convenient Decor (more decoration pieces), Macaw’s Holidays (250+ Christmas + 80+ Halloween decorations), Promenade (pathway/planter village decor).
Thaumon
Thaumcraft-inspired decoration blocks, purely aesthetic — no actual Thaumcraft magic attached.
Small decoration & building utilities (grouped)
Dark Paintings, DarkUtilities, Grass Overhaul, Oxidized (more copper uses), Connectible Chains, Double Doors, Derelict, Windchimes, Amendments, Satisfying Buttons, KleeSlabs, Fast Paintings, Reacharound, Quartz Elevator, Open Block Elevator Mod, Magnum Torch (wide-area mob-spawn prevention), Immersive Lanterns, Connectivity Mod, Kibe, Block Swap.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Amendment.title: Amendments
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Amendment.content:
Amendments
Amendments (by MehVahdJukaar) is a large grab-bag of small vanilla-block tweaks rather than a themed content set, and the pack’s amendments-common.json/amendments-client.json have nearly every tweak turned on. Highlights actually enabled here: carpet stairs/slabs, wall-mountable and swinging (physics-simulated) lanterns, hanging flower pots, a tripwire-hook tool holder, skull piles/skull candles, directional and stackable “double” cakes, ceiling-mountable banners, chain-hung bells (chain_length = 16), swinging hanging signs with real pendulum physics, and 3D snowball/slimeball/fireball projectiles. The standout system is the enhanced cauldron: it supports in-world and hand crafting, dyeing water, and mixing up to 8 potion effects together (potion_mixing_limit = 8), with an explicit table of “inverse” potion pairs (e.g. Speed↔Slowness, Strength↔Weakness) presumably used for effect-cancellation recipes. A “Quill” writing tool for books adds bold/italic/underline/strikethrough/obfuscated text formatting with colored ink — a genuine functional addition, not just decoration.
How you’ll use it here
Amendments quietly makes vanilla decorating feel finished: carpet slabs/stairs for soft floor detailing, hanging flower pots and wall-mounted swinging lanterns for exterior trim, chain-hung bells and hanging signs with real pendulum sway on porches and shopfronts, and ceiling banners in halls. For a lived-in interior, lean on skull piles/candles, double stackable cakes on a table, and the enhanced cauldron as a functional centerpiece (dyeing water, mixing potions in-world). The Quill is a genuine tool — use it to write formatted, colored-ink books for signage or lore drops in a build.
Anticipated questions
Do I need Amendments installed client-side? Generally yes — it changes how many vanilla blocks render (swinging lanterns, 3D projectiles, hanging signs with physics), so it typically needs to be present on the client to display correctly. It’s bundled in the pack, so everyone here has it.
How many potion effects can I stack in the cauldron? Up to 8 (potion_mixing_limit = 8), and the config lists inverse pairs like Speed↔Slowness and Strength↔Weakness that cancel each other.
Is the Quill just cosmetic text? No — it’s a functional writing tool adding bold/italic/underline/strikethrough/obfuscated formatting with colored ink to books, so it’s useful for real in-game signage and lore, not just decoration.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Block-Swa.title: Block Swap
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Block-Swa.content:
Block Swap
Block Swap (by Corgi Taco) is a small utility that silently replaces one block with another, either when a chunk loads/regenerates (retro_gen = true) or via an ID remap table for blocks whose registry name has changed. It’s not decorative in this pack’s usage — it’s modpack plumbing: config/blockswap/block_swap.json5 carries an active swapper map with 30+ entries that merge duplicate ore blocks across the pack’s overlapping tech mods, e.g. modern_industrialization:tin_ore → techreborn:tin_ore, indrev:silver_ore → techreborn:silver_ore, bewitchment:silver_ore → techreborn:silver_ore, and a few outright removals (modern_industrialization:replicator → minecraft:air, betternether:egg_plant → minecraft:air). This exists so that Tech Reborn, Modern Industrialization, Indrev, and Bewitchment don’t each generate their own separate version of the same real-world ore in the world. The state_swapper (block-state-level swaps) and id_remapper (broken-ID recovery) tables are both empty/unused here — only the simple block-to-block swapper is active.
How you’ll use it here
You don’t interact with Block Swap at all — it’s silent modpack plumbing, not a building tool. Its only job here is to merge duplicate ores from the pack’s overlapping tech mods (Tech Reborn, Modern Industrialization, Indrev, Bewitchment) into one canonical block, so mining tin or silver gives a single consistent ore instead of four near-identical variants.
Anticipated questions
Will Block Swap change blocks I’ve already placed in my base? Its swapper runs when a chunk loads/regenerates (retro_gen = true), and here it only targets duplicate tech-mod ores, not decorative blocks — so builds using normal decoration blocks are unaffected.
Can I use it to swap decoration blocks in my own build? Not as configured on this server — the state_swapper and id_remapper tables are empty and the active swapper map is reserved for the pack’s ore de-duplication.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Build-Gui.title: Build Guide
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Build-Gui.content:
Build Guide
Build Guide (brentmaas) is a client-side only mod (81 lang entries, mostly UI text) that projects wireframe shapes — circles and spheres — into the world so a player can see exactly where to place blocks for a perfect curve. Its fabric.mod.json description is explicit that this works “both in singleplayer and multiplayer, even if the server doesn’t have the mod installed” — meaning any player can install it locally for their own building help without needing it added to the modpack or whitelisted server-side. It’s bundled into Prominence II anyway so it’s guaranteed present and consistent for everyone.
config/buildguide.cfg sets asyncEnabled = true (shape generation runs off the main thread, avoiding lag spikes for large shapes), persistenceEnabled = false (projected shapes don’t survive a relog/restart — they’re a temporary building aid, not saved state), shapeListRandomColorsDefaultEnabled = false, and debugGenerationTimingsEnabled = false. Pairs naturally with Building Wands — project the sphere outline with Build Guide, then fill it in fast with a wand.
How you’ll use it here
When you need a clean dome, tower cap, or rounded pond edge, project a circle or sphere wireframe with Build Guide and place blocks exactly on the outline for a perfect curve — no more eyeballing pixel-art arcs. It’s the layout half of the workflow: sketch the shape in wireframe, then fill it in fast with Building Wands. Projected shapes are temporary (persistenceEnabled = false), so treat them as scaffolding you dismiss once the real blocks are down.
Anticipated questions
Do I need Build Guide on the server, or just my own client? Just your own — it’s client-side only and works “even if the server doesn’t have the mod installed.” It’s bundled into Prominence II anyway so everyone has it consistently.
Will my projected shapes survive a relog? No — persistenceEnabled = false means projections are cleared on relog/restart. They’re a live building aid, not saved state.
Does projecting a big sphere lag the game? Generally not — asyncEnabled = true runs shape generation off the main thread specifically to avoid lag spikes on large shapes.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Building-.title: Building Wands
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Building-.content:
Building Wands
Building Wands (nicguzzo) lets a player place a whole run of matching blocks from one item use instead of one block at a time — the classic “point at a wall, extend it 20 blocks” tool. Its 348 lang entries are mostly tooltip/description text for the tool tiers and modes rather than new blocks.
The server’s config/wands.json is worth knowing in detail because it materially changes how the tool behaves here: there are six wand tiers (stone, copper, iron, diamond, netherite, plus a creative-only tier), each with its own placement limit (stone 8 → copper/iron 24 → diamond 32 → netherite 64 → creative 512 blocks per use) and its own durability (stone 256 up to netherite 4096). max_limit is set to 8192 as a hard ceiling (“increment this if your machine can handle it”). Notably, every wand tier has allow_*_to_break set to false — wands are configured to never break from use on this server, regardless of durability running out — and mend_tools is enabled so Mending still works on them anyway. Vein mode and blast mode are both enabled (vein mode follows a connected vein of the same block type; blast mode presumably works in a spherical/radius pattern). There are also “magic bag” limits (17,280 and 172,800) for a linked-inventory feature. destroy_in_survival_drop is false and survival_unenchanted_drops is true, affecting whether wand-placed blocks drop items when broken.
How you’ll use it here
This is the big time-saver for any large build — point at a wall or floor and extend a whole run of matching blocks in one use instead of placing them one at a time. Pick a wand tier for the job: stone covers 8 blocks per use up through netherite’s 64 and the creative tier’s 512, so bigger tiers mean faster large surfaces. Use vein mode to follow a connected patch of one block type (great for swapping or extending an existing surface) and blast mode for radius/area fills. On this server the wands never break from use (allow_*_to_break = false) and Mending still applies, so you can build freely without babysitting durability. Pairs naturally with Build Guide: project the shape, then wand it in.
Anticipated questions
How many blocks can I place at once? It depends on the wand tier — stone 8, copper/iron 24, diamond 32, netherite 64, and the creative-only tier 512 per use, with a hard max_limit ceiling of 8192.
Will my wand break if the durability runs out? No — every tier has allow_*_to_break set to false on this server, so wands never break from use, and mend_tools keeps Mending working on them anyway.
Do wand-placed blocks come from my inventory? Generally yes — building wands consume the matching blocks you’re holding/carrying to place the run, so you need enough of that block on hand.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Chipped-E.title: Chipped-Express
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Chipped-E.content:
Chipped-Express
Chipped-Express (by DevDyna, v1.3.2) is a small, purely-functional companion to Chipped. Its fabric.mod.json description is blunt about its purpose: “Chipped mod still a good but cannot be automated, this mod allow autocrafting using other mods like AE2 or Create.” It ships no new lang entries of its own (no en_us.json was found in the jar) — it isn’t adding blocks or items, it’s adding the crafting-system glue (recipe types/patterns) that lets Applied Energistics 2 autocrafting and Create’s mechanical crafting recognize and produce Chipped’s ~7,000+ block variants automatically, instead of requiring a player to hand-craft each one at a crafting table.
Practically: without Chipped-Express, Chipped’s huge catalog is still fully craftable, just entirely by hand. With it, an AE2 or Create automation setup can treat Chipped blocks like any other autocraftable item — relevant for anyone trying to mass-produce a specific block variant (e.g. hundreds of a single mosaic-plank type) for a large build.
How you’ll use it here
You won’t see any new blocks or items from Chipped-Express — it’s pure crafting-system glue. Its payoff shows up once you have an AE2 or Create automation setup: Chipped’s ~7,000 variants become autocraftable like any other item, so instead of hand-crafting hundreds of one mosaic-plank type for a big build, you request them from your ME system or a mechanical crafter. Only worth bothering with when you’re mass-producing a specific variant; for one-off decorating, hand-crafting Chipped blocks is fine.
Anticipated questions
Do I need Chipped-Express to use Chipped blocks? No — Chipped’s full catalog is craftable by hand without it. Chipped-Express only adds the ability to autocraft those blocks through AE2 or Create.
What do I need set up before this does anything? An AE2 autocrafting network or a Create mechanical-crafting setup — see Storage & Applied Energistics — Getting Started. Chipped-Express is just the integration layer that lets those systems recognize Chipped recipes.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Chipped.title: Chipped
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Chipped.content:
Chipped
Chipped (by Alex Nijjar, Grimbop, Kekie6, ThatGravyBoat — tagline “Every block needs a friend!”) is the single largest content mod in the Building & Decoration category: its en_us.json carries 7,258 lang entries. The bulk of that count comes from combinatorial variant generation — barrels, crates, mosaics, panels, shavings, and torches are each generated for essentially every wood type present in the modpack, including woods added by other mods (e.g. Ad Astra’s froglight variants show up as block.chipped.ad_astra_*_froglight). The result is that almost any base material in the pack — vanilla or modded — gets a matching set of small decorative furniture-adjacent blocks (torches, trapdoors in “airy” style, mosaic planks, shaving textures) rather than builders being limited to oak/spruce/etc.
There’s no dedicated config file for Chipped in config/ and no Patchouli guidebook — it’s pure block-variant content, discovered through the creative menu/JEI rather than an in-game manual. Because Chipped’s blocks are hand-crafted (not autocrafted), the companion mod Chipped-Express exists specifically to make this enormous catalog machine-craftable.
How you’ll use it here
Chipped is your palette-expansion mod: almost any base material in the pack — vanilla or modded — gets a matching set of small decorative blocks (barrels, crates, mosaics, panels, shavings, torches, airy-style trapdoors), so you’re not stuck with plain oak/spruce when detailing a base. Browse the variants through the creative menu or JEI (there’s no guidebook), pick the mosaics and panels that fit your theme, and use them to add texture variety to walls, floors, and trim. Because every variant is hand-crafted at a table, plan ahead for large builds — for mass quantities of one variant, route it through Chipped-Express with AE2 or Create autocrafting.
Anticipated questions
Where’s the Chipped guidebook or config? There isn’t one — Chipped ships no config file and no Patchouli manual here. It’s pure block-variant content, so you discover everything through the creative menu or JEI.
Can I automate crafting all these variants? Not with Chipped alone — its blocks are hand-crafted. The companion Chipped-Express adds the glue that lets AE2 or Create autocraft them; see Storage & Applied Energistics — Getting Started for the mass-crafting setup.
How does Chipped have 7,000+ blocks? They’re generated combinatorially — families like barrels, crates, mosaics, panels, shavings, and torches are produced for essentially every wood type in the pack, including woods added by other mods.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Connectib.title: Connectible Chains
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Connectib.content:
Connectible Chains
Connectible Chains (by legoatoom) lets you shift-click a chain item between two fence posts or walls to string up a decorative catenary — the chain physically sags between the two points instead of rendering as a straight line. The pack’s config (connectiblechains.toml) sets maxChainRange = 7 blocks and chainHangAmount = 7.0 (lower values mean a bigger droop), plus a render quality = 4 for how many segments the curve is drawn with. It’s a pure decoration mod — fence-and-chain bridges, lamp posts, nautical/dock detailing — with no functional side effects beyond the visual connector and its (togglable) block collision.
How you’ll use it here
Shift-click a chain between two fence posts or walls and it hangs in a sagging catenary instead of a rigid line — ideal for fence-and-chain bridge railings, lamp-post connectors, and nautical/dock detailing on piers. With maxChainRange = 7, keep your anchor posts within 7 blocks of each other, and lean on the natural droop to make barriers and decorative runs look hand-strung rather than snapped-to-grid.
Anticipated questions
How far apart can two chain anchors be? Up to 7 blocks (maxChainRange = 7); beyond that the chain won’t connect.
Does it do anything besides look good? No — it’s pure decoration. The only side effect is the visual connector and its (togglable) block collision; there are no functional/redstone effects.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Connectiv.title: Connectivity Mod
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Connectiv.content:
Connectivity Mod
Despite the name suggesting a block-connection/decoration mod (and its placement in this category), Connectivity (by Someaddons) is actually a network stability fix — it has nothing to do with building or decoration. In a modpack this large, vanilla’s packet size and login-timing limits get hit easily (too much data in one login/chunk packet, chat-signature verification hiccups, etc.), and this mod raises or disables those limits so players don’t get disconnected. The pack’s connectivity.json has disableLoginLimits and disablePacketLimits both on, disableChatVerificationDisconnect on (avoids client disconnects over chat-signing edge cases), a stretched logintimeout of 2400 seconds (40 minutes, vs. the default 120s — presumably to tolerate slow modded client startup), a 60s in-game disconnect timeout, and basic malformed/malicious traffic detection enabled with no proxy whitelist configured. Worth knowing this exists if players ever get mysterious connection-related kicks — it’s one of the mods actively working to prevent that.
How you’ll use it here
There’s nothing to build or place — Connectivity is an invisible network-stability fix, not a decoration mod. Its practical value to you is fewer disconnects: it raises vanilla’s packet/login limits so a modpack this large doesn’t kick you during login or big chunk loads. Worth remembering it exists if a friend hits a mysterious connection kick.
Anticipated questions
Is Connectivity why I’m sometimes disconnected? Generally the opposite — it’s actively raising limits to prevent connection kicks. On this server, random “Timed out” disconnects are typically the playit.gg free tunnel flapping between datacenters, not this mod.
Do I need to configure anything? No — the pack’s connectivity.json already has the relevant limits disabled/raised (login limits, packet limits, chat-verification disconnect off, a 2400s login timeout). It just works in the background.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Convenien.title: Convenient Decor
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Convenien.content:
Convenient Decor
Convenient Decor (Mim1q) is smaller than its name suggests as a pure decoration mod (114 lang entries) — a chunk of its content is actually functional wearables and tools rather than static blocks. Its config/convenientdecor.json5 file, gated behind a warning that changes must match on both client and server and require a full restart, exposes feature toggles: a watering can can permanently hydrate farmland with a right-click (on), an umbrella attracts lightning during thunderstorms (on) and slows falling / reduces fall damage when held up (on), rain clothes grant extra hearts while raining/storming (on), and there are dedicated integration toggles for the Origins mod so umbrellas and rain hats/coats interact with Origins’ rain/sunlight power (both on).
So on this server: watering cans are a real farming convenience item (not just decorative), and umbrellas/rain clothes are functional weather-gear with real mechanical effects, not purely cosmetic. All six of these are enabled by default here.
How you’ll use it here
Despite the name, the useful items here are functional gear, not static decor. Craft a watering can to permanently hydrate farmland with a right-click (a real farming shortcut), carry an umbrella to slow your fall / reduce fall damage when held up (and note it attracts lightning in thunderstorms — a hazard, not a bonus), and wear rain clothes for extra hearts while it’s raining or storming. All six of these features are enabled here, so treat them as working equipment when kitting out a base or farm.
Anticipated questions
Is the watering can just decorative? No — it permanently hydrates farmland on right-click, so it’s a genuine farming convenience item, and it’s enabled by default on this server.
Should I hold an umbrella out in a thunderstorm? Be careful — the umbrella attracts lightning during thunderstorms (enabled here). It also slows falling and reduces fall damage when held up, so it’s genuinely useful, just risky in a storm.
Do these need to match on client and server? Yes — the config is gated behind a warning that changes must match on both client and server and require a full restart.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Dark-Pain.title: Dark Paintings
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Dark-Pain.content:
Dark Paintings
Dark Paintings (Darkhax) is a small, single-purpose mod adding “a variety of new paintings to the game” — 100 lang entries, which for a paintings mod means roughly that many individual painting artworks (each painting typically needs just a title/author lang entry). It’s a pure wall-art expansion: more canvas options for interior decoration than vanilla’s fixed painting pool, no new mechanics. Pairs with the same author’s DarkUtilities, also present in this modpack.
No config file ships for it here, and there’s nothing to tune — paintings are placed the same way vanilla paintings are (canvas + item frame-like placement), just from a much larger art pool.
How you’ll use it here
Use Dark Paintings to fill wall space in interiors with far more art variety than vanilla’s fixed pool — roughly 100 individual artworks to choose from. Place them exactly like vanilla paintings (on a wall, item-frame-style), and use them to give galleries, halls, and living spaces distinct character instead of the same handful of default canvases.
Anticipated questions
How do I pick which painting appears? It’s placed the same way as vanilla paintings — the artwork shown depends on the available wall space, just drawn from a much larger art pool.
Is there anything to configure? No — no config file ships for it here and there’s nothing to tune; it’s a pure wall-art expansion with no new mechanics.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/DarkUtili.title: DarkUtilities
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/DarkUtili.content:
DarkUtilities
DarkUtilities (Darkhax) is “a broad assortment of new utility blocks and items” (125 lang entries) that leans more functional/redstone than decorative, despite living in the Building & Decoration category. Its standout feature set is plates — pressure-plate-style trigger blocks with much more specific behavior than vanilla’s: Blank Plate, Vector Plate (and Fast/Extreme/Ultra Vector Plate tiers, implying detection-speed or range variants), Damage Plate, Maim Plate, Player Damage Plate, and a whole family of status-effect plates (Flame, Slowness, Fatigue, Darkness, Hunger, Weakness, Poison, Wither, Alert, Levitation, Misfortune, Slow Fall, Ominous, Frost). Alongside these are mob filter blocks — Undead, Animal, Arthropod, Player, and more — which read as detection/filtering redstone components for selectively triggering on specific mob categories walking over them.
Together these make DarkUtilities a small redstone-trap/detection toolkit — useful for building mob farms with selective triggers, PvP-arena hazard plates, or automated player-detection systems — layered in with the more purely-cosmetic mods in this category. No config file ships for it on this server.
How you’ll use it here
Reach for DarkUtilities when building traps, farms, and arenas rather than pure decoration. Lay Vector Plates (and the Fast/Extreme/Ultra tiers) to shove mobs or items along a floor toward a collection point, use Damage/Maim/status-effect plates (Poison, Wither, Slowness, Levitation, and the rest) as arena hazards or kill floors in a mob farm, and pair them with the mob-filter blocks (Undead, Animal, Arthropod, Player) to trigger only on the mob category you want. Together they make selective mob-sorting and player-detection redstone practical.
Anticipated questions
What’s the difference between the Vector Plate tiers? The Blank/Fast/Extreme/Ultra naming implies increasing push speed or range — use a higher tier where you need mobs or items moved faster/farther across the plate.
Can I trigger a plate only when a specific mob walks over it? Generally yes — that’s what the mob-filter blocks (Undead, Animal, Arthropod, Player, etc.) are for: detection/filtering components that let you fire on a chosen mob category, useful for selective mob-farm triggers or player-detection systems.
Is there a config to tweak these? No config file ships for DarkUtilities on this server, so the plates and filters behave at their defaults.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Decorativ.title: Decorative Blocks
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Decorativ.content:
Decorative Blocks
Decorative Blocks (Stohun, lilypuree; Fabric port by TheWinABagel) adds 71 lang entries centered on structural-decoration pieces rather than furniture: beam, palisade, seat, and support blocks are generated per wood type (mangrove, crimson, warped, bamboo, cherry, acacia, oak, jungle, dark oak, birch, etc.), plus standalone pieces like a big chain and brazier / soul brazier. “Beams” and “supports” read as timber-frame architectural elements — the pieces that make exposed wooden structural framing look intentional rather than like plain log placement — while “palisade” and “seat” cover fencing and outdoor-seating use cases.
It’s a compact mod (71 entries vs. Stoneworks’ 582 or Chipped’s thousands), so it’s best thought of as a focused toolkit for timber-frame and rustic exterior detail rather than a broad decoration library. No config file ships for it on this server.
How you’ll use it here
Reach for this when a wooden build reads as flat log-and-plank boxes and needs structural character. Use beams and supports to frame exposed timber skeletons on a barn, tavern, or bridge, run a palisade as rough fencing around a rustic compound, drop seats for outdoor benching, and set a brazier or soul brazier as a fire-lit centerpiece with a big chain hanging above. Because pieces come per wood type (oak, birch, acacia, dark oak, cherry, crimson, warped, bamboo, etc.), you can match the framing to whatever palette the rest of the build already uses.
Anticipated questions
Does this add furniture like tables and chairs? Not really — it’s structural-decoration focused (beams, supports, palisades, seats, braziers). For sit-at furniture use Handcrafted instead.
Do beams and supports come in every wood type? They’re generated per wood type across the pack’s wood set, so you can generally match most vanilla and modded woods — check the recipe viewer for the exact variant you want.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Derelict.title: Derelict
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Derelict.content:
Derelict
Derelict is a decoration set built around making builds look abandoned and weathered: a full “burned” wood palette (burned planks/log/stairs/slab/fence/door/trapdoor/button/pressure plate/signs, even burned leaves and dried/burned grass), plus per-wood-type “cover boards” (oak through bamboo, including a burned variant) for boarding up windows, and flickering-light blocks. Two hand tools drive the aging theme: an Aging Staff that ages blocks forward (fresh → weathered/burned) and a Waxing Staff that reverses it, mirroring vanilla’s copper wax mechanic but applied to Derelict’s own block set. It also adds a small hostile mob, the Spiderling, which per derelict.json5 has a spiderlingSpawnChance of 10% to spawn when tagged entities die.
The server config sets flickeringLights = "FANCY" (affects emitted light level, better look than “FAST”, cheaper than “FABULOUS”) with a note in the config that hosts with many players or light-sensitive players should consider “FAST” instead — worth knowing if flicker performance ever comes up. The client config adds waxable/ageable block highlight ranges (16 blocks) and crosshair hints when holding the staves or a honeycomb.
How you’ll use it here
Use this to build ruins, abandoned outposts, and post-disaster scenes that fit the Hasturian-era mood. Lay the full burned palette (planks, logs, stairs, slabs, fences, doors, signs, even burned leaves and dried grass) for a torched structure, board up openings with per-wood cover boards, and set flickering-light blocks for an unreliable, guttering glow. The real workflow is the two staves: build fresh and then sweep the Aging Staff over blocks to weather or char them in place, and undo any spot you overdid with the Waxing Staff — so you can dial in exactly how derelict each wall looks.
Anticipated questions
How do I make a block look aged or burned? Hold the Aging Staff and use it on a supported block to age it forward; the Waxing Staff reverses it. The client highlights waxable/ageable blocks within 16 blocks and shows crosshair hints while you hold a staff or honeycomb.
Does anything here actually spawn mobs? Yes — the Spiderling has a 10% chance (spiderlingSpawnChance) to spawn when certain tagged entities die, so a derelict build isn’t purely cosmetic.
Will the flickering lights hurt server performance? They’re set to FANCY here (a middle ground); the config notes that heavily-populated or light-sensitive setups can drop to FAST if flicker ever causes trouble.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Double-Do.title: Double Doors
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Double-Do.content:
Double Doors
Double Doors (by Rick South) makes a pair of identical doors, trapdoors, or fence gates placed side-by-side open and close together, whether triggered by hand, a pressure plate, or a button. The pack’s config (doubledoors.json5) has doors and fence gates enabled but trapdoors disabled (enableTrapdoors = false). It also enables “recursive opening” — click one door in a large connected bank of identical doors/gates (e.g. a big hangar-style entrance) and the mod searches outward up to recursiveOpeningMaxBlocksDistance = 10 blocks to open every connected match at once, not just the immediate neighbor.
How you’ll use it here
Build double-wide entrances that behave like real double doors: place two matching doors side-by-side and one click, pressure plate, or button swings both together — no more opening each half separately. It works on fence gates too, so a wide paddock or courtyard gate opens as a unit. For big builds, a full connected bank of identical doors or gates (a hangar or great-hall entrance) opens all at once via recursive opening, searching up to 10 blocks outward from the one you clicked.
Anticipated questions
Why don’t my double trapdoors open together? Trapdoors are disabled here (enableTrapdoors = false); only doors and fence gates are linked in this pack.
How many doors will one click open in a big gate? It opens every connected matching door/gate the mod can reach within recursiveOpeningMaxBlocksDistance = 10 blocks of the one you triggered.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Fast-Pain.title: Fast Paintings
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Fast-Pain.content:
Fast Paintings
Fast Paintings (by Mehvahdjukaar) converts vanilla paintings from entities into blocks, which is mostly a performance fix — painting entities are notoriously expensive to tick and sync in large numbers, and turning them into blocks avoids that entirely. It also adds a selection GUI for picking which piece of art to place (paintings.toml: use_selection_gui = true, use_vanilla_only = false, so modded/expanded art pools are available, and show_painting_size = true shows dimensions while choosing) and, per the mod’s own config note, model customization. The pack keeps nbt_drop = "OFF" in fastpaintings-common.json, meaning a specific chosen painting doesn’t preserve its exact art via NBT when broken and re-picked up.
How you’ll use it here
Hang art without the vanilla guessing game: place a painting and a selection GUI pops up so you can pick the exact piece you want (with its size shown) instead of cycling randomly. Because the pool isn’t vanilla-only here, any modded/expanded art in the pack is available to choose from, so you can decorate galleries, hallways, and feature walls deliberately. As a bonus it’s a quiet performance win — paintings are blocks now rather than entities, so a wall of them doesn’t tax the server.
Anticipated questions
How do I choose which painting I get? The selection GUI is on (use_selection_gui = true), so placing one opens a picker showing each artwork and its dimensions.
If I break a painting, does it keep the exact art I picked? Generally no — nbt_drop = "OFF" here, so a broken-and-replaced painting doesn’t preserve its specific art via NBT; you’d reselect it on placement.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Grass-Ove.title: Grass Overhaul
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Grass-Ove.content:
Grass Overhaul
Grass Overhaul (ElocinDev, Luna Pixel Studios) is a compact, focused mod (29 lang entries) that does exactly one thing well: it adds stackable, carpet-like sod blocks — slabs, stairs, patches, and full blocks — for every ground-cover surface in the game: Grass, Podzol, Path (dirt path), Dirt, Mycelium, Crimson Nylium, and Warped Nylium. Each surface type gets the full set (e.g. Grass Sod Block/Slab/Stairs/Patch, Podzol Sod Block/Slab/Stairs/Patch), which lets builders create thin, natural-looking terrain transitions and terraced ground detail that vanilla’s single-thickness grass blocks can’t achieve — a “sod patch” in particular acts like a thin carpet-style overlay rather than a full block.
No config file ships for it on this server. It’s a small but high-value mod for terrain and landscaping detail work specifically — the terrain equivalent of what Stoneworks does for stone architecture.
How you’ll use it here
Use sod pieces to soften the hard edges vanilla ground blocks leave behind. Lay sod slabs and stairs to make grass, path, or podzol step down gently into terraced gardens and hillsides, and drop sod patches as thin carpet-style overlays to scatter natural-looking ground cover across a courtyard or forest floor. Because every surface gets the full set — Grass, Podzol, Path, Dirt, Mycelium, and both Nyliums — you can blend biome transitions (grass fading into podzol under trees, nylium creeping across a Nether build) with real height and thickness detail.
Anticipated questions
Which ground types can I get sod for? Grass, Podzol, dirt Path, Dirt, Mycelium, Crimson Nylium, and Warped Nylium — each in block, slab, stairs, and patch form.
What’s a sod patch versus a sod slab? A patch acts like a thin carpet-style overlay laid on top of a surface, while slabs/stairs are half- and stepped-height blocks for terracing — use patches for subtle ground detail, slabs/stairs for shaped terrain.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Handcraft.title: Handcrafted
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Handcraft.content:
Handcrafted
Handcrafted (Alex Nijjar, Kekie6 — “Epic Furniture mod!”) is a dedicated furniture mod with 392 lang entries. Its catalog is a fixed furniture set — bench, chair, corner trim, couch, counter, cupboard, desk, dining bench, drawer, fancy bed, nightstand, pillar trim, shelf, side table, table — reproduced across essentially every wood type in the modpack, plus stone “trim” pieces (e.g. andesite corner/pillar trims) for matching stonework builds. This is the mod that gives Prominence II builds a “lived-in” interior feel — tables and chairs to sit at, cupboards and drawers for storage-flavor decoration, nightstands and fancy beds for bedrooms — rather than relying on vanilla’s bare furniture-less block palette.
No config file for Handcrafted was found under config/, so it runs on its shipped defaults, and there’s no Patchouli guidebook — like most mods in this category it’s discovered through creative search/JEI. It pairs naturally with Supplementaries and Chipped for filling out interiors: Handcrafted for sit-at furniture, the others for smaller shelf-decoration and wall pieces.
How you’ll use it here
This is your go-to for making interiors feel lived-in. Furnish a dining room with a table, chairs, and dining benches; build a kitchen or shop counter from counters and cupboards; line a study with shelves, a desk, and drawers; and finish a bedroom with a fancy bed and matching nightstand. Every piece comes across essentially every wood type in the pack, so you can keep a room’s furniture consistent with its build palette, and the stone “trim” pieces (like andesite corner and pillar trims) let you carry that detailing onto stonework exteriors.
Anticipated questions
Is the furniture functional or just decorative? It’s decoration-focused — chairs, tables, cupboards, and drawers dress a room rather than adding real storage slots. Pair it with Supplementaries/Chipped for shelf pieces and functional storage flavor.
Does it come in the wood type I’m building with? Almost certainly — the full furniture set is reproduced across essentially every wood type in the modpack, plus some stone trims; check the recipe viewer for your specific wood.
Is there a guidebook for it? No Patchouli guidebook and no config here — it runs on defaults, so you discover pieces through creative search / the recipe viewer.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Immersive.title: Immersive Lanterns
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Immersive.content:
Immersive Lanterns
Immersive Lanterns (by Toni) gives lanterns two upgrades: dynamic (moving) light when carried, and Accessories-mod support so a lantern can be worn/equipped rather than just held or placed, complete with swinging physics as you move. The pack’s client config leaves swinging physics on (Lantern Bounciness = 1.0, default) and keeps lanterns on the right hand / front of the player (Left-Handed Lanterns = false, Back Lanterns = false). It’s a cosmetic/QoL mod with no server-side gameplay effect — the swing physics are flagged in the mod’s own lang file as having no performance impact.
Anticipated questions
What does it add? Two upgrades to lanterns: dynamic (moving) light when a lantern is carried, and Accessories-mod support so a lantern can be worn/equipped rather than only held or placed — with swinging physics as you move.
Is it client- or server-side? It’s a cosmetic/QoL mod with no server-side gameplay effect; the swing physics are flagged in the mod’s own lang file as having no performance impact.
Do I hold the lantern or wear it? Either — it can still be held or placed, but Accessories support lets you equip it. The client config keeps lanterns on the right hand / front of the player by default (Left-Handed Lanterns = false, Back Lanterns = false).
Can I turn off the swinging? The pack leaves swinging physics on by default (Lantern Bounciness = 1.0), and it’s a client config value, so it’s a personal visual choice rather than a server setting.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Kibe.title: Kibe
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Kibe.content:
Kibe
Kibe (by D4rkness_King) is a genuine kitchen-sink mod — its own description calls it “a bunch of random, and mostly unoriginal things” — and it doesn’t fit neatly under Building & Decoration; it’s mostly small tech/utility content borrowed in spirit from OpenBlocks and similar mods. Notable additions: colored conveyor belts (regular/fast/express) and colored elevator blocks (all 16 dye colors), tiered cobblestone and basalt generators (MK1–MK5), an XP shower/drain pair, entangled tanks/chests/buckets/bags (linked-inventory teleportation, Ender-chest-style), a chunk loader, a drawbridge, automation blocks (breaker, placer, igniter, wither builder), witherproof block/sand/glass, colored sleeping bags, and cursed dirt (a hostile-mob-spawning grief block, capped by cursedDirtMobCap = 25 in kibe.json).
The pack’s config tunes several of these: magnetRange = 8.0 (an item-magnet effect, likely from a ring/accessory), gliderUnbreakable = true with gliderDurability = 36000 (an elytra-like item), maxRingsPerPlayer = 1 (limits a teleport/utility ring to one at a time), and a chunk loader module that’s present but effectively unrestricted (maxPerPlayer = -1, maxOfflineTime = -1, checkForPlayer = false — chunks stay loaded indefinitely regardless of whether the owning player is online). Given the range of unrelated systems bundled together, this is really a miscellaneous-utility mod that happens to include a few decorative/QoL blocks (sleeping bags, elevators) alongside true automation content.
Anticipated questions
Is this really a Building & Decoration mod? Not really — it’s a kitchen-sink miscellaneous-utility mod that happens to include a few decorative/QoL blocks. Most of its content is small tech/automation borrowed in spirit from OpenBlocks and similar mods.
What decorative/QoL content does it actually add? The building-friendly pieces are colored sleeping bags and colored elevator blocks (all 16 dye colors); the rest (conveyor belts, generators, automation blocks, entangled storage, etc.) is utility/automation content.
What should I watch out for on a server? Its chunk loader is present but effectively unrestricted here (maxPerPlayer = -1, maxOfflineTime = -1, checkForPlayer = false), so loaded chunks stay loaded indefinitely even when the owner is offline. Cursed dirt also spawns hostile mobs as a grief block, capped at cursedDirtMobCap = 25.
Are any of its items limited by config? Yes — a teleport/utility ring is capped at one per player (maxRingsPerPlayer = 1), the elytra-like glider is unbreakable (gliderUnbreakable = true, gliderDurability = 36000), and an item-magnet effect has range 8 (magnetRange = 8.0).

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/KleeSlabs.title: KleeSlabs
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/KleeSlabs.content:
KleeSlabs
KleeSlabs (by BlayTheNinth) fixes a long-standing vanilla annoyance: breaking a double slab normally destroys both halves at once. With this mod, hitting a double slab only breaks the half you’re actually looking at, leaving the other in place. The pack’s config runs it in mode = "ALWAYS" (as opposed to only-while-sneaking or only-while-not-sneaking) with no mod compatibility overrides disabled. Single-mechanic, no other content.
Anticipated questions
What does it change? It fixes the vanilla behavior where breaking a double slab destroys both halves — with KleeSlabs, hitting a double slab only breaks the half you’re actually looking at, leaving the other in place.
Does it add any blocks or items? No — it’s a single-mechanic mod with no other content; it only alters how double slabs break.
Do I have to sneak for it to work? No. The pack runs it in mode = "ALWAYS", so partial slab-breaking applies all the time, not just while sneaking (or not sneaking).

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Macaw's-H.title: Macaw's Holidays
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Macaw's-H.content:
Macaw’s Holidays
Macaw’s Holidays (Sketch Macaw and Sketch Peachy) is a themed seasonal-decoration entry in the Macaw’s family of building mods, adding 250+ Christmas decorations and 80+ Halloween-themed decorations per its own description — 338 lang entries in total confirm a large, dedicated catalog rather than a handful of token items. It’s the mod to reach for if anyone wants to deck out a build for a holiday event: think string lights, ornaments, wreaths, and festive furniture variants for Christmas, and jack-o’-lanterns, cobwebs, and spooky decor variants for Halloween, layered on top of the wood-type-variant pattern common to the rest of this category.
No config file ships for it here, so it runs with all content available by default year-round rather than being date-gated.
Anticipated questions
What does it add? A large seasonal-decoration catalog — 250+ Christmas decorations (string lights, ornaments, wreaths, festive furniture variants) and 80+ Halloween decorations (jack-o’-lanterns, cobwebs, spooky variants), 338 lang entries in total.
Are the decorations only available on their real-world dates? No — no config file ships for it here, so all content is available by default year-round rather than being date-gated.
When would I use it in a build? It’s the mod to reach for when decking out a build for a holiday event, layered on top of the wood-type-variant pattern shared with the rest of this category (pairs with Handcrafted and Chipped).

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Magnum-To.title: Magnum Torch
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Magnum-To.content:
Magnum Torch
Magnum Torch (by Fuzs) adds three upgraded torches — Diamond, Emerald, and Amethyst — that each prevent mob spawns in a large area around them, well beyond vanilla torches’ small light-based radius. The pack’s magnumtorch-server.toml tunes each one differently rather than leaving them identical:

Diamond Torch: 64×32 (horizontal×vertical) ellipsoid, blocks MONSTER-category natural/patrol/structure/jockey spawns.
Emerald Torch: the biggest range at 128×64, cuboid-shaped, blocks CREATURE-category natural and event spawns (so it can push out passive-mob-adjacent event spawns too).
Amethyst Torch: 64×32 ellipsoid, blocks ambient/axolotl/water-creature spawns — i.e. it’s the one aimed at keeping water/cave-ambient mobs away rather than monsters.

All three explicitly still allow spawner-, breeding-, and (mostly) event-based spawns through — they only suppress natural/passive spawning per their configured blocked_spawn_types, so a mob farm or raid won’t be silently broken by having one nearby. This is the sort of config detail worth knowing before placing one near a mob farm.
Anticipated questions
What does it add? Three upgraded torches — Diamond, Emerald, and Amethyst — that each prevent mob spawns in a large area around them, well beyond a vanilla torch’s small light-based radius.
Is it client- or server-side? The spawn-suppression ranges and rules are set server-side in magnumtorch-server.toml.
Will placing one break my mob farm or raid? No — all three still allow spawner-, breeding-, and (mostly) event-based spawns; they only suppress natural/passive spawning per their configured blocked_spawn_types. It’s still worth checking before placing one near a farm.
Which torch does what? Diamond is a 64×32 ellipsoid blocking MONSTER-category spawns; Emerald is the biggest at 128×64 (cuboid) blocking CREATURE-category natural/event spawns; Amethyst is a 64×32 ellipsoid aimed at ambient/axolotl/water-creature spawns.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Open-Bloc.title: Open Block Elevator Mod
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Open-Bloc.content:
Open Block Elevator Mod
A Fabric port (by farrucho) of the classic OpenBlocks Elevator: a single “Elevator Block” that, when stacked in a vertical column, lets an entity ride straight up or down between blocks in that column instead of climbing/falling normally. The pack’s openblocksconfig.properties sets openblocks.elevator.block.range = 20, i.e. a column works up to 20 blocks.
This mod and Quartz Elevator solve the same problem (vertical block-elevators) and both are installed in this pack — Quartz Elevator’s smooth variant reaches much farther (64 blocks) and is player-only, while this one caps at 20 blocks but is the more nostalgic, original OpenBlocks-style block. Having both suggests the modpack leaves it up to the builder’s taste/aesthetic rather than picking one as canonical.
How you’ll use it here
Stack Elevator Blocks in a vertical column to move between floors of a multi-story base — jump to rise to the next block above, crouch to drop to the one below, skipping ladders and staircases entirely. With the pack’s 20-block range each pair of blocks can be up to 20 apart, so a single hop covers a tall room or a couple of floors. Good for the OpenBlocks look; reach for Quartz Elevator instead when a shaft needs to span more than 20 blocks.
Anticipated questions
How far apart can the elevator blocks be? Up to 20 blocks here (openblocks.elevator.block.range = 20) — space them any distance up to that and the jump/crouch teleport still connects them.
Does it only move players? Generally the OpenBlocks-style elevator moves any entity that stands on it and jumps, unlike Quartz Elevator’s player-only variant — check in-world if you want mobs or items to ride it.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Oxidized.title: Oxidized
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Oxidized.content:
Oxidized
Oxidized (Safro) adds “more vanilla+ uses for copper” (38 lang entries) — a small mod, but a functionally dense one, judging by config/oxidized_config.json. Two headline features are enabled on this server: copper rails (copper_rail_range: 50 — an extended-range rail variant, presumably a cheaper/simpler powered-rail alternative) and a copper pulsar (enable_copper_pulsar: true, pulsar_reach: 10 — a redstone pulse-emitting block with a 10-block reach). There’s also a copper golem (enable_copper_golem: true, with a copper_golem_button_chance: 30 — likely the odds it presses a nearby button while wandering, referencing the real Minecraft 1.21 copper golem concept implemented early here) and rose gold tools (enable_rose_gold_tools: true), giving copper an actual tool-tier alongside iron/gold.
The config also tunes a copper-panning mechanic: iron_nugget_chance and gold_nugget_chance at 0.15 each, sand_chance 0.24, gravel_chance 0.12, and a rare emerald_chance of 0.02, plus enable_copper_pan_sound: true — strongly implying a copper pan tool that sifts through gravel/sand for nuggets and the occasional emerald, similar to real-world gold panning. This makes Oxidized one of the more mechanically interesting mods in an otherwise mostly-cosmetic category.
How you’ll use it here
Copper becomes a proper mid-tier metal rather than just a decoration block: lay copper rails (50-block range here) as a cheaper alternative to powered rails on long minecart lines, craft rose gold tools for a tool tier sitting alongside iron and gold, and wire a copper pulsar (10-block reach) into redstone contraptions that need a repeating pulse. For a passive resource loop, use the copper pan to sift gravel and sand for iron/gold nuggets and the occasional emerald. A copper golem may also wander and press nearby buttons, so factor that in around redstone you don’t want triggered.
Anticipated questions
What do I get from panning? Per the config, sifting yields iron and gold nuggets (~15% each), sand and gravel, and a rare emerald (~2%) — a slow trickle, not a farm, so treat it as flavor income rather than a main source.
Are rose gold tools better than iron? They’re a distinct tool tier the mod adds alongside iron and gold; the note doesn’t give exact stats, so compare durability and speed in-game before committing.
What does the copper pulsar do? It emits a redstone pulse with a 10-block reach — generally useful as a repeating clock or remote trigger in redstone builds.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Promenade.title: Promenade
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Promenade.content:
Promenade
Promenade (Hugman) bills itself as “Fancy and simplistic animals, biomes, structures and more!” and, unusually for this category, actually spans decoration blocks, new stone types, world generation, and mob spawns together — 211 lang entries. Decoration-side it adds leaf piles and flower piles for every vanilla leaf/flower type (oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, azalea leaves; dandelion, poppy, blue orchid, allium, tulips, oxeye daisy, cornflower, lily of the valley, wither rose piles) — good ground-clutter detail for naturalistic builds — plus a new stone type, Blunite, with the standard cut-stone family (stairs, slab, wall, column, polished variants).
It also touches world content: config/promenade/ has separate animals.json, monsters.json, biomes.json, and world_features.json files. On this server, animals.json sets spawn weights for capybaras (10) and ducks (10), and monsters.json sets weights for lush creepers (15) and sunken skeletons (20) — these read as Promenade-added mob variants tied to specific biome themes, spawning alongside vanilla mobs rather than replacing them.
Anticipated questions
What does it add? Unusually for this category, it spans decoration, new stone types, world generation, and mob spawns together (211 lang entries).
What’s the decoration content? Leaf piles and flower piles for every vanilla leaf/flower type (oak through mangrove, azalea; dandelion, poppy, tulips, wither rose, etc.) — good ground clutter — plus a new stone type, Blunite, with the standard cut-stone family (stairs, slab, wall, column, polished variants).
Does it add mobs? Yes — it touches world content via config/promenade/. On this server animals.json sets spawn weights for capybaras (10) and ducks (10), and monsters.json sets weights for lush creepers (15) and sunken skeletons (20); these spawn alongside vanilla mobs rather than replacing them.
Is it client- or server-side? Its worldgen and spawn behavior are server-side, driven by the JSON files in config/promenade/ (animals.json, monsters.json, biomes.json, world_features.json).

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Quartz-El.title: Quartz Elevator
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Quartz-El.content:
Quartz Elevator
Quartz Elevator (by Aton-Kish) adds two blocks — Quartz Elevator and Smooth Quartz Elevator — that launch/lift an entity straight up when stood on, functioning like a vertical block-elevator column. The pack’s config (quartzelv.json) sets quartzElevatorDistance = 16 and a notably longer smoothQuartzElevatorDistance = 64 for the smooth variant, with mixTypes = false (a column must be one elevator type throughout to work), isPlayerOnly = true (only players are lifted, not items/mobs), and particle effects on.
This mod and Open Block Elevator Mod do the same job — a block-based vertical elevator — with different block sets and tuning. Quartz Elevator’s variants travel much farther (up to 64 blocks) than Open Block Elevator’s single block (20 blocks by default here), so which one gets used in a build is really a matter of range needed and aesthetic (quartz block vs. the OpenBlocks-style elevator block).
Anticipated questions
What does it add? Two blocks — Quartz Elevator and Smooth Quartz Elevator — that launch/lift an entity straight up when stood on, working as a vertical block-elevator column.
How far do they lift? The plain Quartz Elevator travels quartzElevatorDistance = 16, and the Smooth Quartz variant travels much farther at smoothQuartzElevatorDistance = 64.
Will it lift mobs or dropped items? No — isPlayerOnly = true, so only players are lifted.
Can I mix the two elevator types in one column? No — mixTypes = false, so a column must be a single elevator type throughout to work.
How does it compare to Open Block Elevator? Both do the same block-based vertical-elevator job; Quartz’s variants travel much farther (up to 64) than Open Block Elevator Mod’s single block (20 by default here), so the choice comes down to range needed and aesthetic (quartz vs. the OpenBlocks-style block).

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Reacharou.title: Reacharound
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Reacharou.content:
Reacharound
Reacharound (by spAnser) lets you place a block against the far side of another block you’re looking through — practically, it means you can place blocks (stairs, slabs, etc.) facing correctly without having to walk around to the other side first. The pack config (reacharound.json) leaves it enabled: true with mode: 0 and shows an in-world placement indicator (a { }/|  |-style bracket, animated over 5 ticks) so you can see where the reacharound placement will land before committing. Purely a build-convenience QoL mod.
Anticipated questions
What does it do? It lets you place a block against the far side of another block you’re looking through — so you can place stairs, slabs, and the like facing correctly without walking around to the other side first.
Does it add any blocks or items? No — it’s purely a build-convenience QoL mod with no content of its own.
How do I know where the block will land? It shows an in-world placement indicator (a bracket-style marker, animated over 5 ticks) so you can see where the reacharound placement will go before committing. The pack leaves it enabled: true with mode: 0 in reacharound.json.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Satisfyin.content:
Satisfying Buttons
Satisfying Buttons (by Toni) is a purely client-feel mod: it adds a darkened hover overlay and a soft click sound to vanilla GUI buttons and widgets, nothing more. The pack’s client.json5 keeps the defaults — animation and sound both enabled, a 300 ms hover-darken fade, and a quiet secondary “unhover” sound (volume 0.5, pitch 1.0). It has nothing to do with in-world button blocks despite the name; it’s UI polish, filed here only because it’s a tiny single-mechanic mod.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Stonework.title: Stoneworks
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Stonework.content:
Stoneworks
Stoneworks (by Fuzs) is Twigs’ stone-focused counterpart — “Vanilla stone types in plenty of variations for all your building needs” — and it delivers on that with 582 lang entries. Every vanilla stone type (andesite, diorite, granite, deepslate, etc.) is expanded into a full cut-stone family: bricks, pavers, pillars, plates, shingles, and tiles, each of those further split into slab/stairs/wall forms. Just the andesite subset alone accounts for 20 distinct blocks (bricks, brick slab/stairs/wall, pavers, paver slab/stairs/wall, pillar, plates, plate slab/stairs/wall, shingles, shingle slab/stairs/wall, tiles, tile slab/stairs/wall) — multiplied across every base stone type in the game.
The one config toggle, stoneworks-common.toml, is vanilla_variants_in_creative_tab = true — it controls whether the plain vanilla stone-variant blocks Stoneworks reuses/re-exposes also show up cluttering its dedicated creative tab (left on here). This is the mod to reach for when a build needs stone texture variety — roofing (shingles), flooring (pavers/plates), or decorative trim (pillars) — beyond vanilla’s bricks-and-cobblestone options.
Anticipated questions
What does it add? It expands every vanilla stone type (andesite, diorite, granite, deepslate, etc.) into a full cut-stone family — bricks, pavers, pillars, plates, shingles, and tiles, each further split into slab/stairs/wall forms — for 582 lang entries in total.
When should I reach for it in a build? When a build needs stone texture variety beyond vanilla’s bricks-and-cobblestone: roofing (shingles), flooring (pavers/plates), or decorative trim (pillars).
Is there anything to configure? One toggle in stoneworks-common.toml: vanilla_variants_in_creative_tab = true, which controls whether the plain vanilla stone-variant blocks it re-exposes also clutter its dedicated creative tab (left on here).
How does it relate to Twigs and Decorative Blocks? It’s Twigs’ stone-focused counterpart and complements both — covering the cut-stone end of the building-material spectrum.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Supplemen.title: Supplementaries
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Supplemen.content:
Supplementaries
Supplementaries (MehVahdJukaar, Plantkillable) is a large “vanilla+” grab-bag mod — 607 lang entries — that mixes decoration with genuinely functional redstone/utility blocks: globes, notice boards, spinning pedestals, bunting banners, clocks, sconces, and dozens of similar small pieces that feel like they should have been in vanilla. Its own advancement flavor text is self-aware about this (“Spin a globe at ludicrous speed”, “Use a Wrench to rotate a block”, “Drink from a Chalice”), giving a sense of the range — decorative furniture-scale objects through to small interactive gadgets.
Two config files tune it on this server. supplementaries-client.json controls per-block visual/behavior toggles: the globe shows a random world and displays coordinates, the notice board centers its text, buntings are not set to fast mode, the clock block uses 24-hour format, and the pedestal spins (speed 2.0) with fancy renderers on. supplementaries-common.json tunes gameplay-affecting values — quiver skeleton spawn chance (3%, difficulty-scaled), a flag’s “unbound” radius (64 blocks) and explosion radii (2.0 / 5.15 for different explosive types), and a red-merchant spawn multiplier. No Patchouli guidebook ships with it; blocks are best discovered via JEI/creative search.

What does it add? A large “vanilla+” grab-bag (607 lang entries) that mixes decoration with genuinely functional redstone/utility blocks — globes, notice boards, spinning pedestals, bunting banners, clocks, sconces, and dozens of similar small pieces.

Both. supplementaries-client.json controls per-block visual/behavior toggles (the globe showing a random world with coordinates, notice-board centered text, 24-hour clock, spinning pedestal, etc.), while supplementaries-common.json tunes gameplay-affecting values like quiver-skeleton spawn chance (3%), flag radii, and a red-merchant spawn multiplier.
How do I find all these blocks? No Patchouli guidebook ships with it, so blocks are best discovered via JEI / creative search.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Thaumon.title: Thaumon
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Thaumon.content:
Thaumon
Thaumon (jdlenl, shizotoaster, nageih, isengrimus) is explicitly “Thaumcraft-inspired decoration blocks for modern Minecraft” — 141 lang entries of aesthetic-only content evoking the old Thaumcraft look (arcane research towers, eldritch libraries) without any of Thaumcraft’s actual magic systems attached. The lang file reads like a themed block set: arcane stone tiles, ancient stone (window panes, pillars, tile stairs, brick stairs, polished variants), eldritch stone (slab, stairs, brick stairs), silverwood (an original wood type — slab, fence, window pane, plus “empty” and “dusty” bookshelf variants), greatwood (fence gate, bark — a second original wood type), crystal lamp and crystal stand, amberglass pane, and a research notes item that’s presumably just a lore/decoration book rather than a functional item.
Because it’s purely aesthetic, Thaumon slots in as a theme kit for anyone building a wizard-tower, library, or arcane-laboratory style structure — matching Prominence II’s broader magic-system mods (see Magic & Spells Mods) visually without being mechanically tied to them. No config or Patchouli book ships for it.

Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Twigs.title: Twigs
Mods/Building--and--Decoration/Twigs.content:
Twigs
Twigs (by Ninni) adds 269 lang entries’ worth of new base building materials rather than furniture — the kind of small natural-feeling blocks vanilla is missing. Highlights from its lang file: twig (a stick-like decoration item), bamboo thatch (block/stairs/slab), pebbles, four seashell colors (bronzed, opaline, roseate, tangerine — some of which “play” a sound when used, per the lang key bronzed_seashell.plays), petrified lichen, paper lanterns (multiple color/style variants), standalone lamp blocks, and potted azalea flowers. It’s a materials-first mod: the new items read as texture/detail pieces meant to be scattered into builds (path edges, shorelines, forest floors) rather than a full furniture catalog.
No dedicated config file ships for Twigs on this server, so it runs with default settings. It complements Stoneworks (stone variety) and Decorative Blocks (structural trim pieces) by covering the smaller, more naturalistic end of the building-material spectrum.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat-Mods.title: Core RPG & Combat Mods
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat-Mods.content:
Core RPG & Combat Mods
The beating heart of the pack — the mods that turn Minecraft into an actual RPG. See Combat & Stats, Gear Rarity & Reforging, Talent Tree & Fate Talents for how these systems play.
Zenith Renewed / Zenith Attributes Renewed
A Fabric port of the classic mod Apotheosis. Runs enchanting overhauls, spawner mechanics, tougher bosses, and — most importantly — the weapon/armor “affix” system behind gear rarity (Common through Mythic) and its reforge bonuses. Zenith Attributes Renewed is the math underneath making the extra stats behave.
Pufferfish’s Skills / Pufferfish’s Attributes
The Talent Tree (press N). One point every two levels; Fate Talents near the top define your build. Attributes is the plumbing that lets the tree grant extra stats at all.
Better Combat
Swaps vanilla’s “click and pray” combat for directional swings and proper weapon movesets — the combat system you’re playing with the whole time.
Combat Roll
Adds a stamina-based dodge roll — your i-frame button, core to surviving harder boss fights.
Tierify
Gives armor, weapons, and tools quality tiers of their own, layered on top of the broader Zenith rarity system.
Jewelry (RPG Series)
Rings and necklaces from deep-mined gems, each built to boost a specific archetype. See Accessories & Enchanting.
Artifacts
Powerful, uncraftable trinkets found only while exploring.
Accessories / Accessories Trinkets Compat Layer / Trinkets and Things
The invisible slot system Jewelry and Artifacts plug into.
Marium’s Soulslike Weaponry
Legendary, boss-tier weapons (and the bosses that drop them) — its own Quest Book chapter.
Simply Swords
A whole armory of unique, flashy swords with their own identities and quest chapter.
Transmog
Change gear appearance without touching stats.
Gear-tier & progression mods
MC Dungeons Armors / MC Dungeons Weapons bring Minecraft Dungeons gear into Java for mid-game goals. Advanced Netherite and Mythic Upgrades add tiers above vanilla Netherite. More Totems adds Totem of Undying variants themed after different mobs. Mythic Mounts adds rideable mounts — see the mount-hunting workflow under Creatures, Bosses & Mobs. Dynamic RPG Resource Bars gives animated health/stamina/mana bars. SimplySkills is an extra combat skill tree. More RPG Classes adds extra weapons/spells beyond the main archetype mods.
Archetype / “RPG Series” class mods
Archers (RPG Series) + Archers Expansion = the Ranger path. Wizards (RPG Series) = the Elemental Mage path. Paladins & Priests (RPG Series) = the Holy path. Rogues & Warriors (RPG Series) = the melee-Haste/Assassin path. Death Knights = a dark-magic-and-melee hybrid class. Spellblade Next = magical melee for the hybrid Spellblade build. Full breakdown: Archetypes & Builds.
Combat tweaks (grouped)
Combat Effects (configurable in-fight effects), ReBalance and Resistance Balancer (damage math retuning), Projectile Damage Attribute and RangedWeaponAPI (separate damage stat for ranged weapons), Shield API and Shield Overhaul (shield mechanics/looks), Gun Scaling (scales Soulslike Weaponry guns with ranged-damage stat), Simply Swords Battle Standard Tweaks and Mutant Skeleton Armor Tweaks (balance patches).
Cosmetic gear: armor trims (grouped)
AllTheTrims, DynamicTrim, BetterTrims (trims grant passive effects), More Armor Trims, Better Trim Tooltips, BetterThanMending.
Attribute plumbing (grouped, invisible)
AttributeFix, Custom Entity Attributes, Custom Item Attributes, Eternal Attributes, Extra RPG Attributes — widen the stat “slots” gear/talents/mobs use.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Accessories-T.title: Accessories Trinkets Compat Layer
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Accessories-T.content:
Accessories Trinkets Compat Layer
A thin shim (mod id tclayer, from the same wisp-forest team as Accessories) that exists for one reason: a lot of older accessory content — including this pack’s own Artifacts mod — was written against the original Trinkets API, not the newer Accessories framework. Rather than requiring every such mod to be rewritten, this compat layer re-implements the Trinkets API classes (dev.emi.trinkets.api.*) on top of Accessories and registers itself in fabric.mod.json as "provides": ["trinkets"], so Trinkets-dependent mods think they’re talking to the real Trinkets mod while their items actually live in Accessories’ slot system underneath.
There’s genuinely not much more to it — no items, no config, no player-facing UI of its own. It ships only mixins, a refmap, and a couple of tag files (data/accessories/tags/items/all.json, data/trinkets/tags/items/all.json) to keep both systems’ item tags in sync. Notably, this pack also runs the real Trinkets mod (trinkets-3.7.2.jar) alongside it for mods like Things that depend on genuine Trinkets — so this is plumbing bridging one direction (Trinkets-API mods → Accessories), not a full replacement of Trinkets itself.
Anticipated questions
What does this compat layer actually do?
It’s a thin shim (mod id tclayer) that re-implements the original Trinkets API classes (dev.emi.trinkets.api.*) on top of Accessories, and registers itself as "provides": ["trinkets"] in its fabric.mod.json. Mods written against Trinkets — including this pack’s own Artifacts mod — think they’re talking to real Trinkets, while their items actually live in Accessories’ slot system underneath.
Does it add any items, config, or UI?
No. There’s genuinely nothing player-facing — no items, no config, no menu of its own. It ships only mixins, a refmap, and a couple of tag files (all.json for both accessories and trinkets) to keep the two systems’ item tags in sync.
If it re-implements Trinkets, why does the pack still run the real Trinkets mod?
Because this layer only bridges one direction — Trinkets-API mods pointed at Accessories. Some mods (like Things) depend on genuine Trinkets, so the pack also runs the real trinkets-3.7.2.jar alongside it. This is plumbing, not a full replacement of Trinkets.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Accessories.title: Accessories
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Accessories.content:
Accessories
The base slot-system framework (by wisp-forest) that Jewelry and Artifacts quietly plug into — players never open an “Accessories” menu directly, they just see extra equipment slots appear next to the armor slots. It’s a data-driven successor to the older Trinkets API, built so any mod can register new slot types via datapack JSON instead of hardcoded Java.
By default every player entity gets 12 slots (defined in data/accessories/accessories/entity/default.json): hat, face, necklace, cape, back, hand, ring (this one holds 2 items — you get two ring fingers), wrist, belt, anklet, shoes, and charm. Each slot type ships its own GUI icon and validators (accessories:tag, accessories:component) that decide which items are legal in it — this is the mechanism that lets a Jewelry ring only go in the ring slot and an Artifacts trinket only go where it’s tagged for. Server-side config (config/accessories.json5) on this pack is mostly cosmetic tuning — equip requires not crouching (equipControl: MUST_NOT_CROUCH), hovered slots brighten and cycle, unused slots stay hidden by default — with no gameplay-affecting overrides.
Anticipated questions
How many accessory slots do players get, and what are they?
Every player entity gets 12 slots by default: hat, face, necklace, cape, back, hand, ring, wrist, belt, anklet, shoes, and charm. They appear next to the armor slots rather than in a separate menu.
Which slot holds more than one item?
The ring slot holds 2 items — you get two ring fingers.
How does a slot know which items are legal in it?
Each slot type ships validators (accessories:tag, accessories:component) that decide which items fit. That’s the mechanism that lets a Jewelry ring only go in the ring slot and an Artifacts trinket only go where it’s tagged for.
Does this pack’s config change how accessories play?
No — the server-side config (config/accessories.json5) is mostly cosmetic tuning: equipping requires not crouching (MUST_NOT_CROUCH), hovered slots brighten and cycle, and unused slots stay hidden. There are no gameplay-affecting overrides.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Advanced-Neth.title: Advanced Netherite
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Advanced-Neth.content:
Advanced Netherite
Advanced Netherite (advancednetherite, jar advancednetherite-fabric-2.1.3-1.20.1.jar, by Autovw) adds four full parallel gear tiers directly above vanilla Netherite: Netherite-Iron, Netherite-Gold, Netherite-Emerald, and Netherite-Diamond, each with its own ingot, block, and full armor + tool set (helmet/chestplate/leggings/boots plus axe/hoe/pickaxe/shovel/sword). Crafting is two-stepped: first a shapeless recipe combines an “upgrade to Netherite-X” ingredient with 4 of the matching vanilla ingot (e.g. a Netherite ingot + 4 Iron Ingots → 1 Netherite-Iron Ingot), then a vanilla-style smithing-table transform (using a Netherite Upgrade Smithing Template) upgrades a Netherite-tier item into its Netherite-X counterpart — mirroring exactly how vanilla Diamond→Netherite upgrades work, just one rung higher.
Each of the four tiers carries a themed passive perk baked into its lang/tooltip data: Netherite-Iron armor pacifies Phantoms (its advancement is literally titled “No More Phantoms”), Netherite-Gold armor pacifies Piglins (“Ultimate Piglin distraction suit”), and Netherite-Emerald armor pacifies Endermen (“Endermen?”). Tools get matching passive drop bonuses — the pickaxe has a chance for extra Diamond/Emerald/Raw Gold/Raw Iron drops depending on tier, the hoe has a chance for extra crop drops, and the sword has a chance for extra Ender Pearls off Endermen, Gold Ingots off Piglins, Gold Nuggets off Zombified Piglins, and Phantom Membranes off Phantoms — reinforcing the theme that each metal “specializes” in taming/farming the mob or resource it’s named after. Netherite-Diamond, the top tier, has its own tongue-in-cheek advancement (“Why?” for crafting a Netherite-Diamond Hoe, “Craft a Netherite-Diamond Hoe and visit a psychologist afterwards”). Client-side config options (show_tooltips, matching_durability_bars, enable_search_bar) control whether perk tooltips and a color-matched durability bar are shown; no dedicated per-server config file for gameplay balance was found under config/ (recipes/stats ship baked into the jar’s datapack), so this mod runs on its packaged defaults on this server.
Anticipated questions
What tiers does it add above netherite?
Four parallel tiers directly above vanilla Netherite — Netherite-Iron, Netherite-Gold, Netherite-Emerald, and Netherite-Diamond — each with its own ingot, block, and full armor + tool set.
How do I upgrade to them?
Two steps. A shapeless recipe combines a Netherite ingot + 4 of the matching vanilla ingot into the new ingot (e.g. Netherite + 4 Iron → 1 Netherite-Iron Ingot), then a smithing-table transform with a Netherite Upgrade Smithing Template upgrades a netherite-tier item into its Netherite-X version — exactly like vanilla Diamond→Netherite, one rung higher.
What perks do the tiers give?
Themed passives: Netherite-Iron armor pacifies Phantoms, Netherite-Gold pacifies Piglins, Netherite-Emerald pacifies Endermen; matching tools add drop bonuses (extra ender pearls, gold, crop drops, ore, etc.). Netherite-Diamond is the top tier.
Where does it sit versus Mythic Upgrades?
Advanced Netherite stacks parallel metal tiers on top of netherite; Mythic Upgrades instead sockets gems into netherite gear. The two are compatible. It runs on the jar’s packaged defaults here (no per-server balance config). See Gear Rarity & Reforging.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/AllTheTrims.title: AllTheTrims
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/AllTheTrims.content:
AllTheTrims
By Bawnorton (also author of DynamicTrim and BetterTrims) — “allows any item to be a trim material and makes all armour trimmable.” Vanilla only lets a handful of ingots/gems act as trim materials on standard armor; this mod removes both restrictions at once, letting any item in the game (including modded items) act as a trim material, and letting any armor piece (including modded armor) accept a trim.
This is the foundation the other two trim mods in this pack build on: BetterTrims attaches passive gameplay effects to specific trim materials, and DynamicTrim handles rendering those trims correctly on non-vanilla armor models. This server’s config (allthetrims.json) has debug logging off and includes an anti-reupload watermark message baked in by the modpack author, confirming AllTheTrims ships as a Prominence-II-integrated dependency rather than a drop-in vanilla-only mod.
Anticipated questions
What two restrictions does AllTheTrims remove?
Vanilla only lets a handful of ingots/gems act as trim materials, and only on standard armor. AllTheTrims removes both at once: any item (including modded items) can act as a trim material, and any armor piece (including modded armor) can accept a trim.
Does AllTheTrims itself add gameplay effects to trims?
No. It’s the foundation the other two trim mods build on — BetterTrims attaches the passive gameplay effects to specific trim materials, and DynamicTrim handles rendering trims correctly on non-vanilla armor models.
Who made it?
Bawnorton, who also authored DynamicTrim and BetterTrims.
Is this a plain vanilla-compatible drop-in?
Not quite — the server’s allthetrims.json has debug logging off and carries an anti-reupload watermark baked in by the modpack author, confirming it ships as a Prominence-II-integrated dependency.
