Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Archers-(RPG-.title: Archers (RPG Series)
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Archers-(RPG-.content:
Archers (RPG Series)
Archers (“Draw, Release, Conquer — Master the art of Archery!”) is the Ranger half of the “RPG Series” archetype line — same author (Daedelus) as Better Combat and Combat Roll — and it’s built on top of the Spell Engine framework, the same skill-book system the other class mods (Wizards (RPG Series), Paladins & Priests (RPG Series), Rogues & Warriors (RPG Series)) use. Picking up an Archery Manual puts you on the Path of Archery; the manual’s skill tree grants: Power Shot (a passive that stacks a “Hunter’s Mark” debuff, +5% damage taken per stack, on marked targets), Entangling Roots (a root-and-slow AoE), Barrage (rapid multi-arrow fire), and Magic Arrow (a piercing magical shot that hits every enemy in its path).
Gear-wise it adds a full bow/crossbow lineup — Composite Longbow, Mechanical Shortbow, Royal Longbow, Rapid/Heavy Crossbow, up through Netherite and Crystal/Ruby tiers — plus Archer and Ranger armor sets (cloth and Netherite-Ranger variants) and a parallel line of thrown Spears (Flint through Netherite, plus Aeternium and Ruby tiers). Numbers are server-tuned in config/archers/items.json: pull times and damage scale with tier, e.g. the base Composite Longbow is 30-tick pull / 8 damage, the Netherite Heavy Crossbow is 35-tick pull / 15 damage, and melee spears range from the Flint Spear (4 damage, -3 attack speed) up to the Netherite Spear (7 damage). An Auto-Fire Hook enchant (anvil-applied) auto-releases a fully charged shot for you.
The mod also seeds new structures into vanilla villages — Archery Range buildings (large and small variants) in desert, savanna, plains, taiga, and snowy villages, each staffed by a new Archery Artisan villager profession working from an Archery Artisan Table. Config tweaks on this server: crossbow power-enchant scaling at 0.08/level, quick-charge at 0.1/level, and Infinity is explicitly enabled for crossbows (not a vanilla behavior).
Anticipated questions
How do you start the Archery path?
Pick up an Archery Manual. It puts you on the Path of Archery and its skill tree grants Power Shot, Entangling Roots, Barrage, and Magic Arrow. The system is built on the Spell Engine framework, the same skill-book approach the other RPG Series class mods use.
What does each skill do?
Power Shot is a passive that stacks a “Hunter’s Mark” debuff (+5% damage taken per stack) on marked targets; Entangling Roots is a root-and-slow AoE; Barrage is rapid multi-arrow fire; Magic Arrow is a piercing magical shot that hits every enemy in its path.
What gear does it add, and do the numbers scale?
A full bow/crossbow lineup (Composite Longbow, Mechanical Shortbow, Royal Longbow, Rapid/Heavy Crossbow, up through Netherite and Crystal/Ruby tiers), Archer and Ranger armor sets, and a line of thrown Spears. Numbers scale with tier in config/archers/items.json — the base Composite Longbow is 30-tick pull / 8 damage, the Netherite Heavy Crossbow is 35-tick pull / 15 damage, and spears run from the Flint Spear (4 damage, -3 attack speed) up to the Netherite Spear (7 damage).
Is there a way to auto-release a charged shot?
Yes — the anvil-applied Auto-Fire Hook enchant auto-releases a fully charged shot for you.
What does the mod add to villages?
Archery Range buildings (large and small) in desert, savanna, plains, taiga, and snowy villages, each staffed by a new Archery Artisan villager profession working from an Archery Artisan Table.
Any notable config tweaks on this server?
Crossbow power-enchant scaling is 0.08/level, quick-charge 0.1/level, and Infinity is explicitly enabled for crossbows — not a vanilla behavior.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Archers-Expan.title: Archers Expansion
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Archers-Expan.content:
Archers Expansion
Archers Expansion is a Spell Engine add-on that bolts three full archer subclasses onto Archers (RPG Series) — it explicitly depends on both archers and more_rpg_classes, tying it into the pack’s broader archetype system rather than just adding loose items. Each subclass is its own armor set + spellbook + four unique spells:

Deadeye (spellbook: Bounty List) — a precision/mobility kit: Trick Shot (a bouncing arrow that ricochets between targets), Disabling Shot (jumps the caster back while slowing/damaging the target), Fast Shot (passive Ranged Haste stacking per shot), and Infiltrator’s Arrow (an invisible shot that also grants the caster invisibility).
Tundra Hunter (spellbook: Tundric Hunting) — a cold/control kit: Arctic Volley (8-arrow frost spread), Enchanted Crystal Arrow (stuns and freezes), Frozen Pact (deals damage scaled to a target’s accumulated “Frozen ticks,” then weakens its attack), Frozen Shot (passive stacking frost), and Winter’s Grip (a totem that freezes nearby enemies solid on death).
War Archer (spellbook: War Archery Instructions) — a raw-damage/suppression kit: Dual Shot (fires two arrows at once), Pin Down (roots the target in place), Point-Blank Shot (knockback that scales inversely with range), and Smoldering Arrow (passive burn damage).

Each subclass has its own Netherite-upgradeable armor line (Deadeye Tunic/Hood/Leggings/Boots, Tundra Tunic set, Bowman set for War Archer), and each has its own advancement for collecting the full spell set (“Bounty Hunting,” “Cold Blooded Hunter,” “Load, Hold and Fire!”). It suggests (soft-depends on) Better Combat for its melee-adjacent interactions but doesn’t require it. Together with the base Archers mod this is what the category note calls “the Ranger path” — Archers supplies the weapons and the generic marksman kit, Archers Expansion supplies the build-defining subclass choice on top of it.

Three full archer subclasses, each with its own armor set, spellbook, and four unique spells. Base Archers supplies the weapons and the generic marksman kit; the Expansion supplies the build-defining subclass choice.

Deadeye (spellbook: Bounty List) — a precision/mobility kit; Tundra Hunter (Tundric Hunting) — a cold/control kit; and War Archer (War Archery Instructions) — a raw-damage/suppression kit.
What spells does Deadeye get?
Trick Shot (a bouncing arrow that ricochets between targets), Disabling Shot (jumps the caster back while slowing/damaging the target), Fast Shot (passive Ranged Haste stacking per shot), and Infiltrator’s Arrow (an invisible shot that also grants the caster invisibility).
Does it require Better Combat?
No — it only suggests (soft-depends on) Better Combat for its melee-adjacent interactions, but doesn’t require it.
Is there a goal for collecting a subclass’s spells?
Yes — each subclass has its own advancement for collecting the full spell set (“Bounty Hunting,” “Cold Blooded Hunter,” “Load, Hold and Fire!”), and each armor line is Netherite-upgradeable.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Artifacts.title: Artifacts
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Artifacts.content:
Artifacts
Adds ~45 uncraftable trinkets that only turn up through exploration — chests, campsites, archaeology, suspicious sand/gravel, and mob drops — never via a crafting table. On this server’s tuning (config/artifacts/common.json5), archaeologyChance is 6.25%, everlastingBeefChance is 0.2% per cow/mooshroom kill, and hostile mobs (skeletons, zombies, piglins) have a 0.1% chance to spawn already wearing an artifact. Campsites generate up to 4 times per chunk between Y −60 and Y 40, and 30% of the time hide a Mimic instead of a real loot chest — a classic Artifacts signature. artifactRarity is left at the default 1.0, so chest-loot odds are unmodified from upstream.
The item list itself covers a wide spread of utility rather than raw combat power: mobility (Aqua-Dashers, Bunny Hoppers, Flippers, Snowshoes, Cloud in a Bottle, Umbrella for slow-falling), survival crutches (Crystal Heart for extra hearts, Everlasting Beef/Eternal Steak for infinite food, Antidote Vessel, Obsidian Skull for knockback immunity), damage/utility trinkets (Fire Gauntlet, Vampiric Glove, Thorn Pendant, Shock Pendant, Power Glove), and pure novelty (Whoopee Cushion, Novelty/Plastic Drinking Hat, Helium Flamingo, Kitty Slippers, Cowboy Hat). Artifacts are equipped through Trinkets/Accessories slots rather than armor slots — the mod depends directly on trinkets per its fabric.mod.json, meaning it plugs into the same slot layer as Jewelry, just via the older Trinkets API rather than native Accessories.
Important distinction found while researching: the modpack’s Quest Book chapter literally named “Artifact Reforging” (artifact_reforging.snbt, “S’kellak’s Forge”) is not about this mod. It describes a separate, custom bespoke system of soul-bound legendary weapons in the prominent: namespace — Frostmourne, Fyr’alath, Supernova, Thunderwrath, Apophis, Vaazkar, Orion, Ekavar Staff, and others — forged from a Molten Core dropped after Chapter I of the Void’s Invasion questline, repaired with Encased Remnants, made unbreakable with a Hardening Catalyst (from the Things mod), and upgraded through a 7-node Upgrade Tree (press N) fueled by Molten Remnants. That system is unrelated to the Artifacts mod covered here and is closer kin to Mythic Upgrades / the pack’s custom boss-weapon content.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/AttributeFix.title: AttributeFix
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/AttributeFix.content:
AttributeFix
By Darkhax — “Extends the maximum attribute ranges to allow for higher values.” Vanilla Minecraft hard-caps most attributes (e.g. attack damage, armor) at values far too low for a modded RPG pack where gear rolls can stack dozens of percent bonuses; AttributeFix widens those min/max bounds per-attribute so other mods’ stats don’t silently clamp.
This is genuinely central plumbing on this server: attributefix.json explicitly registers 194 separate attributes it can widen the range of, spanning nearly every RPG mod in the pack — Eternal Attributes, Extra RPG Attributes (extraspellattributes:), Spellblade Next (spellbladenext:), Zenith Attributes Renewed (zenith_attributes:), Pufferfish’s Skills (puffish_skills:), Sortilège, Obscure API, More RPG Classes, and others. Most entries in this server’s config are currently listed with "enabled": false, meaning the widened bound exists but isn’t force-applied unless a value would otherwise be clamped — the mod acts as a safety net across the whole attribute ecosystem rather than actively overriding numbers itself.
Anticipated questions
What problem does AttributeFix solve?
Vanilla Minecraft hard-caps most attributes (attack damage, armor, etc.) at values far too low for a modded RPG pack where gear can stack dozens of percent bonuses. AttributeFix widens those min/max bounds per-attribute so other mods’ stats don’t silently clamp.
How many attributes does it cover on this server?
Its attributefix.json registers 194 separate attributes, spanning nearly every RPG mod in the pack — Eternal Attributes, Extra RPG Attributes (extraspellattributes:), Spellblade Next (spellbladenext:), Zenith Attributes Renewed, Pufferfish’s Skills, Sortilège, Obscure API, More RPG Classes, and others.
If most entries are "enabled": false, does the mod actually do anything?
Yes — the widened bound still exists; it just isn’t force-applied unless a value would otherwise be clamped. The mod acts as a safety net across the whole attribute ecosystem rather than actively overriding numbers itself.
Who made it?
Darkhax.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Better-Combat.title: Better Combat
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Better-Combat.content:
Better Combat
Better Combat (by Daedelus) replaces vanilla’s single “click and pray” swing with a real melee system borrowed from Minecraft Dungeons: every weapon gets its own attack animation, timing, and combo — hitting consecutively performs a combo, and holding the attack button (enabled on this server via isHoldToAttackEnabled) keeps you swinging continuously instead of spam-clicking. It also adds directional/two-handed weapon handling, a reworked sweeping-edge mechanic, and a Feint keybind. The in-game Quest Book flags exactly this under “New Combat Mechanics”: “Each weapon has its own attack animation and time… Consecutive attacks will perform combos… You can hold the attack button to keep attacking continuously.”
The server’s bettercombat/server.json5 has real tuning behind that description: upswing (windup before damage lands) is set to 0.5× weapon cooldown for fast-paced attack initiation; attacks are capped to a 2-tick minimum interval; movement speed is halved (0.5) while attacking, applied smoothly; combos reset after idling for 3.0× the weapon’s cooldown; dual-wielding gets a +20% attack-speed bonus but no damage bonus in either hand. Vanilla sweeping is disabled in favor of Better Combat’s own “reworked sweeping,” which weakens a swing’s damage the more targets it cleaves (up to 4 extra targets, capped at a 50% penalty) — the Sweeping Edge enchantment restores up to half of that penalty at max level. A large fallback_compatibility.json regex table auto-assigns weapon movesets (claymore, halberd, glaive, katana, rapier, twin-blade, spear, mace, etc.) to any weapon whose item ID matches a pattern, which is how every third-party weapon mod in the pack — Marium’s Soulslike Weaponry, Simply Swords, Archers (RPG Series)‘s spears — gets a fitting attack animation without needing explicit support.
Player-vs-entity relations are also config-driven: players, villagers, iron golems, and guard-villagers are set NEUTRAL (only hit if you’re aiming at them), while passive and hostile mobs default to HOSTILE (hit by any swing in range). This is the mod underpinning literally every melee fight in the pack.
Anticipated questions
Do I still have to spam-click to attack?
No. Holding the attack button is enabled on this server (isHoldToAttackEnabled), so you keep swinging continuously instead of spam-clicking. Each weapon has its own animation and timing, and hitting consecutively performs combos.
How do combos work, and do they expire?
Consecutive attacks chain into a combo. The combo resets after you idle for 3.0× the weapon’s cooldown. Note that attacking also halves your movement speed (applied smoothly) and there’s a 2-tick minimum interval between hits.
How does the reworked sweeping attack work?
Vanilla sweeping is disabled. Better Combat’s version weakens a swing’s damage the more targets it cleaves — up to 4 extra targets, capped at a 50% penalty. The Sweeping Edge enchantment restores up to half of that penalty at max level.
Is dual-wielding worth it?
Dual-wielding grants a +20% attack-speed bonus, but no damage bonus in either hand.
How do weapons from other mods get proper animations?
A large fallback_compatibility.json regex table auto-assigns movesets (claymore, halberd, glaive, katana, rapier, twin-blade, spear, mace, etc.) to any weapon whose item ID matches a pattern — which is how Marium’s Soulslike Weaponry, Simply Swords, and other pack weapons get fitting animations without explicit support.
Will I accidentally hit friends and villagers?
No. Players, villagers, iron golems, and guard-villagers are set NEUTRAL — you only hit them if you’re aiming at them. Passive and hostile mobs default to HOSTILE (hit by any swing in range). See Combat & Stats.

It “condenses the tooltips of Trimmed Armor items” — a pure client-rendering/UX mod by Andrew6rant (also co-author of DynamicTrim) that keeps trimmed-armor tooltips readable.

No. It’s mixin-based, client-environment only, with no config or gameplay content — it only affects how tooltips are drawn.
Why is it needed in this pack?
Because BetterTrims and More Armor Trims stack passive-effect text and extra pattern names onto every trimmed piece. Without this mod, a fully-trimmed item could have a noticeably bloated tooltip.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/BetterThanMen.title: BetterThanMending
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/BetterThanMen.content:
BetterThanMending
By legobmw99 — “A mod to improve the mending behavior in vanilla Minecraft.” Vanilla’s Mending enchantment repairs whatever single item is in your hand or hotbar when you pick up XP orbs, which is often the wrong item and encourages awkward hotbar-swap workarounds. This mod changes the targeting logic so Mending repairs more sensibly (across all equipped Mending gear rather than one arbitrary slot) — a quality-of-life fix rather than a new mechanic.
No config file is present on this server; it runs at its shipped defaults. Given how much of this pack’s endgame is built around expensive, hard-to-reforge rare-tier gear, smoother Mending behavior across the whole loadout is a meaningful quality-of-life win rather than a cosmetic tweak.

It reworks the targeting logic so Mending repairs more sensibly — across all equipped Mending gear rather than one arbitrary slot. It’s a quality-of-life fix, not a new mechanic.

No config file is present; it runs at its shipped defaults.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/BetterTrims.title: BetterTrims
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/BetterTrims.content:
BetterTrims
By Bawnorton — “Gives each armour trim material a unique effect when worn.” Turns AllTheTrims’s cosmetic trim system into a genuine gearing choice: each of ~19 trim materials grants a small always-on passive effect while worn, stacking per matching trim piece on the armor set. This server’s config (bettertrims.json) has every material enabled except Amethyst and Glowstone Dust, with the tuned effect values fully readable:

Silver — +5% movement speed, +5% jump height, +20% attack damage, +1.5% attack speed, +25% improved vision.
Nether Brick — Blazes ignore you at 1 piece, Wither Skeletons ignore you at 2, Piglins enrage at 4.
Platinum — Illagers ignore you at 1 piece.
Gold — Piglins ignore you at 1 piece (extending the vanilla gold-nugget behavior to armor trims).
Prismarine Shard — Guardians ignore you at 2 pieces; mining fatigue immunity at 4.
Diamond — 2.5% flat damage reduction. Netherite — 25% fire resistance. Iron — +5.0 mining speed. Copper — +5% swim speed. Redstone — +10% movement speed. Lapis — +30 enchantability. Emerald — 12.5% villager trade discount.
Quartz — +5% bonus XP from kills/mining. Coal — furnace speed boost + 5-block hostile-detection radius. Leather — +0.4 step height. Slime Ball — 25% fall damage reduction + 25% extra knockback + bounce. Ender Pearl — 7.5% dodge chance (but water damages the wearer). Chorus Fruit — 25% dodge chance. Fire Charge — extra fire duration on hit. Dragon’s Breath — 1.25x lingering-cloud radius. Echo Shard — reduced sculk-sensor detection range. Enchanted Golden Apple — extended/stronger absorption.

Anticipated questions
What does BetterTrims change about armor trims?
It “gives each armour trim material a unique effect when worn,” turning AllTheTrims’s cosmetic trim system into a genuine gearing choice: each trim material grants a small always-on passive effect while worn, stacking per matching trim piece on the set.
How many trim materials are there, and are any disabled?
About 19 trim materials. This server’s config (bettertrims.json) enables every material except Amethyst and Glowstone Dust.
Which trim is best for offense?
Silver stands out — +20% attack damage, +1.5% attack speed, +5% movement speed, +5% jump height, and +25% improved vision.
Which trims make hostile mobs ignore me?
Several: Gold makes Piglins ignore you at 1 piece, Platinum makes Illagers ignore you at 1, Nether Brick makes Blazes ignore you at 1 (Wither Skeletons at 2, but Piglins enrage at 4), and Prismarine Shard makes Guardians ignore you at 2 (plus mining-fatigue immunity at 4).
Are there dodge-chance trims, and is there a catch?
Yes — Ender Pearl gives 7.5% dodge chance but water damages the wearer, while Chorus Fruit gives 25% dodge chance.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Combat-Effect.title: Combat Effects
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Combat-Effect.content:
Combat Effects
A small, highly configurable mod by ElocinDev (same author as ReBalance, Resistance Balancer, Custom Entity/Item Attributes and Eternal Attributes) that applies status effects to the player when they fight a matching entity. Config entries key off a regex against the entity ID, a minimum-HP gate (useful for scoping effects to bosses only), and flags for whether the effect fires only when the player gets hit (vs. either side attacking) and whether the effect lands on the entity instead of the player.
On this server the shipped config (combat_effects.json5) is customized beyond the mod’s own documented default: it matches all entities (.*) with at least 300 HP and applies minecells:disarmed (a Minecells status effect) for 200 ticks — i.e. this is scoped to disarm the player in fights against very-high-HP bosses, not a general combat debuff.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Combat-Roll.title: Combat Roll
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Combat-Roll.content:
Combat Roll
Combat Roll (also by Daedelus, the Better Combat author) adds a dedicated dodge-roll ability bound to its own key — the i-frame button that makes harder boss fights survivable. On this server (combatroll/server.json5), a roll grants 4 ticks of invulnerability and locks you out of attacking/using items/jumping for a 10-tick roll duration; you can’t roll again for a 6-second cooldown, and you can’t roll at all while your weapon is on cooldown or while airborne (both explicitly disabled here to keep roll-distance attributes/enchantments from breaking). Despite the “stamina” framing in the category note, the actual gate is hunger, not a separate stamina bar: rolling costs 0.1 exhaustion per roll and requires a food level of at least 6.0 to use.
Three custom enchantments extend the roll: Longfooted (up to level 5, increases roll distance), Acrobat (up to level 10, reduces cooldown between rolls), and Multi-Roll (up to level 4, grants extra rolls before the cooldown kicks in) — all enabled on this server with escalating enchant costs. A small HUD arrow (bottom-left by default) tracks cooldown, with optional sound/flash cues when it’s ready again. The pack’s Quest Book doesn’t give Combat Roll its own dedicated entry (its neighboring “New Defensive Mechanics” quest actually covers the separate Shield Overhaul mod’s bash mechanic instead), but the roll is core to how every boss fight in the pack — including Marium’s Soulslike Weaponry’s legendary-weapon bosses — is meant to be played.
Anticipated questions
How many invulnerability frames does a roll give?
On this server, a roll grants 4 ticks of invulnerability and locks you out of attacking, using items, and jumping for a 10-tick roll duration, followed by a 6-second cooldown before you can roll again.
Does rolling use stamina?
Despite the “stamina” framing, the actual gate is hunger, not a separate stamina bar. Each roll costs 0.1 exhaustion and requires a food level of at least 6.0.
When can’t I roll?
You can’t roll while your weapon is on cooldown or while airborne — both explicitly disabled here to keep roll-distance attributes/enchantments from breaking.
What enchantments improve the roll?
Three custom ones, all enabled: Longfooted (up to level 5, increases roll distance), Acrobat (up to level 10, reduces cooldown between rolls), and Multi-Roll (up to level 4, grants extra rolls before the cooldown kicks in).
Does the Quest Book explain Combat Roll?
No — it doesn’t give Combat Roll its own dedicated entry (the neighboring “New Defensive Mechanics” quest covers the separate Shield Overhaul bash mechanic instead). Still, the roll is core to how every boss fight is meant to be played, including Marium’s Soulslike Weaponry’s legendary-weapon bosses. See Better Combat and Combat & Stats.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Custom-Entity.title: Custom Entity Attributes
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Custom-Entity.content:
Custom Entity Attributes
By ElocinDev (also behind Eternal Attributes, ReBalance, Resistance Balancer, Combat Effects and Custom Item Attributes) — “Customize attributes of entities, globally, per dimension, biome and more.” Ships two config layers: a Basic config (custom_entity_attributes/basic.json5) that matches entities by regex ID and applies a flat attribute-modifier list at a configurable apply chance, and an Advanced config for finer per-dimension/per-biome/per-difficulty control.
This server’s basic config is actively customized, not left empty — it buffs specific bosses directly, e.g. the Minecells boss minecells:conjunctivius gets +15 attack damage and a max-health increase applied at 100% chance. Modifiers support ADDITION, MULTIPLY_BASE, and MULTIPLY_TOTAL operations, and the mod automatically rescales an entity’s spawned HP percentage when max-health is modified (so mobs that spawn at a set HP fraction, like the Wither, still behave correctly).
Anticipated questions
What does Custom Entity Attributes do?
By ElocinDev, it lets you “customize attributes of entities, globally, per dimension, biome and more.”
What are the two config layers?
A Basic config (custom_entity_attributes/basic.json5) that matches entities by regex ID and applies a flat attribute-modifier list at a configurable apply chance, and an Advanced config for finer per-dimension/per-biome/per-difficulty control.
Is this server’s config actually being used?
Yes — the basic config is actively customized, not left empty. It buffs specific bosses directly, e.g. the Minecells boss minecells:conjunctivius gets +15 attack damage and a max-health increase applied at 100% chance.
What modifier operations are supported?
ADDITION, MULTIPLY_BASE, and MULTIPLY_TOTAL. The mod also automatically rescales an entity’s spawned HP percentage when max-health is modified, so mobs that spawn at a set HP fraction (like the Wither) still behave correctly.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Custom-Item-A.title: Custom Item Attributes
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Custom-Item-A.content:
Custom Item Attributes
By ElocinDev — “Customize default attributes of any item. With modded attributes & items supported.” The item-side counterpart to Custom Entity Attributes: lets the pack override or add attribute modifiers baked directly into specific items (as opposed to gear’s normal rolled/reforged stats), scoped per equip slot (mainhand/offhand/head/chest/legs/feet), and optionally force an item to be unbreakable.
This server’s config (custom_item_attributes/overrides.json5) shows it’s used to hand-balance specific problem items rather than broad categories — e.g. minecells:cursed_sword gets a -80% max-health penalty (multiplicative) as its drawback for whatever bonus it grants elsewhere, and spellbladenext:monkeystaff (Pillar of the Monkey King) gets -2 flat attack speed baked in as an intentional weapon-identity tradeoff. Reloads live via /reload, so these are tunable without a restart.
Anticipated questions
What does Custom Item Attributes actually do?
By ElocinDev, it lets the pack override or add attribute modifiers baked directly into specific items — including modded ones — scoped per equip slot (mainhand/offhand/head/chest/legs/feet), and can optionally force an item to be unbreakable.
How is this different from an item’s normal rolled or reforged stats?
These modifiers are hand-set on the item itself, as opposed to gear’s normal rolled/reforged stats. It’s the item-side counterpart to Custom Entity Attributes.
Which items does this server hand-tune, and why?
Two problem items in the server config: minecells:cursed_sword gets a -80% max-health penalty (multiplicative) as a drawback, and spellbladenext:monkeystaff (Pillar of the Monkey King, from Spellblade Next) gets -2 flat attack speed baked in as a weapon-identity tradeoff.
Do I need to restart the server to change these?
No. The overrides reload live via /reload, so they’re tunable without a restart.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Death-Knights.title: Death Knights
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Death-Knights.content:
Death Knights
A dark-magic-and-melee hybrid archetype explicitly “inspired by World of Warcraft,” sitting outside the pack’s main five archetypes (Archetypes & Builds). Adds three Tier II spellbooks (per the e_spell_books quest chapter) built around a shared theme of Runeblades and Runeaxes (Iron/Diamond/Netherite/Ruby/Aeternium, plus one-handed and Great two-handed variants) and full themed armor progressions — Hood/Tunic of Death’s Call as the base set, then Frozen Champion, Plaguebringer, Crimson Guard, Icebound Knight, Blightbringer and Crimson Knight sets. It also adds its own runeblade-specific jewelry (Ring/Necklace of the Eternal Winter, Signet of Death, Ring of Bloodthirst, etc.) and a custom Decaying enchantment that boosts Unholy and Blood Spell Power damage.
The three specs are genuinely distinct kits, not palette swaps:

Tome of Vampiric Knowledge (Blood, Tank) — self-sustain via lifesteal. Death Strike and Marrowrend deal hybrid physical+blood damage; Death Strike heals 10% max HP (or grants equivalent absorption at full health); Marrowrend stacks a Marrowshield Resistance buff that’s consumed by incoming hits; Blood Boil applies Blood Plague, a DoT that heals the Death Knight when they damage an infected target.
Tome of Unholy Teachings (Unholy, single-target DPS) — a disease-stacking rotation. Festering Strike applies/stacks a random disease (Festering Wound → Atrocious/Grievous Plague, which reduce enemy damage and healing respectively); Death Coil detonates disease stacks on the target and spreads a stack to nearby uninfected enemies; Epidemic detonates stacks on all nearby targets at once; Death Grip is a pull-and-slow.
Tome of the Eternal Winter (Frost, multi-target DPS) — “easy to understand but the hardest of all three to master” per the quest text. Obliterate/Frost Strike deal physical+frost damage and can shatter icicles off frozen targets; Remorseless Winter is a constant frost-damage aura with a freeze chance; Agonizing Breath is a frontal frost cone.

Depends on Necronomicon and Eternal Attributes (both also in this pack), and requires Java 21+ bytecode support. attribute.name.death_knights.blood_power / unholy_power are the mod’s two custom spell-power attributes that gear can roll.
Anticipated questions
Where does the Death Knight fit among the pack’s archetypes?
It’s a dark-magic-and-melee hybrid explicitly “inspired by World of Warcraft,” sitting outside the pack’s main five archetypes (Archetypes & Builds). It adds three Tier II spellbooks built around Runeblades and Runeaxes.
What are the three specs and how do they play?
Tome of Vampiric Knowledge (Blood, Tank) — self-sustain via lifesteal, with Death Strike healing 10% max HP and Marrowrend stacking a consumable Marrowshield Resistance buff. Tome of Unholy Teachings (Unholy, single-target DPS) — a disease-stacking rotation using Festering Strike, Death Coil, Epidemic and Death Grip. Tome of the Eternal Winter (Frost, multi-target DPS) — Obliterate/Frost Strike, a Remorseless Winter aura, and Agonizing Breath cone; called the hardest of the three to master.
What gear does it add?
Runeblades and Runeaxes (Iron/Diamond/Netherite/Ruby/Aeternium, in one-handed and Great two-handed variants), full themed armor sets (Death’s Call base, then Frozen Champion, Plaguebringer, Crimson Guard, Icebound Knight, Blightbringer, Crimson Knight), runeblade-specific jewelry, and a custom Decaying enchantment that boosts Unholy and Blood Spell Power damage.
What does it depend on?
It depends on Necronomicon and Eternal Attributes (both in this pack) and requires Java 21+ bytecode support.
Which custom attributes does its gear roll?
blood_power and unholy_power — the mod’s two custom spell-power attributes, defining its Blood and Unholy trees respectively.

Eternal Attributes

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Dynamic-RPG-R.title: Dynamic RPG Resource Bars
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Dynamic-RPG-R.content:
Dynamic RPG Resource Bars
Dynamic RPG Resource Bars (dynamic_resource_bars, jar dynamic_resource_bars-fabric-0.7.1-1.20.1.jar, by Muon) is a client-side HUD mod that replaces vanilla’s health/hunger/armor/air bars with animated, fully repositionable RPG-style bars, plus an optional mana bar for mods that provide a mana resource. It ships an in-game “HUD Element Editor” (drag-to-move, double-click for sub-element tweaks, per-bar resize/anchor/fill-direction/text-behavior controls) so each player can customize their own bar layout without editing files by hand.
On this server, config/dynamic_resource_bars-client.json shows Health and Stamina bars enabled and reskinned (custom background/overlay art at bar-specific pixel dimensions, e.g. health background 184x135, animated over 32 frames), while the Armor bar is hidden, the Air bar runs in “custom” mode (explicitly noted in the mod’s own lang strings as “linked to Stamina on Fabric 1.20.1”), and the Mana bar is set to “OFF” — meaning no compatible mana-providing mod (the mod supports RPGMana, Ars Nouveau, Iron’s Spellbooks, or generic “Mana Attributes”) is currently wired up for display in this pack, even though the toggle exists. The Stamina bar is anchored where the vanilla hunger bar normally sits and is configured to never show numeric text, while Health always shows numeric text — small choices that push the HUD toward a cleaner “just watch the bar” RPG feel rather than exact-number tracking.
As a pure UI/HUD layer, Dynamic RPG Resource Bars doesn’t add items, blocks, or recipes of its own — its role in the pack is to visualize whatever health/stamina/mana values the underlying RPG stat mods (e.g. Pufferfish’s Attributes, SimplySkills) already track, giving players an at-a-glance readout instead of relying on vanilla’s plain hearts and drumsticks.

Health and Stamina are enabled and reskinned; the Armor bar is hidden, the Air bar runs in “custom” mode (linked to Stamina on Fabric 1.20.1), and the Mana bar is set to OFF.

Because no compatible mana-providing mod is currently wired up in this pack — the mod supports RPGMana, Ars Nouveau, Iron’s Spellbooks or generic Mana Attributes, but none is set for display here, even though the toggle exists.
Does it add any items, blocks, or recipes?
No. It’s a pure UI/HUD layer — it only visualizes the health/stamina/mana values that underlying RPG stat mods (e.g. Pufferfish’s Attributes, SimplySkills) already track.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/DynamicTrim.title: DynamicTrim
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/DynamicTrim.content:
DynamicTrim
By Andrew6rant and Bawnorton — “Dynamically render Armour Trim patterns!” A rendering-layer companion to AllTheTrims: vanilla trim patterns are baked to specific armor textures/models, which breaks down once AllTheTrims allows trimming any armor piece (including modded armor with non-vanilla models). DynamicTrim generates the trim overlay dynamically at render time instead, so trims display correctly across the pack’s huge range of custom armor sets (Wizard robes, Paladin plate, Death Knight sets, etc.) rather than only vanilla’s diamond/iron/netherite armor shapes.
Purely a rendering fix with no player-facing config or gameplay content of its own.

Vanilla trim patterns are baked to specific armor textures/models, which breaks down once AllTheTrims allows trimming any armor piece — including modded armor with non-vanilla models. DynamicTrim is the rendering-layer companion that makes that work.

The pack’s huge range of custom armor sets — Wizard robes, Paladin plate, Death Knight sets, and more — rather than only vanilla’s diamond/iron/netherite armor shapes.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Eternal-Attri.title: Eternal Attributes
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Eternal-Attri.content:
Eternal Attributes
By ElocinDev — “Attributes for the Prominence modpack and its custom content mods,” explicitly written for this pack rather than being a generic library port. Registers a themed set of spell-power attributes that other Prominence-custom mods key off directly: Creation Power, Life Power, Death Power, Destruction Power, Unholy Power, Corruption Power, Astral Power, Blood Power, Nature Power, Decaying Power, and Corruption Resistance.
Several of these map straight onto the archetype system: Astral Power is the stat behind the endgame hybrid elemental-mage path referenced in Archetypes & Builds (“Runic Invocations / Astral Magic… blends all three schools via Astral Power”), and Blood Power / Unholy Power are the two spec-defining stats Death Knights uses for its Blood and Unholy trees (that mod lists eternal_attributes as a hard dependency). No standalone config ships for this mod on the server — it’s pure attribute registration, with the actual numbers coming from gear/talents elsewhere in the stack (Zenith Renewed affixes, Talent Tree nodes) and its range-safety handled by AttributeFix.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Extra-RPG-Att.title: Extra RPG Attributes
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Extra-RPG-Att.content:
Extra RPG Attributes
Jar/mod id extraspellattributes, by cleannrooster (Forg) — “For use with RPG series mods.” Despite the generic-sounding jar name, this is a purpose-built defensive/conversion attribute pack for the archetype mods: it adds power-conversion attributes (Attack Damage ⇄ Fire/Frost/Arcane/Healing Power, used by Spellblade Next’s hybrid melee-caster builds) alongside a set of standalone defensive stats — Reabsorption (regenerates Absorption after 4 seconds without being hit), Glancing Blow (chance to take 35% less damage from entity-sourced hits), Spell Suppression (chance for incoming spells to deal 50% less damage), Serenity/Spellbreak (chance for an already-suppressed spell to deal zero damage, capped 75%), Endurance/Defiance (flat damage-taken reduction with diminishing returns), and Determination (a % of health lost is regenerated back over 4 seconds).
It backs six enchantments that grant these stats directly (Suppressing, Defiance, Warding, Spellbreaking/“Evasion” is Glancing Blow’s enchant name, Battle Rouse) and ten trinket items in its own “Extra RPG Attributes Trinkets” item group — rings, amulets, and bracers (Netherite Diamond Ring/Amulet, Gold Quartz Ring/Amulet, Turtle Bracer, Amethyst Bracer, Ring of Undying, Banner of Undying, etc.) that presumably grant these attributes when worn as accessories. AttributeFix’s config lists several extraspellattributes: entries (endurance, spellsuppression) among its 194 tracked attributes, confirming this mod’s stats are part of the pack’s wider attribute-safety net.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Gun-Scaling.title: Gun Scaling
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Gun-Scaling.content:
Gun Scaling
A small bridge mod by Mervyn: “Scales damage of Soulslike Weaponry guns with Ranged Weapon attributes.” Marium’s Soulslike Weaponry’s firearms (a “gun,” a “potato” cannon, and a “matterCannon”) ship with their own flat damage numbers by default — this mod hooks them into the pack’s RPG stat system so ranged-damage gear/talent investment actually affects them, using the formula documented directly in its own config comment:
Hit_Damage = Base_Dmg * (1 + (power_lvl * archers_scale)) * (1 + attr / scaling) * (1 + (proj_vel - gun_vel) / gun_vel)
This server’s config (gun-scaling/gun_scaling.json) sets a damageScalingFactor of 0.85 for generic guns, but tunes the “potato” cannon and “matterCannon” far more aggressively (2.5 and 4.0 respectively), and both of those explicitly scale off the ranged_weapon:damage attribute from RangedWeaponAPI via an ADD operation — meaning stacking ranged-damage stat directly buffs these two specific weapons on this server, while the base “gun” entry has no attribute scaling entries configured at all.
Anticipated questions
What does Gun Scaling do?
A small bridge mod by Mervyn that scales the damage of Marium’s Soulslike Weaponry guns with Ranged Weapon attributes. Those firearms ship with flat damage by default; this mod hooks them into the pack’s RPG stat system so ranged-damage gear and talent investment actually affects them.
Which weapons does it cover, and are they tuned differently?
Three firearms — a “gun,” a “potato” cannon, and a “matterCannon.” The server sets a damageScalingFactor of 0.85 for generic guns but tunes the potato cannon to 2.5 and the matterCannon to 4.0, far more aggressively.
Does stacking ranged-damage stat actually buff these guns?
For the potato cannon and matterCannon, yes — both explicitly scale off the ranged_weapon:damage attribute from RangedWeaponAPI via an ADD operation. The base “gun” entry, however, has no attribute-scaling entries configured at all on this server.
How is the damage calculated?
Per the config’s own formula: Hit_Damage = Base_Dmg * (1 + (power_lvl * archers_scale)) * (1 + attr / scaling) * (1 + (proj_vel - gun_vel) / gun_vel).

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Jewelry-(RPG-.title: Jewelry (RPG Series)
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Jewelry-(RPG-.content:
Jewelry (RPG Series)
Adds a full ring-and-necklace slot game built on six gems — Ruby, Topaz, Citrine, Jade, Sapphire, and Tanzanite — mined from Gem Veins (and their deepslate variant) found underground, plus a dedicated Jeweler villager who trades from a Jeweler’s Kit workbench, and jewelry shop structures that generate in desert, savanna, plains, taiga, and snowy villages. Each gem crafts into a ring or necklace, and every piece scales up through copper → iron → gold → netherite tiers with growing stat bonuses. On this server the numbers are real and archetype-specific: a Sapphire Ring/Necklace adds flat max health, a Topaz Necklace multiplies Arcane and Fire spell power, a Jade Ring multiplies ranged-weapon damage, a Netherite Ruby Ring/Necklace multiplies melee attack damage, and an Iron Ring adds flat armor — the mod hooks directly into the same attribute IDs used by Zenith Attributes Renewed, Ranged Weapon API, and Combat Roll (one Archer ring even boosts combatroll:recharge).
Beyond the craftable tiers, Jewelry adds twelve unique rings/necklaces — one ring and one necklace per archetype/element — each with its own name and flavor text, clearly patterned after World of Warcraft loot: Ring of Fury / Amulet of Torture (attack), Angelista’s Revenge / Medallion of Disdain (dexterity), Thalassian Ranger Band / Darnassian Strider Amulet (archer), Juggernaut Band / Sentinel’s Amulet (tank), Ring of Omnipotence / Amulet of Unfettered Magics (arcane), Sunflare Signet / Pendant of Sunfire (fire), Permafrost Stone / Glacial Shard (frost), Anett’s Embrace / Adria’s Pendant (healing), Ring of Unstable Currents / Amulet of Unrelenting Storms (lightning), and Signet of Captured Souls / Occult Necklace (soul). The in-game quest book (einformation_7new_mechanics) uses the Archer set specifically to explain that Ranged Weapon Damage is “obtained through Talents, Jewelry and from the ranged weapons themselves,” confirming jewelry is treated as a first-class stat source alongside the Talent Tree.
Jewelry depends on spell_power and ranged_weapon_api directly (per its fabric.mod.json), and its rings/necklaces are equipped through the Accessories slot system rather than armor slots.
Anticipated questions
Which six gems does Jewelry use, and where do they come from?
Ruby, Topaz, Citrine, Jade, Sapphire, and Tanzanite — mined from Gem Veins (and their deepslate variant) found underground.
How do jewelry pieces get stronger?
Each gem crafts into a ring or necklace, and every piece scales up through copper → iron → gold → netherite tiers with growing stat bonuses.
What stats do specific pieces give?
A Sapphire Ring/Necklace adds flat max health, a Topaz Necklace multiplies Arcane and Fire spell power, a Jade Ring multiplies ranged-weapon damage, a Netherite Ruby Ring/Necklace multiplies melee attack damage, and an Iron Ring adds flat armor. The mod hooks directly into the attribute IDs used by Zenith Renewed, Ranged Weapon API, and Combat Roll. See Combat & Stats.
Are there unique, non-craftable pieces?
Yes — twelve unique rings/necklaces, one ring and one necklace per archetype/element, each with its own name and flavor text patterned after World of Warcraft loot. See Archetypes & Builds.
Which slots do rings and necklaces use?
They’re equipped through the Accessories slot system, not armor slots.
Who sells jewelry and where are the shops?
A dedicated Jeweler villager trades from a Jeweler’s Kit workbench, and jewelry shop structures generate in desert, savanna, plains, taiga, and snowy villages.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/MC-Dungeons-A.title: MC Dungeons Armors
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/MC-Dungeons-A.content:
MC Dungeons Armors
MC Dungeons Armors (mcda, jar mcda-5.0.2.jar, by Chronosacaria/Kluzzio) ports the named armor sets from Minecraft Dungeons into Java as full 4-piece sets (helmet/chestplate/leggings/boots, each with its own name like “Beehive Tasset” or “Grim Pads”), each carrying its own protection/toughness/knockback-resistance/attack/movement stats and an on-wear special effect. The jar’s lang file lists roughly 74 distinct armor sets (Archer’s, Beehive, Beenest, Champion’s, Hero’s, Titan’s Shroud, Dark, Royal Guard, Evocation, Ember, Verdant, Grim, Wither, Guard’s, Curious, Renegade, Shadow Walker, Phantom, Frost Bite, Stalwart, Ghost Kindler, Mystery-color variants, Highland, Frost, Souldancer, Cave Crawler, Thief, Spider, Black Wolf, Fox/Arctic Fox, Opulent, Gilded Glory, Rugged Climbing Gear, Sprout, Living Vines, Golden Piglin, Glow Squid, Nimble Turtle, Troubadour, Teleportation, Unstable, Sturdy Shulker, Gourdian, Cauldron, and more), each with 2-3 lines of in-game lore tooltip text.
On this server (config/mcda/mcda_enable_armors.json5) only a curated subset of the 74 sets is actually enabled — including Wolf, Ocelot, Black Wolf, Souldancer, Hero, Titan, Arctic Fox, Thief, Spider, Entertainer, Sweet Tooth, Turtle, Full Metal, Plate, Opulent, Dark, Beehive, Soul Robe, Fox, Ghostly, Ghost Kindler, Beenest, Champion, and Emerald — while higher-tier or redundant sets (Frost Bite, Purple/Blue/Green/Red Mystery, Shulker, Frost, Highland, Evocation, Stalwart Mail, Goat, Curious, Gourdian, Verdant, Shadow Walker, Phantom, Reinforced Mail, Living Vines, Archer, Squid, Guards, Piglin, Teleportation, Cave Crawler, Cauldron, Wither, Royal, Gilded, Hungry Horror, Golden Piglin, Snow, Battle, Glow Squid, Sprout, Grim, Sturdy Shulker, Mercenary, Renegade, Climbing Gear, Troubadour, Splendid) are turned off. mcda_armor_stats.json5 tunes each set’s exact numbers per-piece — e.g. Hero’s Armor gives 3/6/8/3 protection (boots/legs/chest/head) with 2.0 toughness and +5% attack damage, while the enabled but unarmored-feeling Wolf Armor gives 2/4/5/2 protection with only +2.5% attack damage and no toughness. Each set’s special effect is a real status-effect proc: Beehive/Beenest grant “Buzzy Hive,” Wither Armor applies Withered, Spider Armor grants wall-climbing, Thief Armor grants Invisibility, Shadow Walker/Phantom/Frost Bite negate fall damage or grant Slow Falling, and Titan’s Shroud/Hero’s Armor grant “Hero of the Village” (better villager prices). The full set of 5 mcda-specific enchantments (Bag of Souls, Burning, Chilling, Cowardice, Deflect, Fire Focus, Fire Trail, Food Reserves, Frenzied, Heal Allies, Lucky Explorer, Poison Focus, Potion Barrier, Reckless, Recycler, Snowball, Surprise Gift, Swiftfooted) is enabled, with only Death Barter disabled, and all are also sellable by villagers. In the quest book, several mcda pieces (Dark Armor’s full set, Souldancer Robe, Titan’s Shroud) appear as reward items in the “New Mechanics” chapter.
Anticipated questions
What does this mod add?
Named 4-piece armor sets from Minecraft Dungeons (helmet/chestplate/leggings/boots), each with its own protection/toughness/knockback/attack/movement stats and an on-wear special effect. The jar carries ~74 sets; only a curated subset is enabled on this server.
What kind of set effects do they have?
Real status-effect procs, not just stats — Thief Armor grants Invisibility, Spider Armor gives wall-climbing, Titan’s Shroud and Hero’s Armor grant “Hero of the Village” (better villager prices), Beehive/Beenest grant “Buzzy Hive,” and Shadow Walker/Phantom/Frost Bite negate fall damage or grant Slow Falling.
Which sets are enabled, and how strong are they?
A curated list including Wolf, Hero, Titan, Souldancer, Thief, Spider, Opulent, Dark, Beehive and more; higher-tier or redundant sets are turned off. Numbers are tuned per-piece — Hero’s Armor gives 3/6/8/3 protection with 2.0 toughness and +5% attack, while Wolf Armor is a lighter 2/4/5/2 with +2.5% attack and no toughness.
Where do they fit in gear progression?
They’re a mid-game armor path that competes on utility through its set effects rather than raw tier, and every piece still runs through Gear Rarity & Reforging. Several (the Dark set, Souldancer Robe, Titan’s Shroud) are quest-book “New Mechanics” rewards.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/MC-Dungeons-W.title: MC Dungeons Weapons
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/MC-Dungeons-W.content:
MC Dungeons Weapons
MC Dungeons Weapons (mcdw, jar mcdw-9.0.4.jar, same authors as MC Dungeons Armors, Chronosacaria/Kluzzio) is the weapon-side companion port from Minecraft Dungeons, adding an entire new weapon-type roster beyond vanilla swords/axes: daggers, hammers, sickles, scythes, spears, glaives, staves, whips, gauntlets, double axes, and a large bow/crossbow line, alongside reskinned/rebalanced swords and axes. The en_us lang file lists around 90+ named weapons, several per weapon-type — daggers alone include Fangs of Frost, Moon Dagger, Tempest Knife, Chill Gale Knife, Resolute Tempest Knife, Shear Dagger, Backstabber, Swift Striker, Void Touched Blade, “The Beginning,” and “The End”; hammers include Sun’s Grace, Bonehead Hammer, Hammer of Gravity, Stormlander, and Boneclub; swords include Hawkbrand, Sinister Sword, Freezing Foil, Heartstealer, Obsidian Claymore, “The Starless Night,” Dancer’s Sword, Nameless Blade, Katana/Master’s Katana/Dark Katana, and Coral/Sponge Striker (ocean-themed); bows include Bonebow, Haunted Bow, Twin Bow, Guardian Bow, “The Purple Storm,” “The Green Menace,” and “The Pink Scoundrel.” A separate mcdw-specific quiver of enchantments (Shadow Shot/Shadow Barb among them) and a Harp Crossbow / Veiled Crossbow both appear as quest-book reward items in the “New Mechanics” chapter alongside the mcda armor pieces, confirming these are treated as intended mid-game progression goals in this pack.
Each weapon’s stats live in config/mcdw/mcdw_stats_config.json5 (30 KB, per-weapon isEnabled/material/damage/attackSpeed/repairIngredient entries) — e.g. the enabled Broadsword hits for 5 damage at -3.0 attack speed with an iron-ingot repair ingredient, Claymore hits for 7 at -3.2 speed, while some entries like Sword of Coral Blade and Sword of Cutlass are explicitly disabled on this server (isEnabled: false). A companion mcdw_enchantments_config.json5 (14 KB) tunes an equally large custom enchantment roster (Ambush, Critical Hit, Void Strike, Pain Cycle, Enigma Resonator, Dynamo, Shadow Form, Enigma Shot, Growing, Void Shot, Overcharge, Committed, Hunter’s Promise, and more) with a global directDamageEnchantmentMultiplier (1.0 here) plus per-enchantment maxLevel, procChance, and isAvailableForRandomSelection/villager-trade toggles — giving admins fine control over how aggressively these Dungeons-style proc enchants show up in loot and trades.
Anticipated questions
What does this mod add?
A port of Minecraft Dungeons weapons into Java — daggers, hammers, sickles, scythes, spears, glaives, staves, whips, gauntlets, double axes, and a large bow/crossbow line, plus rebalanced swords and axes. Around 90+ named weapons, several per type.
How do I get them, and what’s their role?
They’re mid-game progression goals, not top-tier gear. Several — plus a mcdw quiver of enchantments, the Harp Crossbow, and the Veiled Crossbow — appear as reward items in the quest book’s “New Mechanics” chapter, while others come from loot and villager trades. Each has fixed stats in config (the Broadsword hits 5 at -3.0 attack speed, the Claymore 7 at -3.2).
How do they compare to Simply Swords?
Different flavor: MCDW weapons are named Dungeons items with their own proc-enchant roster (Ambush, Critical Hit, Void Strike, Enigma Resonator…), aimed at the mid game. Simply Swords reaches deeper into endgame with its Runic tier and world-loot uniques. Both feed Gear Rarity & Reforging.
Are all of them enabled?
Most are, but a few entries (e.g. Sword of Coral Blade, Sword of Cutlass) are disabled on this server, and how aggressively the proc-enchants show up in loot and trades is admin-tuned per enchantment.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Marium's-Soul.title: Marium's Soulslike Weaponry
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Marium's-Soul.content:
Marium’s Soulslike Weaponry
Marium’s Soulslike Weaponry (“Adds lots of legendary weapons and bosses!”) is a full crossover armory: nearly every weapon is a direct nod to a game/media icon, remade as a craftable soul-infused legendary. The item list reads like a greatest-hits list — Master Sword, Excalibur, Mjölnir, Frostmourne, Moonveil (Elden Ring), Guinsoo’s Rageblade (League of Legends), Kraken Slayer (as both a spear-bow and a crossbow), Sting, Ludwig’s Holy Blade, Dawnbreaker/Genesis Fracture, The Darkin Blade, The Darkin Scythe, Kirkhammer, Draupnir Spear, Night’s Edge, Mehrunes’ Razor, Tonitrus, and the Bloodborne-style Moonlight family (Moonlight Shortsword → Bluemoon → Holy Moonlight Greatsword → Pure Moonlight Greatsword). Weapon types go well beyond swords: pistols, a blunderbuss, a Gatling Gun, and a Hunter Cannon all fire craftable Infused Quicksilver Bullets.
Its own Quest Book chapter walks the whole progression arc. It opens with mining two special deepslate-layer stones (“important into the creation of your soul equipment”) and smelting soul sand for Lost Souls, which become Soul Infused Ingots — the core crafting resource. From there the chapter sends you after four named bosses, each with real flavor text:

The Decaying King (“Here stands a king who lost it all, end his false reign and emerge victorious”) — drops a soul + a Withered Demon Heart used for “Fall of a Kingdom.”
Old Champion’s Remains, found at “the Champion’s Grave” — drops soul + ghost essence for “Exorcism.”
Fallen Icon / its second phase Harbinger of Moonlight — the “Fallen Puppet” → “Retribution” arc: “You have brought back a fallen knight to their rightful body, and now you faced him in their former glory.”
Monarch of Chaos, summoned via a pedestal using a “Shard of Uncertainty” dropped from a Wither-adjacent fight (“The Abyss Stares Back”) — drops the Crown of Chaos / Helm of Chaos / Cape of Chaos set.
The last dragon of the End is also huntable for its “Essence of the Dragon.”

Ranged weapons run on Silver Bullets, described in-quest as “cheap but… it’ll be your debt” — the Hunter Pistol trades a fast reload for single shots, the Blunderbuss is a shotgun-style spread, the Hunter Cannon needs 10 bullets per shot with a long reload, and the Gatling Gun spins up before rapid-firing through your bullet stock fast. Other tools: the Lunar Ring launches ripple-style moonlight waves as a ranged melee option (“Moonwalker”), and a Moonstone Compass (“Guiding Moon”) points toward the nearest boss.
Server-side, most of the roster is left craftable (config/soulsweapons/soulsweapons.json) — Excalibur, Master Sword, Mjölnir, Moonveil, Dragonbane, Bloodlust, and the full Moonlight family all have disable_recipe_*: false. A short deliberate blacklist is turned off: Frostmourne, the Kraken Slayer Bow (the crossbow variant stays enabled), the Chungus Staff, Supernova, and the Arkenplate/Hallowheart armor sets (plus their infused upgrades) are all disabled recipes on this server. Several enchantments unique to the mod (Fast Hands, Posture Breaker, Stagger, Ethereal Ammunition, Explosive Rounds, Misfire Curse, Blight Carrier, Frostsilver, Phantom Trace, Ricochet) are also disabled, leaving Chain Lightning and Tether active.
Anticipated questions
What’s the core crafting resource, and how do I start?
Mine the two special deepslate-layer stones and smelt soul sand into Lost Souls, which become Soul Infused Ingots — the main ingredient for all soul equipment. The mod has its own Quest Book chapter (“Soul Weaponry”) that walks the whole arc from that first soul sand onward.
Which bosses does it add, and what do they drop?
Four named bosses plus the last End dragon. The Decaying King drops a Withered Demon Heart (“Fall of a Kingdom”); Old Champion’s Remains at the Champion’s Grave drops soul + ghost essence (“Exorcism”); the Fallen Icon → Harbinger of Moonlight arc is the “Fallen Puppet → Retribution” fight; the Monarch of Chaos is summoned from a pedestal using a Shard of Uncertainty (dropped by a Wither-adjacent fight) and drops the Crown/Helm/Cape of Chaos set. The last End dragon gives Essence of the Dragon.
What are the legendary weapons?
A crossover roster remade as soul legendaries — Master Sword, Excalibur, Mjölnir, Moonveil, Draupnir Spear, the Darkin Blade and Scythe, and the Moonlight family (Moonlight Shortsword → Bluemoon → Holy Moonlight → Pure Moonlight Greatsword) — most craftable once you have Soul Infused Ingots.
How do the guns work?
All firearms run on craftable Silver Bullets. The Hunter Pistol is single-shot with a fast reload, the Blunderbuss is a spread shotgun, the Hunter Cannon combines 10 bullets into one cannonball shot with a long reload, and the Gatling Gun spins up then rapid-fires through your stock. For how ranged damage numbers scale, see Gun Scaling.
Is the whole roster craftable on this server?
Most of it. The deliberate disabled-recipe blacklist is Frostmourne, the Kraken Slayer Bow (the crossbow variant stays enabled), the Chungus Staff, Supernova, and the Arkenplate/Hallowheart armor sets.

This mod adds new trim patterns; AllTheTrims instead widens what can serve as trim material.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/More-RPG-Clas.title: More RPG Classes
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/More-RPG-Clas.content:
More RPG Classes
More RPG Classes (“Explore the world with new weapons and spells!”) is a smaller, thinner mod alongside SimplySkills and Pufferfish’s Skills — it leans on the same Spell Engine/Spell Power framework (depends on spell_engine >=0.15.0, spell_power >=0.10.2, azurelibarmor) but its jar and config contain comparatively little standalone content. Its item list is limited to a handful of crafting materials — Water Rune, Earth Rune, Air Rune (aqua/terra/storm “stone”), Bear Fur, Wolf Fur, and Hardened Leather — used to make its weapons/armor, which mostly live as entity/armor models rather than distinct items in the jar itself.
It contributes several status effects used across the pack’s combat: Molten Armor (damages armored targets and strips their armor/toughness), Stun, Frozen Solid (can’t move/attack/jump, takes bonus damage while frozen), Fear (reduced attack damage), Grievous Wounds (reduced healing, increased incoming damage), Bleeding, and Collected Soul (stacking soul spell power). It also registers its own attributes — Rage Power, Arcane Fuse, Lifesteal, Damage Reflect — which show up in Zenith Attributes Renewed’s hidden-attributes list, and a small set of elemental-mastery enchantments (Elemental/Air/Earth/Water Mastery, max level 5, +3% elemental spell damage per level per config/more_rpg_classes/enchantments.json). Config is genuinely thin: tweaks_v1.json has exactly one tunable value (a rage-damage-scaling factor), and there’s no dedicated skill tree config for it in this pack — it plugs into the shared spell/attribute ecosystem rather than adding its own Talent Tree category.
Anticipated questions
What items does More RPG Classes contribute?
A handful of crafting materials — Water Rune, Earth Rune, Air Rune, Bear Fur, Wolf Fur, and Hardened Leather — used to make its weapons/armor, which mostly live as entity/armor models rather than distinct items.
What status effects does it add?
Molten Armor (damages armored targets and strips their armor/toughness), Stun, Frozen Solid, Fear (reduced attack damage), Grievous Wounds (reduced healing, increased incoming damage), Bleeding, and Collected Soul (stacking soul spell power).
What do its elemental-mastery enchantments do?
Elemental/Air/Earth/Water Mastery, each max level 5, granting +3% elemental spell damage per level.
Does it add its own Talent Tree category?
No — there’s no dedicated skill tree config for it in this pack; it plugs into the shared spell/attribute ecosystem. Its own attributes (Rage Power, Arcane Fuse, Lifesteal, Damage Reflect) show up in Zenith Attributes Renewed’s hidden-attributes list. See Archetypes & Builds.
How much of it is configurable?
Very little — tweaks_v1.json has exactly one tunable value, a rage-damage-scaling factor.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/More-Totems.title: More Totems
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/More-Totems.content:
More Totems
More Totems (moretotems, jar more-totems-mod-2.16.0.jar, by Hyper_Pigeon) adds seven Totem of Undying variants, each themed after a different mob and granting a unique on-activation effect beyond vanilla’s plain Regeneration/Absorption/Fire Resistance. Craftable by surrounding a vanilla Totem of Undying with 8 of a themed ingredient in a 3x3 shaped crafting grid: the Explosive Totem of Undying (8 Gunpowder, creeper-themed) presumably detonates a controlled blast on save; the Stinging Totem of Undying (bee-themed) applies its “Sniper” or sting-related effect; the Skeletal Totem of Undying (8 Bone) grants a skeleton-archer-styled buff; the Teleporting Totem of Undying blinks the player to safety; the Ghastly Totem of Undying (8 Ghast Tears) ties into the mod’s “Cephalopod”/ghast-flight theming; the Tentacled Totem of Undying leans on the same squid/ghast-adjacent “Cephalopod” effect; and the Rotting Totem of Undying applies a zombie-flavored “Necrosis” effect. The mod also registers two summonable helper entities, a “Totem Bee” and “Totem Zombie,” suggesting at least the Stinging and Rotting totems summon a temporary ally mob on activation rather than (or in addition to) applying a status effect.
No dedicated config file exists for More Totems under config/ on this server (a find for “totem” in the config directory only turns up unrelated Iron Chests netherite-chest configs and Better Archaeology’s separate “totem” items in the quest book) — the mod ships with no exposed server-side tuning, so all seven variants run on their packaged vanilla-recipe defaults. It doesn’t appear in any FTB Quests chapter either; the only “totem” hits in the quest chapters belong to the unrelated Better Archaeology mod’s Torrent/Soul/Growth Totems.
Anticipated questions
How many totems does it add, and how are they crafted?
Seven Totem of Undying variants, each crafted by surrounding a vanilla Totem of Undying with 8 of a themed ingredient in a 3x3 shaped crafting grid.
What are the variants?
The Explosive (8 Gunpowder, creeper-themed), Stinging (bee-themed), Skeletal (8 Bone), Teleporting, Ghastly (8 Ghast Tears), Tentacled, and Rotting (zombie-flavored “Necrosis”) Totems of Undying, each granting a unique on-activation effect beyond vanilla’s plain buffs.
Do any totems summon a helper?
Likely — the mod registers two summonable helper entities, a Totem Bee and Totem Zombie, suggesting at least the Stinging and Rotting totems summon a temporary ally on activation.
Can I tune the totems on this server?
No — no dedicated config file exists for More Totems, so all seven variants run on their packaged vanilla-recipe defaults.
Is it part of the quest book?
No — it doesn’t appear in any FTB Quests chapter (the “totem” quest hits belong to the unrelated Better Archaeology mod).

A one-line balance mod by Stalemated: “Adds crossbow compatibility to the mutant skeleton chestplate,” a boss-drop item referenced elsewhere in the vault (Archetypes & Builds notes it as a Ranger upgrade path). A config-gated patch rather than new content — every feature flag is independently toggleable.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Mythic-Upgrad.title: Mythic Upgrades
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Mythic-Upgrad.content:
Mythic Upgrades
Mythic Upgrades (mythicupgrades, jar mythicupgrades-4.2.0+mc1.20.1.jar, by TriQue) is the other mod that extends progression past vanilla Netherite, but instead of stacking parallel metal tiers like Advanced Netherite, it adds seven brand-new gemstones — Aquamarine, Peridot, Topaz, Ruby, Sapphire, Ametrine, and Jade — each mined from its own ore (with deepslate variants) and smelted into ingots, crystal shards, and potions. Each gem has a full armor set and tool set, but rather than being a standalone tier, each gem’s smithing template (<gem>_upgrade_smithing_template) is applied to existing Netherite equipment (“Add netherite armor, weapon, or tool” + the gem ingot), turning Mythic Upgrades into a literal “socket a gem into your Netherite gear” system layered on top of vanilla Netherite rather than a replacement for it. There’s also an eighth material, Necoium (raw ore + ingot + block), that appears to be a rarer crafting component rather than its own gem-armor line.
Each gem grants a themed armor set-bonus and a themed tool on-hit effect, with exact numbers tuned in config/mythicupgrades-config.json5: Aquamarine applies “Ice Shield” (armor, amplifier 2, 1.0s duration) and Freezes enemies on tool hit (0.5s freeze duration); Peridot applies “Poisonous Thorns” (amplifier 1, 3.0s poison) and its tools poison on hit (amplifier 2, 1.5s); Topaz grants Protection + “Item Mastery” (amplifier 4) + Fire Resistance as its armor bonus, and its tools have 3x durability, burn targets for 10 seconds, and auto-smelt mined loot; Ruby grants Spelunker (amplifier 5) from armor and Haste from tools; Sapphire grants “Damage Deflection” (amplifier 2) from armor, and its tools deal bonus damage equal to 5% of the target’s max health (with a custom death message, “has received enough magic percentage damage to pass away,” when this finishes a kill); Ametrine grants “Arcane Aura” (levitation, amplifier 2, 0.75s) from armor and levitates targets on tool hit (amplifier 4, 0.75s); Jade grants Speed + Jump Boost (both amplifier 2) from armor and a “Bouncer” effect (amplifier 4, 2.0s) from tools. This gives Mythic Upgrades a clearly RPG-elemental identity (ice/poison/fire/haste/damage-magic/levitation/mobility) compared to Advanced Netherite’s mob-pacification theme, and the two mods are explicitly compatible/stackable since Mythic Upgrades’ smithing templates consume Netherite-tier base items — including, presumably, Advanced Netherite’s own upgraded gear.
Anticipated questions
What does it add above netherite?
Seven new gemstones — Aquamarine, Peridot, Topaz, Ruby, Sapphire, Ametrine, and Jade — each mined from its own ore (with deepslate variants), plus a rarer material, Necoium. Each gem has a full armor and tool set.
How do I get the gear — is it a new tier?
Not a standalone tier. Each gem has a smithing template applied to existing Netherite equipment (Netherite item + gem ingot), so it works like socketing a gem into your netherite gear rather than replacing it.
What do the gems actually do?
Each grants a themed armor set-bonus and a tool on-hit effect: Aquamarine = Ice Shield / freeze, Peridot = poison, Topaz = fire + auto-smelt + 3x durability, Ruby = Spelunker / Haste, Sapphire = damage deflection + bonus damage equal to 5% of the target’s max health, Ametrine = levitation, Jade = Speed + Jump Boost + Bouncer.
How does it fit with Advanced Netherite?
They stack — Mythic Upgrades’ templates consume netherite-tier base items, including Advanced Netherite’s own upgraded gear, so you can gem a Netherite-X piece. Both extend progression past netherite, and all of it still flows through Gear Rarity & Reforging.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Paladins--and.title: Paladins & Priests (RPG Series)
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Paladins--and.content:
Paladins & Priests (RPG Series)
The Holy archetype mod, adding two Tier I spellbooks: the Paladin Libram (melee tank/support, crafted with the also-added Claymore, Great Hammer and Mace weapon lines up through Netherite/Aeternium/Ruby tiers) and the Holy Book (pure caster support). Full matching armor progressions exist for both — Paladin/Crusader plate sets and Priest/Prior robe sets — plus dedicated Holy Wands/Staves and Iron→Aeternium/Ruby Kite Shields. A Monk villager profession (with its own Monk Workbench) sells related gear.
Spells split cleanly by role: the Paladin side gets Judgement (AoE strike + stun), Battle Banner (party-wide attack speed/knockback resistance buff), and Divine Protection (blocks a set number of incoming hits); the Priest side gets Heal/Flash Heal, Holy Shock (heal ally + smite enemy in one cast), a channeled Holy Light beam that heals allies and burns enemies simultaneously, Circle of Healing (AoE heal + absorption), and Barrier — a summoned dome that blocks projectiles, magic, and intruding enemies. Config (paladins/tweaks.json) tunes Battle Banner’s numbers directly: +40% attack speed, +40% ranged/spell haste, +50% knockback resistance, plus a 0.3 knockback strength for Barrier.
Per the pack’s own quest book (e_spell_books chapter), the Paladin Libram is a Tier II hybrid — explicitly described as “a combination of a Warrior and a Priest,” craftable from Tier I books rather than found directly. The same quest groups it alongside two other Tank-flavored Tier II books, Oath of Defiance and Oath of Vengeance (both actually belong to Spellblade Next), as the pack’s three tank-oriented hybrid paths.
Anticipated questions
What two spellbooks does the mod add?
The Paladin Libram (melee tank/support) and the Holy Book (pure caster support), both Tier I, with full matching armor progressions and dedicated Holy Wands/Staves and Kite Shields.
What Paladin spells are available?
Judgement (AoE strike + stun), Battle Banner (party-wide attack speed/knockback resistance buff), and Divine Protection (blocks a set number of incoming hits). See Combat & Stats.
What Priest spells are available?
Heal/Flash Heal, Holy Shock (heal ally + smite enemy in one cast), a channeled Holy Light beam, Circle of Healing (AoE heal + absorption), and Barrier (a dome blocking projectiles, magic, and enemies).
What does the config tune?
paladins/tweaks.json sets Battle Banner to +40% attack speed, +40% ranged/spell haste, +50% knockback resistance, plus a 0.3 knockback strength for Barrier.
Is the Paladin Libram Tier I or Tier II?
The pack’s quest book treats it as a Tier II hybrid — “a combination of a Warrior and a Priest,” craftable from Tier I books — grouped with Oath of Defiance and Oath of Vengeance (both from Spellblade Next) as the three tank-oriented hybrid paths.
Who sells the gear?
A Monk villager profession with its own Monk Workbench. See Archetypes & Builds.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Projectile-Da.title: Projectile Damage Attribute
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Projectile-Da.content:
Projectile Damage Attribute
A small API-style mod that adds a generic “projectile damage” attribute so ranged-weapon damage (bows, crossbows, and anything else that fires a projectile) can be modified independently of vanilla’s hardcoded bow math — the same role RangedWeaponAPI plays for weapon creation, but scoped specifically to the damage stat itself.
This server’s config (projectile_damage.json) sets default_bow_damage to 4.0 and default_crossbow_damage to 2.0 as the baseline the attribute scales from, and disables add_default_attributes_for_unspecified_bows/crossbows — meaning only weapons explicitly configured to use this attribute get the custom scaling; anything unlisted falls back to vanilla behavior rather than silently inheriting these defaults. There’s also a status_effect_impact_multiplier_per_stack (0.2) governing how status-effect stacks (e.g. from other RPG mods) scale projectile impact.
This is core plumbing for the Ranger/Archer archetype, working alongside RangedWeaponAPI (whose ranged_weapon:damage attribute is what Gun Scaling actually reads) rather than exposing that exact attribute itself.
Anticipated questions
What does this mod do?
It adds a generic “projectile damage” attribute so ranged-weapon damage (bows, crossbows, and anything else that fires a projectile) can be modified independently of vanilla’s hardcoded bow math.
What baseline damage does the server config set?
projectile_damage.json sets default_bow_damage to 4.0 and default_crossbow_damage to 2.0 as the baseline the attribute scales from.
Do all bows automatically get this scaling?
No — add_default_attributes_for_unspecified_bows/crossbows are disabled, so only weapons explicitly configured to use this attribute get the custom scaling; anything unlisted falls back to vanilla behavior.
What does status_effect_impact_multiplier_per_stack do?
Set to 0.2, it governs how status-effect stacks (e.g. from other RPG mods) scale projectile impact.
How does it relate to RangedWeaponAPI?
It’s core plumbing for the Ranger/Archer archetype, working alongside RangedWeaponAPI (whose ranged_weapon:damage attribute is what Gun Scaling actually reads) rather than exposing that exact attribute itself. See Archetypes & Builds.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Pufferfish's-.content:
Pufferfish’s Attributes
Pufferfish’s Attributes (mod id puffish_attributes) is a small companion library to Pufferfish’s Skills — “adds more attributes to the game.” It has no dedicated config folder on this server (it ships no tunable settings; it just registers attribute types for other mods, especially the Talent Tree, to grant). Its fabric.mod.json explicitly requires Puffish Skills ≥0.12.0 to function, confirming it’s plumbing for that mod rather than a standalone system.
The attributes it adds, per its lang file, cover the stat categories that the prom Talent Tree nodes grant: Stamina, Magic/Melee/Ranged Damage, Fortune, Healing, Jump, Resistance (plus Magic/Melee/Ranged Resistance), Mining/Pickaxe/Axe/Shovel Speed, Sprinting Speed, Knockback, Repair Cost, Armor/Toughness/Protection/Resistance Shred (with elemental sub-variants), Natural Regeneration, Stealth, Life Steal, Fall Reduction, and Bow/Crossbow Projectile Speed. These are exactly the kind of bonuses seen in Talent Tree node definitions like melee_damage+3.5% or stamina+10% — Pufferfish’s Attributes is the attribute registry, Pufferfish’s Skills is the tree that assigns them to nodes.
Anticipated questions
Does Pufferfish’s Attributes have any config or settings to tweak?
No — it ships no tunable settings and has no dedicated config folder on this server. It just registers attribute types for other mods (especially the Talent Tree) to grant.
What does it actually add to the game?
A set of attributes covering the stat categories that the prom Talent Tree nodes grant — Stamina, Magic/Melee/Ranged Damage, Fortune, Healing, Jump, Resistance (plus elemental sub-variants), tool/mining speeds, Knockback, the various Shred stats, Natural Regeneration, Stealth, Life Steal, Fall Reduction, and Bow/Crossbow Projectile Speed.
How does it relate to Pufferfish’s Skills?
It’s a companion library: Pufferfish’s Attributes is the attribute registry, and Pufferfish’s Skills is the tree that assigns those attributes to nodes. Its fabric.mod.json explicitly requires Puffish Skills ≥0.12.0 to function.
Is it a standalone system I interact with?
No — it’s plumbing for other mods rather than a standalone system, which is why it registers attribute types but has no config of its own. See Combat & Stats for how those stats play out.
