Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Pufferfish's-.title: Pufferfish's Skills
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Pufferfish's-.content:
Pufferfish’s Skills
Pufferfish’s Skills (mod id puffish_skills) is a generic, fully data-driven skill-tree engine — “adds a fully configurable skill system to the game.” It supplies the N-key Talent Tree UI, per-category XP/leveling, and node unlock logic, but every actual tree (nodes, connections, XP curve) is authored as JSON under config/puffish_skills/categories/. In this pack there are 14 categories defined in config/puffish_skills/config.json, and this is the mod directly responsible for the Talent Tree system described in the “Talent Tree & Fate Talents” system note.
The main tree is prom (“Talent Tree”), which has 175 nodes and a level cap of 32 with XP required per level following 220 * 1.125^level (from experience.json). It branches from six root/path nodes: path_rogue, path_archer, path_arcane, path_protector, path_fire, and path_frost — the archetype entry points. From the node definitions (definitions.json), examples of real content include:

Rogue’s Path: +1 Physical Damage, +5% Haste.
Pyrotechnic Knowledge (fire path root): +1 Fire Power.
Keystone Fate Talents deep in the tree, e.g. Arcane Archmage (+6 Arcane Power, +25% Spell Critical Damage, but abandons other elements), High Priest (+10 Holy Power but −60% Physical Damage — a full healer respec), and others named fate_knowledge_of_runes_stars, fate_skellaks_blessing, fate_shadow_techniques, fate_sindorei_heritage, fate_decaying_devotion.
Big ascendancy abilities unlocked via keystones: ascendancyBoneArmor (taunt nearby enemies, gain a stacking bone-armor shield up to 6 layers, removed as you take damage), plus ascendancyRighteousShield, ascendancyRighteousHammers, ascendancyRapidfire, ascendancyDissonance, ascendancyCataclysm, ascendancySkywardSunder.
Passive nodes like passive_omnivampirism (+2% lifesteal, procs on melee/ranged/magic hits), passive_critical_thinking, passive_focus_zone, passive_empower, passive_skellaks_call.

Beyond the main tree, each legendary/artifact weapon in the pack gets its own dedicated skill tree, unlocked by obtaining and leveling that specific weapon: thunderwrath (12 nodes), fyralath (12), frostmourne (12), azhar (11), apophis (12), vaazkar (13), orion (19), ekavar_staff (19), supernova (9), ashedar_essence (9), ghaj (11), fury_of_a_thousand_fists (11), and skillet (0 nodes — present in config but not yet populated, a joke-weapon tree for “Granny’s Pan” that hasn’t been filled in). The FTB Quests “Artifact Reforging” chapter ties directly into these — quest lore describes Frostmourne as “a runic artifact infused with soulfrost magic… whoever wields it will become the ruler of the Death Knights,” A’zhar as a demon trapped in a scythe that “will try to betray you,” and Supernova as forged “from remnants of a dying star.” These trees are all textured under a custom prominent_talents: resource namespace, meaning the modpack authors built this content specifically for Prominence rather than using Puffish Skills’ defaults.
SimplySkills sets disableDefaultPuffishTrees=true in its own config, meaning it replaces whatever default trees Puffish Skills ships with its own per-class trees rather than adding to the prom tree — the two systems coexist as separate categories rather than merging.
Anticipated questions
What is Pufferfish’s Skills?
A generic, fully data-driven skill-tree engine that supplies the N-key Talent Tree UI, per-category XP/leveling, and node unlock logic. Every actual tree is authored as JSON under config/puffish_skills/categories/. It’s the mod behind the Talent Tree & Fate Talents system.
How big is the main tree, and what’s its level cap?
The main prom tree (“Talent Tree”) has 175 nodes and a level cap of 32, with XP per level following 220 * 1.125^level. There are 14 categories total defined in config.json.
What are the six archetype entry points?
The prom tree branches from six root/path nodes: path_rogue, path_archer, path_arcane, path_protector, path_fire, and path_frost — the archetype starting points. See Archetypes & Builds.
What are Fate Talents?
Keystone nodes deep in the tree with heavy trade-offs — e.g. Arcane Archmage (+6 Arcane Power, +25% Spell Critical Damage but abandons other elements) and High Priest (+10 Holy Power but −60% Physical Damage, a full healer respec).
Do legendary weapons get their own skill trees?
Yes — each legendary/artifact weapon gets its own dedicated tree, unlocked by obtaining and leveling that specific weapon: e.g. thunderwrath (12 nodes), frostmourne (12), orion (19), ekavar_staff (19), and even skillet (0 nodes — an unfinished joke tree for “Granny’s Pan”).
How does this coexist with SimplySkills?
SimplySkills sets disableDefaultPuffishTrees=true, so it replaces Puffish’s default trees with its own per-class trees rather than merging into the prom tree — the two run as separate categories.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/ReBalance.title: ReBalance
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/ReBalance.content:
ReBalance
A configurable player-damage-balancing mod by ElocinDev/Sweeney with three independent systems, all readable straight from this server’s rebalance.json5:

Dynamic Rebalance (enabled) — scales damage down the more hits you land in quick succession / the lower the target’s health gets, using an attack_speed_weight of 0.2, an 18.0 reduction amount, and a health threshold/minimum (1.0/5.0) so it tapers off rather than cutting damage on already-low-HP targets. should_ignore_first_hit is off, so it applies from the very first swing.
Global Reduction — a flat damage multiplier; present but disabled on this server (enable_global_reduction: false).
PvP Reduction — enabled, multiplying player-vs-player damage by 0.60 (a 40% PvP damage cut), independent of the PvE dynamic system.

This is the mechanism referenced by the “Combat tweaks” section of Core RPG & Combat Mods as one of the “damage math retuning” mods, working alongside Resistance Balancer to shape how punishing combat feels on this specific server rather than at the mod’s raw defaults.
Anticipated questions
What are ReBalance’s three systems?
Dynamic Rebalance, Global Reduction, and PvP Reduction — three independent damage-balancing systems, all configured in rebalance.json5.
What does Dynamic Rebalance do, and is it on?
It’s enabled here. It scales damage down the more hits you land in quick succession and the lower the target’s health gets, using an attack_speed_weight of 0.2 and an 18.0 reduction amount, with a health threshold/minimum (1.0/5.0) so it tapers off rather than punishing already-low-HP targets.
Does it reduce PvP damage?
Yes — PvP Reduction is enabled and multiplies player-vs-player damage by 0.60, a 40% PvP damage cut, independent of the PvE dynamic system.
Is the flat Global Reduction active?
No — Global Reduction (a flat damage multiplier) is present but disabled on this server (enable_global_reduction: false).
Does Dynamic Rebalance spare the first hit?
No — should_ignore_first_hit is off, so it applies from the very first swing. It works alongside Resistance Balancer to shape how punishing combat feels on this server.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Resistance-Ba.title: Resistance Balancer
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Resistance-Ba.content:
Resistance Balancer
A tiny, focused mod by ElocinDev that changes how the vanilla Resistance potion effect mitigates damage. By default Resistance is a flat 20%-per-level reduction in vanilla; this mod replaces that with either a configurable formula or a simpler percentile fallback.
This server ships the mod’s own documented default rather than a custom tweak: enable_custom_formula is false, so it falls back to percentile_reduction_fallback: 0.05 — each level of Resistance reduces damage by 5%, capping Resistance IV at a 20% reduction (identical to the mod’s stock example formula min(RESISTANCE / 4.0, 1.0) * 0.20, just expressed via the simpler per-level path instead of the custom-formula parser). The mod does support an arbitrary custom formula string (variable RESISTANCE) for servers that want a different curve, but that path isn’t in use here.
Anticipated questions
What does Resistance Balancer change?
How the vanilla Resistance potion effect mitigates damage. Vanilla gives a flat 20%-per-level reduction; this mod replaces that with either a configurable formula or a simpler percentile fallback.
What setup does this server use?
The mod’s documented default — enable_custom_formula is false, so it uses percentile_reduction_fallback: 0.05: each level of Resistance reduces damage by 5%.
How much does Resistance IV reduce damage here?
20% — capping at the same value as the mod’s stock example formula min(RESISTANCE / 4.0, 1.0) * 0.20, just reached via the simpler per-level path.
Can the curve be customized?
Yes — the mod supports an arbitrary custom formula string (variable RESISTANCE) for servers that want a different curve, but that path isn’t in use here.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Rogues--and--.title: Rogues & Warriors (RPG Series)
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Rogues--and--.content:
Rogues & Warriors (RPG Series)
The melee half of the archetype line, adding two Tier I books: the Rogue Handbook (Haste/Assassin utility kit) and Warrior’s Codex (bruiser/protector, “a great middle ground for slower Physical Damage builds” per the pack’s quest text). New weapon families back both — Daggers and Sickles for Rogue, Double Axes and Glaives for Warrior, all running the full material ladder from starter tiers through Netherite, Aeternium and Ruby. Matching armor sets exist too: Rogue/Assassin (up to Netherite) and Warrior/Berserker (up to Netherite). An Arms Dealer villager profession (with its own Arms Station workbench) sells related gear.
Rogue spells are stealth/burst tools: Slice & Dice is a stacking self-buff (attacks build stacks, up to a configured max, each adding damage), Shock Powder stuns nearby enemies, Shadowstep repositions you behind a target, and Vanish grants full stealth that breaks on any action or damage taken. Warrior spells are more control/sustain-oriented: Shattering Throw (weapon throw that also shreds target armor), Demoralizing Shout (AoE damage-reduction debuff plus minor damage), Charge (speed + knockback resistance, cleanses movement-impairing effects), and Whirlwind (channeled spin-to-win AoE).
rogues/tweaks.json shows this server has hand-tuned the numbers: Slice & Dice at 0.1 damage/stack up to 10 stacks, Stealth at -50% movement speed with a 0.1x visibility multiplier, Shattered Armor at -30%, Demoralizing Shout at -30% damage, Charge at +50% speed/+50% knockback resist — and it layers in ReBalance-style enchant scaling too: Sharpness (+8%/level), Smite (+12%/level) and Bane of Arthropods (+12%/level) are all explicitly re-enabled and rebalanced here rather than left at vanilla math.
Anticipated questions
What two archetype books does this mod add?
Two Tier I books — the Rogue Handbook (Haste/Assassin utility kit) and the Warrior’s Codex (bruiser/protector, described as a great middle ground for slower Physical Damage builds).
What new weapons and armor come with it?
Daggers and Sickles for Rogue, Double Axes and Glaives for Warrior — all running the full material ladder from starter tiers through Netherite, Aeternium and Ruby — plus matching Rogue/Assassin and Warrior/Berserker armor sets (up to Netherite). An Arms Dealer villager with an Arms Station workbench sells related gear.
What are the Rogue spells?
Stealth/burst tools: Slice & Dice (a stacking self-buff), Shock Powder (stuns nearby enemies), Shadowstep (repositions you behind a target), and Vanish (full stealth that breaks on any action or damage taken).
What are the Warrior spells?
Control/sustain tools: Shattering Throw (weapon throw that shreds target armor), Demoralizing Shout (AoE damage-reduction debuff plus minor damage), Charge (speed + knockback resistance, cleanses movement-impairing effects), and Whirlwind (channeled spin-to-win AoE).
How has this server tuned the numbers?
rogues/tweaks.json hand-tunes them: Slice & Dice at 0.1 damage/stack up to 10 stacks, Stealth at −50% movement speed with a 0.1x visibility multiplier, Shattered Armor at −30%, Demoralizing Shout at −30% damage, and Charge at +50% speed / +50% knockback resist.
Does it change enchantment scaling?
Yes — it layers in ReBalance-style enchant scaling: Sharpness (+8%/level), Smite (+12%/level) and Bane of Arthropods (+12%/level) are all explicitly re-enabled and rebalanced here rather than left at vanilla math.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Shield-API.content:
Shield API
A developer-facing library mod by TheRedBrain — “Creating shields with custom models was never easier!” It provides the framework other mods (armor/weapon mods in the pack that add their own themed shields, e.g. Paladins’ Kite Shields) use to register shields with bespoke models rather than reusing vanilla’s single shield mesh. Like RangedWeaponAPI, it has no player-facing config or in-game content of its own — it’s the invisible dependency that Shield Overhaul’s parry/bash mechanics and the pack’s various custom shield items sit on top of.

It’s a developer-facing library by TheRedBrain that provides the framework other mods use to register shields with custom models — “Creating shields with custom models was never easier!” — instead of reusing vanilla’s single shield mesh (e.g. Paladins’ Kite Shields).
Does it have any config or in-game content?

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Shield-Overha.title: Shield Overhaul
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Shield-Overha.content:
Shield Overhaul
Reworks vanilla shield-blocking into an active-defense system: instant shield raising, parrying, and bashing, built on top of Shield API. This server’s config (shield_overhaul/shield_overhaul.json) has all three enabled (enable_instant_shield_use, enable_parrying, enable_bashing), with concrete tuned numbers:

Parry — a 0.5s parry window, 2s cooldown, and a successful parry stuns the attacker for 1s. Arrow deflection requires a successful parry and multiplies deflected-arrow velocity by 1.0. Bosses are immune to the stun (bosses_immune_to_stun: true) so parrying doesn’t trivialize boss fights.
Bash — 5.0 base damage, 4s cooldown, 1s stun on hit, with a 1.5x reach multiplier and a bash_only_on_ground restriction.
Stun immunity — 5s grace period after being stunned, preventing permanent stun-lock.
Vigor talent scaling at +33% strength per level, and a Flameborn proc (25% chance, 3s burn) referenced in the config, implying at least one gear/enchant hook feeds bonus effects into shield bashing.

This is the mod behind “shield mechanics” in the Core RPG & Combat Mods overview, distinct from the purely cosmetic shield-model support Shield API provides.
Anticipated questions
What can I do with a shield beyond blocking?
On this server all three active-defense features are enabled: instant shield raising, parrying, and bashing. It reworks vanilla blocking into an active-defense system built on top of Shield API.
How does parrying work?
There’s a 0.5s parry window with a 2s cooldown, and a successful parry stuns the attacker for 1s. A successful parry can also deflect arrows (deflected-arrow velocity is multiplied by 1.0).
Can I parry-stun a boss?
No. Bosses are immune to the stun (bosses_immune_to_stun: true) so parrying doesn’t trivialize boss fights.
What does a shield bash do?
Bash deals 5.0 base damage with a 4s cooldown, applies a 1s stun on hit, and has a 1.5x reach multiplier. It’s restricted to the ground (bash_only_on_ground).
Can I be stun-locked forever?
No. After being stunned you get a 5s grace period of stun immunity, preventing permanent stun-lock.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Simply-Swords.title: Simply Swords
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Simply-Swords.content:
Simply Swords
Simply Swords is a full weapon-type expansion first, and a legendary-armory second. It adds fourteen new weapon classes — cutlass, rapier, glaive, warglaive, spear, sai, katana, claymore, longsword, twinblade, greathammer, greataxe, chakram, scythe, and halberd — each crafted in the standard iron/gold/diamond/netherite tiers plus a Runic tier above netherite. Weapon type genuinely changes the numbers (weapon_attributes.json5): claymores get +2 bonus damage, greataxes +3, greathammers +4, halberds +3, and scythes +1, while sais (-3) and rapiers/chakrams (-1) trade damage for other stats; longswords swing at -2.4 attack speed baseline. Runic weapons additionally socket a Runefused Gem (or Netherfused Gem for a rarer variant) that rolls one of a dozen-plus procs — Echo, Berserk, Onslaught, Nullification, Precise (30% chance), Mighty (30%), Stealthy (30%), Renewed, Accelerant, Spellshield (15%), Spellforged, Soulshock, and both a Spell/War “Battle Standard” banner effect — most of which are enabled on this server.
Above Runic sits a whole armory of unique, hand-named legendaries, each with a dedicated Quest Book entry and real lore text (from simply_swords.snbt). A sample of what’s actually in the pack:

The Watcher (a claymore) — “It watched a great Paladin slay a Beast. But he who kills cannot be far from a Beast himself.”
Brimstone Claymore — dragon-slaying flavor: “To slay a Dragon.”
Storm’s Edge / Stormbringer — a paired lightning duo: “Two Storms, chained together by a single Handle… Let the Land thunder with my Storm!”
Soulkeeper, Soulstealer, Soulrender, Soul Pyre — a themed set of soul-magnet blades (“Like a Magnet for Souls. Loves sewing them together as if they were Fabric.“)
Slumbering Lichblade → Waking Lichblade → Awakened Lichblade — an explicit three-stage upgrade chain culminating in “AT FULL POTENTIAL.”
Longsword of the Plague — cursed flavor: “The Blade’s inscription tells that the Title of Plaguelord was bestowed upon the poor soul that accepted it.”
Others found in-chapter: Bramblethorn, Watching Warglaive, Emberblade, Hearthflame, Twisted Blade, Frostfall, Molten Edge, Livyatan, Icewhisper, Arcanethyst, Thunderbrand, Mjolnir (Simply Swords’ own version, separate from the one in Marium’s Soulslike Weaponry), Shadowsting, Whisperwind, Emberlash, Waxweaver, Hiveheart, Star’s Edge, Wickpiercer, Dreadtide, Tempest, Flamewind, Ribboncleaver, and Caelestis. There’s also a Dormant Relic → Tainted Relic / Righteous Relic branching relic that the quest explicitly frames as a moral choice: “Dormant Power Lies Beneath… Tainted and Twisted… All Mighty!”

Every unique above is individually toggleable in simplyswords_extra/loot_config.json5 and is enabled on this server, dropping from world loot at configured rarity weights (standardLootTableWeight: 0.021, down to uniqueLootTableWeight: 0.0055 for the named legendaries — Runic sits at 0.016). Runic weapons also carry their own proc-effect layer (runic_effects.json5) — Freeze, Shielding, Stoneskin, Swiftness, Trailblaze, Weaken, Frost Ward, Wildfire, Momentum, Imbued — each with its own chance/duration, e.g. Freeze at 15% for 120 ticks, Swiftness at 15% for 300 ticks. There’s also a separate balance-tweak addon jar, Simply Swords Battle Standard Tweaks, installed alongside it — not covered in this note, but it retunes the banner/standard abilities (haste amplifiers, AoE radii) referenced in battle_standard_tweaks.json.
Anticipated questions
How many weapon types does Simply Swords add, and does the type matter?
Over fifteen classes (cutlass, rapier, glaive, warglaive, spear, sai, katana, claymore, longsword, twinblade, greathammer, greataxe, chakram, scythe, halberd). Type genuinely changes the numbers — greathammers get +4 bonus damage, greataxes and halberds +3, claymores +2, while sais (-3) and rapiers/chakrams (-1) trade damage for speed or reach. See Better Combat for how these actually swing.
What is the Runic tier?
A crafted tier above netherite. Runic weapons carry a socket that takes a Runefused Gem (or the rarer Netherfused Gem), which rolls one of a dozen-plus procs — Echo, Berserk, Onslaught, Precise, Mighty, Spellshield, Soulshock and more — on top of a separate proc-effect layer (Freeze, Swiftness, Stoneskin, Wildfire…).
How do I make the gems?
Melt down unique weapons into Empowered Remnants. Combine a Runic Tablet + an Empowered Remnant in a Smithing Table for a Runefused Gem; combine an Empowered Remnant + a Netherite Ingot for a Netherfused Gem. Then click the gem to identify which power you rolled.
Where do the unique legendaries come from?
World loot and strong enemies — the quest book lists real drop chances: Obsidilith 40%, the Ender Dragon 35%, Night Lich 30%, Nether Gauntlet 25%, Conjunctivius 15%, Decaying King 15%. Every named unique is enabled on this server and drops at low rarity weights (uniques as low as 0.0055), each with its own Quest Book entry and lore.
Where does Simply Swords sit in gear progression?
Runic weapons and the named uniques sit above netherite, and every drop still runs through Gear Rarity & Reforging for rarity rolls and reforging.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/SimplySkills.title: SimplySkills
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/SimplySkills.content:
SimplySkills
SimplySkills is “a comprehensive skill tree mod with a focus on combat specialisations” that builds its own content on top of the Pufferfish’s Skills API (it depends on puffish_skills >=0.12.0 and puffish_attributes >=0.4.0) rather than adding to the pack’s prom Talent Tree. Its config explicitly sets disableDefaultPuffishTrees: true, meaning it swaps in a completely separate set of custom trees: config/simplyskills/ ships one JSON5 file per specialisation — Warrior, Ranger, Wayfarer, Berserker, Wizard, Spellblade, Initiate, Cleric, Crusader, Necromancer, and Rogue — alongside general.json5 (shared systems) and misc.json5.
Mechanically it adds real combat verbs and buff/debuff effects rather than just flat stats: status effects like Berserking (stacking offensive buffs per hit), Bloodthirsty (heal on kill), Evasion, Stealth (total invisibility, breaks on dealing/taking damage), Barrier (negate next hit), and elemental “Attunement” stacks (Arcane/Soul/Holy/Fire/Frost/Lightning, each +2% of that spell-power type per stack) — signalling deep integration with the Spell Engine/Spell Power mod family it depends on. Warrior’s config alone (warrior.json5) exposes over 20 tunable passives: Armor Mastery (10% proc chance above a 15-armor threshold), Shield Mastery, Rebuke (25% chance, applies Weakness), Spellbreaker (25% chance to explode incoming spell projectiles in a 4-block radius), Goliath (fall-distance-based bonus), Death Defy (a last-stand mechanic below 30% HP), Frenzy, and Twinstrike/Swordfall procs.
general.json5 also reveals a Dynamic Adaptive Scaling (DAS) system — hostile mobs within a 64-block radius get their Health/Attack/Armor/Toughness/Speed/Knockback-Resistance scaled up based on nearby players’ skill investment (e.g. DASHealth: 1.6 with a 1.085 per-point multiplier) — and a Dynamic Difficulty Reduction (DDR) system for softening fights when a player’s HP and gear fall behind, though DDR is disabled on this server (enableDDR: false) while DAS is enabled (enableDAS: true). Ascendancy (a second, more powerful ability tier per specialisation) is also enabled (enableAscendancy: true), and tree resets are allowed without XP loss on death (treeResetOnDeath: false).
Anticipated questions
What specialisations does SimplySkills add?
It ships one custom skill tree per specialisation: Warrior, Ranger, Wayfarer, Berserker, Wizard, Spellblade, Initiate, Cleric, Crusader, Necromancer, and Rogue, alongside shared general.json5 and misc.json5 files.
Does this use the same trees as the pack’s prom Talent Tree?
No. It builds on Pufferfish’s Skills API (see Pufferfish’s Skills) and sets disableDefaultPuffishTrees: true, swapping in a completely separate set of custom trees rather than adding to the pack’s prom Talent Tree & Fate Talents.
Is this just flat stat bonuses?
No — it adds real combat verbs and buff/debuff effects like Berserking (stacking offensive buffs per hit), Bloodthirsty (heal on kill), Evasion, Stealth (total invisibility that breaks on dealing/taking damage), Barrier (negate next hit), and elemental “Attunement” stacks.
Do enemies get tougher as I level up?
Yes. The Dynamic Adaptive Scaling (DAS) system is enabled — hostile mobs within a 64-block radius get Health/Attack/Armor/Toughness/Speed/Knockback-Resistance scaled up based on nearby players’ skill investment. The opposite Dynamic Difficulty Reduction (DDR) system is disabled on this server.
What is Ascendancy?
A second, more powerful ability tier per specialisation. It’s enabled on this server (enableAscendancy: true).
Do I lose my skill tree if I die?
No. Tree resets are allowed without XP loss on death (treeResetOnDeath: false).

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Spellblade-Ne.title: Spellblade Next
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Spellblade-Ne.content:
Spellblade Next
Real name “Spellblades and Such” — the magical-melee hybrid mod behind the pack’s Spellblade archetype. Adds elemental Spellblades and Claymores (Arcane, Frost, Fire, each with an upgraded named variant — Crystal Cutlass, Glacial Gladius, Flaming Falchion), matching casting Orbs, and a Runeblaze Rifle for a gun-caster variant. Its core hook, per its own in-game tooltip, is the Spellblade passive: “Upon casting a spell with this Spellblade, you gain Strength and Haste equal to a quarter of your power relating to the spell’s school, for up to however long the cooldown of the spell is” — i.e. casting temporarily buffs your melee.
It’s also where the pack’s two Tier II “tank oath” books actually live (despite being grouped with Paladins in the quest book): Oath of Defiance (Defiant Stance passively stacks self-heals off incoming damage, active version pounds the shield for AoE armor-based damage; Bolster stacks armor; Shield Shatter throws the shield) and Oath of Vengeance (built around a stacking Fervor resource — Overpower, Soul of Vengeance, and staff-based spins like Cudgel Strike / Vaulting Slam / Monkey King’s Reckoning). Beyond those, it adds several Tier III evolution books referenced in the quest chapter: Phoenix Rites (fire, self-burning “Phoenix Curse” DoT engine, Phoenix Dive), Echoes Unleashed (arcane, stacking “Unleash” that repeats your spells), and Deathchill Tome (frost, “chill faster / heat up slower” passive with a heavy debuff). A Thesis of Awakening mechanic lets you dedicate to a single spell for +50% spell power/haste on it, and Tabula Rasa + Spell Oils let you rebind spells onto arbitrary casting items.
The mod also ships its own light invasion/boss content: a Hexblade module that can spawn a Magus boss and a Hexblade Portal, an optional Glass Ocean area with weather changes on phase-end and a horde-spawn toggle (all present but tuned down on this server — spawnmodifier 0.6, magisterXP 0, horde off). Depends on Extra RPG Attributes for its “power converted to attack damage” style attributes (Fire/Frost/Arcane Power → Attack Damage and back), visible directly in its lang file.
Anticipated questions
What archetype is this mod behind, and what does it add?
It’s the real “Spellblades and Such” mod, the magical-melee hybrid behind the pack’s Spellblade archetype (see Archetypes & Builds). It adds elemental Spellblades and Claymores (Arcane, Frost, Fire — with upgraded variants Crystal Cutlass, Glacial Gladius, Flaming Falchion), casting Orbs, and a Runeblaze Rifle gun-caster variant.
What is the Spellblade passive?
Per its in-game tooltip: casting a spell with a Spellblade grants you Strength and Haste equal to a quarter of your power in that spell’s school, lasting up to the spell’s cooldown. Casting temporarily buffs your melee.
Where do the Tier II tank oath books live?
Here, despite being grouped with Paladins in the quest book. Oath of Defiance (Defiant Stance self-heals off incoming damage, Bolster stacks armor, Shield Shatter throws the shield) and Oath of Vengeance (a stacking Fervor resource with Overpower, Soul of Vengeance, and staff spins).
What Tier III evolution books does it add?
Phoenix Rites (fire, self-burning “Phoenix Curse” DoT engine), Echoes Unleashed (arcane, stacking “Unleash” that repeats your spells), and Deathchill Tome (frost, “chill faster / heat up slower” with a heavy debuff).
What do Thesis of Awakening and Tabula Rasa do?
Thesis of Awakening lets you dedicate to a single spell for +50% spell power/haste on it. Tabula Rasa plus Spell Oils let you rebind spells onto arbitrary casting items.
Is the Hexblade/Magus boss content active on this server?
It’s present but tuned down: spawnmodifier 0.6, magisterXP 0, and the horde-spawn toggle is off.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Tierify.title: Tierify
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Tierify.content:
Tierify
Tierify (mod id tiered) “adds quality tiers to armor, weapons and tools” — a separate, simpler rarity ladder than Zenith Renewed’s affix system, layered on top of it. Tierify’s own tiers are Common → Uncommon → Rare → Epic → Legendary → Mythic (confirmed directly from its lang file, assets/tiered/lang/en_us.json, which defines these six quality labels across every gear category it touches: armor, tools, melee, ranged, fishing, shields, elytra, and staff/wand items). This is the ladder the “Gear Rarity & Reforging” system note describes as the pack’s overall progression — Tierify supplies the top tier (Legendary) that Zenith’s own guidebook doesn’t have, since Zenith’s native rarity system tops out at Mythic.
On this server, config/tierify-common.json5 enables Tierify quality modifiers on loot containers, entity equipment, crafted items, and merchant/villager items, and defines a three-tier reforging-material system tied to specific ores:

Tier I — Limestone (Overworld, crafted from Limestone Blocks or Diorite Blocks): can reforge to Common/Uncommon/Rare/Epic.
Tier II — Pyrite (Nether; crafted from Pyrite Dust or smelted from Ancient Debris): reforges to Uncommon/Rare/Epic/Legendary.
Tier III — Galena: reforges to Rare/Epic/Legendary/Mythic.

Reforge odds are tunable via reforgeModifier (0.9, decreasing the chance of rolling the best available quality), plus small positive nudges from levelzReforgeModifier (+0.01 per smithing level) and luckReforgeModifier (+0.02 per luck point). The client config (tierify-client.json5) confirms the in-game Anvil screen gets a dedicated reforging tab, tooltips show the tier, and item names get a quality “plate” overlay. The FTB Quests “Reforging” chapter frames this as a full progression arc, capped by an “Eternal Challenge” advancement for reforging one hundred Mythic items — titled “Become a Mythic Blacksmith.”
Anticipated questions
What are Tierify’s quality tiers?
Six: Common → Uncommon → Rare → Epic → Legendary → Mythic, applied across armor, tools, melee, ranged, fishing, shields, elytra, and staff/wand items.
How is this different from Zenith Renewed’s rarity?
Tierify (mod id tiered) is a separate, simpler rarity ladder layered on top of Zenith Renewed’s affix system. It supplies the top Legendary tier that Zenith’s own ladder lacks (Zenith tops out at Mythic). See Gear Rarity & Reforging.
How do I reforge gear, and what materials do I need?
There’s a three-tier reforging-material system tied to ores: Tier I — Limestone (Overworld) reforges to Common/Uncommon/Rare/Epic; Tier II — Pyrite (Nether, also smeltable from Ancient Debris) reforges to Uncommon/Rare/Epic/Legendary; Tier III — Galena reforges to Rare/Epic/Legendary/Mythic.
Can I improve my reforge odds?
Yes, slightly. reforgeModifier (0.9) decreases the chance of the best available quality, but levelzReforgeModifier adds +0.01 per smithing level and luckReforgeModifier adds +0.02 per luck point.
Where do I reforge in-game?
The Anvil screen gets a dedicated reforging tab; tooltips show the tier and item names get a quality “plate” overlay.
Is there an endgame reforging goal?
Yes — an “Eternal Challenge” advancement for reforging one hundred Mythic items, titled “Become a Mythic Blacksmith.”

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Transmog.title: Transmog
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Transmog.content:
Transmog
Lets you reskin any weapon or armor piece to look like a different item without touching its actual stats. The in-game Quest Book frames it as its own school of magic: “Transmogrification is a type of magic that allows you to change the shape of any object without altering its function, letting you to mask your items into another, including weapons and armors. It does not give any benefit aside from being purely cosmetic.”
Mechanically, you craft a Transmogrification Table and power it with Amethyst — every reskin costs amethyst, but no items are consumed, and you must actually own the item whose appearance you want to copy (so you can’t fake owning a Frostmourne skin without one). A second trick unlocked via the quest chapter uses a Void Fragment as the transmog material to hide a piece entirely — the “Illusion of Nothing,” useful for players who want invisible boots/helmets without losing the enchantments underneath. Server config (config/transmog.json) has rendering set to IN_WORLD (other players see your transmogged look, not just you), tooltip detail set to FULL, and PvP-disable duration left at 0 (transmog isn’t suppressed after combat).
This exists specifically because the pack’s other weapon mods — Simply Swords, Marium’s Soulslike Weaponry, and the S’kellak’s Forge legendary artifact weapons — hand out gear with strong, very distinct stats attached to very distinct models. Transmog is the release valve: keep the strongest weapon’s stats, wear the look you actually want.
Anticipated questions
Does transmog change my item’s stats?
No. It reskins any weapon or armor piece to look like a different item without touching its actual stats — purely cosmetic, as the Quest Book itself states.
How do I transmog an item, and what does it cost?
Craft a Transmogrification Table and power it with Amethyst. Every reskin costs amethyst, but no items are consumed. You must actually own the item whose appearance you want to copy.
Can I make a piece of gear invisible?
Yes. A quest-chapter trick uses a Void Fragment as the transmog material to hide a piece entirely — the “Illusion of Nothing” — useful for invisible boots or helmets without losing the enchantments underneath.
Do other players see my transmogged look?
Yes. Server config sets rendering to IN_WORLD, so other players see your transmogged appearance, not just you. Transmog also isn’t suppressed after combat (PvP-disable duration is 0).
Why does the pack include this?
Because its weapon mods — Simply Swords, Marium’s Soulslike Weaponry, and S’kellak’s Forge legendary artifacts — hand out gear with strong, very distinct stats on very distinct models. Transmog lets you keep the strongest weapon’s stats while wearing the look you want.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Trinkets-and-.title: Trinkets and Things
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Trinkets-and-.content:
Trinkets and Things
Two jars covering one lineage. Trinkets (by Emi/C4) is the original data-driven accessory-slot framework this pack still runs natively — it predates and inspired Accessories, and defines its own default slots via datapack: head/hat, head/face, chest/necklace, chest/back, chest/cape, hand/glove, hand/ring, offhand/glove, offhand/ring, legs/belt, and feet/shoes + feet/aglet. It ships no items of its own — it’s pure plumbing, the same role Accessories plays for newer mods, just for older Trinkets-native content (Artifacts itself depends directly on trinkets, not just Accessories).
Things (by glisco) is the addon that actually fills those Trinkets slots with real items, and it’s a lot more colorful than the “invisible plumbing” framing suggests. Standouts on this server: Hardening Catalyst (“apply in an anvil to make any item unbreakable”) — the exact item the S’kellak’s Forge questline requires to make legendary artifact weapons unbreakable, tying Things directly into the Core RPG artifact-reforging system; Displacement Tome, a rechargeable multi-destination teleport tool charged with Ender Pearls; Ender Pouch (portable ender chest access); Moss Necklace (Regeneration II in light — tuned to level 2 in config/things.json5), Mining Gloves (permanent Haste II), Riot Gauntlet (permanent Strength), Hades Crystal (permanent Fire Resistance, stacks with the Enchanted Wax Gland), Rabbit Foot Charm (Jump Boost II), Broken Watch (+50% status effect duration), Item Magnet, Container Key (lock/unlock containers), and Socks, a wearable with five selectable speed tiers up to “Usain Bolt” and a toggleable Jump Boost. Things also adds an Agglomeration system for merging two same-slot trinkets into one item, though this pack has it explicitly disabled (enableAgglomeration: false).
Anticipated questions
What’s the difference between Trinkets and Things?
Trinkets (by Emi/C4) is the data-driven accessory-slot framework — pure plumbing that defines the slots (head, face, necklace, back, cape, glove, ring, belt, shoes, and more) but ships no items. Things (by glisco) is the addon that actually fills those slots with real wearable items.
How do I make an item unbreakable?
Use the Hardening Catalyst (“apply in an anvil to make any item unbreakable”). It’s the exact item the S’kellak’s Forge questline requires to make legendary Artifacts weapons unbreakable.
What standout accessories does Things add?
Highlights include Displacement Tome (rechargeable multi-destination teleport, charged with Ender Pearls), Ender Pouch (portable ender chest), Moss Necklace (Regeneration II in light), Mining Gloves (permanent Haste II), Riot Gauntlet (permanent Strength), Hades Crystal (permanent Fire Resistance), Rabbit Foot Charm (Jump Boost II), Broken Watch (+50% status effect duration), and Socks (five selectable speed tiers up to “Usain Bolt”).
Can I merge two trinkets into one?
Not on this server. Things’ Agglomeration system for merging two same-slot trinkets is explicitly disabled (enableAgglomeration: false).
Why run Trinkets when the pack also has Accessories?
Trinkets is the original framework this pack still runs natively for older Trinkets-native content — Artifacts itself depends directly on trinkets, not just Accessories. See Accessories Trinkets Compat Layer.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Wizards-(RPG-.title: Wizards (RPG Series)
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Wizards-(RPG-.content:
Wizards (RPG Series)
The Elemental Mage archetype mod. Adds three Tier I Tomes obtained from the Spell Binding Table — Tome of Arcane, Tome of Fire, Tome of Frost — each its own ranged-caster sub-path with matching Wands, Staves (including Netherite and gemstone-tier Crystal/Ruby/Smaragdant staves), and full Wizard/Arcane/Fire/Frost robe sets (hat, top, bottom, boots, up to Netherite). A Wizard Merchant villager profession sells related gear.
Each school plays differently: Arcane stacks Arcane Charge off Arcane Bolt/Missiles/Blast and dumps it with Arcane Beam or a forward Blink for burst; Fire layers Scorch, Fireball, a channeled Fire Breath cone, area Meteors, and a persistent Wall of Flames for sustained damage; Frost kites with Frost Shard/Frostbolt (which ricochets between targets), locks enemies down with Frost Nova → Frozen (immobile, extra-vulnerable to frost follow-up), and can go defensive with Frost Shield or ultimate with Blizzard. The pack’s own quest book explicitly calls Fire “high crit chance,” Frost “constant/quick damage with crowd control,” and Arcane the biggest single hits.
On this server wizards/tweaks.json only tunes arcane_charge_damage_per_stack (0.15) beyond the defaults — the class is otherwise stock. Per the e_spell_books quest chapter, Wizards’ three Tomes are the Tier I feed-in for the Tier III Astral Invocations hybrid book (Runic Invocations / Astral Magic), which blends all three schools via Astral Power into the hardest, most build-defining spellbook in the pack (39 possible spells).
Anticipated questions
What archetype is this, and how do I start?
It’s the Elemental Mage archetype (see Archetypes & Builds). You start with one of three Tier I Tomes obtained from the Spell Binding Table: Tome of Arcane, Tome of Fire, or Tome of Frost, each its own ranged-caster sub-path with matching Wands, Staves, and robe sets.
How do the three schools play differently?
Arcane stacks Arcane Charge and dumps it with Arcane Beam or Blink for burst (the biggest single hits). Fire layers Scorch, Fireball, Fire Breath, Meteors, and Wall of Flames for sustained damage (high crit chance). Frost kites with Frost Shard/Frostbolt, locks enemies down with Frost Nova → Frozen, and defends with Frost Shield or Blizzard (constant/quick damage with crowd control).
Where do I buy Wizard gear?
A Wizard Merchant villager profession sells related gear.
Is the Wizard class rebalanced on this server?
Barely. wizards/tweaks.json only tunes arcane_charge_damage_per_stack (0.15) beyond the defaults — the class is otherwise stock.
What do the three Tomes lead into?
They’re the Tier I feed-in for the Tier III Astral Invocations hybrid book, which blends all three schools via Astral Power into the hardest, most build-defining spellbook in the pack (39 possible spells).

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Zenith-Attrib.title: Zenith Attributes Renewed
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Zenith-Attrib.content:
Zenith Attributes Renewed
Zenith Attributes Renewed (mod id zenith_attributes) is described by its own fabric.mod.json as simply “the core attribute engine for Zenith Renewed” — it is plumbing, not a content mod in its own right. It bundles several sub-libraries (AdditionalEntityAttributes, attributes, cardinal-components, PlayerAbilityLib, reach-entity-attributes) that give Minecraft’s attribute system the extra hooks Zenith Renewed’s affixes need (armor pierce/shred, arrow velocity/damage, dodge chance, cold damage, current-HP-based damage, draw speed, etc.).
config/zenith_attributes.cfg mostly consists of a large “Hidden Attributes” list — attributes contributed by other mods (Additional Entity Attributes, Eternal Attributes, Estrogen, Obscure API, Reach Entity Attributes, More RPG Classes, Tierify, Thermoo, and more) that are deliberately hidden from the in-game Attributes GUI so the player-facing stat screen doesn’t get cluttered. This confirms Zenith Attributes Renewed acts as a shared attribute clearinghouse for the whole modpack’s RPG-stat layer, not just for Zenith Renewed’s own gear. The GUI itself (toggleable, on by default) and icon-aware sorting of attribute names are its only other player-visible features.
Anticipated questions
Is this a content mod?
No. Per its own fabric.mod.json it’s “the core attribute engine for Zenith Renewed” — pure plumbing, not a content mod in its own right.
What does it actually provide?
It bundles sub-libraries (AdditionalEntityAttributes, attributes, cardinal-components, PlayerAbilityLib, reach-entity-attributes) that give Minecraft’s attribute system the extra hooks Zenith Renewed’s affixes need — armor pierce/shred, arrow velocity/damage, dodge chance, cold damage, current-HP-based damage, draw speed, and more.
Why are some attributes hidden from the Attributes GUI?
Its config keeps a large “Hidden Attributes” list — attributes contributed by other mods (Additional Entity Attributes, Eternal Attributes, Estrogen, Obscure API, Reach Entity Attributes, More RPG Classes, Tierify, Thermoo, and more) — deliberately hidden so the player-facing stat screen doesn’t get cluttered. This makes it a shared attribute clearinghouse for the whole modpack’s RPG-stat layer, not just Zenith’s own gear.
What can I see or toggle as a player?
The Attributes GUI itself (toggleable, on by default) and icon-aware sorting of attribute names are its only player-visible features. See Combat & Stats.

Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Zenith-Renewe.title: Zenith Renewed
Mods/Core-RPG--and--Combat/Zenith-Renewe.content:
Zenith Renewed
Zenith Renewed (mod id zenith) is a Fabric port of Apotheosis, and it is the mod that actually runs the pack’s gear-rarity/affix system. It overhauls enchanting, adds “affix items” (gear with rolled stat bonuses and special effects), gem sockets, and a Reforging Table for re-rolling those affixes. On this server the Adventure, Spawner, and Village modules are disabled (config/zenith/zenith.cfg: Enable Adventure Module=false, Enable Spawner Module=false, Enable Village Module=false) while the Enchantment, Potion, and Garden modules are enabled — so Apotheosis’s boss/dungeon-spawner/village-trading features are off, but its enchanting rework and the affix-item/gem/reforging pipeline are live.
Zenith’s own rarity ladder (per its in-game guidebook, the “Chronicle of Shadows”) has 5 tiers: Common → Uncommon → Rare → Epic → Mythic (no “Legendary” — that name belongs to Tierify’s separate ladder). Each rarity gates how many stat affixes, special-effect affixes, and gem sockets an item can roll: Common gets one stat bonus; Uncommon gets two stats and possibly a socket; Rare gets three stats plus a special effect, a socket, and a small durability bonus; Epic gets up to four stats, two effects, and two sockets; Mythic tops out at four stats, two-to-three effects, and three sockets plus a significant durability bonus. Special-effect affixes (“Rare+ only”) range from combat procs to utility — examples pulled from the lang file: Vampiric (lifesteal on hit), Thunderstruck (attacks deal AoE lightning damage to nearby enemies), Cleaving (chance to hit extra nearby enemies), Executing (instantly kills enemies below a % HP threshold), Telepathic (drops teleport straight to your inventory), and Festive (chance for a slain enemy to become a “Loot Piñata”). Gems (Cracked/Chipped/Flawed/[blank]/Flawless/Perfect quality prefixes, i.e. common→ancient) socket into gear via a Smithing Table and provide their own bonus, including boss/dimension-themed gems like the Gem of the Ravenous Blood Lord (Nether) and Endersurge Gem (End).
Reforging uses a Simple Reforging Table (up to Rare rarity) or an upgraded Reforging Table (Epic+), fed with rarity-tier materials (Mysterious Scrap Metal → Timeworn Fabric → Luminous Crystal Shard → Arcane Sands → Godforged Pearl → Manifestation of Infinity, for Common through Ancient) plus a Sigil of Rebirth as fuel; it offers three possible new affix rolls per attempt, similar to an enchanting table. Other utility items include the Sigil of Socketing (adds a socket), Sigil of Withdrawal (strips all gems), and Sigil of Unnaming (removes the affix name). Zenith Attributes Renewed supplies the underlying attribute framework this whole system runs on.
Anticipated questions
What is Zenith Renewed?
A Fabric port of Apotheosis (mod id zenith), and the mod that actually runs the pack’s gear-rarity/affix system. It overhauls enchanting and adds affix items, gem sockets, and a Reforging Table. See Gear Rarity & Reforging.
Which Apotheosis modules are active on this server?
The Enchantment, Potion, and Garden modules are enabled; the Adventure, Spawner, and Village modules are disabled — so its enchanting rework and the affix/gem/reforging pipeline are live, but boss/dungeon-spawner/village-trading features are off.
What is Zenith’s rarity ladder?
Five tiers: Common → Uncommon → Rare → Epic → Mythic (no “Legendary” — that belongs to Tierify’s separate ladder). Rarity gates how many stat affixes, special-effect affixes, and gem sockets an item can roll, from Common (one stat) up to Mythic (four stats, two-to-three effects, three sockets, big durability bonus).
What are special-effect affixes?
Rare+ only affixes ranging from combat procs to utility — examples include Vampiric (lifesteal), Thunderstruck (AoE lightning), Cleaving (hit extra enemies), Executing (instant-kill below a % HP), Telepathic (teleport drops to inventory), and Festive (chance for a “Loot Piñata”).
How do gems and sockets work?
Gems come in quality prefixes (Cracked/Chipped/Flawed/[blank]/Flawless/Perfect, i.e. common→ancient) and socket into gear via a Smithing Table, providing their own bonus — including boss/dimension-themed gems like the Gem of the Ravenous Blood Lord (Nether) and Endersurge Gem (End).
How does reforging work?
Use a Simple Reforging Table (up to Rare) or an upgraded Reforging Table (Epic+), fed with rarity-tier materials (Mysterious Scrap Metal → Timeworn Fabric → Luminous Crystal Shard → Arcane Sands → Godforged Pearl → Manifestation of Infinity) plus a Sigil of Rebirth as fuel. It offers three possible new affix rolls per attempt.
What do the other Sigils do?
Sigil of Socketing adds a socket, Sigil of Withdrawal strips all gems, and Sigil of Unnaming removes the affix name.

Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs.content:
Creatures, Bosses & Mobs
Bosses generally have a recommended player level — check the quest before engaging. See Progression & Level Caps.
Bosses of Mass Destruction
Genuinely high-threat optional bosses for when you’ve outgrown everything else — built to be fought with real endgame gear, not stumbled into.
Mutant Monsters
Twisted, oversized versions of familiar mobs — a solid step up in danger from vanilla enemies.
Mobs of Mythology
A whole cast of mythological creatures for variety in what you’re fighting.
Friends & Foes
The mobs that got voted down (or forgotten) in Mojang’s old Mob Votes, expanded into fuller additions.
Naturalist
New ambient wildlife with real behavior — makes the Overworld feel more alive outside of combat.
Mythic Mounts — rideable flying/ground creatures
The pack’s dedicated tamable-mount mod. Confirmed flying mounts: Dragon (health 40 base / rarest, subterranean spawn, hostile until tamed with gold/diamond/emerald, biggest stats + 9-slot storage), Griffon (health 35, common in mountain biomes, tames on rabbit/mutton, peaceful), Nether Bat (health 25, Nether-only, hostile until tamed), Żar-ptak “Firebird” (health 20, rare village-adjacent spawn, tames on golden apple — note: its in-game display name is Polish for “Firebird,” which is why it looks like it starts with “Z”), Giant Moth (health 10, fragile). NOT flyers despite appearances: Courier Bird (too heavy to fly, runs instead) and Colelytra. Also includes non-flying mounts: Acencia (climbing cat), Archelon (giant sea turtle), Geckotoa/Riding Lizard (ground lizards), Dire Wolf, Nightmare (hostile Nether fire-steed).

Summoning Staff (2 Feathers + Ender Pearl / Stick + Name Tag / Stick + Bell) links to a tamed mount on right-click, then recalls it to you instantly from any distance — the fix for a flying mount that’s wandered off. Flying mounts also simply won’t take off while leashed.
All mount base stats (health/speed/attack/taming items/spawn biomes) are configured server-side in MythicMountsConfig.json and can be looked up precisely rather than guessed.

Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Advent.title: AdventureZ
Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Advent.content:
AdventureZ
AdventureZ (v1.4.20, by Globox_Z) is a large exploration-and-monsters mod that ships its own in-game Patchouli guidebook covering roughly thirty new creatures, bosses, and items. Its cast spans overworld wildlife (Deer, Iguana, Mammoth, Desert Rhino, Enderwarthog), Nether threats (Piglin Beast, Blaze Guardian, Shaman, Orc), and a set of structured end-game encounters: the Amethyst Golem (spawns from generating geodes), the Blackstone Golem, The Eye, and a tameable/rideable Dragon.
The two headline bosses are wired into this pack’s level-gated boss roster: the Blackstone Golem at character level 25 and The Eye at level 50. Per the guidebook’s own lore text, the Blackstone Golem is “the most deadliest creature in the world of Minecraft” — summoned at a Golem Altar, and on death it splits into smaller Mini Blackstone Golems that can subsequently be found wandering basalt deltas. The Eye “will drain any energy you got until you are a dead corpse” and is summoned at a dedicated shrine; killing it grants a “fame” effect required to hatch the mod’s signature Dragon egg (built in a nest at the player’s base, fed Orc skin or raw meat to grow through two size stages, eventually saddleable and — once large enough — capable of carrying a chest and breathing fire).
This server’s adventurez.json5 leaves most spawn weights at their defaults but deliberately disables two mobs outright — the Nightmare (nightmare_spawn_weight: 0) and the Enderwarthog (enderwarthog_spawn_weight: 0) — while keeping golem summoning, Eye summoning, dragon hatching, and the various loot/enchant tooltip features all enabled. (Note: this pack’s own “Nightmare” fire-steed is actually supplied by Mythic Mounts, not AdventureZ — the two mods happen to share the name for unrelated mobs, which is presumably why this config disables AdventureZ’s version.)
Anticipated questions
Q: What level should I be before fighting AdventureZ’s bosses?
A: This pack gates the Blackstone Golem at character level 25 and The Eye at level 50 (soft requirements, not hard-blocked). See Progression & Level Caps.
Q: How do I get the tameable Dragon?
A: Kill The Eye to gain a “fame” effect required to hatch the Dragon egg; build a nest at your base and feed the hatchling Orc skin or raw meat to grow it through two size stages, until it’s saddleable and — once large enough — can carry a chest and breathe fire.
Q: What happens when I kill the Blackstone Golem?
A: It splits into smaller Mini Blackstone Golems, which can afterward be found wandering basalt deltas. It’s summoned at a Golem Altar.
Q: Why can’t I find the Nightmare or Enderwarthog from this mod?
A: This server’s adventurez.json5 disables both (nightmare_spawn_weight: 0, enderwarthog_spawn_weight: 0). The pack’s Nightmare fire-steed instead comes from Mythic Mounts.

Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Beekee.title: Beekeeper Hut
Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Beekee.content:
Beekeeper Hut
Beekeeper Hut (v2.0.1, by Faboslav) is the second official Friends & Foes addon in this pack, again registering directly under the friendsandfoes namespace instead of its own. It adds a small generated structure — a beekeeper’s hut, built from multiple wall/roof/base-plate NBT pieces and fenced with moobloom-flower decoration — populated with a bee, a villager (the addon-enabled Beekeeper profession from Friends & Foes), and, fittingly, a Moobloom, plus its own loot-barrel table. This gives Friends & Foes’ beekeeper villager profession an actual place to spawn and be found in the world, rather than existing only as a profession players could theoretically assign.
This server’s friendsandfoes.json (the shared config file both Friends & Foes addons read from) has enableBeekeeperVillagerProfession, generateBeekeeperAreaStructure, and a beekeeperAreaStructureWeight of 2 all enabled, so the hut generates naturally in the world rather than needing to be found via a separate spawn mechanic.
Anticipated questions
Q: Where does the Beekeeper villager profession come from?
A: It’s the Beekeeper profession from Friends & Foes, enabled here via enableBeekeeperVillagerProfession; the hut gives it an actual place to spawn and be found.
Q: Does the beekeeper hut generate naturally in the world?
A: Yes — generateBeekeeperAreaStructure is on with a beekeeperAreaStructureWeight of 2, so it generates naturally rather than needing a separate spawn mechanic.
Q: What will I find inside a beekeeper hut?
A: A bee, a villager with the Beekeeper profession, and a Moobloom, plus its own loot-barrel table — built from wall/roof/base-plate pieces fenced with moobloom-flower decoration.

Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Bosses.title: Bosses of Mass Destruction
Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Bosses.content:
Bosses of Mass Destruction
Bosses of Mass Destruction (BOMD, v1.7.5-1.20.1, by Barribob — still tagged “Beta”) adds four standalone overworld/nether bosses meant to punctuate the mid-to-late game: the Night Lich, the Obsidilith, the Nether Gauntlet, and the Void Blossom. Three of the four are wired directly into this pack’s boss-gating system (boss_level_definitions.json5): the Night Lich is gated at character level 10, the Nether Gauntlet at level 15, and the Obsidilith at level 40 (all soft requirements, not hard-blocked). The Void Blossom sits outside the level-gate list entirely — an optional fourth fight rather than a progression checkpoint.
Per this server’s bosses_of_mass_destruction.json5 config, the four bosses are tuned as: Night Lich — 650 HP, 300 XP on death, fires a slowness-inflicting missile (7 damage, 60-tick slowness), can summon undead-type mobs (zombies, skeletons, drowned, husks, strays, wither skeletons, zoglins, zombie villagers, zombified piglins, even the vanilla Wither) toward a “summon counter,” dropping a Soul Star after 50 counted kills, and can spawn Comets with a 3.0 explosion strength. Obsidilith — the tankiest of the four at 2000 HP, 20 armor, 36 attack, 500 XP, passively heals, spawns an obsidian pillar on death, and its anvil-slam attack has a 4.0 explosion strength. Nether Gauntlet — 900 HP, 8 armor, 16 attack, 500 XP, passively heals, drops Ancient Debris on death, and its charged punch explodes at size 4.0 (1.5x on a normal punch). Void Blossom — 1250 HP, 10 armor, 30 attack, 500 XP, no special death effect configured. The mod also ships supporting projectile/summon entities (Blue Fireball, Soul Star, Spore, Petal Blade) used by these fights.
Because BOMD sits in the same level-gated boss roster as vanilla’s Ender Dragon, AdventureZ’s Blackstone Golem and The Eye, and several other modpack bosses (Souls Weapons’ Accursed Lord/Draugr, Minecells’ Conjunctivius, Archon’s Null, Spellblade Next’s Magus, Eldritch End’s The Faceless, and the pack’s own Hastur Magus finale), it functions as one of several structured checkpoints in the pack’s overall difficulty curve rather than an isolated add-on fight.
Anticipated questions
Q: What levels are the BOMD bosses gated at?
A: The Night Lich at level 10, the Nether Gauntlet at level 15, and the Obsidilith at level 40 (all soft requirements); the Void Blossom is unlisted — an optional fight rather than a progression checkpoint. See Progression & Level Caps.
Q: Which BOMD boss is the toughest?
A: The Obsidilith — 2000 HP, 20 armor, 36 attack, and it passively heals; its anvil-slam has a 4.0 explosion strength and it spawns an obsidian pillar on death.
Q: What do these bosses drop?
A: The Night Lich drops a Soul Star (after its summon counter reaches 50 counted kills), the Nether Gauntlet drops Ancient Debris, and the fights give 300–500 XP on death.
Q: How does the Night Lich fight work?
A: 650 HP; it fires a slowness-inflicting missile (7 damage, 60-tick slowness), summons undead toward a “summon counter,” and can spawn Comets with 3.0 explosion strength, dropping a Soul Star after 50 counted kills.

Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Caraca.title: Caracal mob
Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Caraca.content:
Caracal mob
Caracal mob (v1.20-2.3.3, by AqUpd, Maity and u/SociopathyKathy) is a small, focused addition: a single new tameable-cat-family creature, the Caracal, modeled after the real African/Asian wild cat. Per its own biome tag data (caracal_spawning_biomes.json), it’s configured to spawn naturally in exactly one biome type — Savanna — making it a rare, regionally-flavored find rather than a common companion animal like vanilla cats or wolves.
The mod ships no configuration file in this pack, so it runs on its stock behavior and spawn rules. Its lang file confirms a small but complete behavior set (hiss, scream, purr, death, eat, and beg-for-food sound cues), suggesting cat-like AI — likely tameable and capable of begging for food from the player, consistent with vanilla ocelot/cat behavior patterns.
Anticipated questions
Q: Where do Caracals spawn?
A: Only in Savanna biomes, per its caracal_spawning_biomes.json — a rare, regionally-flavored find rather than a common companion animal like vanilla cats or wolves.
Q: Can I tame a Caracal?
A: Its sound set (hiss, scream, purr, eat, beg-for-food) suggests cat-like AI, so it’s likely tameable and can beg for food, consistent with vanilla ocelot/cat behavior — though the mod ships no config here to confirm the exact rules.
Q: Is the Caracal configurable on this server?
A: No — it ships no configuration file in this pack, so it runs on its stock behavior and spawn rules.

Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Creepe.title: Creeper Overhaul
Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Creepe.content:
Creeper Overhaul
Creeper Overhaul (v3.0.2, art by Joosh, dev by ThatGravyBoat) replaces the single vanilla creeper with fifteen biome-specific creeper types: Badlands, Bamboo, Beach, Cave, Dark Oak, Desert, Dripstone, Hills, Jungle, Mushroom, Ocean, Savannah, Snowy, Spruce, and Swamp Creepers. Each has its own texture and, per the mod’s own description, some are “friendlier than others” than a standard creeper. Every variant also gets its own spawn egg and a set of biome-appropriate death/hurt sound subtitles — the Ocean Creeper is the standout mechanically, with dedicated “inflate”/“deflate” subtitles pointing to underwater-specific behavior not shared by the other fourteen.
This server’s creeperoverhaul.jsonc has spawning enabled for all fifteen variants individually (each allow<Biome>CreeperSpawning flag is true) and keeps destroyBlocks: true, so these creepers still grief terrain like a vanilla creeper. The one thing left off is replaceDefaultCreeper under the client section — meaning the plain vanilla creeper texture/model is left untouched rather than being reskinned, so players will see both vanilla-textured creepers and the biome variants depending on where they spawn.
Anticipated questions
Q: Do these creepers still blow up my builds?
A: Yes — destroyBlocks is left true, so all fifteen biome creepers still grief terrain like a vanilla creeper. See Progression & Level Caps.
Q: Why do I still see plain vanilla creepers too?
A: replaceDefaultCreeper is left off, so the vanilla creeper texture/model is untouched — you’ll see both vanilla-looking creepers and biome variants depending on where they spawn.
Q: How many creeper types are there, and where do they spawn?
A: Fifteen biome-specific types (Badlands, Bamboo, Beach, Cave, Dark Oak, Desert, Dripstone, Hills, Jungle, Mushroom, Ocean, Savannah, Snowy, Spruce, Swamp), each with spawning individually enabled in creeperoverhaul.jsonc.
Q: Which creeper is the most unusual?
A: The Ocean Creeper — it has dedicated “inflate”/“deflate” subtitles pointing to underwater-specific behavior the other fourteen don’t share.

Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Flower.title: Flowery Mooblooms
Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Flower.content:
Flowery Mooblooms
Flowery Mooblooms (v2.0.2, by Faboslav) is a small, official addon for Friends & Foes — it doesn’t register its own mod namespace at all, instead dropping its textures and variant data straight into assets/friendsandfoes/ and data/friendsandfoes/moobloom_variants/. It gives the Moobloom (Friends & Foes’ flower-topped cow) one extra coat variant per overworld flower: Allium, Azure Bluet, Blue Orchid, Cornflower, Dandelion, Lilac, Lily of the Valley, Orange Tulip, Oxeye Daisy, Peony, Pink Tulip, Poppy, Red Tulip, Rose Bush, Sunflower, and White Tulip — sixteen recolors in total, each a straightforward reskin rather than a new mechanic.
Because it’s a texture/variant-only addon with no config file of its own, its only tunable setting is Friends & Foes’ own moobloomSpawnWeight (4, in this pack’s friendsandfoes.json) and group size (2–4) — Flowery Mooblooms just widens the pool of what a spawned Moobloom can look like.
Anticipated questions
Q: What does Flowery Mooblooms actually add?
A: Sixteen extra Moobloom coat variants — one per overworld flower — each a straightforward reskin of Friends & Foes’ flower-topped cow, not a new mechanic.
Q: Which flower variants can a Moobloom have?
A: Sixteen in total: Allium, Azure Bluet, Blue Orchid, Cornflower, Dandelion, Lilac, Lily of the Valley, Orange Tulip, Oxeye Daisy, Peony, Pink Tulip, Poppy, Red Tulip, Rose Bush, Sunflower, and White Tulip.
Q: Does it have its own spawn settings?
A: No — it’s texture/variant-only with no config file, so its only tunables are Friends & Foes’ own moobloomSpawnWeight (4) and group size (2–4). It just widens the pool of what a spawned Moobloom can look like.

Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Friend.title: Friends & Foes
Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Friend.content:
Friends & Foes
Friends & Foes (v3.0.9, by Faboslav) is the pack’s implementation of the mobs Mojang put to a community vote and then never added — the Glare, Copper Golem, Rascal, and Moobloom from various Minecraft Live mob votes, plus a set of original “vanilla-like” additions: the Crab, Iceologer, Illusioner-adjacent Player Illusion, Mauler, Tuff Golem, and Wildfire. Rather than porting the mob-vote losers as-is, Faboslav expanded each with fuller mechanics and structures: Copper Golems can generate as a standalone structure or inside Ancient Cities and oxidize lightning rods over time; Crabs spawn in small groups (2–4) and can be ridden on shoulders like parrots; Glares are small light-seeking mobs that can grief certain blocks if enabled; Iceologers and Illusioners get their own cabin/shack/training-ground structures and can appear in raids; Maulers are aggressive desert/badlands/savanna predators (spawn weights 8/16/32 respectively — most common in savanna); Tuff Golems can spawn inside strongholds; and Wildfires are guardians of a dedicated “Citadel” structure.
This server’s friendsandfoes.json has every one of these features enabled, including all the bonus generated structures (Copper Golem area + Ancient City variant, Iceologer cabin, Illusioner shack and training grounds, Citadel, and — via the Beekeeper Hut addon config living in this same file — a beekeeper villager profession and beekeeper area structure). Two dedicated addon jars extend Friends & Foes further in this pack: Flowery Mooblooms (one Moobloom recolor per flower type) and Beekeeper Hut (the beekeeper structure/profession itself), both by the same author and both reading their settings from this shared config file rather than one of their own.
Anticipated questions
Q: What mobs does Friends & Foes add?
A: The mob-vote mobs Mojang never shipped — Glare, Copper Golem, Rascal, and Moobloom — plus originals like the Crab, Iceologer, Mauler, Tuff Golem, and Wildfire.
Q: Can I ride a Crab?
A: Yes — Crabs spawn in small groups of 2–4 and can be ridden on your shoulders like parrots.
Q: Where do Maulers spawn?
A: In desert, badlands, and savanna, with spawn weights of 8/16/32 respectively — most common in savanna, where they’re aggressive predators. See Progression & Level Caps.
Q: Where do I find the Copper Golem or the Wildfire?
A: Copper Golems generate as a standalone structure or inside Ancient Cities (and oxidize lightning rods over time); Wildfires guard a dedicated “Citadel” structure.

Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Hellio.title: Hellion's Sniffer+
Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Hellio.content:
Hellion’s Sniffer+
Hellion’s Sniffer+ (v0.3.0, by HellionGames) undersells itself with the tagline “basic improvements to the Sniffer from the 1.20 update” — in practice it adds a whole new underground biome built around the Sniffer’s ancient-plant theme. Its Timeless Grotto biome (a cave-type biome tagged into the overworld’s cave generation) grows a dedicated Stone Pine wood set (log, planks, stairs, slabs, doors, fences, signs, boats, and a chest boat), plus Ivy and Fiddlefern/Tall Fiddlefern vegetation and moss patches, giving Sniffer-adjacent exploration its own distinct underground look rather than reusing existing stone/wood palettes.
The mod ships no configuration file in this pack, so the Timeless Grotto generates under its default worldgen rules. It’s a content addition rather than a creature mod in the traditional sense — the Sniffer itself is vanilla 1.20, so this mod’s job is purely to give the biome it’s thematically tied to some genuinely new blocks and flora to discover.
Anticipated questions
Q: What does Hellion’s Sniffer+ actually add?
A: A new underground cave biome — the Timeless Grotto — with a dedicated Stone Pine wood set (logs, planks, stairs, slabs, doors, fences, signs, boats, chest boat), plus Ivy, Fiddlefern/Tall Fiddlefern, and moss patches.
Q: Does it change the Sniffer itself?
A: No — the Sniffer is vanilla 1.20; this mod’s job is purely to give its thematically-tied biome genuinely new blocks and flora. It’s a content/biome addition rather than a creature mod.
Q: Where does the Timeless Grotto generate?
A: It’s a cave-type biome tagged into the overworld’s cave generation, and with no config file in this pack it generates under its default worldgen rules.

Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Mobs-o.title: Mobs of Mythology
Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Mobs-o.content:
Mobs of Mythology
Mobs of Mythology (v2.1.2, by Pixel Dream Studios, steficy, AzureDoom, karelien and Bandit-Bytes) adds six creatures drawn from folklore rather than a single mythology: the Automaton (a hostile construct, 100 HP / 16 attack, always-hostile toggleable), the Chupacabra (16 HP / 6 attack, common spawn weight 20), the Kobold and armed Kobold Warrior (20 HP scavengers that can optionally steal items, weights 4 and 6, the warrior adding 6 armor and 5.5 attack), the Drake (30 HP / 5 attack, spawn weight 10, a small draconic mob rather than a boss), and the Sporeling — a mushroom-person with two color variants (red and brown) that each carry a huge bank of joke one-liners triggered on interaction (puns about fungi, “spore-tacular” wordplay, and a couple of stoner jokes about being “blazed”).
This server’s mobs_of_mythology.properties keeps all six enabled at their default health/damage/spawn-weight values, with shouldKoboldsSteal left off (kobolds don’t pickpocket the player) and the Sporeling as the most common spawn of the group (weight 16, well above the Drake’s 10 or Chupacabra’s 20-vs-population). None of the six are wired into the pack’s boss-gating system, so they read as roaming mid-tier wildlife/threats rather than structured encounters — a lighter-weight complement to the pack’s more heavily systemized bosses like Bosses of Mass Destruction or AdventureZ.
Anticipated questions
Q: Are any Mobs of Mythology creatures bosses?
A: No — none of the six are wired into the pack’s boss-gating system, so they read as roaming mid-tier wildlife/threats rather than structured encounters. See Progression & Level Caps.
Q: Which of these mobs is the most dangerous?
A: The Automaton — a hostile construct with 100 HP and 16 attack, the toughest of the six; most others (Chupacabra, Kobold, Drake) sit around 16–30 HP.
Q: Do Kobolds steal my stuff?
A: Not on this server — shouldKoboldsSteal is left off, so kobolds don’t pickpocket the player even though the mod supports it.
Q: What’s the deal with the Sporeling?
A: It’s a mushroom-person with red and brown variants that fire off a huge bank of joke one-liners on interaction; it’s also the group’s most common spawn (weight 16).

More Axolotl Variants Mod
More Axolotl Variants Mod (MAVM, v1.2.6, by AkashiiKun) expands vanilla’s five axolotl colors with ten additional variants: Lucia, Wilder, Golden, Green, Skulk, Black, Red, Glowxolotl, White, and Cyanide. It’s built on a small companion library, More Axolotl Variants API, which this pack also has installed as a hard dependency. A couple of the names hint at biome/theme tie-ins beyond simple recoloring — “Skulk” suggests a Deep Dark-flavored variant and “Glowxolotl” suggests a glow-ink-sac-style luminous effect — consistent with the mod’s general approach of using vanilla’s existing axolotl-variant system to slot in extra colors alongside the original Leucistic/Wild/Gold/Cyan/Blue set.
The pack also carries a disabled axolotl-item-fix-1.1.7.jar.disabled, but that’s a different, unrelated mod (“Axolotl Item Fix”) — not part of this mod and not currently active.

Q: How many new axolotl colors does this add?
A: Ten variants on top of vanilla’s five: Lucia, Wilder, Golden, Green, Skulk, Black, Red, Glowxolotl, White, and Cyanide.
Q: Do the variant names hint at special effects?

Q: What’s the axolotl-item-fix jar I see disabled?

Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/More-M.title: More Mob Variants
Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/More-M.content:
More Mob Variants
More Mob Variants (v1.3.1, by nyuppo) doesn’t add any new creature types — it purely reskins existing vanilla mobs using Minecraft 1.20’s built-in variant/texture system (the same mechanism vanilla uses for cat breeds and painting art). This server’s copy ships biome- and condition-based texture pools for Cats, Chickens, Cows, Pigs, Sheep, Skeletons, Spiders, Wolves, and Zombies — Wolves get by far the largest set (28 variant entries, expanding on vanilla’s own wolf-variant vote with color pools like ashen, black, chestnut, pale, rusty, snowy, spotted, striped, and “woods,” each tagged to spawn in specific biomes), while Skeletons get regional reskins including increased sandy (desert-biome) and mossy (jungle/swamp-biome) variants.
The mod’s settings.json in this pack enables muddy pigs (pigs that visually get dirty after wallowing in mud, no cooldown timeout configured) and sets a 25% chance for a baby animal to roll its own independent random variant rather than inheriting a parent’s look. Because it only touches vanilla mob types, it’s the “wildlife re-texturing” counterpart to mods like Creeper Overhaul and Naturalist that add genuinely new creatures — More Mob Variants just makes the vanilla ones feel less uniform across biomes.
Anticipated questions
Q: Does More Mob Variants add new mobs?
A: No — it purely reskins existing vanilla mobs (Cats, Chickens, Cows, Pigs, Sheep, Skeletons, Spiders, Wolves, Zombies) using 1.20’s built-in variant system, so they feel less uniform across biomes.
Q: Which mob gets the most variants?
A: Wolves, by far — 28 variant entries (ashen, black, chestnut, pale, rusty, snowy, spotted, striped, “woods,” and more), each tagged to spawn in specific biomes.
Q: What are muddy pigs?
A: The mod’s settings.json enables muddy pigs — pigs that visually get dirty after wallowing in mud (no cooldown configured). It also gives baby animals a 25% chance to roll their own random variant instead of inheriting a parent’s look.

Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Mutant.title: Mutant Creepers No Explody
Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Mutant.content:
Mutant Creepers No Explody
Mutant Creepers No Explody (v1.0.0, by Mervyn) is a tiny, single-purpose compatibility patch built specifically for this pack’s combination of mods — its own description states it directly: “Prevents Mutant Monsters’ explosions from griefing blocks and entities in OPAC-claimed areas.” Technically it’s just one mixin class (MutatedExplosionMixin) that hard-depends on Mutant Monsters being installed, and it exists purely to make Mutant Creeper explosions respect Open Parties and Claims land protection the way vanilla creeper explosions already do.
Without this patch, a rare Mutant Creeper (spawning at only 0.05% of vanilla creeper weight, per Mutant Monsters’ config) wandering into a claimed base could blow craters through builds that OPAC is supposed to protect. This mod closes that gap without touching Mutant Monsters’ balance or spawn rates at all — it only changes what the explosion is allowed to destroy, and only inside claimed territory.
Anticipated questions
Q: What does Mutant Creepers No Explody do?
A: It’s a compatibility patch that stops Mutant Monsters’ explosions from griefing blocks and entities inside Open Parties and Claims-protected land — one mixin class, with no change to spawn rates or balance.
Q: Will a Mutant Creeper still wreck my unclaimed builds?
A: Yes — the patch only changes what the explosion is allowed to destroy inside claimed territory; outside claims a Mutant Creeper (spawning at 0.05% of vanilla creeper weight) can still blow craters.
Q: Does it need Mutant Monsters installed?
A: Yes — it hard-depends on Mutant Monsters and exists purely to make Mutant Creeper explosions respect land claims the way vanilla creeper explosions already do.

Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Mutant.title: Mutant Monsters
Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Mutant.content:
Mutant Monsters
Mutant Monsters (v8.0.8, by shcott21, Chumbanotz, Fuzs and tdstress — the long-running “Mutant Creatures” successor) adds oversized, drastically buffed variants of five vanilla mobs: Mutant Creeper, Mutant Enderman, Mutant Skeleton, Mutant Snow Golem, and Mutant Zombie (plus a Mutant Zombie Villager and the joke/secret “Spider-Pig”). Each has its own dangerous signature mechanic — the Mutant Creeper detonates in a chain of smaller “Creeper Minions,” the Mutant Enderman teleports and splits into Endersoul Fragments/Clones, the Mutant Skeleton dual-wields and fires volleys, and so on. These are rare, high-threat overworld/nether encounters rather than common mobs: in this server’s mutantmonsters-common.toml, every mutant’s spawn weight is set to just 0.05% of its vanilla counterpart’s weight, so they spawn in any biome/dimension their vanilla base mob can, but extremely infrequently.
The mod also adds a “Mutant X” infection mechanic — per mutantmonsters-server.toml, hitting a target with the right potion effect can transform a vanilla creeper/enderman/skeleton/snow golem/zombie/pig into its mutant (or, for pigs, the Spider-Pig) form on the spot, rather than only encountering them via natural spawns. An Endersoul Hand item lets players teleport up to 128 blocks. Because mutant creepers still explode and can grief blocks/entities even inside Open Parties and Claims-protected land, this pack pairs Mutant Monsters with the small compatibility mod Mutant Creepers No Explody, which specifically suppresses that griefing inside claimed areas.
Anticipated questions
Q: How rare are Mutant Monsters?
A: Very — every mutant’s spawn weight is set to just 0.05% of its vanilla counterpart’s, so they appear in the same biomes/dimensions but extremely infrequently as rare, high-threat encounters. See Progression & Level Caps.
Q: Can I turn a normal mob into a mutant?
A: Yes — the “Mutant X” infection lets you hit a vanilla creeper/enderman/skeleton/snow golem/zombie/pig with the right potion effect to transform it into its mutant form (or, for pigs, the Spider-Pig) on the spot.
Q: What does the Endersoul Hand do?
A: It lets players teleport up to 128 blocks.
Q: Do Mutant Creepers still grief claimed land?
A: No — this pack pairs the mod with Mutant Creepers No Explody, which suppresses that explosion griefing inside Open Parties and Claims-protected areas.
