Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Mythic.title: Mythic Mounts
Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Mythic.content:
Mythic Mounts
Mythic Mounts (v7.2) is the pack’s dedicated tamable-mount mod, and it’s entirely config-driven — every creature’s health, speed, attack, diet, taming items, and spawn conditions live in MythicMountsConfig.json, which this server has read directly to confirm the numbers below. Its roster splits cleanly into flyers, ground mounts, and two look-alikes that turn out not to fly at all.
Flying mounts. The Dragon is the rarest and most dangerous: 40 base health, hostile until tamed (only a 5% taming chance per attempt, using gold ingot, diamond, or emerald), a 9-slot inventory, and specialAbilitiesEnabled set true. It only spawns subterraneously, capped at just 1 per 256-chunk region with a mere 10% roll chance even then — making it the single hardest mount in the mod to find. The Griffon is the common alternative: 35 health, tamed peacefully with rabbit or mutton (no hostility flag), spawning at a generous 70% roll chance across mountainous biomes (windswept hills, windswept gravelly hills, windswept forest, snowy slopes, and jagged peaks). The Nether Bat (25 health) is Nether-exclusive, spawning only in Crimson and Warped Forests, hostile until tamed on porkchop. The Żar-ptak — Polish for “Firebird,” and its actual in-game display name, which is why it visually starts with “Ż” rather than “F” — is a rare village-adjacent spawn (20 health, only a 2% roll chance, capped at 5 per 256-chunk region) tamed exclusively with golden apples. The Giant Moth is the most fragile flyer at just 10 health, spawning only in Dark Forests and tamed with any flower item.
Look-alikes that don’t fly. The Courier Bird and Colelytra both read as flying candidates but aren’t: the Courier Bird’s own in-game lore states these tropical, parrot-like birds have “grown too hefty to fly” and instead sprint on powerful legs, making them popular messenger mounts; the Colelytra — a colorful beetle native to Mushroom Islands that lives peaceably alongside mooshrooms — has no flight mechanic mentioned anywhere in its lore or config.
Ground mounts. Rounding out the roster: Acencia (a leopard-like climbing cat of snowy forests, tamed on mutton/salmon), Archelon (a giant sea turtle of deep lukewarm oceans, tamed on cod/salmon, capped at 2 per 256-chunk region), Geckotoa/Giant Geckotoa (a subterranean riding lizard, capped at 1 per region), Riding Lizard (a smaller desert-dwelling lizard, hostile until tamed), Dire Wolf (old-growth forest predator, tamed on bone), and Nightmare (a hostile fire-steed of basalt deltas and soul sand valleys, only a 3% taming chance using bone, coal, or charcoal — notably, this pack’s Nightmare comes from Mythic Mounts, not from AdventureZ’s same-named mob, which this pack has deliberately disabled to avoid the overlap).
The Summoning Staff is the mod’s key utility item: crafted from 2 Feathers + an Ender Pearl on the top row, a Stick + Name Tag on the middle row, and a Stick + Bell on the bottom row. Right-click a tamed mount once to link the staff to it, then right-click again from anywhere to instantly warp that mount to the rider’s side — though per its own in-game description, the staff “will fail if the linked mount is too far away,” so it has a hard range limit rather than unlimited reach. One more universal quirk applies across the whole mod: flying mounts refuse to take off while leashed with a lead.
Anticipated questions
Q: What’s the rarest, hardest mount to get?
A: The Dragon — hostile until tamed with only a 5% taming chance (gold ingot, diamond, or emerald), spawning only subterraneously at 1 per 256-chunk region with a 10% roll chance even then.
Q: What’s a good beginner flying mount?
A: The Griffon — 35 health, tamed peacefully with rabbit or mutton, spawning at a generous 70% roll chance across mountainous biomes (windswept hills/gravelly hills/forest, snowy slopes, jagged peaks).
Q: How does the Summoning Staff work?
A: Right-click a tamed mount once to link the staff to it, then right-click again to warp it to your side — but it “will fail if the linked mount is too far away,” so it has a hard range limit. Recipe: 2 Feathers + an Ender Pearl (top row), a Stick + Name Tag (middle), a Stick + Bell (bottom).
Q: Why won’t my flying mount take off?
A: Flying mounts refuse to take off while leashed with a lead — remove the lead first.

Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Natura.title: Naturalist
Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Natura.content:
Naturalist
Naturalist (v5.0pre3, by Starfish Studios) is a pure ambient-wildlife mod — it adds no bosses or hostile threats, just realistic and semi-exotic animals to flesh out the overworld’s biomes. Its roster covers North American wildlife (Alligator, Bass, Bear, Bluejay, Boar, Canary, Cardinal, Catfish, Coral Snake, Deer, Duck, Finch, Firefly, Rattlesnake, Robin, Snail, Sparrow, plus a Forest Fox and Forest Rabbit) alongside a savanna/safari set (Elephant, Giraffe, Hippo, Lion, Rhino, Zebra, Vulture) and smaller terrarium-style additions (Lizard, Snake, Tortoise, Dragonfly, Butterfly, Catterpillar).
This server’s naturalist.json keeps effectively the entire roster enabled — only the Butterfly is turned off (butterflyRemoved: true, spawn weight zeroed), likely for performance or visual-clutter reasons since butterflies are a purely decorative, spawn-heavy mob in the original mod. Every other animal keeps its default spawn weight and group size (savanna megafauna like the Lion and Rhino are deliberately rare — spawn weights of 3 and 1 respectively, group sizes 1–3 — while flocking birds and shoal fish like the Bluejay, Canary, Cardinal, Finch, Sparrow and Bass spawn in groups of 3–6 at weight 10). None of these animals are aggressive or boss-tier; Naturalist exists purely to make explored biomes feel populated, complementing the pack’s higher-threat creature mods rather than competing with them.
Anticipated questions
Q: Are any Naturalist animals dangerous?
A: No — Naturalist is a pure ambient-wildlife mod that adds no bosses or hostile threats; it exists purely to make explored biomes feel populated.
Q: Which animal is turned off on this server?
A: Only the Butterfly (butterflyRemoved: true, spawn weight zeroed) — likely for performance/visual-clutter reasons, since butterflies are a decorative, spawn-heavy mob.
Q: Why are lions and rhinos so hard to find?
A: Savanna megafauna are deliberately rare — the Lion has a spawn weight of 3 and the Rhino just 1 (group sizes 1–3) — whereas flocking birds and shoal fish spawn in groups of 3–6 at weight 10.

Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Tiny-S.title: Tiny Skeletons
Mods/Creatures,-Bosses--and--Mobs/Tiny-S.content:
Tiny Skeletons
Tiny Skeletons (v8.0.1, by Fuzs — the same developer behind Mutant Monsters’ “Mutant Skeleton”) is a small, focused mod that adds shrunken Baby Skeleton, Baby Wither Skeleton, and Baby Stray variants of the three vanilla skeleton types. It ships no configuration file in this pack, so it runs on default behavior — the baby versions are presumably rarer, weaker, faster-moving reskins in the same spirit as vanilla’s baby zombies, rather than a threat upgrade.
The mod pairs with a separate small addon in this pack, Mutant Skeleton Armor Tweaks (v2.1.0, by Stalemated), which specifically patches Mutant Monsters’ Mutant Skeleton to properly support crossbows — this server’s mutant_skeleton_armor_tweaks.json has the leggings and boots equipment-effect tweaks enabled but leaves the chestplate’s draw-speed buff, crossbow tweak, and skull-multishot options disabled, keeping the mutant skeleton’s crossbow behavior closer to its original balance.
Anticipated questions
Q: What does Tiny Skeletons add?
A: Shrunken Baby Skeleton, Baby Wither Skeleton, and Baby Stray variants of the three vanilla skeleton types; with no config file here it runs on default behavior.
Q: Are baby skeletons a bigger threat than normal ones?
A: Not per this note — with no config they run on default behavior and are presumably rarer, weaker, faster-moving reskins in the spirit of vanilla baby zombies, rather than a threat upgrade.
Q: What’s the Mutant Skeleton Armor Tweaks addon for?
A: It patches Mutant Monsters’ Mutant Skeleton to properly support crossbows. On this server only the leggings and boots equipment-effect tweaks are enabled — the chestplate draw-speed buff, crossbow tweak, and skull-multishot options are left off, keeping the mutant skeleton close to its original balance.

Mods/Dimensions--and--Space-Travel/Ad-As.title: Ad Astra Cable Fix
Mods/Dimensions--and--Space-Travel/Ad-As.content:
Ad Astra Cable Fix
A tiny, purely technical patch mod (by Antigravity, ad_astra_cable_fix-1.0.0.jar, ~2 mixin classes) that exists to fix a specific stability bug: Ad Astra machines crashing from nested fluid/energy transactions when external item or fluid pipes (from other tech mods) interact with them. It works by mixing into MachineFluidTransactionMixin and RecipeMachineTickMixin to prevent the double-transaction conflict rather than adding any new content, items, or blocks of its own.
In a modpack like Prominence II that layers multiple automation mod ecosystems on top of Ad Astra’s own machines (fuel loaders, oxygen distributors, cable networks), this kind of cross-mod pipe interaction is exactly where crashes tend to surface — this mod is the silent fix keeping that combination stable.
Anticipated questions
Q: What does Ad Astra Cable Fix actually do?
A: It’s a tiny patch mod (about two mixin classes) that stops Ad Astra machines from crashing due to nested fluid/energy transactions when item or fluid pipes from other tech mods interact with them. It adds no new items, blocks, or content of its own.
Q: Do I need to craft or configure anything for it?
A: No — it runs silently in the background to keep Ad Astra stable alongside the pack’s other automation mods, and only matters when those cross-mod pipe interactions happen.

Mods/Dimensions--and--Space-Travel/Ad-As.title: Ad Astra Giselle Addon
Mods/Dimensions--and--Space-Travel/Ad-As.content:
Ad Astra: Giselle Addon
A automation-focused add-on for Ad Astra (by gisellevonbingen, Ad-Astra-Giselle-Addon-fabric-1.20.1-6.19.jar, tagline “Just add good things in my think for Ad Astra”). It bolts on machines that make late-game space bases actually automatable instead of hand-managed: a Fuel Loader that auto-refuels any nearby rover or rocket within a configurable range, an Automation NASA Workbench that lets rocket assembly itself be automated/powered rather than done by hand at the crafting-table version, a Rocket Sensor that reads a rocket’s state (fuel loaded, flying up, launch countdown, lander present) out as a redstone comparator signal for automation/alarm builds, and portable Oxygen Cans (plus a Netherite-tier variant) so oxygen can be carried and dispensed without lugging buckets everywhere.
It also adds four new enchantments that shrink the gear grind: Space Breathing (breathe in Ad Astra dimensions, drawing from an Oxygen Can in inventory), Space Fire Proof and Acid Rain Proof (energy- or durability-gated protection), and Gravity Normalizing (personal gravity normalization without needing a room-sized machine). The server’s config/ad_astra_giselle_addon.jsonc tunes all of this — Oxygen Can capacity/transfer rates, Fuel Loader tank size (648,000 mB) and 2-block working range, Automation NASA Workbench energy draw, Gravity Normalizer’s per-block energy cost and 31-block max span, and the exact energy/durability costs for each new enchantment’s per-tick upkeep.
Anticipated questions
Q: What does the Giselle Addon add to Ad Astra?
A: Automation machines for space bases — a Fuel Loader that auto-refuels nearby rovers and rockets, an Automation NASA Workbench for powered rocket assembly, a Rocket Sensor that outputs a rocket’s state as a redstone comparator signal, and portable Oxygen Cans (plus a Netherite-tier variant).
Q: What new enchantments does it add?
A: Space Breathing (breathe in Ad Astra dimensions by drawing from an Oxygen Can), Space Fire Proof, Acid Rain Proof, and Gravity Normalizing (personal gravity normalization without a room-sized machine).
Q: How big is the Fuel Loader’s range and tank?
A: On this server it has a 648,000 mB tank and a 2-block working range, per config/ad_astra_giselle_addon.jsonc.

Mods/Dimensions--and--Space-Travel/Ad-As.title: Ad Astra
Mods/Dimensions--and--Space-Travel/Ad-As.content:
Ad Astra
Ad Astra (by Alex Nijjar, ad_astra-fabric-1.20.1-1.15.20.jar) is the flagship space-travel mod in this category, and it ships its own in-game Patchouli guidebook (“Astrodux”) with four chapters — The First Launch, The Moon, Surviving Mars, and The Hot Planets — that lay out the entire progression path. The journey starts on a launch pad built from a NASA Workbench: gather cone, plates, fins, tanks and an engine, assemble a tier-1 steel rocket, fuel it (oil is skimmed from ocean oil spouts and refined into fuel at a Fuel Refinery — a full launch-and-return trip needs at least six buckets), craft a space suit (steel-tier, needs an Oxygen Loader to convert water into oxygen), and launch. From there the tiers stack: Moon (steel rocket, Desh ore found underground, home to underground Lunarian villages and Lunarian Wandering Traders who sell oxygen/fuel/launch pads for emeralds) → Mars (tier-2 desh rocket, yields Ostrum) → Venus & Mercury (tier-3 ostrum rocket, requires a full Netherite Space Suit with permanent fire resistance or you burn to death almost instantly, yields Calorite) → Proxima Centauri’s Glacio (tier-4 calorite rocket, a bitterly cold but oxygenated world — “the end of the Ad Astra progression for now” per the book’s own text).
Survival off-world revolves around sealed-room life support: an Oxygen Distributor (fed by a Water Pump drawing an infinite water source) pressurizes up to 6,000 blocks of a properly sealed structure so you can ditch the suit indoors, but breaching the seal triggers a violent “rapid depressurization” Air Vortex that sucks unprotected entities out and kills them — cable ducts (not bare cables, which aren’t solid) are needed to keep pipes/wires from leaving gaps. A Gravity Normalizer does the same trick for artificial gravity (0-G to 2-G) in orbit and space stations, which are pre-built, expandable structures placed from the planet-select screen and protected from other players spawning nearby. Progression tech includes a Cryo Freezer that turns ice shards (or plain ice/packed ice/blue ice) into far more fuel-efficient Cryo Fuel, solar panels that generate more power the closer they sit to the sun or in vacuum/orbit, rovers with built-in internet radio, a Jet Suit with two flight modes (ascend / boosted-elytra-style) for the hot-planet endgame, and the Ti-69 handheld that reads local oxygen/temperature/gravity at a glance.
The server’s config/ad_astra.jsonc runs close to defaults: oxygen, temperature, and gravity damage are all left enabled (not disabled), air vortexes on breach are on, and rockets leave the atmosphere for space at Y=600. Tuned energy/fluid numbers exist per machine tier (e.g. Ostrum-tier Cryo Freezer: 500 energy in/out, 100,000 capacity, 10,000 mB fluid tank) but nothing here is nerfed toward easy mode — this is meant to be a genuine, gated tech climb, which is why it leans hard on the pack’s tech-automation stack for power generation and material processing before a rocket ever leaves the pad.
Anticipated questions
Q: How do I reach space and get to the Moon?
A: Build a NASA Workbench and assemble a tier-1 steel rocket (cone, plates, fins, tanks, engine), refine skimmed oil into fuel (a full launch-and-return trip needs at least six buckets), craft a steel space suit with an Oxygen Loader, then launch from a launch pad. The in-game “Astrodux” guidebook’s “The First Launch” chapter walks you through it.
Q: What’s the planet progression order?
A: Moon (steel rocket) → Mars (tier-2 desh rocket) → Venus & Mercury (tier-3 ostrum rocket) → Proxima Centauri’s Glacio (tier-4 calorite rocket), which the guidebook calls the end of the Ad Astra progression for now.
Q: Why do I keep dying instantly on Venus and Mercury?
A: They require a full Netherite Space Suit with permanent fire resistance — without it you burn to death almost immediately. Oxygen, temperature, and gravity damage are all left enabled on this server.
Q: How do I breathe indoors without wearing the suit?
A: An Oxygen Distributor (fed by a Water Pump on an infinite water source) pressurizes up to 6,000 blocks of a properly sealed room, but breaching the seal triggers a deadly rapid-depressurization Air Vortex — use cable ducts, not bare cables, to keep the seal airtight.

Mods/Dimensions--and--Space-Travel/Bette.title: Better End
Mods/Dimensions--and--Space-Travel/Bette.content:
Better End
Better End (originally by paulevs, now co-maintained with Quiqueck/Bulldog83; better-end-4.0.11.jar, mod id betterend) turns the vanilla End from a flat chorus-fruit island around a dragon fight into a fully biome-diverse dimension. It adds 29 distinct biomes, ranging from lush to hostile to purely decorative-cave variants: Amber Land, Blossoming Spires, Chorus Forest, Crystal Mountains, Dragon Graveyards, Dry Shrubland, Dust Wastelands, Eterial Grove, Foggy Mushroomland, Glowing Grasslands, Ice Starfield, Lantern Woods, Megalake and Megalake Grove, Neon Oasis, Nightshade Redwoods, Old Bulbis Gardens, Painted Mountains, Shadow Forest, Sulfur Springs, Umbra Valley, Umbrella Jungle, plus several underground-only cave biomes (Empty/Lush Aurora Cave, Empty/Lush Smaragdant Cave, Jade Cave, Empty End Cave). There’s even a meta-achievement for visiting every one of them (“Visit all BetterEnd Biomes”).
Population-wise it introduces six new mobs: the Cubozoa (a floating jellyfish-like creature), Dragonfly, End Fish, End Slime, Shadow Walker, and Silk Moth — giving the End actual ambient wildlife and threats beyond endermen and the dragon. Combined with new plants, terrain generation, and building materials unique to each biome, Better End is effectively a full worldgen overhaul mod rather than a small content add-on, which is why several smaller mods in this category (BetterEnd Crashed Ships, Eldritch End) are built as direct extensions on top of it.
Anticipated questions
Q: What does Better End change about the End?
A: It overhauls the flat vanilla End into a fully biome-diverse dimension with 29 distinct biomes — from lush regions like Foggy Mushroomland and Glowing Grasslands to hostile ones and underground-only cave biomes — plus new plants, terrain generation, and per-biome building materials.
Q: Are there new creatures out there?
A: Yes — six new mobs: the Cubozoa (a floating jellyfish), Dragonfly, End Fish, End Slime, Shadow Walker, and Silk Moth, giving the End ambient wildlife and threats beyond endermen and the dragon.
Q: Is there any reward for exploring all the biomes?
A: Yes — there’s a meta-achievement, “Visit all BetterEnd Biomes,” for reaching every one of them.
Q: Should I gear up before heading out there?
A: It’s not purely scenic — Better End adds threat mobs like the Shadow Walker on top of the usual endermen and the dragon fight, so bring combat gear; see Progression & Level Caps.

Mods/Dimensions--and--Space-Travel/Bette.content:
Better Nether
Better Nether (originally by paulevs, now maintained by quiqueck; mod id betternether, jar better-nether-9.0.10.jar, built on the shared BCLib library) is the Nether’s equivalent of Better End — a full worldgen overhaul replacing the vanilla nether-wastes-and-basalt-deltas monotony with 24 distinct biomes: Bone Reef and Sulfuric Bone Reef, Crimson Glowing Woods and Crimson Pinewood, Flooded Deltas, Gravel Desert, Magma Land, Nether Grasslands and Poor (Nether) Grasslands, Nether Jungle, Nether Mushroom Forest (plus its Edge variant), Nether Swampland and Nether Swampland Terraces, Old Fungiwoods, Old Swampland, Old/dead Upside Down Forest, Soul Plain, and Wart Forest (plus Edge). It also adds seven new mobs — the Firefly, Flying Pig, Hydrogen Jellyfish, Jungle Skeleton, Naga (with its own projectile), and wandering Skull — giving the Nether real fauna beyond piglins and ghasts. Like Better End, it ships achievement-style completion tracking (“Visit all BetterNether Biomes”) and per-biome/edge/sub-biome toggle options for server tuning.
Note on the jar naming: the modpack’s mods/ folder also contains a separate bwncr-fabric-1.20.1-3.17.2.jar, but its fabric.mod.json identifies it as “Bad Wither No Cookie Reloaded” (mod id bwncr) — an unrelated server-side sound-silencing utility (mutes local mob/entity sounds like sheep eating grass) by Kreezxil/Eleksploded, not a Better Nether rebrand. The actual Better Nether content described above ships in better-nether-9.0.10.jar (mod id betternether, GitHub quiqueck/BetterNether) — the two jars are entirely separate, unrelated mods. See Bad Wither No Cookie Reloaded for that other mod’s own note.
Anticipated questions
Q: What does Better Nether do?
A: It’s a full worldgen overhaul of the Nether — the counterpart to Better End — replacing the vanilla wastes-and-basalt-deltas monotony with 24 distinct biomes like Wart Forest, Nether Jungle, Magma Land, Soul Plain, and the Upside Down Forest.
Q: Does it add new mobs?
A: Yes — seven, including the Firefly, Flying Pig, Hydrogen Jellyfish, Jungle Skeleton, Naga (with its own projectile), and a wandering Skull, giving the Nether real fauna beyond piglins and ghasts.
Q: Is the bwncr jar in the pack part of Better Nether?
A: No — despite the similar name, bwncr-fabric-1.20.1-3.17.2.jar is “Bad Wither No Cookie Reloaded,” an unrelated sound-silencing utility. Better Nether’s actual content ships in better-nether-9.0.10.jar. See Bad Wither No Cookie Reloaded.

Mods/Dimensions--and--Space-Travel/Deepe.content:
Deeper and Darker
Deeper and Darker (by Kyanite Mods, mod id deeperdarker, deeperdarker-fabric-1.20-1.3.3-plus-b.jar) is an entirely new dimension called the Otherside, reached by expanding on the vanilla Deep Dark’s sculk theme rather than replacing an existing dimension. It adds four biomes — Deeplands (the hub biome), Blooming Caverns, Echoing Forest, and Overcast Columns — continuing the sculk/warden aesthetic into fully explorable terrain instead of the small pocket biome vanilla offers.
Its mob roster leans into “corrupted deep-sea/sculk horror” themes: the Angler Fish, Sculk Centipede, Sculk Leech, Sculk Snapper, Shattered, Shriek Worm, Sludge, and Stalker all populate the Otherside with escalating threat, alongside dimension-specific boats. Server-side config (config/deeperdarker.json5) exists for tuning generation and mob behavior. As a standalone new dimension rather than an overworld/Nether/End rework, it sits alongside The Bumblezone as one of the pack’s “extra pocket dimensions” rather than a vanilla-dimension overhaul like Better End or Better Nether (BWNCR).
Anticipated questions
Q: What is the Otherside?
A: A brand-new dimension that expands the vanilla Deep Dark’s sculk theme into fully explorable terrain, with four biomes: Deeplands (the hub), Blooming Caverns, Echoing Forest, and Overcast Columns.
Q: How do I get there?
A: It’s reached by building on the vanilla Deep Dark’s sculk theme rather than by replacing an existing dimension — the note doesn’t spell out an exact portal recipe beyond that it continues on from the Deep Dark.
Q: How dangerous is it?
A: Very — the Otherside is populated by corrupted sculk-horror mobs (Angler Fish, Sculk Centipede, Sculk Leech, Sculk Snapper, Shattered, Shriek Worm, Sludge, and Stalker) with escalating threat, so gear up first; see Progression & Level Caps.

Mods/Dimensions--and--Space-Travel/Drago.content:
Dragonfight Mod
Dragonfight Mod (by Someaddons, mod id dragonfight, dragonfight-fabric-1.20.1-4.7.jar, requires the cupboard library) rebuilds the vanilla Ender Dragon encounter into a genuinely harder fight rather than the usual “shoot crystals, hit dragon during perch” pattern. Per this server’s config/dragonfight.json, the pack runs it noticeably tougher than default: dragon difficulty is set to 2 (vanilla is 0, mod default is already 2), mob spawn amount is doubled (mobSpawnAmountModifier: 2.0) so more reinforcements pour in during the fight, phantoms spawn when a crystal is destroyed at range and blazes+phantoms spawn on crystal respawn to punish players who hang back, and the dragon has explosion damage immunity enabled (so crystal detonations near it don’t chip its health for free). Working in the mod’s favor for players, though, lightning strikes are disabled entirely (disableLightning: true) and its anti-flight ability is turned off (antiflightAbility: false), so elytra/rocket flight isn’t punished mid-fight — a deliberate softening given the pack also leans on flight via Ad Astra gear and allow-flight=true server-wide.
New hazards introduced by the mod include a custom “weakexplosion” death message, a gravity-affecting “dragon’s flight magic” debuff that can be inflicted mid-fight (with its own warning/hurt messages), and configurable custom mob-spawn lists tied to crystal destruction/respawn events. It’s a pure combat-difficulty layer on the vanilla End fight — no new biomes or blocks — making it a natural pairing with the worldgen-focused Better End and the eye-hunt rework in End Remastered.
Anticipated questions
Q: How is the Ender Dragon fight different here?
A: Dragonfight Mod rebuilds it into a genuinely harder encounter — on this server dragon difficulty is set to 2, mob spawns are doubled, phantoms spawn when you destroy a crystal from range, blazes and phantoms spawn on crystal respawn, and the dragon has explosion-damage immunity so crystal blasts near it don’t chip its health for free.
Q: Can I still use elytra or rocket flight during the fight?
A: Yes — the mod’s anti-flight ability is turned off and lightning strikes are disabled on this server, a deliberate softening since the pack leans on flight via Ad Astra gear and server-wide allow-flight.
Q: How tough is it — should I prepare?
A: Noticeably tougher than vanilla, with doubled reinforcements and a gravity-affecting “dragon’s flight magic” debuff that can hit you mid-fight, so come well geared; see Progression & Level Caps.

Mods/Dimensions--and--Space-Travel/Eldri.title: Eldritch End
Mods/Dimensions--and--Space-Travel/Eldri.content:
Eldritch End
Eldritch End (by ElocinDev, mod id eldritch_end, Eldritch_End-FABRIC-MC1.20.1-0.3.4.jar) is a Lovecraft-inspired horror expansion built on top of the End dimension. Its two biomes are the Hasturian Wastes and the Primordial Abyss — notably, “Hasturian” directly echoes this modpack’s own subtitle, Prominence II: Hasturian Era, making this one of the more thematically load-bearing mods in the pack rather than incidental flavor content.
It adds a genuinely unsettling bestiary: The Eldritch Eye, The Faceless (with “Hastur’s Image” as a related entry), Aberration, Ominous Eye, Tentacle and Undead Tentacle, and Dendler, alongside Lovecraftian-flavored gear and loot — a Necronomicon, Eldritch Artifact, Corrupted/Corruption Relic, Silver Key, and a full Etyrite armor set (helmet/chestplate/leggings/boots) crafted from a new “Etyr” ore/ingot line. A named boss encounter, X’al, The Faceless Eye, appears as a summonable/spawnable threat with an area-damage void-energy attack. It depends on the necronomicon and azurelib libraries. config/eldritch_end/ holds its server-side tuning.
Anticipated questions
Q: What is Eldritch End?
A: A Lovecraft-inspired horror expansion built on top of the End dimension, adding two biomes — the Hasturian Wastes and the Primordial Abyss (the “Hasturian” name directly echoes the pack’s own subtitle, Prominence II: Hasturian Era).
Q: Is there a boss?
A: Yes — X’al, The Faceless Eye, a summonable/spawnable threat with an area-damage void-energy attack, alongside an unsettling bestiary (the Eldritch Eye, the Faceless, Aberration, Tentacle and Undead Tentacle, Dendler, and more); see Progression & Level Caps.
Q: What gear and loot does it add?
A: Lovecraftian items including a Necronomicon, Eldritch Artifact, Corrupted/Corruption Relic, Silver Key, and a full Etyrite armor set crafted from a new “Etyr” ore/ingot line.

Mods/Dimensions--and--Space-Travel/End-R.title: End Remastered
Mods/Dimensions--and--Space-Travel/End-R.content:
End Remastered
End Remastered (by jack_bagel Dev, maxmitchelson Dev, and artists gilvoisard/And; mod id endrem, fabric-end-remastered-5.2.4.jar) reworks the classic “hunt down a stronghold with Eyes of Ender” loop by splitting the single vanilla Eye of Ender into 17 themed variants, each tied to a different source: the Old Eye (desert pyramid loot), Rogue Eye (jungle temple), Nether Eye (nether bridge chest), Cold Eye (igloo), Magical Eye (woodland mansion or evoker drop), Black Eye (buried treasure), Lost Eye (abandoned mineshaft), Wither Eye (wither drop), Guardian Eye (elder guardian drop), Cursed Eye (bastion treasure), Exotic Eye, Evil Eye, Undead Eye (skeleton horse), Cryptic Eye, Corrupted Eye (pillager outpost), Witch Eye/Witch Pupil (witch drop), each with its own flavor-text lore entry and a matching advancement (“Fortune Seeker,” “Welcome To The Jungle,” “Arghh, Where be Me Ship?,” etc.).
On this server the mod is configured conservatively via config/endrem.json: vanilla Eye of Ender usage and throwing are both disabled (ENABLE_EYE_OF_ENDER: false, THROW_EYE_OF_ENDER: false), and eyes don’t randomly spawn already-placed in portal frames — so the alternate-eye loot hunt is the primary intended path here rather than a bonus layered on top of vanilla eye-throwing. Both the Cryptic Eye and Evil Eye are left obtainable. As a lightweight, config-driven “reforge the path to the End” mod, it complements the heavier worldgen overhauls in this category (Better End, Eldritch End) without touching biomes or terrain itself.
Anticipated questions
Q: Why can’t I craft or throw a normal Eye of Ender?
A: On this server End Remastered disables vanilla Eye of Ender usage and throwing (ENABLE_EYE_OF_ENDER: false, THROW_EYE_OF_ENDER: false), so the alternate-eye loot hunt is the intended path to the End rather than vanilla eye-throwing.
Q: How do I open the End portal then?
A: You collect from 17 themed Eye variants, each tied to a different source — e.g. the Old Eye from a desert pyramid, Nether Eye from a nether bridge chest, Cold Eye from an igloo, or Magical Eye from a woodland mansion / evoker drop — and each has its own advancement.
Q: Where do all the eyes come from?
A: They’re tied to structures and mobs across the world — desert pyramids, jungle temples, igloos, woodland mansions, buried treasure, abandoned mineshafts, bastions, and pillager outposts among them; see Structures.

Pirate’s Doom
Pirate’s Doom (by Kyber_6 and Pixel Dream Studios, mod id piratesdoom, piratesdoom-1.0.0-fabric.jar) is a small pirate-themed Nether content mod — per its own tagline, “because nothing says ‘game over’ to piracy like a fiery descent into the depths of hell.” It’s a lightweight codebase (a single Fabric entrypoint class plus a file-loading utility, no dedicated lang file or config in this pack), suggesting its content is largely data/resource-driven rather than a large new systems layer, in keeping with its role as a smaller thematic add-on rather than a full dimension overhaul.
It sits alongside Better Nether as Nether-flavored content in this category, giving the Nether a pirates-meet-hellscape theme to complement Better Nether’s biome and mob overhaul.

Q: What is Pirate’s Doom?
A: A small pirate-themed Nether content mod that gives the Nether a “pirates-meet-hellscape” flavor, sitting alongside Better Nether to complement its biome and mob overhaul.
Q: Does it add a whole new dimension or bosses?
A: No — it’s a lightweight thematic add-on (a single Fabric entrypoint class, with no dedicated lang file or config in this pack), so its content is largely data/resource-driven rather than a full dimension overhaul.

Mods/Dimensions--and--Space-Travel/The-B.title: The Bumblezone
Mods/Dimensions--and--Space-Travel/The-B.content:
The Bumblezone
The Bumblezone (by TelepathicGrunt, mod id the_bumblezone, the_bumblezone-7.9.10+1.20.1-fabric.jar) is a full bee-themed pocket dimension with a genuinely large content footprint — its English lang file alone carries over 1,300 entries, easily the biggest of the smaller-dimension mods in this category. Its biomes read like a honeycomb fever dream: Pollinated Fields and Pollinated Pillar, Sugar Water Floor, Hive Wall and Hive Pillar, Crystal Canyon, Floral Meadows, Howling Constructs, and the aptly-named Bumbling Beepartments — plus its own “Beeography” completion tracker for visiting every biome, mirroring Better End and Better Nether (BWNCR)‘s biome-completion achievements.
The dimension has real threats, not just cosmetic bee theming: Beehemoth and Queen Beehemoth anchor a boss-tier “Bee Queen” fight (with a visible Friendship meter), backed by mobs like the Honey Slime, Rootmin, Sentry Watcher, and assorted projectile/hazard entities (Pollen Puff, Dirt Pellet, Stinger Spear, Bee Stinger, Honey Crystal Shard, Electric Ring/Purple Spike/Cosmic Crystal entities). Per the mod’s own description, entry is advancement-gated — the mod’s tagline explicitly points players to “check out the advancements for how to play the mod,” meaning access isn’t as simple as building a portal from day one. Server config lives at config/the_bumblezone.json.
Anticipated questions
Q: How do I get into the Bumblezone?
A: Entry is advancement-gated — the mod itself points players to “check out the advancements for how to play the mod,” so access isn’t as simple as building a portal on day one.
Q: Is there a boss to fight?
A: Yes — the Beehemoth and Queen Beehemoth anchor a boss-tier “Bee Queen” fight (with a visible Friendship meter), backed by mobs like the Honey Slime, Rootmin, and Sentry Watcher; see Progression & Level Caps.
Q: What’s actually in the dimension?
A: A full bee-themed pocket dimension with biomes like Pollinated Fields, Sugar Water Floor, Crystal Canyon, Floral Meadows, and the Bumbling Beepartments, plus a “Beeography” tracker for visiting them all.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
Exploration, Dungeons & Structures Mods
When Dungeons Arise
A whole family of elegant, dangerous roguelike dungeons and structures scattered across the world — reliably one of the best “there’s something worth finding over there” mods in the pack.
YUNG’s suite
Completely redesigns vanilla structures so they’re bigger and better laid out: YUNG’s Better Dungeons, Better Desert Temples, Better Jungle Temples, Better Mineshafts, Better Nether Fortresses, Better Ocean Monuments, Better Strongholds, Better Witch Huts, Better End Island, plus Bridges (naturally generating bridges) and YUNG’s API underneath them all.
Regions Unexplored
Adds almost 70 new Overworld biomes, dramatically expanding terrain variety.
More structures to explore (grouped)
Philip’s Ruins (200+ structures), Sky Villages (villages in the clouds), Moog’s Voyager Structures (80+ hand-built Overworld structures, built on the shared Moog’s Structure Lib — correction: “Moog’s End Structures” is not actually an installed mod, only Voyager Structures + its shared library exist), The Graveyard (graveyard-themed bosses/structures/mobs, see Creatures, Bosses & Mobs), Better Archeology, Explorations, Explorify, Towns and Towers, ChoiceTheorem’s Overhauled Village, Integrated Villages, Villagers Plus, The Lost Castle, Simply Houses, Aquamirae (ocean ship graveyard with dangerous deep-sea creatures), Mine Cells (Dead Cells-style roguelike dungeon).
Explorer’s Compass / Nature’s Compass
Search tools — Explorer’s Compass finds structures, Nature’s Compass finds biomes. Use before a long walk.
World-flavor mods (grouped)
Geophilic, River Redux, Swampier Swamps, Nether Depths Upgrade, Frostiful, Winterly, Rare Ice.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: Aquamirae
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
Aquamirae
By Obscuria — “Ship graveyard with terrible deep sea creatures.” Aquamirae builds a sprawling sunken ship graveyard structure into the ocean, guarded by a genuinely dangerous deep-sea bestiary: the Anglerfish, Eel, Maw, Spinefish, and Maze Rose patrol the wrecks, while the Golden Moth and the ghostly Captain Cornelia (both rendered in colored name text client-side, marking them as notable/unique spawns) sit above the ordinary mob tier. The graveyard centers on a maze structure guarded by the Mother of the Maze — a boss-tier mini-dungeon guardian — and a Pillagers Patrol roams nearby, tying the wrecks into the pack’s wider pillager content. A Poisoned Chakram-wielding Tortured Soul rounds out the enemy roster.
Surviving and looting the graveyard requires actual preparation: Aquamirae adds an Oxygen Tank item for extended underwater exploration, and drops a full progression of gear — a Three-Bolt Suit (diving-suit-style full armor set: helmet/chestplate-equivalent/leggings/boots) and an even more powerful Abyssal set (“of the Blinding Abyss” — Tiara, Brigantine, Leggings, Boots, Heaume), plus unique weapons like the Coral Lance, Dagger of Greed, Angler’s Fang, Fin Cutter, Poisoned Blade, Remnant’s Saber, and Divider. Loot containers include Pirate Pouches and Treasure Pouches, and there are two custom music discs (“Forsaken Drownage” by Krossy, “Horizon” by Bertsz) found in the wrecks. No server-side config file overrides Aquamirae’s defaults.
Anticipated questions
Q: What do I need before diving the ship graveyard?
A: Bring the Oxygen Tank for extended underwater exploration; Aquamirae also drops a Three-Bolt Suit diving armor set and the stronger Abyssal set (“of the Blinding Abyss”) as you progress through the wrecks.
Q: What’s the main boss here?
A: The graveyard centers on a maze guarded by the Mother of the Maze, a boss-tier dungeon guardian. The ghostly Captain Cornelia and Golden Moth are notable unique spawns above the ordinary mob tier.
Q: How dangerous is it?
A: Very — the wrecks are patrolled by a dangerous deep-sea bestiary (Anglerfish, Eel, Maw, Spinefish, Maze Rose, Tortured Soul) plus a Pillagers Patrol. Gear up first; see Progression & Level Caps for threat scaling.
Q: Are there unique rewards worth the risk?
A: Yes — unique weapons like the Coral Lance, Angler’s Fang and Dagger of Greed, loot in Pirate/Treasure Pouches, and two custom music discs (“Forsaken Drownage”, “Horizon”) found in the wrecks.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: Better Archeology
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
Better Archeology
Adds a proper archeology loop on top of vanilla’s brush-and-suspicious-sand mechanic: new Fossiliferous Dirt and Suspicious Red Sand variants to brush through, decayed Rotten Log/Planks/Stairs/Fence/Door ruin blocks, cracked/infested mud bricks, and Ancient Vases that shatter for loot when broken. The centerpiece is animal and villager fossils — Villager, Ocelot, Wolf, Sheep, Chicken, Creeper, and Guardian fossils, each collectible as a Skull or Body piece and each carrying a genuine gameplay effect when assembled/placed: Ocelot and Wolf fossils scare off Creepers and Skeletons respectively within a configurable radius (default 20 blocks), the Chicken fossil grants Slow Falling, and the Guardian fossil grants Water Breathing. There’s also an Evoker Trap block for player-built dungeons.
Beyond fossils, Better Archeology adds craftable Artifacts built from Artifact Shards, which grant custom enchantments — Penetrating Strike (ignores a third of a target’s Protection-enchant damage reduction), Tunneling, and Soaring Winds (a 0.5x flight-speed boost) — plus three placeable Totems: Radiance (periodically damages nearby hostile mobs in a 10-block radius), Torrent (gives the player an activation speed boost), and Growth (randomly bonemeals crops in a 5-block radius). All of these systems are live on the server at their shipped defaults (config/betterarcheology-common.toml, config/betterarcheologyconfig.properties) — nothing has been tuned away from stock.
Anticipated questions
Q: What do the animal fossils actually do?
A: Assembled/placed fossils carry real effects — the Ocelot fossil scares off Creepers and the Wolf fossil scares off Skeletons within a configurable radius (default 20 blocks), the Chicken fossil grants Slow Falling, and the Guardian fossil grants Water Breathing.
Q: How do I get Artifacts and what do they give?
A: Craft them from Artifact Shards; they grant custom enchantments like Penetrating Strike (ignores a third of a target’s Protection reduction), Tunneling, and Soaring Winds (a 0.5x flight-speed boost).
Q: What are the Totems for?
A: Three placeable Totems — Radiance (periodically damages nearby hostiles in a 10-block radius), Torrent (activation speed boost), and Growth (randomly bonemeals crops in a 5-block radius).

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: ChoiceTheorem's Overhauled Village
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
ChoiceTheorem’s Overhauled Village (CTOV)
“Enhances and creates new villages and pillager outposts that perfectly fit into your Minecraft world” — CTOV is the most extensive of the pack’s village mods in raw structure count. It replaces vanilla village generation with heavily biome-themed variants, each shipped in Small/Medium/Large size tiers: Beach, Christmas, Dark Forest, Desert, Desert Fortified, Jungle, Jungle Tree, Badlands (Mesa), Badlands Fortified, Japanese-style Mountain, Alpine Mountain, Mushroom, Plains, Plains Fortified, Savanna, Savanna Native-American-style, Snowy, Swamp, Swamp Fortified, and Taiga — around 20 distinct village themes times 3 size tiers. It depends on lithostitched for its structure-set plumbing.
Like Towns and Towers, this overlaps in purpose with the pack’s other village mods but at a different layer: CTOV supplies the actual new village structures/themes, while Towns and Towers reworks vanilla’s existing village/outpost pool and biome coverage, Integrated Villages changes village behavior and Create-machine integration, and Villagers Plus adds new professions and trades that populate whichever villages generate.
Anticipated questions
Q: How is CTOV different from the pack’s other village mods?
A: CTOV supplies the actual new biome-themed village structures (around 20 themes in Small/Medium/Large tiers), while Towns and Towers reworks vanilla’s village/outpost pool, Integrated Villages changes village behavior, and Villagers Plus adds professions and trades.
Q: What village types can I find?
A: Heavily biome-themed variants — Beach, Desert, Jungle, Badlands, Mountain (Japanese and Alpine styles), Mushroom, Plains, Savanna, Snowy, Swamp, Taiga and more, several with Fortified variants.
Q: How do I locate one?
A: Use Explorer’s Compass to point to the nearest village structure.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: Explorer's Compass
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
Explorer’s Compass
By ChaosTheDude — a craftable compass that locates and points to the nearest instance of any generated structure (village, stronghold, ocean monument, any of the pack’s added structures, etc.), with the direction/HUD overlay shown even while chat is open. On this server it’s configured generously: unlimited durability (compassDurability: 0, meaning it never breaks), zero XP cost per search (defaultXpLevel: 0), a 10,000-block max search radius, and up to 100 repeated searches for the next instance of an already-found structure type. No structures are blacklisted from search. Players in creative/cheat mode or who are opped can also teleport directly to a located structure.
Anticipated questions
Q: How do I find a specific structure?
A: Craft the Explorer’s Compass, open it, pick any generated structure type (village, stronghold, monument, or any of the pack’s added structures) and it points to the nearest instance — the HUD overlay shows even with chat open.
Q: Does it break or cost XP?
A: No — on this server it’s set to unlimited durability (never breaks) and zero XP cost per search, with a 10,000-block max search radius and up to 100 repeat searches for the next instance.
Q: Can I teleport to what I find?
A: Only players in creative/cheat mode or who are opped can teleport directly to a located structure; normal survival players must travel there.
Q: What about finding biomes instead?
A: Use its sister mod Nature’s Compass for biomes.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
Explorify
Billed as “a simplistic, vanilla-friendly collection of new structures,” Explorify adds fourteen new structure types to the world: Dark Forest Settlements, Campsites, Taverns, Desert Shrines, Ruins, Mausoleums, Watchtowers (plains/taiga/savanna variants), Supply Caches (birch/dark/desert/forest/jungle/mangrove/taiga variants), Badlands Pyramids, Black Spirals, Mangrove Huts, Farmsteads, Guide Posts (cold/warm), and End Shipwrecks. All fourteen are enabled on the server (config/explorify/structure_toggles.json5), and their generation spacing/separation/frequency values are all at the mod’s shipped defaults (config/explorify/structure_settings.json5) — nothing has been tuned. Most structures generate at spacing 24–48 chunks apart depending on type, giving a fairly dense scatter of new points of interest across explored terrain.

Q: What structures does Explorify add?

Q: How common are they?
A: Most generate at spacing 24–48 chunks apart depending on type (shipped defaults, untuned), giving a fairly dense scatter across explored terrain.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: Frostiful
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
Frostiful
By TheDeathlyCow — “A Frosty Vanilla+ Survival Experience,” and the most mechanically deep of the pack’s winter-flavor mods. Adds a full cold/freezing survival layer on top of vanilla, all currently running at shipped defaults (config/frostiful.json, no server tuning applied):

Environmental cold: nights and cold/freezing biomes shift ambient temperature down (night −1, cold biome −1, freezing biome −3), wetness from rain or touching water increases freezing rate, and standing near light sources or fire provides passive warmth.
Freezing mechanics: passive freezing is currently disabled by default (doPassiveFreezing: false), as is ambient wind spawning — meaning the more punishing weather-hazard side of the mod isn’t actively harassing players in this world, though the underlying systems (icicles, frost damage, wind particles) are present and configurable.
Icicles: form during weather when light levels are low enough (max light 8, min skylight 11 to form), can grow more during rain/thunder, become unstable and fall, and can be thrown as weapons — a thrown icicle deals 1 base + 3 extra damage and applies a large freeze buildup.
New hostile content: “Chillager” patrols (a frost-themed pillager variant) are enabled, Strays now carry Frost Arrows, and a “Frostologer” enemy type has its own heat-drain and passive-freezing combat kit — including an intolerance to heat (takes bonus damage/effects above a heat threshold).
Combat items: an Ice Breaker weapon (base 3 damage + 1 per level), a Frost Wand (25-block max range, 120-tick cooldown, roots targets for 100 ticks), and Packed Snowballs that both freeze (500 units) and deal bonus damage to freeze-vulnerable enemy types.
Netherite gear grants innate frost resistance (0.5), and gear can generate with Fur or Skate armor-trim upgrade templates.

Anticipated questions
Q: Will I freeze to death on this server?
A: Passive freezing is disabled by default (doPassiveFreezing: false), as is ambient wind spawning — so the harshest weather-hazard side isn’t actively harassing players, though cold biomes and nights still lower ambient temperature and wetness speeds freezing.
Q: How do I stay warm?
A: Stand near light sources or fire for passive warmth; Netherite gear grants innate frost resistance, and gear can take Fur or Skate armor-trim upgrades.
Q: What new enemies does it add?
A: “Chillager” frost-pillager patrols, Strays that carry Frost Arrows, and the Frostologer, which has a heat-drain/passive-freezing combat kit but takes bonus damage above a heat threshold. See Progression & Level Caps for threat context.
Q: What are the icicles for?
A: They form during weather at low light, become unstable and fall, and can be thrown as a weapon (1 base + 3 extra damage plus a large freeze buildup).

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: Geophilic
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
Geophilic
By bebebea_loste (also responsible for Explorify) — described as “a subtle-ish overhaul of vanilla Overworld biomes.” Rather than adding wholly new biomes the way Regions Unexplored does, Geophilic reworks the look and feel of existing vanilla biomes for more visual variety on the ground, aiming to stay recognizably vanilla rather than exotic. No server-side config override is present.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: Mine Cells
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
Mine Cells
By Mim1q — brings the roguelike dungeon-crawler Dead Cells into Minecraft nearly wholesale, complete with an in-game Patchouli guidebook (minecells_guidebook) documenting every dimension, boss, mob, and weapon. Players enter through randomly-spawned Doorways in the Overworld — each Doorway displays coordinates rounded to multiples of 1024, and two doorways sharing the same displayed coordinates always lead to the same instance of the dungeon. Doorways can be broken, carried, and replaced, and Dimensional Runes (granted on first visiting a dimension) let players redirect an existing Doorway to a new destination.
The dimension chain, in intended progression order: Prisoners’ Quarters (former holding cells for the criminal and diseased) → Promenade of the Condemned (open-ground swarm fights, houses the required Vine Rune for further progress) → Ramparts (guard towers, heavily populated with monsters — note the server explicitly disables Ramparts’ vanilla fall-death protection, letting players explore its depths at their own risk) → Black Bridge, guarded by the boss Concierge → Insufferable Crypt, guarded by the boss Conjunctivius.
Bosses: the Concierge is a mutated former prison guard who fights close-range with knockback-fist attacks and fire-shockwave gauntlets, then escalates to leaping crush attacks as his health drops. Conjunctivius is a chain-bound mutated mass that dashes (telegraphed by a red particle beam), fires toxic tears, and — at a health threshold — becomes temporarily invulnerable while summoning Sewer’s Tentacles to fight in her place.
Regular enemies span a real bestiary: Buzzcutter (flying fang-attackers), Grenadier (long-range explosive lobber), Inquisitor (wall-piercing magic orbs), Leaping Zombie (common jumper), Mutated Bat (fragile but unpredictable dash-striker), Protector (grants nearby monsters temporary invulnerability, harmless alone — a priority kill-target), Runner (heavy melee, teleports to fleeing players), Sewer’s Tentacle (ambushes from underground), Shieldbearer (immune to frontal attacks, periodically shield-charges), Sweeper (flaming shockwave sweep), and Undead Archer.
Loot/weapons are extensive and mechanically distinct rather than reskins — the Cursed Sword instantly kills its wielder on any hit taken in exchange for high power, the Blood Sword stacks a Bleeding effect that detonates at 7 stacks, the Phaser teleports the player behind a nearby enemy, the Tentacle weapon is a grapple/mobility tool as much as a weapon, and there’s a full parry-focused shield line (Rampart, Bloodthirsty, Assault, Greed, Ice, Cudgel) alongside multiple specialized bows and crossbows. Elevators (crafted from Elevator Assemblers + chains, or naturally spawned) provide vertical traversal within dungeon dimensions.
Server tuning (config/minecells-common.json5, config/minecells-client.json5): disableFallProtection: true (Ramparts fall damage is live), unlockedBossEntry: false (default — boss-room doors stay locked/one-way as intended), autoWipeData: true (dungeon data auto-resets after major mod updates), elevator max assembly height 256 blocks at default speed/acceleration, and Conjunctivius’s tentacle-weapon max stretch distance left at the default 24 blocks. This makes Mine Cells one of the two “meatiest” dungeon mods in the exploration category alongside Aquamirae.
Anticipated questions
Q: How do I get into the dungeon?
A: Enter through randomly-spawned Doorways in the Overworld. Each shows coordinates rounded to multiples of 1024, and two Doorways with the same displayed coordinates always lead to the same dungeon instance; Dimensional Runes let you redirect a Doorway.
Q: What’s the progression order?
A: Prisoners’ Quarters → Promenade of the Condemned (holds the required Vine Rune) → Ramparts → Black Bridge (boss: Concierge) → Insufferable Crypt (boss: Conjunctivius).
Q: How dangerous is it, and can I die from falling?
A: Very — Ramparts has its vanilla fall-death protection disabled on this server (disableFallProtection: true), so you explore its depths at your own risk, on top of a large hostile bestiary. See Progression & Level Caps.
Q: Are the weapons worth it?
A: They’re mechanically distinct, not reskins — e.g. the Cursed Sword (huge power but any hit taken kills you), the Blood Sword (Bleeding stacks that detonate at 7), and the Phaser (teleports you behind an enemy), plus a full parry-shield line. There’s also an in-game Patchouli guidebook documenting everything.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: Moog's Structure Lib
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
Moog’s Structure Lib
Moog’s Structure Lib (jar moogs_structure_lib-1.1.0-1.20-1.20.4-fabric.jar, by FinnDog, mod id moogs_structures) is a small shared library mod described simply as “A library mod for generating structures.” It has no player-facing content of its own — no structures, no items — but is the required dependency that Moog’s Voyager Structures declares in its fabric.mod.json ("moogs_structures": "*"), and would equally be required by any other Moog’s-family structure mod (such as the not-currently-installed Moog’s End Structures).
Functionally it fills the same role for the “Moog’s” mod family that YUNG’s API fills for the YUNG’s suite: shared structure-placement/generation code that keeps the sibling mods from duplicating boilerplate.
Anticipated questions
Q: Does Moog’s Structure Lib add anything I can find in-world?
A: No — it has no player-facing content, no structures and no items. It’s a shared library (“A library mod for generating structures”).
Q: Why is it in the pack?
A: It’s the required dependency Moog’s Voyager Structures declares ("moogs_structures": "*"); without it that mod won’t load.
Q: How does it compare to YUNG’s API?
A: It fills the same role for the Moog’s family that YUNG’s API fills for the YUNG’s suite — shared structure-placement/generation code so sibling mods don’t duplicate boilerplate.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
Moog’s Voyager Structures
Moog’s Voyager Structures (jar MoogsVoyagerStructures-1.20-5.0.4.jar, by FinnDog) adds — per its own description — “life, fun and variety to your Minecraft world! Explore awesome new structures made with vanilla blocks and entities, and discover loot, enemies, and villagers along the way.” It’s explicitly built to “keep the vanilla feel of the game” rather than introduce a distinct art style, and its jar contains 285 .nbt structure files — a scale comparable to Philip’s Ruins in this pack.
It declares a hard dependency on moogs_structures in its fabric.mod.json, i.e. on Moog’s Structure Lib, which must be present for it to load. This server also carries a small companion jar, lootintegrations_moog-1.8.jar, which patches Moog’s structure loot tables to integrate with other installed mods’ items rather than staying vanilla-only — a detail worth knowing if a Moog structure’s chest loot looks more varied than expected.
Anticipated questions
Q: Where do these structures generate?
A: Across the Overworld — new structures built with vanilla blocks and entities, keeping the vanilla feel. See Finding Structures & Exploration for tracking them down.
Q: What’s inside them?
A: Loot, enemies, and villagers, per the mod’s own description. Chest loot can look more varied than expected because the companion lootintegrations_moog-1.8.jar patches its loot tables to include other installed mods’ items.
Q: How much content does it add?
A: Its jar contains 285 .nbt structure files — a scale comparable to Philip’s Ruins.
Q: Does it need anything else to work?
A: Yes — it hard-depends on Moog’s Structure Lib (moogs_structures), which must be present for it to load.

Nature’s Compass
Explorer’s Compass’s sister mod, also by ChaosTheDude — instead of structures, it locates the nearest instance of a chosen biome (a genuinely useful pairing given how many biome-adding mods run in this pack: Regions Unexplored, Geophilic, River Redux, Swampier Swamps, and others). No biomes are blacklisted from search.

A: No — it’s configured with unlimited compass durability and zero XP cost per search.

Q: How does it relate to Explorer’s Compass?
A: It’s the sister mod by the same author (Explorer’s Compass) and is configured to match; Explorer’s Compass locates structures, Nature’s Compass locates biomes.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: Nether Depths Upgrade
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
Nether Depths Upgrade
By Scouter — gives the Nether’s lava seas an actual ecosystem, turning “swim through lava” from a death sentence into a survivable (with prep) activity worth doing. Adds an entire school of lava-dwelling fish: Blazefish, Bonefish, Wither Bonefish, Eyeball Fish, Fortress Grouper, Glowdine, Lava Pufferfish, Magma Cube Fish, Obsidianfish, Searing Cod, and the hostile Soul Sucker. Each is genuinely useful, not just decorative — they can be fished with a dedicated Lava Bobber (a lava-compatible fishing rod bobber) and brewed/bottled into potions: Potion of Lava Vision (see clearly underlava), Potion of Glowing (from Glowdine), Potion of Wither (from Lava Pufferfish), and Potion of the Steadfast Treader (a resistance effect, from Obsidianfish) — each available as base, splash, lingering, and tipped-arrow variants.
The mod also adds a new enchantment, Hell Strider, which grants speed and ease of movement while swimming through molten rock, plus new blocks: Crimson/Warped Kelp and Seagrass (lava-safe aquatic plants), Lava Glass, and Lava Sponges (regular and “wet”) for soaking up lava the way vanilla sponges soak up water. No server-side config override exists — it runs at shipped defaults.
Anticipated questions
Q: Is swimming the Nether’s lava seas survivable now?
A: With prep, yes — the mod turns “swim through lava” into a survivable activity worth doing, giving the lava seas a full ecosystem.
Q: How do I catch the lava fish?
A: With a dedicated Lava Bobber, a lava-compatible fishing-rod bobber.
Q: What are the fish good for?
A: They brew/bottle into potions — Lava Vision, Glowing (from Glowdine), Wither (from Lava Pufferfish), and Steadfast Treader (from Obsidianfish) — each in base, splash, lingering, and tipped-arrow variants.
Q: Is there anything to help me move through lava?
A: Yes — the Hell Strider enchantment grants speed and ease of movement while swimming through molten rock.
Q: Any hostile mobs to watch for?
A: The Soul Sucker is the hostile addition among the otherwise-useful fish.

Philip’s Ruins
Philip’s Ruins (jar PhilipsRuins1.20.1-5.7-Fabric.jar, by Philip) is a pure structure-generator mod — its own description is blunt: “It adds over 200 new structures to your Minecraft world.” Counting the actual .nbt structure files packed into the jar confirms 287 individual structures, organized into a wide range of structure_set definitions (e.g. ancient_crypt, ancient_dungeon, and many more) so they spread across different biomes and generation rules rather than piling into one category.
This server also loads a Philip’s Ruins × Better End compatibility datapack (config/paxi/datapacks/ichphilipp-s-endcity-better-end-1-18-1.zip, delivered through the Paxi datapack-loader mod), which reworks one of Philip’s Ruins’ End-city-style structures to fit properly into Better End’s custom End biomes rather than vanilla End terrain. No standalone config/ file exists for the mod itself, so its structure rarity/spawn weighting runs at the values baked into that compat-aware default.
Anticipated questions
Q: How many structures does this add, and where?
A: Over 200 by its description — 287 actual .nbt files — spread across many biomes via a wide range of structure_set definitions (e.g. ancient_crypt, ancient_dungeon). See Finding Structures & Exploration.
Q: Does it work with Better End’s custom End?
A: Yes — the server loads a Philip’s Ruins × Better End compat datapack (via Paxi) that reworks one of its End-city-style structures to fit Better End’s End biomes rather than vanilla End terrain.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: Regions Unexplored
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
Regions Unexplored
Regions Unexplored (jar RegionsUnexploredFabric-0.5.6+1.20.1.jar, by UHQ_Games with contributions from KirboSoftware and Loxi) is a large Overworld biome-expansion mod — its own description says “almost 70 new biomes,” and the server’s config file (config/regions_unexplored/regions_unexplored-common.toml) confirms 82 individual biome toggles, essentially all left at their default true. The added biomes range from familiar-sounding variants (Boreal Taiga, Cold Boreal Taiga, Frozen Pine Taiga, Cold River, Gravel Beach, Grassy Beach) to genuinely novel terrain types: Fungal Fen, Hyacinth Deeps, Mycotoxic Undergrowth, Scorching Caves, Redstone Hell, Bayou, Joshua Desert, Baobab Savanna, Rocky Reef, Tropical River, Willow Forest, Eucalyptus Forest, Bamboo Forest, Smouldering Woodland, Redwoods, Towering Cliffs, Mauve Hills, Outback, Arid Mountains, Highland Fields, Alpha Grove, Barley Fields, Orchard, Temperate Grove, Clover Plains, Rainforest, and more.
The only feature disabled in config is toggle_custom_regions = false — an unrelated experimental “custom regions” system, not a biome. Every actual biome toggle is on, so this pack runs Regions Unexplored at essentially full breadth. The mod also ships several regions_unexplored-secondary-region-*.toml.bak files (disabled/backed-up secondary region configs), suggesting the region-layering system beyond the primary/common config isn’t actively customized here either.
Anticipated questions
Q: How many biomes does it add?
A: Almost 70 by its description; the config confirms 82 biome toggles, essentially all left at true, so it runs at near-full breadth. Locate specific ones with Nature’s Compass / Finding Structures & Exploration.
Q: What kinds of biomes?
A: From familiar variants (Boreal Taiga, Cold River, Gravel Beach) to genuinely novel terrain — Fungal Fen, Hyacinth Deeps, Mycotoxic Undergrowth, Scorching Caves, Redstone Hell, Bayou, Baobab Savanna, and many more.
Q: Is anything disabled?
A: Only toggle_custom_regions = false — an unrelated experimental “custom regions” system, not a biome. Every actual biome toggle is on.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
Sky Villages
Sky Villages (jar SkyVillages-1.0.4-1.19.2-1.20.1-fabric.jar, by Y3SON and Aurelj) does exactly what it says: villages generate floating in the clouds instead of on the ground, “entirely randomly,” with each sky town having “a distinctive and unique look.” Its structure set is built the same way vanilla villages are — modular building pieces keyed to villager professions — confirmed by the mod’s own .nbt files: weaponsmith, mason, loom, librarian, fletcher, cartographer, and alchemist houses, plus farm plots, a fountain, a plain villager house, five separate bridge-piece variants for connecting the floating platforms, and a standalone villager-spawn piece.
This server loads Sky Villages with five cross-mod compatibility datapacks via Paxi (config/paxi/datapacks/): compat patches for The Graveyard, Waystones, Supplementaries, Practical Plushies, and Farmer’s Delight. In practice this means Sky Villages’ loot tables, decor blocks, and/or structure pieces have been adjusted to properly incorporate items and blocks from those other installed mods rather than just falling back to plain vanilla equivalents.

Q: Where do these villages generate?
A: Floating in the clouds instead of on the ground, placed entirely randomly, each with a distinctive look. See Finding Structures & Exploration.

A: Modular villager-profession buildings (weaponsmith, mason, loom, librarian, fletcher, cartographer, alchemist), farm plots, a fountain, bridge pieces linking the platforms, and villager-spawn pieces — built like vanilla villages.
Q: Does its loot include items from other mods?

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: Swampier Swamps
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
Swampier Swamps
By andrew0030 — overhauls the Swamp biome and the Wild Update’s mangrove-swamp additions with several small but interconnected systems, all live at their shipped defaults (config/swampier_swamps.json5):

Moist Fertile Farmland: farmland within 3 blocks of water can turn into a more fertile variant, and crops there grow 6x faster than vanilla.
Swamp Gas: an explosive, poisonous gas hazard (explosion strength 6, applies negative effects like Poison to anything that walks through the cloud) that also works as furnace fuel (4000-tick burn time).
“Swallow Me Waldo” frogs: a named frog that can swallow and effectively kill entities, dealing double its 10-base damage by default — capable of taking down very tough mobs if left unchecked.
Growing Lily Pads: Small → Regular → Large Lily Pads grow over time and spawn more around themselves; they also sink under large entities standing on them and eventually break (rather than just going collision-less).
Bald Cypress trees: can grow from 2x2 Oak sapling plantings (like vanilla’s Jungle-tree mechanic), enabled in all biomes on this server.
Altered brewing recipes: the Leaping potion now uses Frog Legs instead of Rabbit Paws, and a new Luck potion recipe uses Rabbit Paws.

Anticipated questions
Q: What does it change about swamps?
A: It overhauls the Swamp and mangrove-swamp with several interconnected systems at shipped defaults — fertile farmland, swamp gas, special frogs, growing lily pads, bald cypress trees, and altered brewing.
Q: Is anything here dangerous?
A: Yes — Swamp Gas is an explosive, poisonous hazard (explosion strength 6, applies Poison), and the “Swallow Me Waldo” frog can swallow and effectively kill entities, dealing double its 10-base damage.
Q: Any farming benefit?
A: Moist Fertile Farmland — farmland within 3 blocks of water can become a fertile variant where crops grow 6x faster than vanilla.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: The Graveyard
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
The Graveyard
The Graveyard (jar The_Graveyard_3.1_(FABRIC)_for_1.20.1.jar, by Finallion; the jar filename says 3.1 while its internal fabric.mod.json still reports version 3.0) adds “new bosses, structures, mobs and blocks themed around the graveyard.” Its structures range from small roadside graves (with desert, savanna, and mountain biome-specific variants) up through crypts, small and large graveyards, a memorial tree, a giant mushroom grave, a haunted house, and altar/ruins structures.
The server’s config (config/graveyard/the-graveyard-3.0-config.json5) leaves every structure enabled, but tunes the mob and loot side:

Mobs: ghoul (weight 25, groups of 2–5, burns in sunlight), reaper (weight 5, groups of 2–3), and nightmare (weight 10, solo, does not burn in sunlight) are all active. A fourth mob, corrupted_pillager, is explicitly disabled (enabled: false, weight 0) — it ships with the mod but doesn’t spawn on this server.
Hordes: the horde-spawn event is enabled, attempting up to 40 mob spawns roughly once per Minecraft day (24000 ticks) with up to 1200 ticks of random jitter.
Loot: urns are configured with a double-chest inventory (urnHasDoubleInventory: true), giving more loot per urn than the mod’s default single-chest size.
Boss: the Corrupted Champion (summoned via staff fragments) runs a full multiphase fight — 400 HP in its casting phase, 200 HP hunting phase, 14 armor/12 toughness, and spell abilities including corpse-falling, healing, levitation, and skull projectiles, capping at 30 summoned minions in groups of up to 5. The large graveyard’s wither-skeleton spawner is left as-is (disableWitherSkeletonSpawner: false), i.e. not swapped down to a plain skeleton spawner.

Because it adds real boss/mob content, it’s also referenced from Creatures, Bosses & Mobs in the parent category note.
Anticipated questions
Q: What’s inside The Graveyard’s structures?
A: Everything from small roadside graves (desert/savanna/mountain variants) through crypts, small/large graveyards, a memorial tree, a giant mushroom grave, a haunted house, and altar/ruins — all enabled in config.
Q: What mobs will I face, and how dangerous?
A: Ghouls (weight 25, burn in sunlight), reapers (weight 5), and nightmares (weight 10, don’t burn in sunlight); a horde event attempts up to 40 spawns roughly once per Minecraft day. The corrupted_pillager is disabled and won’t spawn here. See Bosses & Recommended Levels.
Q: Is there a boss?
A: Yes — the Corrupted Champion (summoned via staff fragments), a multiphase fight: 400 HP casting / 200 HP hunting, 14 armor / 12 toughness, with corpse-fall, healing, levitation, and skull-projectile spells, up to 30 minions.
Q: Is the loot better here?
A: Urns use a double-chest inventory (urnHasDoubleInventory: true), giving more loot per urn than the mod’s default single-chest size.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: Towns and Towers
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
Towns and Towers
A structure-overhaul mod (by Kubek, Biban_Auriu and Cristelknight999, built on the cristellib/kaisyn structure framework) that replaces vanilla villages and pillager outposts with new, more detailed builds, and adds pillager outposts to every biome that previously lacked one — badlands, beach, birch forest, desert, flower forest, forest, grove, jungle, meadow, mushroom fields, ocean, old-growth taiga, savanna, snowy beach/plains/slopes, sparse jungle, sunflower plains, swamp, taiga, snowy taiga, and wooded badlands, plus cross-mod exclusives (e.g. a Mediterranean-biome outpost for compatible worldgen mods). It also ships themed loot tables for its structures — Mediterranean, piglin, badlands, jungle, mushroom, and swamp house variants each have their own bespoke barrel/chest loot. All structure toggles are enabled and spacing/separation values are left at their documented defaults (villages/outposts ~48/24 chunks apart) in config/towns_and_towers/.
This is one of four village/settlement-overhaul mods running simultaneously in the pack (alongside ChoiceTheorem’s Overhauled Village, Integrated Villages, and Villagers Plus) — their scopes are complementary rather than truly redundant: Towns and Towers rebuilds vanilla village/outpost structures and adds biome coverage, CTOV adds entirely new biome-themed village variants (including small/medium/large size tiers), Integrated Villages changes village mechanics and Create integration, and Villagers Plus adds new villager professions and trades on top of whichever structures generate.
Anticipated questions
Q: What does Towns and Towers change?
A: It replaces vanilla villages and pillager outposts with more detailed builds and adds pillager outposts to nearly every biome that previously lacked one. See Finding Structures & Exploration.
Q: Which biomes get new outposts?
A: Badlands, beach, birch forest, desert, flower forest, forest, grove, jungle, meadow, mushroom fields, ocean, old-growth taiga, savanna, snowy variants, sparse jungle, sunflower plains, swamp, taiga, and wooded badlands — plus cross-mod exclusives like a Mediterranean outpost.
Q: Does it have its own loot?
A: Yes — themed loot tables (Mediterranean, piglin, badlands, jungle, mushroom, and swamp house variants) each with bespoke barrel/chest loot.
Q: How does it fit with the other village mods?
A: It’s one of four complementary village mods — it rebuilds vanilla structures and adds biome coverage, while ChoiceTheorem’s Overhauled Village, Integrated Villages, and Villagers Plus handle new variants, mechanics, and professions.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: Villagers Plus
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
Villagers Plus
Adds four new villager professions — Alchemist, Occultist, Horticulturist, and Oceanographer — each with their own workstation building and trade pool, and each buildable into any of CTOV/Towns and Towers’ biome village variants (plains, taiga, savanna, snowy, desert weights are all configured per-biome in config/villagersplus.json5; the Oceanographer’s workstation is weighted highest at 15 versus 10 for the others in every biome). Villagers gain up to 2 new trade offers per profession level (max), and the Wandering Trader can carry up to 5.
The standout mechanical detail: the Alchemist’s workstation can explode. can_explode is enabled with an explosion_chance of “1 in 3” per interaction — a genuine risk/reward element baked into what’s otherwise a peaceful villager-trading mod. There’s also an Enchanted Basin that stores up to 500 XP, transferring 50 per interaction, letting players bank experience with a villager rather than only via bottles.
This is the fourth of the pack’s village-overhaul mods, but unlike the other three it doesn’t touch village generation at all — it only adds new professions/trades/workstations that populate whatever villages CTOV, Towns and Towers, and Integrated Villages produce.
Anticipated questions
Q: What new villagers does it add?
A: Four professions — Alchemist, Occultist, Horticulturist, and Oceanographer — each with its own workstation and trade pool, buildable into CTOV / Towns and Towers village variants.
Q: Is there any risk to trading with them?
A: Yes — the Alchemist’s workstation can explode, with can_explode enabled at a 1-in-3 chance per interaction: a genuine risk/reward element.
Q: Can I store XP with a villager?
A: Yes — the Enchanted Basin stores up to 500 XP, transferring 50 per interaction.
Q: Does it change village generation?
A: No — unlike the other three village mods, it only adds professions/trades/workstations to whatever villages CTOV, Towns and Towers, and Integrated Villages produce.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: When Dungeons Arise
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
When Dungeons Arise
When Dungeons Arise (jar DungeonsArise-1.20.x-2.1.58-fabric-release.jar, by Aureljz, DiamondTown & Zephyrusj) is one of the biggest single contributors of hand-built content in the pack: its data/dungeons_arise/structures/ folder ships 42 distinct structure families, most with several NBT variants for different mob loadouts or loot tiers (e.g. the Undead Pirate Ship has separate captain, ranged-skeleton and skeleton-juggernaut variants; the Wishing Well has five potion-effect variants — speed, regen, wither, resistance, haste — plus a no-effect fallback). Notable finds include the Coliseum, the Illager Castle/Fort/Hall/Windmill/Corsair/Galley set, the airship-themed Heavenly Rider/Conqueror/Challenger, the mythology-flavored Typhon and Ceryneian Hind bosses, the Foundry, Mining System and Scorched Mines, the Shiraz Palace, Keep Kayra, Plague Asylum, Bandit Village/Towers, the Mushroom Village/House/Mines trio, Greenwood Pub/Towers, a Bathhouse, Jungle Tree House, Monastery, Lighthouse, Aviary, Merchant Campsite, Small Blimp, Small Prairie House, Fishing Hut, Infested/Abandoned Temples, and a Mechanical Nest.
Many structures award Explorer Map filled-map items (e.g. “Illager Castle Explorer Map”) tied to advancement triggers, nudging players toward specific landmarks rather than pure random wandering. No dedicated config file exists under prominence2/config/ for this mod, so it’s running with the pack’s default spawn rarity and structure toggles — unlike the YUNG’s suite, nothing here has been hand-tuned for this server.
Anticipated questions
Q: How much does it add?
A: 42 distinct structure families, most with several NBT variants for different mob loadouts or loot tiers — one of the biggest hand-built content contributors in the pack. See Finding Structures & Exploration.
Q: What are some notable finds?
A: The Coliseum, the Illager Castle/Fort/Hall set, airship-themed Heavenly Rider/Conqueror/Challenger, mythology bosses Typhon and Ceryneian Hind, the Foundry, Shiraz Palace, Keep Kayra, Plague Asylum, and many more.
Q: How do I locate its structures?
A: Many award Explorer Map items (e.g. “Illager Castle Explorer Map”) tied to advancement triggers, nudging you toward specific landmarks rather than pure wandering. See Bosses & Recommended Levels for the boss-bearing structures.
Q: Is its rarity tuned on this server?
A: No — no dedicated config file exists, so it runs at default spawn rarity and structure toggles, unlike the hand-tuned YUNG’s suite.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: Winterly
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
Winterly
By PinkGoosik and VioletSomik — a lighter, more decoration-focused winter-expansion mod that complements Frostiful’s survival-mechanics depth. Generates new cold-biome terrain features by default: underground icicles, Cryomarble deposits, and frozen grass/flowers. Also adds gift boxes (server-configured to hold up to 3 items) for a holiday-flavor loot/gifting mechanic. One feature is explicitly disabled on this server: seasonal mobDecorations (cosmetic winter dressing on mobs, meant to only trigger during an in-game “winter” period) is turned off (config/winterly.json: "enabled": false), so mobs do not get winter cosmetic reskins here.
Anticipated questions
Q: What does Winterly add?
A: A lighter, decoration-focused winter expansion — new cold-biome terrain features by default (underground icicles, Cryomarble deposits, frozen grass/flowers) plus gift boxes.
Q: What are the gift boxes?
A: A holiday-flavor loot/gifting mechanic; they’re server-configured to hold up to 3 items.
Q: Do mobs get winter reskins here?
A: No — the seasonal mobDecorations feature is explicitly disabled on this server ("enabled": false), so mobs get no winter cosmetic dressing.
Q: How does it relate to Frostiful?
A: It complements Frostiful’s survival-mechanics depth with decoration-focused content.
