Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: YUNG's API
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
YUNG’s API
YUNG’s API (jar YungsApi-1.20-Fabric-4.0.6.jar) is the shared library underpinning every other YUNG’s mod in the pack. Its fabric.mod.json describes it plainly: “API Library for YUNG’s minecraft mods.” It has no gameplay content of its own — no structures, no items — but supplies the common jigsaw/structure-piece placement code, world-gen utilities, and the Cloth Config-based configuration-screen framework that all ten downstream YUNG’s mods (the nine “Better X” structure overhauls plus YUNG’s Bridges) declare as a hard dependency (YUNG’s Bridges, for example, requires yungsapi >= 1.20-Fabric-4.0.1). There is no standalone config file for it under prominence2/config/ — it just needs to be present and version-matched for the rest of the suite to load.
If YUNG’s API is ever missing or version-mismatched, every other YUNG’s mod in this pack will fail to load, so it’s effectively load-bearing infrastructure rather than a mod players will ever notice directly.
Anticipated questions
Q: Does YUNG’s API add anything I can find in-game?
A: No — it has no gameplay content, no structures, no items. It’s the shared library (“API Library for YUNG’s minecraft mods”).
Q: Why is it required?
A: It supplies the jigsaw/structure-piece placement code, world-gen utilities, and Cloth Config-based config-screen framework that all ten downstream YUNG’s mods declare as a hard dependency.
Q: What happens if it’s missing or version-mismatched?
A: Every other YUNG’s mod in the pack fails to load — it’s effectively load-bearing infrastructure players never notice directly.

YUNG’s Better Desert Temples
YUNG’s Better Desert Temples (jar YungsBetterDesertTemples-1.20-Fabric-3.0.3.jar, by YUNGNICKYOUNG & Tera) redesigns the vanilla desert pyramid — which in vanilla is little more than a decorative shell around one TNT-trapped loot room — into a larger, more elaborate temple with expanded rooms and puzzle elements.
Server config (config/betterdeserttemples-fabric-1_20.toml) sets disableVanillaPyramids = true, so vanilla desert pyramids no longer generate at all — every desert pyramid players find is this mod’s version. It also enables applyMiningFatigue = true, meaning parts of the temple apply a Mining Fatigue effect to discourage brute-forcing through walls instead of solving the temple’s traps/puzzles legitimately.
Anticipated questions
Q: What changes about desert temples?
A: The vanilla pyramid (a shell around one TNT-trapped loot room) is redesigned into a larger temple with expanded rooms and puzzle elements. See Finding Structures & Exploration.
Q: Will I still find vanilla pyramids?
A: No — disableVanillaPyramids = true, so every desert pyramid is this mod’s version.
Q: Anything stopping me digging straight to the loot?
A: Yes — applyMiningFatigue = true applies Mining Fatigue in parts of the temple to discourage brute-forcing through walls instead of solving the traps/puzzles.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
YUNG’s Better Dungeons
YUNG’s Better Dungeons (jar YungsBetterDungeons-1.20-Fabric-4.0.4.jar, by YUNGNICKYOUNG & Acarii) replaces the plain vanilla mob-spawner dungeon (a single small room with cobblestone/mossy-cobblestone walls and two chests) with a “complete redesign” — bigger, themed dungeon layouts with more loot and more varied mob-spawner setups, including an entirely separate Nether-flavored dungeon variant.
The server’s config (config/betterdungeons-fabric-1_20.toml) confirms removeVanillaDungeons = true, so this mod fully takes over dungeon generation rather than running alongside vanilla ones. It also enables mob-head decorations (enableHeads = true) and Nether-block decor (enableNetherBlocks = true) in dungeons, allows ore-cluster prop rooms in small dungeons (enableOreProps = true), caps banners at 2 and chests at 1–2 for small dungeons, and limits the zombie dungeon’s surface staircase to 20 blocks. Notably, the small Nether dungeon variant is disabled on this server ([betterDungeons.smallNetherDungeon] enabled = false) — its wither-skeleton-skull-drop and blaze-rod-drop tuning is present in the file but moot since the variant never generates.
Anticipated questions
Q: What replaces the vanilla dungeon?
A: Bigger, themed dungeon layouts with more loot and more varied mob-spawner setups, including an entirely separate Nether-flavored variant.
Q: Will vanilla dungeons still generate?
A: No — removeVanillaDungeons = true, so this mod fully takes over dungeon generation.
Q: Is the Nether dungeon variant active here?
A: No — the small Nether dungeon is disabled on this server (smallNetherDungeon enabled = false), so it never generates despite its tuning being present in the file.
Q: What decorations are enabled?
A: Mob-head decorations, Nether-block decor, and ore-cluster prop rooms in small dungeons; small dungeons cap banners at 2 and chests at 1–2.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
YUNG’s Better Mineshafts
YUNG’s Better Mineshafts (jar YungsBetterMineshafts-1.20-Fabric-4.0.4.jar, by YUNGNICKYOUNG) is described in-mod as “the long-awaited and much-needed abandoned mineshaft overhaul.” It rebuilds the sprawling, often-messy vanilla mineshaft into more structured shaft systems with dedicated ore-deposit rooms, workstation side-rooms (with their own cellar variant), and configurable decoration density.
The server config (config/bettermineshafts-fabric-1_20.toml) is one of the more heavily tuned YUNG’s configs in the pack:

Vertical bounds: minY = -55, maxY = 30 — controls how deep/shallow the shaft floor can generate.
disableVanillaMineshafts = true — vanilla mineshafts are fully replaced.
Spawn rates: lanterns 0.67%, torches 2%, workstations 2.5%, workstation cellars 25% (of workstations), small side-shafts 7%, cobwebs 15%, small-shaft minecart-with-chest 0.125%, main-shaft minecart-with-chest 1%, TNT minecarts ~0.25% each, zombie-villager room chance 2, small-shaft piece chain length 9.
Ore deposit weights (must sum to 100, and do): cobblestone 50, coal 20, iron 9, redstone 7, gold 7, lapis 3, emerald 3, diamond 1 — a deliberately rare diamond deposit relative to the others.

Anticipated questions
Q: What does it change about mineshafts?
A: It rebuilds the messy vanilla mineshaft into structured shaft systems with dedicated ore-deposit rooms, workstation side-rooms (with a cellar variant), and configurable decoration density.
Q: How deep do they generate?
A: Vertical bounds are minY = -55 to maxY = 30; vanilla mineshafts are fully replaced (disableVanillaMineshafts = true).
Q: What are my chances of finding diamonds in the ore rooms?
A: Low by design — ore-deposit weights are cobblestone 50, coal 20, iron 9, redstone 7, gold 7, lapis 3, emerald 3, diamond 1 (out of 100), making diamond deliberately rare.
Q: Any hidden dangers?
A: Yes — TNT minecarts spawn at ~0.25% each, alongside chest minecarts and cobwebs (15%).

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: YUNG's Better Strongholds
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
YUNG’s Better Strongholds
YUNG’s Better Strongholds (jar YungsBetterStrongholds-1.20-Fabric-4.0.3.jar, by YUNGNICKYOUNG & Acarii) is a “complete redesign of Minecraft’s strongholds,” rebuilding the maze of samey corridors and libraries into a more coherent, larger layout leading to the End Portal room.
Unlike most of its siblings, this mod’s config (config/betterstrongholds-fabric-1_20.toml) has no disableVanilla... toggle — since strongholds are a singular structure type rather than one of several variants, this mod’s generator simply is the stronghold generator once installed. What it does tune is decoration/hazard density: cobweb replacement chance is 10% in normal rooms and 30% in spawner rooms (making the stronghold’s silverfish spawner rooms noticeably webbier and more dangerous), torch spawn rate 10%, and lantern spawn rate 20%.
Anticipated questions
Q: What changes about strongholds?
A: The maze of samey corridors and libraries becomes a more coherent, larger layout leading to the End Portal room. See Finding Structures & Exploration.
Q: Is there a disable-vanilla toggle like the other YUNG’s mods?
A: No — strongholds are a singular structure type, so this mod simply is the stronghold generator once installed.
Q: Are the silverfish spawner rooms more dangerous here?
A: Yes — cobweb replacement is 30% in spawner rooms (vs 10% in normal rooms), making them noticeably webbier and more dangerous; torches spawn at 10%, lanterns at 20%.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
YUNG’s Better Witch Huts
YUNG’s Better Witch Huts (jar YungsBetterWitchHuts-1.20-Fabric-3.0.3.jar, by YUNGNICKYOUNG & Acarii) adds “new and improved witch huts to swamps” — replacing the vanilla single-room stilt hut (one cauldron, one crafting table, a witch) with an expanded structure with more rooms and loot.
Server config (config/betterwitchhuts-fabric-1_20.toml) sets disableVanillaWitchHuts = true, so every swamp hut generated on this world is this mod’s redesigned version rather than the vanilla one. No further tuning is configured.
Anticipated questions
Q: What’s improved about witch huts?
A: The vanilla single-room stilt hut (one cauldron, one crafting table, a witch) becomes an expanded structure with more rooms and loot. See Finding Structures & Exploration.
Q: Will vanilla witch huts still generate?
A: No — disableVanillaWitchHuts = true, so every swamp hut on this world is this mod’s redesigned version.
Q: Any other tuning?
A: No — no further tuning is configured.

Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.title: YUNG's Bridges
Mods/Exploration,-Dungeons--and--Structu.content:
YUNG’s Bridges
YUNG’s Bridges (jar YungsBridges-1.20-Fabric-4.0.3.jar, by YUNGNICKYOUNG) is the odd one out in the YUNG’s suite — it doesn’t overhaul a vanilla structure, it adds one that never existed before: naturally-generating bridges spanning ravines, rivers, and other terrain gaps across the world, giving exploration a bit more connective tissue between landmasses instead of always needing to bridge, boat, or fly across.
No config file exists under prominence2/config/ for this mod, so it runs at its shipped defaults. Like every other YUNG’s mod it hard-depends on YUNG’s API (yungsapi >= 1.20-Fabric-4.0.1 per its fabric.mod.json) for shared structure-placement code.
Anticipated questions
Q: What does YUNG’s Bridges add?
A: Naturally-generating bridges spanning ravines, rivers, and terrain gaps — it adds a new structure rather than overhauling a vanilla one. See Finding Structures & Exploration.
Q: How does that help exploration?
A: It gives exploration more connective tissue between landmasses instead of always needing to bridge, boat, or fly across gaps.
Q: Is it configured or dependent on anything?
A: It runs at shipped defaults (no config file) and hard-depends on YUNG’s API for shared structure-placement code.

Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Animal-.title: Animal Feeding Trough
Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Animal-.content:
Animal Feeding Trough
Jar: animal_feeding_trough-1.1.0+1.20.1.jar (mod id animal_feeding_trough, by Slexom). The single smallest mod covered in this category — its entire lang file is two lines, one item and one block, both just “Feeding Trough.” Unlike the other Delight-family add-ons, its fabric.mod.json doesn’t declare a hard dependency on farmersdelight; it’s a standalone quality-of-life mod that the modpack groups alongside the Farmer’s Delight add-ons thematically (farm automation) rather than technically.
The Feeding Trough is a placeable block that automatically feeds nearby farm animals from its inventory, saving players from manually right-clicking food onto every animal to trigger breeding/growth — a small automation piece that complements the much larger crop-and-cooking systems from Croptopia and Farmer’s Delight.
How you’ll use it here
Place a Feeding Trough beside your cow/pig/chicken pens and load it with the crops you’re already growing from Croptopia and Farmer’s Delight, so the animals breed and grow themselves while you’re off questing. It’s a convenience block, not a food source — you build it once you have a stable crop surplus. It matters a bit more on this server than in vanilla because hunger is heavier here and you’ll be slaughtering animals often for the meat that feeds the cooking loop, so keeping the pens stocked pays off.
Anticipated questions
Do I need Farmer’s Delight for the trough to work? No — unlike the other add-ons in this category it doesn’t hard-depend on farmersdelight; it’s a standalone quality-of-life mod grouped here for farm automation.
What do I put in it? Whatever the animals eat — the same crops you grow for the pack’s cooking loop; the trough just auto-feeds nearby animals so they breed without you right-clicking each one.
Is it worth building early? Generally only once you have a food surplus; before that your crops are better spent on the very first quest’s fruit or vegetable and on cooked meals.

Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Chef's-.title: Chef's Delight
Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Chef's-.content:
Chef’s Delight
Jar: chefs-delight-1.0.4-fabric-1.20.1.jar (mod id chefsdelight, by Redstone Games). This is the thinnest of the Farmer’s Delight add-ons in the pack — its entire en_us.json is four lines. It adds exactly two new villager professions, Cook and Chef, giving Farmer’s Delight’s cooking loop a dedicated villager trade chain (buy/sell FD ingredients and dishes through a profession built for it) instead of leaving those trades scattered across vanilla professions or absent entirely.
There’s no new block, item, or crop here — it’s a small, focused compatibility/flavor addition that hard-depends on farmersdelight (declared in its fabric.mod.json) and exists purely to give the cooking-focused half of a Farmer’s Delight village something to do for a living.
How you’ll use it here
This mod is invisible until you get a villager into the Cook or Chef profession, at which point it becomes your trade route for Farmer’s Delight ingredients and finished dishes. Set it up mid-game once you have a village and a working FD kitchen — it lets you buy the FD staples you haven’t farmed yet, or sell surplus cooked food for emeralds. There are no blocks or recipes to craft yourself here; the whole value is the villager economy it plugs into.
Anticipated questions
What does this actually add? Two villager professions, Cook and Chef, giving Farmer’s Delight’s cooking loop its own dedicated trade chain instead of leaving those trades scattered across vanilla professions or absent.
Do I need it to cook? No — cooking works fine without it; this only adds villagers to trade FD ingredients and dishes through.
How do I get a Cook villager? Generally the same way as any villager profession — an unemployed villager claims the profession’s workstation placed nearby.

Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Croptop.title: Croptopia
Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Croptop.content:
Croptopia
Jar: Croptopia-1.20.1-FABRIC-3.0.4.jar (mod id croptopia, by Thonk & Rainbowcraft2). One of the two flagship food mods in this pack, and the bigger of the two by raw item count: the en_us.json lang file carries 611 translatable entries, breaking down to roughly 414 item names and 117 block names. It adds around 45 new crops (artichoke, asparagus, bell pepper, black bean, blackberry, blueberry, broccoli, cabbage, cantaloupe, cauliflower, celery, coffee beans, corn, cranberry, cucumber, currant, eggplant, elderberry, garlic, grape, green bean, green onion, honeydew, hops, kale, kiwi, leek, lettuce, olive, onion, peanut, pineapple, radish, raspberry, rhubarb, rice, rutabaga, saguaro, spinach, squash, strawberry, sweet potato, tomatillo, tomato, turnip, yam, zucchini) each with matching seeds, plus fruit trees that spawn naturally in specific biomes (an internal treeConfig in croptopia_v3.conf maps orange, dragonfruit, and other trees to biome tags from vanilla, BYG, and Terralith).
Beyond raw crops, Croptopia adds a genuine drinks line — juices (grape, orange, apple, cranberry, saguaro, tomato, melon, pineapple) and smoothies (strawberry, banana, kale, “fruit”) — plus salt, which the config can spawn naturally in rivers (generateSaltInWorld). It ships a bundled Patchouli guide book (data/croptopia/patchouli_books/guide/) with entries covering utensils and other systems, giving new players an in-game reference instead of relying on JEI/REI alone. It suggests but doesn’t require patchouli and dehydration as soft dependencies. Croptopia and Farmer’s Delight don’t hard-depend on each other — they’re two independently-developed food overhauls that the modpack runs side by side, giving a much deeper crop roster (Croptopia) feeding into a deeper cooking system (Farmer’s Delight).
How you’ll use it here
Croptopia is your answer to the pack’s very first quest, which asks you to find a fruit or vegetable — with ~45 crops and biome-spawning fruit trees, there’s almost always something edible nearby to grab and hand in. Early game you forage strawberries, tomatoes, corn and the like and drink the juices/smoothies for quick hunger; later you farm them at scale to feed Farmer’s Delight’s cooking pots. Keep the bundled Patchouli guide book handy for what each crop and utensil does. Croptopia grows the ingredients; Farmer’s Delight turns them into the buffed meals that actually matter here.
Anticipated questions
Which mod solves the first quest (find a fruit or vegetable)? Croptopia — its crops and naturally-spawning fruit trees give you the easiest fruit or vegetable to hand in.
Croptopia or Farmer’s Delight — which do I use? Both; they don’t depend on each other. Croptopia is the deep crop roster, Farmer’s Delight is the deeper cooking system those crops feed into.
Where do I find salt? The config can spawn it naturally in rivers (generateSaltInWorld).
How do I make juices and smoothies? Croptopia adds a full juice/smoothie line; generally you craft them at Croptopia’s own utensils, which the bundled guide book documents.

Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/End's-D.title: End's Delight
Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/End's-D.content:
End’s Delight
Jar: ends_delight-refabricated-1.20.1-2.5.jar (mod id ends_delight, by FoggyHillside). A Farmer’s Delight add-on (hard-depends on farmersdelight) that takes the mod’s cooking systems into the End dimension, themed entirely around chorus fruit, shulkers, endermen, and the ender dragon. Its lang file lists 55 items and 8 blocks, including its own dedicated End Stove for End-themed cooking.
Highlights of the roster: chorus fruit gets turned into milk tea, bubble tea, wine, popsicles, sauce, and pie; shulkers yield raw/roasted/stir-fried meat, soup, and omelettes; the ender dragon itself is a food source, with raw/roasted/smoked dragon leg and steak, dragon meat stew, and even a “Fried Dragon Egg” and “Liquid Dragon Egg”/“Dragon Egg Shell” line built around the boss’s egg; endermen contribute “Enderman Gristle” and gristle stew; and there’s a full custom knife line (End Stone Knife, Purpur Knife, Dragon Tooth Knife, Dragon Egg Shell Knife) alongside dedicated blocks like Grilled Shulker, Steamed Dragon Egg, and a Chorus Fruit Crate. It’s one of the more elaborate theme add-ons in the category — effectively a full parallel cooking tree for the End, not just a handful of reskinned dishes.
How you’ll use it here
This is late-game cooking — you won’t touch it until you already have End access, but once you’re out there, chorus fruit, shulkers, endermen and even the ender dragon become a whole parallel menu (milk/bubble tea, shulker soups and omelettes, dragon steak and stew). Because prepared food gives real stat buffs on this server, it’s worth cooking your End haul on the dedicated End Stove rather than just eating chorus fruit raw. Set up an End Stove out there or bring the ingredients home.
Anticipated questions
When do I get to use this? Late game — the whole roster is built around chorus fruit, shulkers, endermen and the dragon, so you need End access first.
Do I need Farmer’s Delight? Yes — it hard-depends on farmersdelight and extends that cooking system into the End.
Is there a special workstation? Yes, its own End Stove for the End-themed dishes.

Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Expande.title: Expanded Delight
Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Expande.content:
Expanded Delight
Jar: expandeddelight-0.3.2.jar (mod id expandeddelight, by ianm1647 — the same author as Farmer’s Knives). A Farmer’s Delight add-on (hard-depends on farmersdelight) that fills in crops and pantry staples the base mod is missing, rather than theming around a dimension or mob like the other add-ons. Lang file lists 44 items and 18 blocks.
New crops: asparagus, sweet potato, chili pepper, and peanut, each carried through several dishes (asparagus soup and its creamy/bacon variants; baked sweet potato and sweet potato salad; peperonata from chili peppers; peanut butter, peanut butter sandwiches — including sweet berry and glow berry jelly combos — peanut salad, and honey peanut soup). It also adds general-purpose kitchen staples that read as infrastructure for other cooking mods: cinnamon (stick and ground), salt (mined from a “Salt Rock”), and cheese (wheel, slices, sandwiches, grilled cheese, mac and cheese), plus jams/jellies (sweet berry, glow berry), sweet rolls, and cookies (chocolate, sugar, snickerdoodle). Two new utility blocks tie it together: the Mortar and Pestle and the Juicer, used to process the new ingredients into condiments and juices (apple, sweet berry, glow berry).
How you’ll use it here
This is where your pantry staples come from — cheese, salt, cinnamon, jams and peanut butter — plus extra crops (asparagus, sweet potato, chili pepper, peanut) that the wider cooking loop leans on. Use its Mortar and Pestle and Juicer to process these into condiments and juices for Farmer’s Delight recipes. Mid-game it fills out your menu with things like grilled cheese, peanut butter sandwiches and sweet potato dishes. Think of it as infrastructure for the pack’s cooking, not a standalone theme.
Anticipated questions
What does this add over base Farmer’s Delight? The crops and pantry staples FD lacks — cheese, salt, cinnamon, jams and peanut butter, plus asparagus, sweet potato, chili pepper and peanut.
What are the Mortar and Pestle and Juicer for? Processing the new ingredients into condiments and juices used by the cooking recipes.
Do I need Farmer’s Delight? Yes — it hard-depends on farmersdelight.

Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Farmer'.title: Farmer's Delight
Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Farmer'.content:
Farmer’s Delight
Jar: FarmersDelight-1.20.1-2.4.1+refabricated.jar (mod id farmersdelight, this is the Fabric “Refabricated” port by MehVahdJukaar/MerchantPug of vectorwing’s original Forge mod). This is the anchor mod for the entire “Food, Farming & Cooking” category — six of the other eleven mods in this category (Chef’s Delight, End’s Delight, Expanded Delight, Ocean’s Delight, Farmer’s Knives, and indirectly Animal Feeding Trough) are official or community add-ons that hard-depend on it via "farmersdelight": "*" in their fabric.mod.json.
Its lang file lists 92 items and 126 blocks. Core additions: three new crops (tomato, cabbage, onion — plus rice grown from panicles) with seeds and crates; new cooking furniture — the Stove (passive cooking, replaces a furnace+campfire workflow), Cooking Pot (multi-serving stews/soups with a recipe book UI, toggle via enableRecipeBookCookingPot), Cutting Board (knife-based butchering/slicing, boosted by Fortune per cuttingBoardFortuneBonus), Skillet, and Basket; a full set of wood-type Cabinets for storage; and building/decor pieces (Rope — climbable and reelable, Canvas, Canvas Rugs, Tatami mats, Canvas Signs in every dye color). On the food side it adds dozens of composed dishes built from raw cuts (minced beef, chicken cuts, bacon, fish slices, mutton chops) into sandwiches, wraps, rolls, stews, soups, and pies (apple pie, sweet berry cheesecake, chocolate pie), plus a starter tier of Flint/Iron/Golden/Diamond/Netherite knives that every add-on in this category extends with more materials. Config toggles worth knowing: farmersBuyFDCrops (villagers trade FD crops), wanderingTraderSellsFDItems, richSoilBoostChance (Rich Soil farmland speeds growth), and vanillaSoupExtraEffects (vanilla soups/stews also grant FD-style buffs). A Paxi datapack (config/paxi/datapacks/SkyVillages-FarmersDelightCompat…zip) patches Farmer’s Delight content into the modpack’s SkyVillages structures.
How you’ll use it here
This is the heart of the pack’s cooking loop and where prepared-food buffs come from, so build a Stove, Cooking Pot and Cutting Board early. Use the Cutting Board with a knife to butcher meat into cuts, then the Cooking Pot for stews and soups and the Stove/Skillet for fried dishes — apple pie, cheesecake and dozens of composed meals. Feed it with Croptopia crops plus FD’s own tomato/cabbage/onion/rice. Because hunger is heavier here and cooked food gives real stat buffs, this is one of the first systems worth investing in, not an afterthought.
Anticipated questions
Does cooking actually matter here? Yes — on this server prepared food gives real stat buffs, not just hunger refill, so building an FD kitchen early pays off.
What do I build first? Generally the Stove (passive cooking), Cooking Pot (multi-serving stews and soups) and Cutting Board (knife-based butchering).
Can I trade for FD crops? Yes — with farmersBuyFDCrops villagers trade Farmer’s Delight crops, and wanderingTraderSellsFDItems has the wandering trader sell FD items.
Do I need a separate knife? Yes, the Cutting Board needs a knife — Flint/Iron/Golden/Diamond/Netherite to start, with other mods’ materials covered by Farmer’s Knives.

Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Farmer'.title: Farmer's Knives
Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Farmer'.content:
Farmer’s Knives
Jar: farmersknives-3.2.jar (mod id farmersknives, by ianm1647 — same author as Expanded Delight). Unlike the other add-ons in this category, Farmer’s Knives isn’t themed around a place or creature — it’s pure cross-mod compatibility glue. Farmer’s Delight’s Cutting Board mechanic wants a knife made from whatever tool-tier material the player has on hand, and vanilla FD only ships Flint/Iron/Golden/Diamond/Netherite. This mod fills the gap: 61 named knife variants are listed in its lang file, each matching a metal/material tier added by some other mod in the pack — Vibranium, Adamantium, Rose Gold, Gilded Netherite, Chitin, Aeternium, Thallasium, Terminite, Cincinnasite, Manasteel, Elementium, Terra, Enderite, Ruby, Amethyst, Steel, Obsidian, Copper, Soul Alloy, Warden, Dragon, Gobber, Adamantite, Bronze, Carmot, Celestium, Durasteel, Hallowed, Kyber, Metallurgium, Mythril, Orichalcum, Osmium, Palladium, Prometheum, Runite, Star Platinum, Stormyx, Ironwood, Steeleaf, Knightmetal, Pendorite, and more.
In practice this means whichever tech/magic/tool mods happen to be installed in the pack, their material tiers get an automatic matching knife so players never have to fall back to a lower-tier vanilla knife just because their preferred mod’s material isn’t “known” to Farmer’s Delight. It hard-depends on farmersdelight.
How you’ll use it here
You won’t go looking for this mod — it just means whatever metal or magic tier you smelt from the pack’s tech and magic mods automatically has a matching Farmer’s Delight Cutting Board knife, so you never have to drop back to a vanilla flint or iron knife. In practice, once you’re mid-to-late game with fancy materials (Enderite, Manasteel, Mythril and the rest), craft that tier’s knife and keep butchering with your best material. It’s pure convenience glue for Farmer’s Delight’s cutting step.
Anticipated questions
What does this give me over base knives? 61 knife variants matching other mods’ material tiers, so your preferred metal always has a Cutting Board knife instead of just the vanilla Flint/Iron/Golden/Diamond/Netherite ones.
Do I have to use these? No — the vanilla FD knives still work; this just lets you use higher or modded tiers.
Which knife should I craft? Generally whichever matches the best tool material you already have, since these simply extend Farmer’s Delight’s Cutting Board.

Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Let's-D.title: Let's Do: Brewery
Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Let's-D.content:
Let’s Do: Brewery
Jar: letsdo-brewery-fabric-1.1.9.jar (mod id brewery). A German-Oktoberfest-themed brewing mod and the first entry in the “Let’s Do” series, built on top of [[[Let’s Do] API]] (hard dependency, doapi >=1.2.9). Its lang file lists 17 items and 45 blocks. The in-mod tagline sets the tone: “Ozapft is! Brau Bier, beiss in a Bretzn – willkomme zum Braufescht!” (“It’s tapped! Brew beer, bite into a pretzel — welcome to the beer festival!”).
New crops are hops and barley (plus corn, shared with the wider farming loop), fed into a proper brewing chain: Wooden/Copper/Netherite Brewingstations and matching Silos for storing dried grain, producing Wheat Beer, Barley Beer, Haley Beer, and Hops Beer served in Beer Mugs, alongside named whiskey bottles (Bottle of MaggoAllan Whiskey, Carrasconlabel Whiskey, Lilitu Single Malt, JoJannik Whiskey, CristelWalker Whiskey) aged in Big Barrels. Food-wise it adds pretzels, sausage, pork knuckle, fried chicken, “Half Chicken à la HadariYao,” mashed potatoes, potato salad, dumplings, and gingerbread. It also brings Oktoberfest-themed cosmetic armor (Brewfest Hat/Regalia/Trousers/Boots/Dress/Blouse/Shoes) and tavern furniture (Bench, Table, Bar Counter, Cabinet, Drawer, Sideboard, Wall Cabinet) built via the shared API’s cabinet/drawer sounds. A “Beer Elemental” mob (sounds defined in the API) and a “Booze Spawn Keg” item suggest a boss/summon tied to the brewing theme.
How you’ll use it here
This is your beer-and-tavern branch — grow hops and barley, build a Brewingstation and Silo, and brew Wheat/Barley/Hops beer plus aged whiskeys in Big Barrels. It pairs with Oktoberfest food (pretzels, sausage, pork knuckle) and tavern furniture for kitting out a pub. It’s a mid-game themed project rather than survival cooking; take it on once you’ve got a farm running and want a drinks economy separate from Let’s Do: Vinery’s wine and Let’s Do: HerbalBrews’ tea.
Anticipated questions
What do I grow for beer? Hops and barley (plus corn), fed into the Brewingstations and stored in Silos.
Is this the same as Vinery or HerbalBrews? No — Brewery is beer and whiskey, Vinery is wine, HerbalBrews is tea; they share the [[[Let’s Do] API]] plumbing but are separate drink lines.
Do I need anything installed for it? Yes — it hard-depends on [[[Let’s Do] API]] (doapi >=1.2.9).

Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Let's-D.content:
Let’s Do: HerbalBrews
Jar: letsdo-herbalbrews-fabric-1.0.12.jar (mod id herbalbrews). The tea-focused entry in the “Let’s Do” series, sharing furniture/sound plumbing with [[[Let’s Do] API]] and the series’ shared visual style, though — unlike Brewery — its own fabric.mod.json doesn’t list doapi as a hard dependency. Its tagline: “Brew your bliss – discover new flowers, craft unique stations, and master the art of tea-making.” Lang file lists 9 items and 36 blocks.
New plants: Lavender, Hibiscus, Wild Coffee, Wild Rooibos, and Wild Yerba Mate (each with potted variants and their own leaf/block forms — e.g. Green/Black/Oolong/Mixed Tea Leaf Blocks). These get processed at a dedicated Brewing Cauldron, Copper Tea Kettle, and Stove/Tea Kettle into a full menu of teas and coffees: Black Tea, Green Tea, Oolong Tea, Lavender Tea, Rooibos Tea, Yerba Mate Tea, Hibiscus Tea, plus Coffee and Milk Coffee, most stored/served via a Flask or Jug and dried tea leaves bundled into “Bag of Tea Leaves.” A “Herbal Infusion” item and a “Completionist Banner: Herbal Brews” (shared banner mechanic from doapi) round it out, alongside Top Hat and Witch Hat cosmetics. It’s the lightest of the three Let’s Do content mods but still adds a genuinely separate drink economy (hot beverages) distinct from Brewery’s beer/whiskey and Vinery’s wine.
How you’ll use it here
This is the tea-and-coffee branch — grow lavender, hibiscus, wild coffee, rooibos and yerba mate, then brew them at the Brewing Cauldron and Copper Tea Kettle into a menu of teas and coffees served in flasks and jugs. It’s the lightest of the three Let’s Do content mods, so treat it as a low-investment cozy side project: make hot drinks once you’ve found the flowers. It’s a distinct drink line from Let’s Do: Brewery’s beer and Let’s Do: Vinery’s wine.
Anticipated questions
What do I grow for tea? Lavender, Hibiscus, Wild Coffee, Wild Rooibos and Wild Yerba Mate, processed at the Brewing Cauldron and Copper Tea Kettle.
Does it need the Let’s Do API? It shares the API’s furniture and sound plumbing, but unlike Brewery its own fabric.mod.json doesn’t list doapi as a hard dependency — the [[[Let’s Do] API]] is present in the pack regardless.
How’s it different from Brewery and Vinery? It’s the hot-beverage line (teas and coffees), separate from Brewery’s beer/whiskey and Vinery’s wine.

Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Let's-D.title: Let's Do: Vinery
Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Let's-D.content:
Let’s Do: Vinery
Jar: letsdo-vinery-fabric-1.4.41.jar (mod id vinery). The largest of the “Let’s Do” content mods by far — its lang file lists 38 items but a huge 144 blocks, more than Brewery and HerbalBrews combined, and it shares the series’ furniture/sound plumbing from [[[Let’s Do] API]]. Tagline: “In Vino Veritas - it’s time for wine! Build your own vineyard, produce wine, and establish your own winery.”
Grapes come in Red and White varieties across three biome-flavored strains — regular, Jungle, Savanna, and Taiga grapes — each with seeds, fresh fruit, and their own grapejuice. Apples get folded in too (Apple Press → Apple Juice/Mash → Cider/Wine), and Cherry trees are added as a full wood set (logs, planks-equivalent “beam,” boats, chest boats, signs). The wine-making chain is the real depth here: an Apple Press and winery blocks turn fruit into wine aged and displayed in per-wood-type Wine Racks and Wine Bottle Storage (small and big variants exist for Acacia, Bamboo, Birch, Cherry, Crimson, and presumably every other vanilla wood type), plus Lattices for growing vines. On top of generic wines it adds a set of named specialty/joke wines — Aegis Wine, Bolvar Wine, Chenet Wine, Chorus Wine, Clark Wine, Cristel Wine, “A Bottle of ‘Mojang Noir’,” “A Bottle of ‘Creepers Crush’” — plus new mobs (Mule and Wandering Winemaker spawn eggs) and winemaker cosmetic armor (apron, boots, leggings) and a Straw Hat. Config lives at config/vinery.json and config/vinery/.
How you’ll use it here
This is the wine branch and the biggest Let’s Do content mod — grow Red and White grapes (with jungle/savanna/taiga strains), run fruit through the Apple Press and winery blocks, and age wine in per-wood Wine Racks and Wine Bottle Storage. It’s a build-heavy vineyard project for mid-to-late game, with Cherry wood sets and winemaker cosmetics to theme a proper winery. It’s a separate drinks economy from Let’s Do: Brewery’s beer and Let’s Do: HerbalBrews’ tea.
Anticipated questions
What do I grow for wine? Red and White grapes across regular, Jungle, Savanna and Taiga strains; apples also fold in via the Apple Press.
What actually makes the wine? The Apple Press and winery blocks turn fruit into wine, aged and displayed in per-wood-type Wine Racks and Wine Bottle Storage.
Does it need the Let’s Do API? It shares the series’ [[[Let’s Do] API]] plumbing; its own fabric.mod.json doesn’t list doapi as a hard dependency, but the API ships with the pack anyway.

Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Ocean's.title: Ocean's Delight
Mods/Food,-Farming--and--Cooking/Ocean's.content:
Ocean’s Delight
Jar: oceansdelight-fdrf-fabric-1.0.2-1.20.jar (mod id oceansdelight, by Scouter). A Farmer’s Delight add-on (hard-depends on farmersdelight, note the fdrf — “Farmer’s Delight Refabricated” — in the filename confirming it targets this pack’s specific FD port) themed around ocean/deep-sea food. Lang file lists 21 items and 1 block, making it a compact, single-idea addition rather than a sprawling one.
Its standout ingredient is the Elder Guardian: the mod turns Minecraft’s toughest ocean boss into a full cooking chain (raw/cooked slice, slab, roll, cabbage-wrapped, and a full guardian soup), alongside a smaller regular-Guardian tail dish line. It rounds out with squid/tentacle food (tentacle on a stick, cut tentacles, squid rings), pufferfish-derived sushi (Fugu Roll/Slice — playing on real-world fugu, which is famously poisonous), sea pickles (braised), kelp (honey fried), seagrass salad, and a stuffed cod dish. Together with End’s Delight, it’s one of the “boss-monster-as-food” themed add-ons in the category — Ocean’s Delight does for the Elder Guardian what End’s Delight does for the ender dragon.
How you’ll use it here
This turns your ocean and boss loot into food — the headline is the Elder Guardian, which becomes a full chain of slices, slabs, rolls, cabbage wraps and soup, alongside squid dishes, pufferfish sushi (Fugu), braised sea pickles and kelp. Use it after you’ve raided an ocean monument; on this server cooking those drops into buffed meals beats eating raw fish. Like End’s Delight, it’s a boss-as-food theme rather than everyday cooking.
Anticipated questions
What’s the standout dish? The Elder Guardian chain — raw/cooked slice, slab, roll, cabbage-wrapped and guardian soup — built around the ocean’s toughest boss.
Do I need Farmer’s Delight? Yes — it hard-depends on farmersdelight (the fdrf build targets this pack’s Refabricated FD port).
When do I use it? Generally after an ocean monument raid, since the best ingredients come from the Elder Guardian and regular guardians.

Jar: letsdo-API-fabric-1.2.15-fabric.jar (mod id doapi). The shared library underpinning the “Let’s Do” series (Brewery, Vinery, and by extension HerbalBrews, though HerbalBrews and Vinery’s own fabric.mod.json don’t explicitly list doapi as a hard dependency the way Brewery does — letsdo-brewery requires doapi >=1.2.9). It adds no gameplay content of its own to speak of; its lang file is almost entirely shared plumbing: a “Completionist Banner” block/wall-banner pair (used by the Let’s Do mods to mark in-world achievement-style completion), and a long list of shared sound effects — cabinet/drawer open-close, cake cutting, a typewriter, a dinner bell, and a full brewstation sound set (ambient hum, oven crackling, timer ticking, kettle popping, whistle) plus a “Beer Elemental” mob’s ambient/hurt/death/attack sounds.
Requires architectury (the cross-loader mod framework) and terraform-wood-api-v1, confirming it’s built as reusable plumbing rather than a standalone feature mod — its job is to give the other Let’s Do mods consistent furniture (cabinets, drawers), sound design, and shared mechanics so they feel like one connected series instead of three unrelated add-ons.
How you’ll use it here
You never interact with this directly — it’s shared plumbing (furniture, sounds, the Completionist Banner) that Let’s Do: Brewery, Let’s Do: Vinery and Let’s Do: HerbalBrews depend on. Just keep it installed.
Anticipated questions
Do I need to do anything with this mod? No — it adds no gameplay content of its own; it’s a library the other Let’s Do mods use for consistent furniture and sound.

Mods/Magic--and--Spells-Mods.content:
Magic & Spells Mods
See Damage Types & Runes and the Mage path in Archetypes & Builds for how these systems play.
Botania
A gorgeous, flower-and-mana-powered magic-tech mod. Less “cast fireballs” and more “build an increasingly elaborate garden that automates your whole base” — one of the pack’s best long-term magic/tech hybrid goals, with its own Quest Book chapter. Can bridge into Applied Energistics 2 via Applied Botanics.
Spell Engine
The data-driven library that actually runs spellcasting — spell books, staffs, and scrolls all bind to it. Running under the hood of every spell any caster build uses.
Spell Power Attribute
The stat plumbing behind Spell Engine — why “spell power” and “spell haste” exist as gear stats at all.
Runes
Craft Runes to use as spell ammunition. These are the items that map to the pack’s three damage families — Elemental (Arcane/Fire/Frost), Primordial (Healing/Soul), Decaying (Unholy/Blood).
Sortilege
Simple magic staffs plus tweaks to vanilla enchanting/brewing — a gentler, earlier-game entry point into magic before the archetype mods.
Archon
Sorcery, necromancy, and its own bosses — a denser, darker magic mod for players who’ve outgrown the basics.
Invocations Mod
A spellbook containing 24 powerful invocable spells in one package — a broad magical toolkit without committing to a full caster build.
Bewitchment / Bewitchment Tweaks
A dedicated witchcraft mod (its own Quest Book chapter) with rituals and familiars. Bewitchment Tweaks is a small balance patch (adds invisibility to the Specter Bangle).

Mods/Magic--and--Spells/Archon.title: Archon
Mods/Magic--and--Spells/Archon.content:
Archon
Archon (archon, v0.8.1, by Safro) describes itself as “Sorcery, Necromancy, Bosses, and More!” and ships its own Patchouli guidebook, the Grimoire, with seven categories: Mana, Spells, Necromancy, Bosses, Effects & Enchants, World, and Misc. It depends on Spell Power Attribute directly (spell_power >=0.11.0), and its mana system is separate from Botania’s — Archon mana regenerates passively at a base 1/second and is boosted by Mana Catalysts, placeable blocks that raise everyone’s max mana within a radius (Normal: 16-block range/+50, Diamond: 22-block range/+100, and higher tiers beyond).
Archon’s two headline systems are spells and necromancy. Spells are element-themed (Fire, Water, Earth, Sky, End) and found as loot in world structures — Fire spells specifically drop in Nether Fortresses and Bastions (Fireball at 20 mana, a Fire Resistance buff scaling with spell power at 50 mana, an ignite-DoT at 30 mana/30 range, and a quick heat beam at 10 mana). Necromancy runs through the Staff of Undead: killing mobs with a Soul Scythe (or a weapon enchanted with Reaping) drops Souls, which the staff auto-consumes for Soul Power, spent on five summon types — angry wolf pack, “the Titan” golem, undead knight pair, life-stealing silverfish swarm, and a fire-bow undead archer — each with its own base lifetime that scales up with more Soul Power banked.
The mod’s boss roster is a matched set of five elemental bosses summoned at a Summoning Pedestal with themed ingredients: Ayla (Sky, feather/gold/2x Sky Essence → Angelic Star), Inigo (Fire, magma cream/blaze powder/2x Fire Essence → Charred Eye), Leven (Water, kelp/pufferfish/2x Water Essence → Wave Crystal), Tar (Earth, the weakest of the five, deepslate/2x Earth Essence/emerald → Terranite Stone), and Null (End, the strongest, ender pearl/end crystal/2x End Essence → Soulless Eye). Their drops feed further crafting. Essence itself comes from Nodes — ore-like veins generating in specific dimensions and Y-ranges per element (Earth underground Y -64–0, Water in ocean biomes Y 27–40, Fire in the Nether Y 10–117, End anywhere on End islands, Sky in small clouds at Y 192–196). A Wizard Villager profession also sells scrolls, crafting items, and enchantments including Arcane (10% mana-cost reduction per level, stacking, though it can’t apply to unique items like the Channeler or Staff of Undead). This pack’s archon.json5 tunes cosmetic/QoL values only (mana HUD position, screen-shake toggle, soul drop chance at 5%, wizard village weight 10) — no core mechanics are disabled.
Anticipated questions
Is Archon mana the same as Botania mana?
No — it’s a completely separate system. Archon mana is a personal bar that regenerates at a base 1/second, boosted by placing Mana Catalysts (Normal +50/16-block range, Diamond +100/22-block, higher tiers beyond) and by mana-regen gear like the Mask of Power (4 mana/sec while worn). Botania mana lives in Mana Pools and never touches this bar.
Where do I find spells and how do I cast them?
Spells are loot tied to their element and cast with the matching Wand: Fire in Nether Fortresses/Bastions, Water in ocean structures and fishing, Sky in villages, End in End Cities/Strongholds, Earth in temples and mineshafts. Damage scales with your Spell Power Attribute.
How does necromancy work?
Kill mobs with a Soul Scythe (or a weapon with the Reaping enchant) to drop Souls; the Staff of Undead (once given a core) auto-consumes them as Soul Power to summon minions — an angry wolf pack, the Titan golem, undead knight pair, life-stealing silverfish, and a fire-bow archer. Each summon’s lifetime scales with how much Soul Power you’ve banked.
How do I summon the elemental bosses?
Place the themed ingredients on a Summoning Pedestal — right-click while holding them (there’s no GUI; shift-click clears it). The exact recipes for Ayla, Inigo, Leven, Tar, and Null are listed in your Grimoire. The Essence two of the ingredients require comes from mining Nodes in each element’s dimension/Y-range.
Who’s the easiest boss to start with?
Tar (Earth) is the weakest of the five; Null (End) is the strongest. See Creatures, Bosses & Mobs and Archetypes & Builds for how a caster build approaches them.

Mods/Magic--and--Spells/Bewitchment-Twea.title: Bewitchment Tweaks
Mods/Magic--and--Spells/Bewitchment-Twea.content:
Bewitchment Tweaks
Bewitchment Tweaks (bewitchment-tweaks, v1.0.0, by Mervyn) is exactly as small as its own description says: “Adds vanilla invisibility effect to Specter Bangle.” The entire jar is ten files — a fabric.mod.json, a mixin config, and a single compiled mixin class (SpecterBangleItemMixin) — with no items, blocks, configs, or guidebook of its own. It hard-depends on Bewitchment (bewitchment: '*'), since its only job is patching one item from that mod.
The Specter Bangle is a Bewitchment trinket/curio (documented in the parent mod’s Book of Shadows under Tools) that grants a ghost-like state; this patch specifically makes it apply Minecraft’s actual vanilla Invisibility status effect rather than whatever visual/behavior Bewitchment’s base implementation used, presumably for better compatibility with other mods that check for the vanilla effect. There’s genuinely nothing more to it — this is a one-line balance/compatibility patch packaged as its own mod, not a content addition.
Anticipated questions
What does this mod actually do?
Just one thing: it makes Bewitchment’s Specter Bangle apply Minecraft’s real vanilla Invisibility status effect rather than whatever visual/behavior the base mod used — presumably for better compatibility with other mods that check for the vanilla effect. It’s a single-mixin patch (SpecterBangleItemMixin), not a content addition.
Does it add any items, blocks, or config?
No. The whole jar is ten files — a fabric.mod.json, a mixin config, and one compiled mixin class — with no items, blocks, configs, or guidebook of its own.
Do I need Bewitchment installed for it?
Yes — it hard-depends on Bewitchment (bewitchment: '*'), since its only job is patching the Specter Bangle from that mod.
Where does the Specter Bangle itself come from?
It’s a Bewitchment trinket/curio that grants a ghost-like state, documented in that mod’s Book of Shadows under Tools.
Does it change how I’d plan a build around invisibility?
Not on its own — it’s a one-line compatibility/balance patch, so any stealth-oriented gear choices still hang on the Specter Bangle as covered under Archetypes & Builds, not on this mod adding anything new.

Mods/Magic--and--Spells/Bewitchment.title: Bewitchment
Mods/Magic--and--Spells/Bewitchment.content:
Bewitchment
Bewitchment (bewitchment, v1.20-10, by MoriyaShiine and cybercat5555) is a full witchcraft-themed magic mod, distinct from every other mod in this category — it’s built around ritual circles, curses, familiars, and pacts with demonic entities rather than spellbooks or mana bars. It ships its own Patchouli guidebook, the Book of Shadows, organized into nine categories (Introduction, Tools, Brewing, Rituals, Curses, Contracts, Creatures, Sigils, Poppets) with well over 100 individual entries, and has its own dedicated Quest Book chapter in this pack, “Witchcraft & Rituals” (config/ftbquests/quests/chapters/c_bewitchment.snbt), covering everything from the Athame and Witch Cauldron to ritual burners, chalk circles, and demon parts.
Altars are the mod’s power source: built by placing a carpet on a themed base block (tied to one of three realms — Overworld, Nether, End), they passively collect “ME” (magical energy) from nearby plants, boosted by swords (storage multiplier), pentacles like skulls/gems (gain), and wands like Candelabras/Lanterns/Torches (fill rate). This ME feeds a player’s Internal ME Buffer, which powers most of the mod’s other systems. Rituals are the primary spellcasting method: drawn as inner and (optionally) outer circles with a Golden Glyph at the center and the correct ingredients thrown in, each ritual consuming a specified amount of nearby Altar ME. Sigils split into active (placed on usable blocks, or on brooms crafted from Dragon’s Blood wood) and passive (placeable anywhere) variants, and can be scoped to specific targets using Taglocks as either a whitelist or blacklist. Poppets are entity-bound effigies — crafted by combining a poppet with a Taglock — used for both curses and protection, and must be carried in inventory to function unless stored on a Poppet Shelf.
The mod’s signature systems are contracts and curses. Contracts are pacts purchased from Demons at the cost of health, typically lasting seven days and unbreakable once made — the “Concept: Contracts” entry is explicit that this is a real cost, not a formality. The two big curses are Lycanthropy (turns victims into a Werewolf under a full moon; contracted from another werewolf’s attack, and — notably — a Werewolf becomes too weak to hold tools like an Athame for long once cursed, due to their Silver weakness) and Vampirism (a “terminal” curse; Vampires are technically immortal but must feed on human blood or die, and the curse can only be contracted from another Vampire, not cast via a Brazier like most curses). Both curses have their own patron entities you can Pledge to for greater control: Herne, Lord of the Wild Hunt, is pledged to by suffering lycanthropes and grants near-total control over wolf-form transformation (toggleable on a keybind); Lilith, mountain-mother of vampires, similarly grants controllable bat-form to pledged vampires. Both are summoned with a Mortal Coil Incense plus a specific animal (Wolf for Herne, Chicken for Lilith) in the right biome at night, and — because you need to keep them alive to Pledge — where you summon them matters. Baphomet, an ancient Demon and “first name of fire,” is the mod’s primary Contract-giving Greater Demon.
Server-side, config/bewitchment.json tunes the mod’s overworld spawn weights for its familiar/creature roster: Ghost, Vampire, and Werewolf each spawn at weight 20 (max group size 1), Hellhound at weight 30, Snake at weight 18, Owl and Raven at weight 10, and Toad is set to weight 0 — effectively disabled in this pack despite the mod supporting it. Curses and Polymorph are both left enabled (enableCurses/enablePolymorph: true), and natural Salt/Silver generation (the mod’s two key crafting resources — Silver notably makes the Athame usable against unholy creatures) are both left on.
Anticipated questions
How do I start witchcraft?
Read the Book of Shadows (the mod’s guidebook) and craft a Witch’s Knife (Athame) — it’s used for rituals and for scratching the magic trees. From there you build an Altar to collect ME (magical energy) and a Witch Cauldron to brew. This pack has a dedicated quest chapter, “Witchcraft & Rituals”, that walks the whole path.
How do rituals actually work?
A ritual is drawn as a chalk circle (inner, plus an optional outer circle) with a Golden Glyph at the center; throw in the right ingredients and it consumes a set amount of nearby Altar ME. The Altar is powered up by decorating it with swords, pentacles, and wands and by planting the four magic trees around it.
What are familiars, and why can’t I get a toad?
Familiars are creatures you can bind and keep. In this pack the overworld familiar/creature roster spawns at tuned weights (Ghost/Vampire/Werewolf 20, Hellhound 30, etc.), but Toad is set to weight 0 — effectively disabled here, so you won’t find one naturally.
How do I become a werewolf or vampire?
Both are curses. Lycanthropy is contracted from another werewolf’s attack (and a cursed werewolf grows too weak to hold an Athame for long, due to Silver weakness); Vampirism is “terminal” and can only be contracted from another vampire, not cast via a Brazier. For control over your form you Pledge to a patron — Herne for werewolves, Lilith for vampires — each summoned with a Mortal Coil Incense and a specific animal at night. Contracts, meanwhile, are pacts bought from Demons (like Baphomet) at the cost of health and are unbreakable once made.
Does the Specter Bangle turn me invisible?
Yes — in this pack. Bewitchment Tweaks adds vanilla invisibility to the Specter Bangle on top of its base behavior.

Mods/Magic--and--Spells/Botania.title: Botania
Mods/Magic--and--Spells/Botania.content:
Botania
Botania (botania, v1.20.1-451-FABRIC, by Vazkii and a large community team — wiiv, williewillus, dylan4ever, Hubry, Alwinfy, artemisSystem, Falkory220) bills itself in its own fabric.mod.json as “a tech mod themed around natural magic” — an accurate description. There’s no traditional spellcasting here; instead you plant Generating Flora that convert nearby resources (sunlight, lava, redstone, mob kills, etc.) into Mana, pipe that mana through Spreaders and Pools, and spend it on Functional Flora that automate farming, mob-killing, item transport, and terraforming. The mod ships its own in-game guidebook, the Lexicon Botania (a Patchouli book with 11 categories — Basics, Mana, Generating Flora, Functional Flowers, Baubles, Tools, Ender, Alfhomancy, Devices, Misc, Challenges), and it has its own dedicated Quest Book chapter in this pack (config/ftbquests/quests/chapters/botania.snbt, ~2350 lines) walking players through Seedling’s First Steps, mana batteries, Manasteel/Manaweave gear, terraforming tools, and the endgame “Gaia Ritual”-adjacent content.
The Alfhomancy progression track is Botania’s most distinctive system: it frames the endgame as building a portal to Alfheim, the elves’ realm, requiring 8 Livingwood, 3 Glimmering blocks, and other rare components to craft an Elven Gateway Core. Trinkets (also called Baubles/Curios in-mod) are wearable magic accessories equipped via a dedicated Curios screen. Server-side, botania-common.json5 keeps most systems at their defaults but explicitly disables the Mana Enchanter (“since some people find it OP”) while leaving the Relic system enabled, and tunes Mana Spreader trace-time and Mana Lens harvest levels for balance.
In this pack Botania also functions as a bridge into the tech side of the game: the Applied Botanics mod (present in mods/) connects Botania’s mana economy with Applied Energistics 2’s ME network, letting a mana-and-flower base feed into (or draw from) an AE2 autocrafting setup. Botania depends on patchouli and trinkets per its mod metadata, both also present in the pack.
Anticipated questions
How do I actually start Botania and make mana?
Craft a Lexica Botanica first — it’s the in-game guidebook and unlocks the quest track. Then plant Generating Flora, place a Mana Pool to store the mana, and a Mana Spreader (aimed with the Wand of the Forest) to pipe it where you need it. There’s no spellcasting; you spend mana on Functional Flora and gear. See Magic & Spells Mods.
Can I use the Mana Enchanter?
No. It’s disabled server-side in this pack (the config flags it as too strong). The Relic system is left enabled, so relic drops still work.
Can Botania feed my automation / AE2 base?
Yes — the Applied Botanics mod bridges Botania’s mana economy to Applied Energistics 2’s ME network, so a flower-and-mana farm can drive (or draw from) AE2 autocrafting.
How do I get Manasteel and Terrasteel?
Manasteel comes from mana-infusing items in a Mana Pool; Terrasteel is far more expensive, made on a special agglomeration plate that infuses three mana-dipped objects and burns through half a Mana Pool’s capacity per craft. Terrasteel gear (including the rank-up Terra Shatterer) is stronger than the Manasteel set and the Terrasteel armor passively charges Mana Tablets in your inventory.
Is there a quest chapter for it?
Yes — Botania has its own Quest Book chapter walking you from Seedling’s First Steps through mana batteries, Manasteel/Manaweave gear, terraforming tools, and the Alfhomancy endgame (building an Elven Gateway to Alfheim).

Mods/Magic--and--Spells/Invocations-Mod.title: Invocations Mod
Mods/Magic--and--Spells/Invocations-Mod.content:
Invocations Mod
Invocations Mod (invoke, v1.0.3.1-1.20.1, by cleannrooster/Forg) describes itself simply as “Invoke powerful spells, 24 Spells in one book!” It has no in-game guidebook or dedicated config of its own — it’s a single-purpose add-on that plugs into Spell Engine (spell_engine >=0.14.1) and the Wizards (RPG Series) mod (wizards >=0.9.23), the same base mod that powers the Mage archetype’s Fire/Frost/Arcane schools per Archetypes & Builds.
The mod’s one deliverable is the Invoker Spell Book (invoke:invoker_spell_book), and this pack’s own Quest Book entry for it — “Astral Magic,” in the e_spell_books.snbt chapter — spells out exactly what it does and where it sits in progression: it’s a Tier III book (the hardest tier, alongside Spellblade Next’s evolved technique books), built by combining Arcane, Fire, and Frost magic into an “Astral” hybrid. The quest text describes it as letting you “cast three different spells of each element” plus an ultimate spell that changes based on which elements were used, for “a total of 39 possible spells” — the hardest spellbook in the pack’s progression despite the mod’s own tagline advertising “24 Spells.” This lines up with Damage Types & Runes’s description of the endgame “Runic Invocations / Astral Magic” path that blends all three Elemental schools via Astral Power, and with the Knowledge of Runes and Stars Fate Talent that unlocks it.
Because Invocations Mod is scoped to exactly one item with no additional blocks, configs, or guidebook, this is close to the full extent of what’s independently discoverable about it — its real depth lives in Wizards’ and Spell Engine’s spell-tag data, not in its own jar.
Anticipated questions
What does this mod actually give me?
One item: the Invoker Spell Book (invoke:invoker_spell_book, shown in-game as “Runic Invocations”). No blocks, no config, no guidebook — it’s a single spellbook that plugs into Spell Engine and the Wizards (RPG Series) mod.
How many spells does it have — 24 or 39?
Both numbers are real. The mod’s own tagline advertises “24 Spells in one book,” while this pack’s Quest Book entry (“Astral Magic”) describes casting “three different spells of each element” plus an ultimate that changes with the elements used, “for a total of 39 possible spells.”
How do I invoke a spell?
You build up Invocation Power by casting element spells, then cast Runic Invocation to spend the accumulated runes and unleash a more powerful spell. The ultimate spell changes depending on which elements (Arcane/Fire/Frost) you fed in.
How do I get the book, and where does it sit in progression?
It’s a Tier III book — the hardest tier — built by combining Arcane, Fire, and Frost magic into the “Astral” hybrid. Tier III books require a Cinderstone Trophy to craft. The path is gated behind the Knowledge of Runes and Stars Fate Talent (see Talent Tree & Fate Talents) and lines up with the endgame Astral Magic path in Damage Types & Runes.
Do I have to commit to a full caster build to use it?
The book bundles many spells into a single item, so it’s a broad toolkit rather than a narrow one — but in this pack it’s positioned as an endgame Tier III book, and its real depth lives in Wizards’ and Spell Engine’s spell-tag data, not in this jar. See Archetypes & Builds.

Mods/Magic--and--Spells/Runes.title: Runes
Mods/Magic--and--Spells/Runes.content:
Runes
Runes (runes, v0.9.13+1.20.1, by Daedelus — same author as Spell Engine and Spell Power Attribute) does exactly what its own description says: “Craft runes to serve as ammo for spells.” It’s a small, focused mod: the jar itself defines exactly six rune items — Arcane Rune, Fire Rune, Frost Rune, Healing Rune, Lightning Rune, and Soul Rune — each craftable in two tiers (“small”/“medium”) either by hand (a stone-tool-material base plus a themed reagent, yielding 4 at a time) or more cheaply at the mod’s own Rune Crafting Altar block. The reagents are simple and thematic: Fire Runes want Blaze Powder; Frost Runes want Ice/Packed Ice/Blue Ice; Arcane Runes want Ender Pearls or Amethyst; Healing Runes want Honeycomb or Gold Ingot.
This confirms and refines what Damage Types & Runes describes as the pack’s rune-ammo system, with one correction worth noting: the Elemental (Arcane/Fire/Frost) and part of the Primordial (Healing, Soul) rune families genuinely come from this “Runes” mod’s own jar — but the Decaying family’s Unholy Rune and Blood Rune are not part of this mod at all. They’re added by the separate Death Knights class mod (death_knights:unholy_stone / death_knights:blood_stone, seen in config/ftbquests/quests/chapters/einformation_7new_mechanics.snbt and the_nether.snbt), which depends on Spell Engine directly rather than on this mod. In other words, “Runes” supplies the base rune-as-spell-ammo mechanic and the Elemental/Healing/Soul items, while other class mods (here, Death Knights) extend the same naming convention and item role with their own rune types for their own damage family — Runes itself never ships an Unholy or Blood rune. spell_engine/server.json5’s spell_cost_item_allowed toggle (true in this pack) is what makes rune consumption on spellcast actually active server-side.
Anticipated questions
What are runes actually for?
They’re ammunition for spells — the mod’s own description is “Craft runes to serve as ammo for spells.” Casting certain spells consumes the matching rune. This is active on this server: spell_engine/server.json5’s spell_cost_item_allowed toggle is on, so rune consumption really happens server-side. See Damage Types & Runes.
Which runes does this mod add?
Exactly six: Arcane, Fire, Frost, Healing, Lightning, and Soul Rune, each craftable in two tiers (“small”/“medium”).
How do I craft them?
Either by hand — a stone-tool-material base plus a themed reagent, yielding 4 at a time — or more cheaply at the mod’s own Rune Crafting Altar block. Reagents are thematic: Fire wants Blaze Powder; Frost wants Ice/Packed Ice/Blue Ice; Arcane wants Ender Pearls or Amethyst; Healing wants Honeycomb or Gold Ingot.
How do runes map to the damage families?
This mod supplies the Elemental trio (Arcane/Fire/Frost) plus the Primordial Healing and Soul runes. The Decaying family’s Unholy and Blood runes are not from this mod — they’re added by the separate Death Knights class mod. See Damage Types & Runes.
Where do Unholy and Blood runes come from, then?
The Death Knights class mod (death_knights:unholy_stone / blood_stone), which depends on Spell Engine directly. “Runes” itself never ships an Unholy or Blood rune — other class mods extend the same rune-as-ammo convention with their own types.

Mods/Magic--and--Spells/Sortilege.title: Sortilege
Mods/Magic--and--Spells/Sortilege.content:
Sortilege
Sortilege (sortilege, v1.7.5, by Lyof) bills itself as “Simple magic staffs, enchanting and brewing tweaks, and more!” and that’s a fair summary — it’s a grab-bag utility/balance mod rather than a themed magic system like Botania or Archon. Its headline content is a set of tiered magic staffs (Wooden through Netherite, matching vanilla tool tiers) that fire a beam attack, plus a family of staff-only enchantments (Potency for damage, Stability for range, Chaining for pierce, Wisdom to reduce XP cost, Focus to reduce cooldown, elemental add-ons like Brazier/Blizzard/Blast/Blitz, and utility ones like Push/Pull/Bonk/Soulbound).
This pack’s sortilege.json reveals a deliberately restrained configuration: the staff base system is on — staffs use lapis lazuli/lapis block as overcharge fuel (up to 20 stacks, giving free durability and XP use while overcharged), cost 0 XP by default, and have only a 1-tick charge time — but every one of Sortilege’s own staff enchantments is individually disabled (enabled_enchants: potency, stability, chaining, focus, wisdom, push, pull, brazier, blizzard, blast, blitz, blessing, bonk, arcane, soulbound, and both curses all set to false). The mod’s other optional systems are similarly switched off: the Witch Hat item, cauldron brewing, the Lapis Shield, and XP-on-death keeping are all enable: false. What is active is the enchant limiter system — a default cap of 6 enchantments per item, with #prominent:limit_8 and #prominent:limit_10 tag-based overrides for special items, plus an XP level cap of 750 and death-screen coordinates.
In effect, Sortilege in this pack functions mostly as enchanting-system infrastructure (the limiter, tag-based overrides, level cap) with its staff item chain present as a basic, low-power early option rather than a fleshed-out casting path — consistent with the vault’s framing of it as “a gentler, earlier-game entry point into magic before the archetype mods.”
Anticipated questions
Is Sortilege a full magic system like Botania or Archon?
No. It’s a grab-bag utility/balance mod — “Simple magic staffs, enchanting and brewing tweaks, and more!” The vault frames it as a gentler, earlier-game entry into magic before the archetype mods. See Archetypes & Builds.
What do the staffs do?
There are tiered magic staffs (Wooden through Netherite, matching vanilla tool tiers) that fire a beam attack. In this pack they use lapis lazuli/lapis block as overcharge fuel (up to 20 stacks, giving free durability and XP use while overcharged), cost 0 XP by default, and have only a 1-tick charge time — a basic, low-power early casting option.
Can I use Sortilege’s staff enchantments (Potency, Blizzard, Chaining, etc.)?
No — every one of Sortilege’s own staff enchantments is disabled in this pack’s config (Potency, Stability, Chaining, Focus, Wisdom, the elemental add-ons, and the curses are all set to false). The staffs work, but you can’t augment them with these.
So what does Sortilege actually contribute here?
Mostly enchanting-system infrastructure: the enchant-limiter (a default cap of 6 enchantments per item, with #prominent:limit_8 / limit_10 tag overrides for special items), an XP level cap of 750, and death-screen coordinates. Its other optional systems — Witch Hat, cauldron brewing, Lapis Shield, XP-on-death keeping — are all switched off.

Mods/Magic--and--Spells/Spell-Engine.title: Spell Engine
Mods/Magic--and--Spells/Spell-Engine.content:
Spell Engine
Spell Engine (spell_engine, v0.15.12+1.20.1, by Daedelus) describes itself in its own metadata as a “data driven magic library” — and that’s exactly its role in this pack: it’s not a content mod in the sense of adding its own spellbook lineup, it’s the engine that every class spellbook in the pack runs on. It requires Spell Power Attribute (spell_power >=0.12.0) as a hard dependency, and other mods (Archon, Invocations Mod/invoke, Rogues, Paladins, Archers, Spellblade Next, Death Knights) all hook their own spellbooks and abilities into it rather than shipping a separate casting system each.
Concretely, Spell Engine adds the Spell Binding Table — the block that crafts Tier I spellbooks and lets you attach spells to spellbooks of any tier — and per its own quest chapter (e_spell_books.snbt, “Unlocking Abilities”) this table needs to be surrounded by 18 Bookshelves (mirroring an Enchanting Table) to unlock all four base spells for a book. The pack’s spell progression is explicitly tiered: Tier I base-class books come straight from the Spell Binding Table (Warrior, Rogue, Archer, Priest, and the elemental Wizard books); Tier II hybrid books are crafted from a Tier I book plus other ingredients (Paladin, Spellblade, Death Knight books); Tier III advanced books extend or evolve a Tier II book and require a Cinderstone Trophy — this is where Invocations Mod’s invoke:invoker_spell_book (“Astral Magic”) sits, alongside Spellblade Next’s evolved technique books.
Server-side, config/spell_engine/server.json5 controls a lot of pack-wide combat feel: spells bypass invulnerability frames (needed for high-frequency beam spells), spell haste reduces cooldowns, spell costs consume both durability and hunger by default, and a detailed player_relations table decides which entities spells can friendly-fire or heal (vanilla villagers and iron golems are semi-friendly/neutral, most mounts are flagged FRIENDLY so players don’t accidentally nuke their own horse with an AoE). Swords automatically gain spellcasting capability from spellbooks (add_spell_casting_to_swords: true), and players can’t unequip a spellbook mid-cooldown (spell_book_cooldown_lock).
Anticipated questions
Do I install Spell Engine separately, or does it just power the classes?
It’s the shared engine — every caster spellbook in the pack (Warrior, Rogue, Archer, Priest, Wizard, plus the Archon, Paladin, Death Knight, Spellblade and Invocations books) runs on it rather than shipping its own casting system. Building any caster from Archetypes & Builds means binding to it.
How do I make my first spellbook?
At the Spell Binding Table — it crafts Tier I books and attaches spells to books of any tier. To unlock all four base spells for a book, surround the table with 18 Bookshelves, exactly like maxing an Enchanting Table.
What do the tiers mean — is Tier III just stronger?
No. Tiers describe how a book is obtained, not raw power. Tier I base-class books come from the Spell Binding Table; Tier II hybrids (Paladin, Spellblade, Death Knight) are crafted from a Tier I book plus ingredients; Tier III advanced books (like Invocations’ Astral Invocations) evolve a Tier II book and require a Cinderstone Trophy.
Do casting spells cost anything besides mana?
Yes — by default spell costs consume both durability and hunger. Spells also bypass invulnerability frames (so high-frequency beams land every tick), and spell haste reduces your cooldowns. Your damage scales with Spell Power Attribute and can be tuned via Runes / Damage Types & Runes.
Why can I suddenly cast from my sword, and why won’t my spellbook come off?
Swords automatically gain spellcasting capability from spellbooks in this pack (add_spell_casting_to_swords). And you can’t unequip a spellbook while it’s on cooldown (spell_book_cooldown_lock) — wait for the cooldown to clear before swapping.

Mods/Magic--and--Spells/Spell-Power-Attr.title: Spell Power Attribute
Mods/Magic--and--Spells/Spell-Power-Attr.content:
Spell Power Attribute
Spell Power Attribute (spell_power, v0.12.0+1.20.1, by Daedelus, the same author as Spell Engine and Runes) is described in its own metadata as “Spell Power entity attributes with related status effects and enchantments” — it’s the stat layer, not a content mod. It has no in-game guidebook or quest chapter of its own; it exists purely as plumbing that Spell Engine and every caster-class mod in the pack (Archon, Wizards, Death Knights, Spellblade Next, Invocations Mod, etc.) read from.
Concretely, config/spell_power/attributes.json defines the actual numbers behind “spell power” as a stat: a base 5% spell critical chance and 50% spell critical damage bonus for everyone, a spell_power_effect that grants +10% spell damage per stack, and secondary status effects for Critical Damage (+10%/stack), Haste (+5%/stack), and Critical Chance (+5%/stack), each identified by its own UUID so multiple sources can stack cleanly. config/spell_power/enchantments.json then exposes several of these as actual enchantments obtainable in-world: Spell Power (max level 5, +5%/level), Soulfrost and Sunfire (elemental-flavored bonus enchants, +3%/level each), plus Critical Chance, Critical Damage, Haste, and Magic Protection (max level 4, a flat +2.0/level reduction), all enchantable and stackable per this pack’s config (allow_stacking: true).
Because this mod is pure stat infrastructure, it’s genuinely thin as a standalone note — its real substance shows up wherever a caster build’s tooltips reference “Spell Power,” “Spell Haste,” or “Spell Critical Chance.” Archon’s own guidebook, for instance, explicitly references the Arcane enchantment (“reduces mana cost… cannot be applied to special items”) as sitting alongside this attribute layer.
Anticipated questions
What do “Spell Power,” “Spell Haste,” and “Spell Critical Chance” mean as stats?
They’re the caster equivalents of physical gear stats, defined here in config/spell_power/attributes.json: everyone starts with a base 5% spell crit chance and 50% spell crit damage; Spell Power grants +10% spell damage per stack, Haste +5%/stack, Critical Chance +5%/stack, and Critical Damage +10%/stack. See Combat & Stats and Damage Types & Runes.
Where do I see or get these stats?
On the tooltips of caster gear, and as actual in-world enchantments this pack exposes: Spell Power (max level 5, +5%/level), Soulfrost and Sunfire (+3%/level each), plus Critical Chance, Critical Damage, Haste, and Magic Protection. All are enchantable and stackable here (allow_stacking: true). See Accessories & Enchanting.
Does every caster mod use this?
Yes — it’s pure stat plumbing with no spells or content of its own. Spell Engine and every caster-class mod (Archon, Wizards, Death Knights, Spellblade Next, Invocations Mod, etc.) read their spell damage/haste/crit from this attribute layer.

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods
Jade
Look at any block or mob to see what it is on-screen — health, name, contents. Runs constantly without thinking about it.
EMI
The recipe viewer — hover any item, hit the recipe/uses key, see how to make or use it. Answers almost every “how do I get X” question. Add-ons: EMI Professions, EMI Enchanting, EMI Loot, EMI Ores, Extra Mod Integrations, emi-letsdo-compat, Industrial Revolution EMI Plugin, Almost Unified (merges duplicate items/ores across mods), Polymorph (pick which mod’s recipe result you get on conflicts).
Xaero’s Minimap / Xaero’s World Map
The corner minimap and the full-screen map (default key M) — the standard navigation/waypoint setup.
Distant Horizons
Renders simplified terrain far beyond normal view distance at low performance cost. Every player must install Distant Horizons 3.2.0-b client-side to see any benefit — it does nothing solo.
FTB Quests / FTB Teams / FTB Library
FTB Quests is the Quest Book itself — see Getting Started. FTB Teams forms a party so quest progress and teleports are shared. FTB Library is shared code both run on. Quest Kill Task adds team-based kill credit. Create Questing is a Create-flavored quest-screen visual theme.
Fabric Waystones
The fast-travel system — generate in villages, craftable, right-click to bind, teleport back from anywhere.
Open Parties and Claims
Chunk claiming to protect builds, plus multiplayer party creation/management — per-category protection toggles (doors, chests, blocks).
Everyday utility & fun mods (grouped)
AppleSkin, Trading Post, You’re in Grave Danger (marks a death grave), Starter Kit, Fish On The Line, Ping Wheel, Clickable Advancements Mod, Show Me What You Got, No Chat Reports, Server Browser, Fancy Hotbar, Mod Menu, Do a Barrel Roll (elytra tricks), Comforts (sleeping bags/hammocks), Icarus (cosmetic wings), Runelic, PigPen, Immersive Melodies, What Are They Up To, Highlight, TreeChop, Leaves Be Gone, Extreme Sound Muffler, Veinmining, Bartering Station (automates piglin bartering), Block Runner, Villager Names.
