Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Almost-Uni.title: Almost Unified
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Almost-Uni.content:
Almost Unified
Almost Unified (almostunified, v0.11.0, by Almost Reliable) is the pack’s item/tag unification layer — it exists because Prominence II runs multiple overlapping tech mods (Create, Tech Reborn, Modern Industrialization, Industrial Revolution) that each add their own copper ingot, steel plate, or bronze gear as separate, non-interchangeable items. Without unification, a recipe from one mod would silently reject an otherwise-identical ingot from another. Almost Unified merges these into single interchangeable items/tags across the board, driven by a mod-priority order so it’s deterministic which mod’s texture and item wins when duplicates are collapsed.
This install’s config/almostunified/unify.json sets modPriorities to ["minecraft", "kubejs", "crafttweaker", "create", "techreborn", "modern_industrialization", "indrev"] — meaning when duplicate materials exist, Create’s variant is generally preferred over Tech Reborn’s, which is preferred over Modern Industrialization’s and Industrial Revolution’s. It unifies 48 materials — everything from common ones (copper, iron, gold, coal, tin, lead) to modded specialties (aeternium, mithril, enderium, signalum, constantan, elementium, cinnabar, tungsten, uranium) — across a template set of tag suffixes (_nuggets, _dusts, _gears, _gems, _ingots, _raw_materials, _ores, _plates, _rods, _blocks, _wires, _storage_blocks, plus raw-ore variants). A short ignoredItems/ignoredTags exclusion list carves out items that shouldn’t be merged despite matching the pattern — e.g. Industrial Revolution’s nikolite line and Better End/Better Nether’s unique ingots stay untouched, and c:copper_blocks is explicitly excluded from tag unification. startup.json’s serverOnly = false means the unification also applies client-side (so EMI/JEI-style displays reflect the merged items, not just crafting behavior).
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods
EMI
Polymorph
EMI Ores

Anticipated questions

What does this mod actually do? It merges duplicate/overlapping items from multiple tech mods (Create, Tech Reborn, Modern Industrialization, Industrial Revolution) into single interchangeable items/tags, so a recipe won’t silently reject an otherwise-identical ingot from a different mod.
When duplicates are merged, whose version wins? A priority order in unify.json: minecraft, kubejs, crafttweaker, create, techreborn, modern_industrialization, indrev — so Create’s variant is generally preferred, then Tech Reborn’s, and that mod’s texture/item is the one kept.
Does it affect what I see in EMI, or only crafting? Both — serverOnly = false, so unification applies client-side too and recipe displays reflect the merged items, not just crafting behavior.
Are any materials deliberately left un-merged? Yes — an ignoredItems/ignoredTags list carves out exceptions like Industrial Revolution’s nikolite and Better End/Better Nether’s unique ingots, and c:copper_blocks is excluded from tag unification.
How many materials get unified? 48, ranging from common ones (copper, iron, gold, coal, tin, lead) to modded specialties (aeternium, mithril, enderium, signalum, tungsten, uranium, and more).

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/AppleSkin.title: AppleSkin
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/AppleSkin.content:
AppleSkin
AppleSkin (appleskin, v2.5.2, by squeek502) is a long-running, well-known QoL mod that adds food-related HUD information Minecraft normally hides: exact hunger/saturation values on food tooltips, a saturation overlay on the hunger bar, and a preview of exactly how much hunger/health a food item in hand would restore before eating it.
This server’s appleskin.json5 has essentially every overlay turned on: tooltip values shown automatically without needing to hold Shift (showFoodValuesInTooltipAlways = true), the saturation HUD overlay, the hunger/health-restore-preview overlays for both main-hand and off-hand food, a food-exhaustion progress bar underlay, vanilla icon-shake animation matching, and food debug info in the F3 screen — nothing is left at a partial/minimal config, meaning the pack wants full nutritional visibility surfaced by default rather than opt-in.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods

Anticipated questions

What does this mod add? Food HUD info Minecraft normally hides: exact hunger/saturation values on tooltips, a saturation overlay on the hunger bar, and a preview of how much hunger/health a held food would restore before eating.
Do I have to hold Shift to see food values? No — showFoodValuesInTooltipAlways = true, so tooltip values show automatically without holding Shift.
Does the restore preview work for off-hand food too? Yes — the preview overlays are enabled for both main-hand and off-hand food.
Is this a stripped-down config here? No — essentially every overlay is on (saturation HUD, exhaustion bar underlay, F3 debug food info), so the pack surfaces full nutritional info by default.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Bad-Wither.title: Bad Wither No Cookie Reloaded
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Bad-Wither.content:
Bad Wither No Cookie Reloaded
A small client-side sound-muting utility (jar bwncr-fabric-1.20.1-3.17.2.jar, package com.kreezcraft.badwithernocookiereloaded). Lets you individually silence specific game sounds that some players find grating: the Wither’s ambient noise, the Wandering Trader, the Ender Dragon, thunder/lightning, plus a custom “Silence Us” list where you can add any other sound event by ID (e.g. entity.sheep.step) via the /listen command.
Correction worth flagging: earlier documentation for this pack (including this vault’s original Dimensions & Space Travel category note) assumed this jar’s bwncr filename prefix meant “Better Nether.” It does not — the real Better Nether mod ships in a separate jar (better-nether-9.0.10.jar, id betternether) and is documented at Better Nether. This mod is unrelated to dimension content entirely; it’s purely a sound-muffling QoL tool, functionally similar to Extreme Sound Muffler but scoped to a specific short list of sounds rather than arbitrary mute/volume control.

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It’s a client-side sound-muting utility that lets you individually silence specific game sounds some players find grating.

How do I mute another sound? Add any sound event by ID (e.g. entity.sheep.step) to the “Silence Us” list via the /listen command.
Is this “Better Nether”? No — despite the bwncr filename prefix, it’s unrelated to Better Nether (a separate betternether jar). It’s purely a sound-muffling tool, similar to Extreme Sound Muffler but scoped to a short fixed list.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Bartering-.title: Bartering Station
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Bartering-.content:
Bartering Station
Bartering Station (Fuzs, barteringstation, v8.0.0) automates vanilla piglin bartering: place the block, keep it stocked with gold ingots, and it feeds gold to any piglins in range and collects whatever they barter back — “still running around bartering manually? Let’s put those lazy piglins to work instead,” per its own description. config/barteringstation-server.toml gives it a search radius of horizontal_range = 12 blocks and vertical_range = 4 blocks to find eligible piglins, and a barter_delay = 300 ticks (15 seconds) cooldown between barter attempts — deliberately slower than vanilla’s raw 120-tick (6-second) manual barter timer, since the piglin being “inspected” takes half that delay and the other half is a cooldown baked in on top. The GUI shows how many piglins were found nearby for the current cycle, and config/barteringstation-client.toml renders the cooldown as directional arrows on the block by default (cooldown_render_type = "ARROWS", with OVERLAY, BOTH, or NONE as alternatives).
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods

Anticipated questions

What does this block do? It automates piglin bartering: keep it stocked with gold ingots and it feeds gold to nearby piglins and collects whatever they barter back.
How far does it reach for piglins? A horizontal range of 12 blocks and a vertical range of 4 blocks.
How often does it barter? Every 300 ticks (15 seconds) per attempt — deliberately slower than vanilla’s manual barter timer.
How do I know it’s working? The GUI shows how many piglins were found nearby for the current cycle, and the block renders the cooldown as directional arrows by default.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Block-Runn.title: Block Runner
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Block-Runn.content:
Block Runner
Block Runner (Fuzs, blockrunner, v8.0.4) rewards actually building paths: standing on tagged “fast” blocks like path/road blocks gives a walking-speed multiplier, while tagged “slow” blocks (mud, etc.) do the opposite — the mod’s own tagline is that it “encourages path building.” config/blockrunner.json defines six speed tiers via block tags, from #blockrunner:very_slow_blocks (0.45×) up through normal ground to #blockrunner:very_quick_blocks (1.55×), with intermediate slightly_slow (0.85×), slow (0.65×), slightly_quick (1.15×), and quick (1.35×) steps in between. config/blockrunner-client.toml adds a tooltip showing the exact multiplier on affected blocks (block_speed_multiplier_tooltip = true) and, notably, disables the FOV widening vanilla normally applies at higher speeds (disable_field_of_view_changes = true), so running fast on a paved road doesn’t also distort the camera the way sprinting does.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It gives a walking-speed multiplier when you stand on tagged “fast” blocks (like path/road blocks) and slows you on tagged “slow” blocks (like mud) — it’s designed to encourage path building.
How much faster or slower can it make me? Six tiers via block tags, from very-slow at 0.45× up through normal ground to very-quick at 1.55× (with 0.65×, 0.85×, 1.15×, and 1.35× steps in between).
How do I know a block’s multiplier? A tooltip shows the exact multiplier on affected blocks.
Does running fast distort my view like sprinting? No — the config disables the FOV widening vanilla applies at higher speeds, so the camera doesn’t warp.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Clickable-.title: Clickable Advancements Mod
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Clickable-.content:
Clickable Advancements Mod
Clickable Advancements Mod (clickadv, Someaddons, v1.20.1-3.8) does exactly what it says: advancement toasts that get posted to chat become clickable links you can open directly, instead of having to dig through the Advancements screen to find what you just earned. The one setting in config/clickadv.json, showAllInLocalChat (default true), broadens vanilla’s behavior — normally chat only shows advancements that get broadcast server-wide, but with this on every advancement you personally earn posts locally too, including “hidden text” category-only advancements.
Related

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It turns advancement toasts posted to chat into clickable links you can open directly, instead of digging through the Advancements screen to find what you just earned.
Do only server-wide advancements show up in chat? No — with showAllInLocalChat on (the default), every advancement you personally earn also posts to your local chat, including “hidden text” category-only advancements.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Comforts.title: Comforts
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Comforts.content:
Comforts
Comforts (Illusive Soulworks, comforts, v6.4.0) adds sleeping bags and hammocks in 16 dye colors each — portable sleep spots that skip the day (or, for hammocks, flip day to night) without setting a new spawn point the way a bed does. That distinction is the whole point of the mod: it’s built for adventuring parties who want to camp and skip a dangerous night without accidentally relocating their respawn to some random cave.
config/comforts-server.toml shows this pack running close to defaults but with real tuning: sleeping bags only work at NIGHT and hammocks only work during DAY (sleepingBagUse / hammockUse), so the two items are deliberately non-overlapping — a hammock is how you skip forward through the day, a sleeping bag is how you skip through the night. autoUse: true means simply placing one prompts the sleep animation automatically. sleepingBagBreakChance is set to 0, so unlike some configurations, bags in this pack are not consumed on use. Both items count toward phantom-spawn prevention the same as a vanilla bed (hammocksStopPhantoms / sleepingBagsStopPhantoms: true), and daySleepingPercentage is left at -1, meaning it falls back to the world’s normal playerSleepingPercentage game rule for how many players need to sleep to skip the night.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods

Anticipated questions

What does this mod add? Sleeping bags and hammocks in 16 dye colors each — portable sleep spots that skip time without setting a new spawn point the way a bed does.
Why use it instead of a bed? So an adventuring party can camp and skip a dangerous night without accidentally relocating their respawn to some random spot.
What’s the difference between the sleeping bag and the hammock here? Sleeping bags only work at night (to skip through the night); hammocks only work during the day (to skip forward through the day) — they’re deliberately non-overlapping.
Do sleeping bags get used up? No — sleepingBagBreakChance is set to 0, so bags aren’t consumed on use in this pack.
Do they stop phantoms? Yes — both count toward phantom-spawn prevention the same as a vanilla bed.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Create-Que.title: Create Questing
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Create-Que.content:
Create Questing
Create Questing (create_questing, v1.0.0, by ElocinDev) is a purely cosmetic add-on for FTB Quests: a Create-themed visual skin for the quest-book screen (blueprint-paper backgrounds, Create-styled chapter borders), applicable globally or per-chapter. It requires ftbquests as a hard dependency and does nothing without it.
This server’s create_questing.json scopes the theme narrowly rather than applying it everywhere: enable_theme_only_in_create_chapters = true restricts the Create skin to the chapters actually named Create and Blueprint (matching the create chapter in FTB Quests’s live chapter list), with blueprint_background_scale = 0.5, blueprint_background_opacity = 0.9, and the background overlay tinted pure white (255, 255, 255) — so other, non-Create-themed chapters keep FTB Quests’ default look rather than being reskinned unnecessarily.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods
FTB Quests

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It’s a purely cosmetic Create-themed skin for the FTB Quests quest-book screen (blueprint-paper backgrounds, Create-styled chapter borders).
Does it change gameplay? No — it’s cosmetic only, and it does nothing without FTB Quests, which is a hard dependency.
Does it reskin every chapter? No — this server restricts the skin to the Create/Blueprint chapters (enable_theme_only_in_create_chapters = true); other chapters keep FTB Quests’ default look.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Distant-Ho.title: Distant Horizons
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Distant-Ho.content:
Distant Horizons
Distant Horizons (distanthorizons, v3.2.0-b, by James Seibel and a large contributor list) generates and renders simplified LOD (level-of-detail) terrain far beyond the game’s normal view/simulation distance, at a low performance cost — the mod’s own description frames it as seeing “much farther without turning your game into a slideshow.” It works by maintaining a separate, coarser terrain database alongside the real world data, so distant mountains and coastlines render as low-poly approximations instead of vanishing into fog. Every player must install Distant Horizons 3.2.0-b client-side to see any benefit at all — a player without it sees normal vanilla fog and gets nothing from the server-side portion of the mod.
The server’s config/DistantHorizons.toml currently runs the deliberately conservative “share-only” profile: enableServerGeneration = false (the server won’t generate new LOD terrain ahead of exploration), distantGeneratorMode = "PRE_EXISTING_ONLY" (LOD data is only ever built from chunks that have genuinely been explored/generated already, never speculatively pre-generated), numberOfThreads = 2 and threadRunTimeRatio = "1.0" (modest, unthrottled CPU budget), and verticalQuality = "MEDIUM" (mid-tier LOD fidelity, between the cheapest HEIGHT_MAP and the most detailed PIXEL_ART). This is a deliberate rollback: on 2026-07-11 the server briefly ran heavy generation (enableServerGeneration=true, FEATURES mode, 4 threads) with an active 2000-chunk pregen, but FEATURES mode’s approximate generator didn’t match Prominence’s modded worldgen closely enough and produced visible client-side graphical glitches. The pregen was cancelled and the config reverted the same day, and the resulting 2.8 GB stale overworld LOD cache was wiped and allowed to rebuild cleanly from real explored terrain — it had regrown to roughly 300 MB of legitimate data by 2026-07-12 before the stale backup copy was deleted during cleanup. DH rewrites its own config on shutdown, so any live edit to DistantHorizons.toml only sticks if made while the server is stopped.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods
Getting Started

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It generates and renders simplified LOD terrain far beyond the normal view distance at low performance cost, so distant mountains and coastlines render as low-poly approximations instead of vanishing into fog.
Do I need to install anything client-side? Yes — every player must install Distant Horizons 3.2.0-b client-side, or they just see normal vanilla fog and get nothing from it.
Does the server pre-generate distant terrain ahead of me? No — it runs a conservative “share-only” profile (enableServerGeneration = false, PRE_EXISTING_ONLY), so LOD is only built from chunks that have genuinely been explored.
Why isn’t heavy generation used? It was tried briefly, but FEATURES mode’s approximate generator didn’t match Prominence’s modded worldgen and caused client-side graphical glitches, so it was reverted the same day.
Can I edit the DH config while the server is running? No — DH rewrites its own config on shutdown, so edits only stick if made while the server is stopped.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Do-a-Barre.title: Do a Barrel Roll
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Do-a-Barre.content:
Do a Barrel Roll
Do a Barrel Roll (do_a_barrel_roll, enjarai, v3.6.1) turns elytra flight into a full flight-sim: it adds a roll axis on top of vanilla’s pitch/yaw, so you can genuinely barrel-roll and loop-de-loop instead of just gliding flat. config/do_a_barrel_roll-client.json shows the pack running with mostly vanilla-leaning defaults — activation_behaviour: VANILLA (single jump to activate, no triple-jump gimmick), roll/yaw axes not swapped, momentum-mouse flying off — but banking is on (enable_banking: true, banking_strength: 20.0), which adds a continuous realistic yaw/pitch drift based on current roll so turns feel like a plane banking rather than a rigid 90-degree snap; automatic righting is left off, so players have to manually recover from a roll. The mod’s own description bills it as “Microsoft Flight Simulator for Minecraft elytras,” and it explicitly breaks OptiFabric and older Controlify versions.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods
Icarus

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It turns elytra flight into a flight-sim by adding a roll axis on top of vanilla’s pitch/yaw, so you can genuinely barrel-roll and loop-de-loop instead of gliding flat.
How do I activate the roll flight? A single jump — the pack uses activation_behaviour: VANILLA (no triple-jump gimmick).
Do turns feel like a real plane? Yes — banking is on (strength 20.0), adding continuous realistic yaw/pitch drift based on your roll, so turns bank rather than snapping rigidly.
Does it auto-level me out of a roll? No — automatic righting is left off, so you recover from rolls manually.
Does it conflict with anything? Yes — it explicitly breaks OptiFabric and older Controlify versions.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/EMI-Enchan.title: EMI Enchanting
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/EMI-Enchan.content:
EMI Enchanting
EMI Enchanting (emi_enchanting, v0.1.2, by fzzyhmstrs) is an EMI addon dedicated to enchantment information: look up an enchantment and see how to obtain it (enchanting table odds, loot sources), what items it can legally be applied to, and — importantly in a modpack this size, where multiple mods add competing or overlapping enchantments — which other enchantments it’s mutually exclusive with. That exclusion data is normally buried in code/data-pack files; surfacing it in EMI avoids the trial-and-error of finding out an enchant conflict only after wasting an anvil combine.
It’s a lightweight, config-free plugin (no entry in config/ beyond what EMI itself provides) from the same author as EMI Loot, and the two are commonly installed as a pair.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/EMI-Loot.title: EMI Loot
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/EMI-Loot.content:
EMI Loot
EMI Loot (emi_loot, v0.7.9, by fzzyhmstrs) folds Minecraft’s loot-table system into EMI: look up an item and see every chest it can spawn in, every block/mob it drops from, and results from gameplay loot sources like fishing or archaeology brushing — the categories the mod calls parseChestLoot, parseBlockLoot, parseMobLoot, parseGameplayLoot, and parseArchaeologyLoot, all enabled in this install’s emi_loot_config.toml. Chest loot entries are shown compacted (compactLoot on for every category) rather than as one row per possible roll, and drop-chance percentages are displayed to one decimal place (chanceDecimalPlaces = 1) with condition text rendered as tooltips (conditionStyle = "tooltip") instead of inline clutter.
The config also has directDrops enabled across the board (chest/block/mob/gameplay/archaeology), and a skippedKeys list that filters out noisy internal loot-function entries (like limit_count or fill_player_head) that would otherwise show up as meaningless recipe steps. Debug logging for untranslated tables is off for all categories, meaning this is a production-tuned config, not a development build.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/EMI-Ores.title: EMI Ores
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/EMI-Ores.content:
EMI Ores
EMI Ores (emi_ores, v1.2, by Abbie) adds ore-generation information directly into EMI’s item lookup: check an ore item and see where it actually spawns in the world — biome restrictions, Y-level ranges, vein characteristics — without alt-tabbing to a wiki or JEI-style worldgen viewer mod. In a pack with dozens of modded ores stacked across vanilla, Tech Reborn, Modern Industrialization, and Industrial Revolution (later reconciled by Almost Unified), knowing where to dig for a specific material is exactly the kind of lookup this closes.
It’s a minimal addon — this install’s emi_ores-client.json is a 33-byte stub, so it’s running effectively stock/default settings.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/EMI-Profes.content:
EMI Professions
EMI Professions (emiprofessions, v1.0.4, by Mrbysco & ShyNieke) is a small EMI addon that adds villager profession information into EMI’s item lookups. Looking up a profession-related item (a job-site block like a lectern, smoker, or fletching table) surfaces which villager profession it assigns and what that profession trades, folding villager-trading knowledge into the same lookup workflow players already use for crafting recipes instead of requiring a separate wiki check.
It requires EMI 1.1.10+ and Minecraft 1.20.1+Java 17, and is purely additive — it has no config file of its own in this install and just registers extra recipe-viewer pages on top of the base EMI catalog.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/EMI.title: EMI
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/EMI.content:
EMI
EMI (emi, v1.1.22, by Emi) is the pack’s recipe viewer — the JEI/REI-family mod that answers “how do I make this” and “what is this used for” for every recipe type registered by every mod. Hover an item and hit the recipe/usage hotkeys and EMI overlays a scrollable panel of matching recipes, drag-and-drop-fillable directly into a crafting grid where the game supports it. Because Prominence II runs dozens of tech, magic, and cooking mods with their own custom machines and recipe types (Create sequenced assembly, AE2 patterns, Tech Reborn machines, Botania mana recipes, and more), EMI’s recipe-type API is what keeps every one of them discoverable without a wiki.
EMI itself ships no server-side config — behavior is almost entirely client-driven — but this install carries a custom emi.css (~10 KB) in config/, meaning the pack has hand-tuned EMI’s on-screen styling rather than shipping it stock. The real depth comes from its addon ecosystem: EMI Professions, EMI Enchanting, EMI Loot, EMI Ores, Extra Mod Integrations, and emi-letsdo-compat each bolt on a specific category of information EMI doesn’t natively know, while Almost Unified and Polymorph work alongside it to keep the sea of duplicate/conflicting recipes from different tech mods sane. A handful of other EMI plugins are also present but disabled (emicompat, emiffect, emitrades — all .jar.disabled), suggesting the pack maintainers trimmed the addon set down to the ones actually needed.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Extra-Mod-.title: Extra Mod Integrations
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Extra-Mod-.content:
Extra Mod Integrations
Extra Mod Integrations (extra-mod-integrations, v0.4.7, by Kneelawk) is EMI’s broad-spectrum compatibility addon — its stated goal is literally “support for as many mods as possible.” Where the other EMI addons in this pack are narrow and single-purpose (loot tables, enchantments, ore locations), this one is the catch-all that renders recipe types the base EMI API doesn’t otherwise understand cleanly, filling gaps left by mods that implement unusual or non-standard crafting systems.
It sits alongside two more targeted, mod-specific EMI plugins also present in the pack — indrev-emi-plugin for Industrial Revolution and ae2-emi-crafting for Applied Energistics 2 (currently disabled) — rather than replacing them; Extra Mod Integrations covers the long tail everything else misses.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Extreme-So.title: Extreme Sound Muffler
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Extreme-So.content:
Extreme Sound Muffler
Extreme Sound Muffler (LeoBeliik, extremesoundmuffler, v3.51) is a client-side-only mod that lets each player selectively mute or lower the volume of individual sounds — anything from a specific mob noise to a specific block’s ambient loop — down to anywhere between silent and 90%, rather than only having vanilla’s blanket category sliders. config/extremesoundmuffler.json5 blacklists whole categories from being muffled by default (forbiddenSounds: ["ui.", "music.", "ambient."], so menu clicks, music discs, and ambient cave sounds stay untouched by accident), while modsMuffled is left empty — no mod’s entire sound set is being globally muffled pack-wide. It also adds a configurable “Muffle” button to the inventory screen (both survival and creative, separately positionable) and supports placeable in-world “anchors” that mute sounds within a radius (maxAnchorRange: 32 blocks by default). Because it’s clientside-only, each player runs their own settings — nothing here affects what other players hear.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It’s a client-side-only mod that lets each player selectively mute or lower the volume of individual sounds, rather than only using vanilla’s blanket category sliders.
How quiet can I make a sound? Anywhere between silent and 90% volume.
Do music and menu sounds get muffled by accident? No — the UI, music, and ambient categories are blacklisted from muffling by default.
Can I mute sounds only in a certain area? Yes — you can place in-world “anchors” that mute sounds within a radius (default 32 blocks).
Does my muffling affect other players? No — it’s client-side only, so each player runs their own settings and nothing affects what others hear.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/FTB-Librar.title: FTB Library
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/FTB-Librar.content:
FTB Library
FTB Library (ftblibrary, v2001.2.9, by the FTB Team) is the shared foundational code and UI toolkit that every other FTB mod in the pack is built on — it provides the common GUI framework, config system, and utility code that FTB Quests and FTB Teams both require (ftblibrary >=2001.2.1 / >=2001.2.0 respectively) to run at all. It adds nothing directly visible to players by itself; its entire purpose is being the plumbing underneath the mods that are visible.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/FTB-Quests.title: FTB Quests
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/FTB-Quests.content:
FTB Quests
FTB Quests (ftbquests, v2001.4.13, by the FTB Team) is the Quest Book itself — Prominence II’s structured progression system, guiding players from “punch a tree” through the pack’s dozens of integrated mods via chaptered, reward-granting checklists rather than leaving discovery entirely to wiki-diving or EMI lookups. It’s the mod referenced directly in Getting Started and is functionally the pack’s spine: it depends on Architectury, and on FTB Library and FTB Teams to function at all.
This server’s live quest data (config/ftbquests/quests/chapters/) contains 33 chapters, and their names map almost one-to-one onto the pack’s major integrated mods and content pillars: getting_started, main_story, and elhasturian_era alongside dedicated chapters for applied_energistics_2, botania, create, tech_reborn, modern_industrialization, industrial_revolution, powah, the_nether, the_bumblezone, deeper_and_darker, to_the_end, dplanets_and_space (Ad Astra-style space progression), eenchanting, e_spell_books, c_bewitchment, archon, artifact_reforging, d_the_art_of_transmogrification, simply_swords, gear_mariums_soulslike_weaponry, reforging, gadgets, 8the_prision, the_scarred_night, dmastering_fatew, 4trophy_collection, collectibles/collectibles_2, and a seasonal a_jolly_christmas chapter. A separate reward_tables/ directory (runes, wands, tier-4 rings, transmog skins, metal blocks, eyes, spell enchants) backs randomized quest reward pools rather than fixed single-item payouts. The Starter Kit hands every new player an ftbquests:book on spawn (see Starter Kit), meaning the quest book is quite literally the first item a new player holds.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/FTB-Teams.title: FTB Teams
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/FTB-Teams.content:
FTB Teams
FTB Teams (ftbteams, v2001.3.1, by the FTB Team) adds the ability to form parties/teams whose members share FTB Quests progress and rewards — it’s the mod that turns quest completion from a solo checklist into something a group can tackle together, so one player claiming a quest reward doesn’t leave teammates locked out. It depends on Architectury and FTB Library, and FTB Quests itself declares a hard dependency on FTB Teams (>=2001.1.4) — quests can’t function without it.
Team-based kill credit specifically (making sure any team member’s kill counts toward a shared kill-quest) is handled by the separate add-on Quest Kill Task, since base FTB Teams only manages team membership/permissions, not quest-objective-specific credit logic.

What does this mod do? It adds parties/teams whose members share FTB Quests progress and rewards, so one player claiming a reward doesn’t leave teammates locked out.
Is it required for quests? Yes — FTB Quests declares a hard dependency on FTB Teams, so quests can’t function without it.
Does it make a teammate’s kills count toward my kill-quests? Not by itself — base FTB Teams only manages membership/permissions; team kill credit is handled by the separate Quest Kill Task add-on.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Fabric-Way.title: Fabric Waystones
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Fabric-Way.content:
Fabric Waystones
Fabric Waystones (fwaystones, v3.3.3, by LordDeatHunter, package name “Wraith Waystones”) is the pack’s fast-travel backbone: place or find a waystone block, right-click to bind/discover it, and teleport back to it from anywhere later. It depends on owo (a shared Fabric UI/config library) and is the mod Xaero’s World Map/Xaero’s Minimap waypoints exist alongside for getting around a large modded world without walking or relying purely on Nether-portal shortcuts.
This server’s config.json5 generates waystones naturally in villages (generate_in_villages = true, 1 per village via min_per_village/max_per_village = 1, village_waystone_weight = 200), and the file contains an extensive add_waystone_structure_piece map wiring waystone spawns into dozens of custom village variants from the pack’s structure mods — desert, taiga, savanna, plains, and numerous “Kaisyn” village packs (Polynesian, Iberian, Rustic, Viking, Mediterranean, Tudor, Swiss, Mushroom, Swedish, Badlands Pueblo, Romanian, Tribal, and more) — meaning waystone placement was deliberately hooked into this pack’s specific worldgen rather than left at vanilla defaults. Teleportation cost is set to cost_type = "LEVEL" (XP levels, not items) with base_cost = 1 and cost_per_block_distance = 0.0 — meaning every waystone jump costs a flat 1 XP level regardless of distance travelled. Waystones can be broken by "ANYONE" (permission_level_for_breaking_waystones), have waystone_block_hardness = 4.0, and free_local_void_teleport = true grants a no-cost teleport back to a “local void” bookmark. Discovery via map item is disabled (discover_waystone_on_map_use = false), so waystones must be visited in person to be bound.

What does a teleport cost? A flat 1 XP level per jump, regardless of distance.
Can I discover a waystone from a map without visiting it? No — map discovery is disabled, so waystones must be visited in person to be bound.
Who can break a waystone? Anyone — the break permission is set to “ANYONE.”

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Fancy-Hotb.title: Fancy Hotbar
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Fancy-Hotb.content:
Fancy Hotbar
Fancy Hotbar (fancy_hotbar, ElocinDev, v1.0.0) is a purely cosmetic HUD mod that redraws the vanilla hotbar and experience counter using a resource pack, described in its own metadata as “fancy hotbar for your hotbary needs, requires a resourcepack!” config/fancy_hotbar.json5 has both pieces enabled — custom_hotbar.enable and custom_experience_number.enable are both true, with the XP counter tinted a custom gold color (xp_color: 16099138) and no offsets applied to either element’s position.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It’s a purely cosmetic HUD mod that redraws the vanilla hotbar and experience counter using a resource pack.
Does it change gameplay? No — it’s cosmetic only, and it requires a resource pack to display.
What’s enabled here? Both the custom hotbar and the custom experience number, with the XP counter tinted a custom gold color.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Fish-On-Th.title: Fish On The Line
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Fish-On-Th.content:
Fish On The Line
Fish On The Line (fishontheline, Rick South / Serilum, v3.5) is a single-mechanic QoL mod: it rings a bell held in your offhand the moment something bites your fishing line, so you don’t have to stare at the bobber. The server’s config/fishontheline.json5 keeps the default mustHoldBellInOffhand = true, meaning the audio cue only fires if a bell is actually equipped offhand while fishing — no bell, no ring. It ships a ModMenu config-screen integration so the setting is reachable in-game.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods
Villager Names

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It rings a bell held in your offhand the moment something bites your fishing line, so you don’t have to stare at the bobber.
Does it ring if I’m not holding a bell? No — mustHoldBellInOffhand = true, so the cue only fires if a bell is actually equipped in the offhand while fishing.
Where do I change its setting? Through its ModMenu config-screen integration in-game.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Highlight.title: Highlight
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Highlight.content:
Highlight
Highlight (ThatGravyBoat, highlight, v2.0.1) is a small visual-polish mod that replaces the rigid, boxy block-selection outline vanilla uses on certain blocks with shapes that actually follow the block’s real geometry — stairs, slabs, fences, and similar angled/partial blocks get a selection highlight that matches their model instead of a plain cube. It carries no user-facing configuration; it just changes rendering. Depends on Resourceful Lib (bundled) and ships an optional “Highlight Extended” companion resource pack for further-refined shapes. Note there is a separate, similarly-named Highlighter mod in this pack’s mods folder — that one is currently disabled (.jar.disabled) and is a different mod entirely.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It replaces vanilla’s boxy block-selection outline with shapes that follow the block’s real geometry, so stairs, slabs, and fences get a highlight matching their model instead of a plain cube.
Is there anything to configure? No — it carries no user-facing configuration; it just changes rendering (with an optional “Highlight Extended” resource pack for further-refined shapes).
Is this the same as the “Highlighter” mod? No — a separate, similarly-named Highlighter mod is present in the pack but disabled; it’s a different mod entirely.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Icarus.title: Icarus
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Icarus.content:
Icarus
Icarus (Cammie & Up, icarus, v2.13.1) adds a wide range of colorful, cosmetic wing sets worn as Trinkets accessories rather than replacing the elytra — so players can have a flight-capable back item that actually looks distinct per-character. config/icarus.jsonc sets armor_slows: true (wearing armor still reduces flight performance, same tradeoff as vanilla elytra) and enables looping (can_loop_de_loop: true), while can_slow_fall is off. Wings here have unlimited durability (wings_durability: 0) and are capped from flying infinitely high (max_height_enabled: true, max_height_above_world: 64 blocks above the world’s height limit), with required_food_amount: 6.001 meaning flight is cut off once hunger drops below roughly 3 food points. It depends on Trinkets, ResourcefulConfig, and Common Networking under the hood.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods
Do a Barrel Roll

Anticipated questions

What does this mod add? A wide range of colorful, cosmetic wing sets worn as Trinkets accessories rather than replacing the elytra, so a flight-capable back item can look distinct per character.
Does wearing armor affect flight? Yes — armor_slows: true, the same tradeoff as the vanilla elytra.
Do the wings wear out? No — they have unlimited durability here.
Can I fly infinitely high? No — flight is capped at 64 blocks above the world’s height limit.
Does flying use hunger? Yes — flight cuts off once hunger drops below roughly 3 food points.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Immersive-.title: Immersive Melodies
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Immersive-.content:
Immersive Melodies
Immersive Melodies (Luke100000, immersive_melodies, v0.5.0) lets players compose and play custom MIDI melodies on in-game instruments — its own tagline is “play custom melodies on various instruments and annoy your friends!” config/immersive_melodies.json sets maxAudibleDistance: 48 blocks and stopGameMusicForPlayers: true (the ambient music track ducks out while someone’s actively playing nearby, so it doesn’t clash), while stopGameMusicForMobs: false leaves mob-triggered music alone. Mobs can also pick up and play dropped instruments themselves (forceMobsToPickUp: true), though several hostile mobs — wither skeletons, piglins, zombified piglins, zombies, pillagers, skeletons — have their instrument volume dialed down to 1% (mobInstrumentFactors) so they don’t turn combat encounters into a concert. A built-in keyboard-to-MIDI mapping (scancodeToMidi) lets players play live using number/letter keys rather than only uploading pre-made files.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It lets players compose and play custom MIDI melodies on in-game instruments (its own tagline: “play custom melodies on various instruments and annoy your friends”).
Does it clash with the game’s music? No — ambient music ducks out while someone’s actively playing nearby (stopGameMusicForPlayers: true), and melodies only carry within 48 blocks.
Can mobs play instruments too? Yes — mobs can pick up dropped instruments, but several hostile mobs have their instrument volume dialed down to 1% so combat doesn’t become a concert.
Do I have to upload MIDI files? No — a built-in keyboard-to-MIDI mapping lets you play live using number/letter keys.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Jade.title: Jade
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Jade.content:
Jade
Jade (jade, v11.13.1, by Snownee) is a Hwyla fork — the mod that puts a small info panel on-screen showing whatever block or entity you’re looking at: name, mod source, block states, container contents preview, mob health, and (for tile entities like AE2 grid nodes) live machine data. It runs passively all the time and is one of the mods a player stops consciously noticing within the first hour, which is exactly the point.
This server’s jade.json runs the dark theme (jade:dark), display mode TOGGLE, overlay anchored bottom-left at (0.01, 0.98) and scaled to 0.75, with the overlay deliberately hidden from the F3 debug screen and the tab list (hideFromDebug/hideFromTabList both true) so it doesn’t clutter either. Jade ships a plugin system with per-mod integrations — sort-order.json shows registered providers for Applied Energistics 2 (ae2:charger, ae2:crafting_monitor, ae2:grid_node_state, ae2:power_storage, etc.) and Extended AE (extendedae:jade_chamber, extendedae:jade_wireless), on top of vanilla providers for beehives, brewing stands, campfires and more — so machine and container mods across the pack get tailored tooltips rather than a generic fallback.
Related

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It puts a small info panel on-screen showing whatever block or entity you’re looking at — name, mod source, block states, container preview, mob health, and live machine data for tile entities.
What theme and position is it set to here? The dark theme, TOGGLE display mode, anchored bottom-left and scaled to 0.75.
Does it clutter the F3 screen? No — it’s deliberately hidden from the F3 debug screen and the tab list.
Does it show useful info for modded machines? Yes — it has per-mod integrations (e.g. AE2 charger/crafting monitor/grid nodes, Extended AE) so machine and container mods get tailored tooltips rather than a generic fallback.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Leaves-Be-.title: Leaves Be Gone
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Leaves-Be-.content:
Leaves Be Gone
Leaves Be Gone (Fuzs, leavesbegone, v8.0.0) speeds up vanilla’s slow, random leaf-decay tick so that leaves left floating after a tree is cut down disappear promptly instead of hanging in the air for minutes. config/leavesbegone-server.toml sets the window to minimum_decay_ticks = 5 through maximum_decay_ticks = 20 — leaves start checking for decay within a quarter-second to one second of losing their supporting logs, a huge acceleration over vanilla’s much longer random-tick-based timer. It’s a natural companion to TreeChop in this pack: TreeChop already clears most connected leaves the instant a tree is felled, and Leaves Be Gone mops up whatever’s left (leaves just out of TreeChop’s maxBreakLeavesDistance, or from trees chopped by other means).
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods
TreeChop

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It speeds up vanilla’s slow, random leaf-decay so leaves left floating after a tree is cut disappear promptly instead of hanging in the air for minutes.
How fast do leaves decay with it? Within about a quarter-second to one second of losing their supporting logs (5–20 ticks), far faster than vanilla.
How does it relate to TreeChop? TreeChop already clears most connected leaves the instant a tree is felled, and Leaves Be Gone mops up whatever’s left — leaves just out of TreeChop’s range, or trees chopped by other means.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Mod-Menu.title: Mod Menu
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Mod-Menu.content:
Mod Menu
Mod Menu (modmenu, TerraformersMC, v7.2.2) is the standard Fabric mod-list and config-screen hub — it adds a “Mods” button to the title screen listing every installed mod with its icon, description, and links, and doubles as the entry point for any mod’s in-game config screen. It’s foundational rather than decorative: a large share of the mods in this pack (Fish On The Line, Villager Names, No Chat Reports, Icarus, Do a Barrel Roll, Runelic, PigPen, and others) register a modmenu entrypoint specifically so their settings are reachable through here, and Mod Menu itself intentionally breaks the older/incompatible better_mod_button mod to avoid two competing implementations of the same button.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It’s the standard Fabric mod-list and config hub — it adds a “Mods” button to the title screen listing every installed mod, and is the entry point for any mod’s in-game config screen.
Why is it foundational rather than decorative? Many mods in this pack (Fish On The Line, Villager Names, No Chat Reports, Icarus, and others) register a modmenu entrypoint specifically so their settings are reachable through it.
Does it conflict with anything? Yes — it intentionally breaks the older better_mod_button mod to avoid two competing implementations of the same button.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/No-Chat-Re.title: No Chat Reports
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/No-Chat-Re.content:
No Chat Reports
No Chat Reports (nochatreports, Aizistral, v1.20.1-v2.2.2) strips the cryptographic signatures Mojang attaches to chat messages so they can no longer be tied back to a player’s Mojang/Microsoft account or submitted through vanilla’s Player Chat Reporting feature — relevant on this server specifically because online-mode=true is required for the EasyAuth mixed cracked/premium setup (see the main server doc §10a), which means premium players’ real accounts are in play. config/NoChatReports/NCR-Common.json leaves demandOnClient: false (players aren’t forced to install it client-side to connect), and config/NoChatReports/NCR-Client.json layers on privacy defaults beyond the core signature-stripping: telemetry is disabled and its button removed (disableTelemetry, removeTelemetryButton), the report button is hidden outright (alwaysHideReportButton), and insecure/modified/system message warning icons are all suppressed. NCR-ServerPreferences.json is left at its default empty signingModes, so the server doesn’t override client signing-mode choices.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It strips the cryptographic signatures Mojang attaches to chat messages, so they can’t be tied back to a player’s account or submitted through vanilla’s chat-reporting feature.
Why is it relevant on this server? Because online-mode=true is required for the EasyAuth mixed cracked/premium setup, meaning premium players’ real accounts are in play.
Do I have to install it to connect? No — demandOnClient: false, so players aren’t forced to install it client-side to join.
What else does it change client-side? It disables telemetry (and removes its button), hides the report button outright, and suppresses insecure/modified/system message warning icons.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Open-Parti.title: Open Parties and Claims
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Open-Parti.content:
Open Parties and Claims
Open Parties and Claims (openpartiesandclaims, v0.25.10, by Xaero96 and contributors) does two related jobs: chunk claiming (protecting builds from griefing/unwanted edits by other players) and force-loading claimed chunks, plus a party system for grouping players so location sharing and claim permissions extend to the whole group. The mod’s own description explicitly calls out that Xaero’s Minimap and World Map are recommended to fully visualize claims and party member positions — see Xaero’s Minimap and Xaero’s World Map.
This server’s openpartiesandclaims-server.toml is heavily tuned: parties support up to maxPartyMembers = 64 and maxPartyAllies = 64, using primaryPartySystem = "argonauts_guilds" as the underlying party backend and permissionSystem = "prometheus" for permission checks. Claims allow maxPlayerClaims = 500 chunks per player, a maxClaimDistance = 5 (how far a new claim can be from existing ones), and claims auto-expire after playerClaimsExpirationTime = 8760 hours (exactly one year) of inactivity, converting to unclaimed rather than lingering forever. Protection is broken into a long list of individually player-configurable toggles — door/button/chest/furnace/anvil/beacon/enchanting-table interaction exceptions, crop trampling, entity access rules for villagers/zombies/livestock, projectile and explosion protection, nether portal handling, and more — with per-player settings persisted to world/data/openpartiesandclaims/player-configs/<uuid>.toml (only written on save events, not instantly). This server’s owner Toubz has door-locking specifically configured (Doors = 0, fromParty = true, meaning doors are locked to non-party members) — see the project’s own operational notes for the exact RCON syntax (openpac player-config set <key> <value>, run as the player). claimWelcomeMessages = true means players get a chat notice when entering someone else’s claimed territory.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods
Xaero’s Minimap
Xaero’s World Map
FTB Teams

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? Two related jobs — chunk claiming (protecting builds from griefing) and force-loading claimed chunks — plus a party system for grouping players so location sharing and claim permissions extend to the whole group.
How many chunks can I claim? Up to 500 chunks per player.
Do claims last forever if I stop playing? No — claims auto-expire after 8760 hours (exactly one year) of inactivity and convert back to unclaimed.
Can I control exactly what others can do in my claim? Yes — protection is broken into many player-configurable toggles (doors, buttons, chests, crop trampling, entity access, explosions, and more).
What visualizes my claims and party members? Xaero’s Minimap and World Map, which the mod explicitly recommends — see Xaero’s Minimap and Xaero’s World Map.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/PigPen.title: PigPen
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/PigPen.content:
PigPen
PigPen (Darkhax, pigpen, v15.0.3) brings “the classic Pig Pen Cipher” into Minecraft as an in-game font, the same substitution cipher used for real-world puzzle boxes and ARGs, for anyone building secret messages, puzzle rooms, or lore text into signs and books. Like its sibling mod Runelic (same author, same minimal structure — just a font plus ModMenu contact links), it adds no gameplay systems of its own.
Related

Runelic

Anticipated questions

What does this mod add? The classic Pig Pen Cipher as an in-game font — the same substitution cipher used for real-world puzzle boxes and ARGs — for secret messages, puzzle rooms, or lore text on signs and books.
Does it add any gameplay systems? No — like its sibling Runelic, it’s just a font with ModMenu contact links, no mechanics of its own.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Ping-Wheel.title: Ping Wheel
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Ping-Wheel.content:
Ping Wheel
Ping Wheel (pingwheel, Luken, v1.12.1) brings the “ping” callout mechanic from games like Apex Legends or Deep Rock Galactic into Minecraft — a radial wheel lets you mark a location, item, or danger for your whole party to see as a waypoint, without needing to type in chat. The server’s config/pingwheel.server.json sets playerTrackingEnabled: true and a modest anti-spam limit (rateLimit: 5, msToRegenerate: 1000 — 5 pings banked, regenerating one per second), while config/pingwheel.json tunes the client visuals: pings last 7 seconds, render up to 400 blocks away, and raycast out to 1024 blocks to find what you’re pointing at. It also ships an optional Simple Voice Chat integration entrypoint, though that mod isn’t installed in this pack.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods
Show Me What You Got

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It brings the “ping” callout mechanic from games like Apex Legends into Minecraft — a radial wheel lets you mark a location, item, or danger as a waypoint for your whole party, without typing in chat.
Can I spam pings endlessly? No — there’s an anti-spam limit of 5 pings banked, regenerating one per second.
How far do pings work? They render up to 400 blocks away and raycast out to 1024 blocks to find what you’re pointing at, lasting 7 seconds.
Does it need Simple Voice Chat? No — it ships an optional Simple Voice Chat integration, but that mod isn’t installed in this pack.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Polymorph.title: Polymorph
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Polymorph.content:
Polymorph
Polymorph (polymorph, v0.49.10, by Illusive Soulworks) solves the crafting-conflict problem that comes from running a mod-dense pack: when two or more recipes produce the same result from a similar/identical set of ingredients (a common collision between overlapping tech mods), vanilla just silently picks one and the player never gets a say. Polymorph adds a small on-screen picker so the player can choose which mod’s recipe/result they actually want when a conflict is detected, rather than being stuck with whatever the game arbitrarily resolved.
This install’s polymorph-integrations.toml enables the quickbench third-party integration (quickbench = true) — the config’s own comment flags that enabling third-party integrations “introduces instability and performance overheads” and recommends disabling them first if troubleshooting crashes, so this is a deliberate, opted-in feature rather than a default. Polymorph is a natural complement to Almost Unified: Almost Unified reduces conflicts up front by merging duplicate items/tags, while Polymorph handles whatever recipe ambiguity remains.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods
EMI
Almost Unified

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It solves crafting conflicts: when two recipes produce the same result from similar/identical ingredients, it adds an on-screen picker so you choose which mod’s recipe you want, instead of the game silently picking one.
What’s the quickbench setting about? This install opts into the quickbench third-party integration; the config warns that third-party integrations can add instability/overhead and suggests disabling them first when troubleshooting crashes.
How does it relate to Almost Unified? They complement each other — Almost Unified merges duplicate items/tags up front, while Polymorph handles whatever recipe ambiguity remains.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Quest-Kill.title: Quest Kill Task
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Quest-Kill.content:
Quest Kill Task
Quest Kill Task (questkilltask, v0.2.0, by MuonR) is a small, focused add-on for FTB Quests that adds team-based kill credit: without it, a “kill 10 zombies” quest task only tracks kills made by the specific player who claimed/started that task. With Quest Kill Task installed, any kill made by any member of the same FTB Teams party counts toward the shared objective, so a group tackling a quest chapter together isn’t forced to grind identical kill counters in parallel.
It’s a thin, dependency-driven mod (fabric-api, Minecraft 1.20.1, Java 17+) with no meaningful config of its own — it exists purely to patch this one specific gap in FTB Quests’ default kill-task behavior.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods
FTB Quests
FTB Teams

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It’s a focused FTB Quests add-on that adds team-based kill credit — any kill by any member of the same FTB Teams party counts toward a shared kill objective.
What problem does it fix? Without it, a “kill 10 zombies” task only tracks the specific player who started it, forcing a group to grind identical kill counters in parallel.
Is there anything to configure? No — it’s a thin, dependency-driven mod with no meaningful config; it exists purely to patch this one gap.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Runelic.title: Runelic
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Runelic.content:
Runelic
Runelic (Darkhax, runelic, v18.0.4) adds a “Runelic” font system to the game — a fantasy rune alphabet usable as an in-game font, typically for signs, books, or lecterns that want to look mystical rather than legible. It’s a tiny, focused utility mod: no gameplay mechanics, just a font resource plus the surrounding Fabric plumbing (Bookshelf dependency, ModMenu links to Darkhax’s Discord/Patreon/CurseForge pages). It shares an author and a near-identical structure with PigPen, another Darkhax font/cipher mod in this pack.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Server-Bro.title: Server Browser
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Server-Bro.content:
Server Browser
Server Browser (serverbrowser, Thonk, v1.3.1) adds an in-game browser for finding other servers running the same modpack, pulled from minecraft.multiplayerservers.net. It’s pre-configured for Prominence II specifically: config/ServerBrowser/serverbrowser.json sets modPackFilter: "Prominence II [RPG]" (so the browser only lists other Prominence II servers), a bisectPackID of 19073, and an official server entry pointing at prom2.moddedmc.net that gets pinned to the top of the list as “Featured.” This server itself (a private address) isn’t in that official list — it’s a private whitelist-only instance — so the feature mainly surfaces other public Prominence II communities to players browsing from here.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It adds an in-game browser for finding other servers running the same modpack, pre-configured to list Prominence II servers specifically.
Will it show this server? No — this is a private whitelist-only instance and isn’t in the official list, so the feature mainly surfaces other public Prominence II communities.
Is there a featured server? Yes — an official entry pointing at prom2.moddedmc.net is pinned to the top of the list as “Featured.”

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Show-Me-Wh.title: Show Me What You Got
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Show-Me-Wh.content:
Show Me What You Got
Show Me What You Got (smwyg, Apace, v1.1.1) lets you post the item currently in your hand into chat as a rich, hoverable link other players can inspect — the classic “check this out” flex, without them needing to be standing next to you. It’s a tiny mod with one piece of user-facing text: chat shows [stale link] if someone clicks an item link that’s no longer valid (e.g. the sender’s game session ended or the item changed).

What does this mod do? It lets you post the item currently in your hand into chat as a rich, hoverable link other players can inspect, without them needing to stand next to you.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Starter-Ki.title: Starter Kit
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Starter-Ki.content:
Starter Kit
Starter Kit (starterkit, v7.4, by Rick South) gives every player configurable starting gear the very first time they join the world, rather than dropping them in with a completely empty inventory.
This server’s active kit (config/starterkit/kits/starterkit.txt) is deliberately lean: a stone sword, 12 bread, a shield in the off-hand slot, and — notably — an ftbquests:book (the FTB Quests quest book), meaning the very first item a new player effectively “has” is the quest book that’s meant to guide the rest of their playthrough, not combat or building gear. addExistingItemsAfterKitSet = true means anything already in a player’s inventory when the kit is applied (e.g. items from other join-time mods) is preserved rather than wiped, and enableFTBIslandCreateCompatibility = true re-applies the kit if a player uses FTB Team Islands’ /ftbteamislands create command. The pack’s config/starterkit/kits/inactive/ folder retains several unused alternate kits — a Witch kit (splash potions of swiftness/healing/poison/harming), a Lumberjack kit (efficiency-enchanted iron axe plus saplings), an Archer kit, and an older/simpler default kit — suggesting the pack maintainers experimented with class-style starting loadouts before settling on the single minimal quest-book-first kit that’s live today.
Related

FTB Quests
Getting Started

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It gives every player configurable starting gear the first time they join, instead of dropping them in with an empty inventory.
What’s in this server’s kit? A stone sword, 12 bread, a shield in the off-hand slot, and an ftbquests:book (the quest book).
Why include the quest book? So the very first item a new player effectively has is the quest book meant to guide the rest of their playthrough, not combat or building gear.
Are items I already have wiped when the kit applies? No — addExistingItemsAfterKitSet = true preserves anything already in the inventory.
Are there other kits? Several unused alternates (Witch, Lumberjack, Archer, and an older default) are retained in an inactive folder, but only the minimal quest-book-first kit is live.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Trading-Po.title: Trading Post
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Trading-Po.content:
Trading Post
Trading Post (tradingpost, v8.0.2, by Fuzs) turns villager trading from one-villager-at-a-time into a single consolidated screen: interact with one villager and it pulls in every trade from every eligible villager nearby, letting you “rule the village” and trade with the whole population at once instead of walking between individual trade GUIs.
This server’s tradingpost-server.toml sets a search radius of horizontal_range = 24 blocks and vertical_range = 16 blocks around the interacted villager, but enforce_range = false — so the configured range isn’t actually being enforced server-side, effectively pulling in trades pack-wide rather than strictly locally (worth knowing if trade results ever seem to include villagers “too far away” to make sense of). teleport_xp = true means XP dropped by trades teleports to the player rather than needing to be manually collected, and close_empty_screen = true auto-closes the consolidated screen once a villager’s trades run out.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It consolidates villager trading — interact with one villager and it pulls in every trade from every eligible villager nearby, so you trade with the whole population at once.
What’s the search range? 24 blocks horizontally and 16 vertically around the interacted villager.
Why might trades from “too far” villagers show up? Because enforce_range = false — the configured range isn’t actually enforced server-side, effectively pulling trades pack-wide.
Do I have to collect trade XP manually? No — teleport_xp = true, so trade XP teleports to the player.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/TreeChop.title: TreeChop
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/TreeChop.content:
TreeChop
HT’s TreeChop (hammertater, treechop, v0.19.0) turns axe-based logging into a real “chopping” mechanic: hit a tree enough times and the whole trunk fells and drops as loot instantly, rather than block-by-block breaking. config/treechop-common.toml uses the logarithmic chop-counting algorithm (a = 10.0) rather than linear, so bigger trees need proportionally fewer chops-per-block than small ones would suggest — a deliberate anti-grind curve. Felling also takes out the connected leaves: up to maxLeavesBlocks = 1024 leaf blocks within maxBreakLeavesDistance = 7 of any log get destroyed along with a tree of up to maxTreeBlocks = 320 logs, and non-decaying (“persistent,” player-placed) leaves are ignored so player builds using leaf blocks aren’t accidentally chopped away.
Player-facing behavior is tunable per-session in config/treechop-client.toml: sneaking defaults to INVERT_CHOPPING (holding shift temporarily disables chopping so you can break single logs normally), felling is on by default, and chopping in creative mode is off by default (though sneaking can still force it). A handful of items are explicitly blacklisted from triggering chops even though they can break logs — Botania’s Terra Axe, Mekanism’s Atomic Disassembler, and several practicaltools greataxes — likely to avoid conflicts between TreeChop’s felling logic and those mods’ own multi-block-break mechanics. It integrates with Jade/WTHIT for tooltip info and pairs naturally with Leaves Be Gone, which speeds up the decay of whatever leaves TreeChop doesn’t clear outright.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods
Leaves Be Gone

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It turns axe-based logging into a “chopping” mechanic — hit a tree enough times and the whole trunk fells and drops as loot at once, instead of block-by-block breaking.
Do bigger trees take proportionally more chops? No — it uses a logarithmic curve, so bigger trees need proportionally fewer chops-per-block, a deliberate anti-grind design.
Does felling clear leaves too? Yes — up to 1024 leaf blocks within 7 of any log are destroyed with the tree, but persistent player-placed leaves are ignored so builds aren’t chopped away.
How do I break a single log without felling? Sneak — holding shift defaults to INVERT_CHOPPING, temporarily disabling chopping so you can break single logs normally.
Does it work in creative mode? Not by default — chopping in creative is off, though sneaking can still force it.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Veinmining.title: Veinmining
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Veinmining.content:
Veinmining
Vein Mining (Illusive Soulworks, veinmining, v1.5.0) adds a genuine enchantment — not a keybind hack — that, once applied to an axe, pickaxe, shovel, or hoe, mines an entire connected vein of matching blocks in one hit. It’s RARE rarity, single-level, obtainable at enchanting tables, from villager trades, and as loot (config/veinmining-common.toml).
The real substance is in config/veinmining-server.toml. Without the enchantment at all, maxBlocksBase = 0 blocks vein-mine (i.e. nothing happens); each enchantment level adds maxBlocksPerLevel = 50, so on this single-level-max setup, one enchanted tool can chain up to 50 blocks per swing. Vein mining works diagonally (diagonalMining = true) and is capped by which blocks qualify: blocks = "CONFIG_LIST" restricts it to #c:ores, #forge:ores, and #minecraft:logs rather than every block type, and a groupsList of roughly 60 modded ore tags (adamantite, aetherium, mythril, orichalcum, unobtainium, and dozens more from the pack’s mod roster) ensures each ore type only chains with its own kind, not with unrelated ores that happen to be adjacent. Durability is respected realistically: limitedByDurability = true stops the chain once the tool would break, preventToolDestruction = true guarantees the tool itself survives (it just stops working once it hits 1 durability), and addToolDamage/addExhaustion both apply normal per-block wear and hunger cost for every block mined, so vein mining isn’t a free lunch — it’s the same total cost as mining each block manually, just faster and safer for chained collapses.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods

Anticipated questions

What does this mod add? A genuine enchantment (not a keybind hack) that, applied to an axe, pickaxe, shovel, or hoe, mines an entire connected vein of matching blocks in one hit.
How do I get the enchantment? It’s a RARE, single-level enchantment, obtainable at enchanting tables, from villager trades, and as loot.
How many blocks can one swing chain? Up to 50 — each level adds 50, and this setup is single-level-max.
What blocks can it vein-mine? Only ores and logs (#c:ores, #forge:ores, #minecraft:logs), and each modded ore type only chains with its own kind, not with unrelated adjacent ores.
Is vein mining a free lunch? No — it applies normal per-block durability wear and hunger cost for every block, so it’s the same total cost as mining each block manually, just faster; the tool also won’t destroy itself (it stops at 1 durability).

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Villager-N.title: Villager Names
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Villager-N.content:
Villager Names
Villager Names (Rick South / Serilum, villagernames, v8.2) gives every villager and villager-like entity (wandering traders, zombie villagers, etc.) a randomly assigned personal name instead of the plain “Villager” label, using separate male and female name pools. config/villagernames.json5 has this pack running with _useCustomNames: true alongside the built-in _useMaleNames/_useFemaleNames lists, meaning names are drawn from both the mod’s defaults and a custom list editable in mods/villagernames/customnames.txt; nameModdedVillagers: true extends naming to villager-like entities added by other mods in the pack, not just vanilla ones. Shares its author, dependency stack (Serilum’s Collective library), and overall structure with Fish On The Line.
Related

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It gives every villager and villager-like entity (wandering traders, zombie villagers) a randomly assigned personal name from separate male and female name pools, instead of the plain “Villager” label.
Can I add my own names? Yes — with _useCustomNames: true, names are drawn from both the mod’s defaults and a custom list editable in mods/villagernames/customnames.txt.
Does it name modded villagers too? Yes — nameModdedVillagers: true extends naming to villager-like entities added by other mods, not just vanilla ones.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/What-Are-T.title: What Are They Up To
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/What-Are-T.content:
What Are They Up To
What Are They Up To (Corosus, watut, v1.20.1-1.2.3) is a social-presence mod that lets you see, at a glance, what nearby players are doing: it shows a live “is typing” indicator when someone’s composing a chat message, an idle icon after a few minutes of inactivity, and — the deeper feature — a small floating visual of the actual GUI (chest, crafting table, etc.) a nearby player has open, mirroring their mouse movement and clicks in near-real time. config/watut-server.toml sets distanceRequiredToShowGUIInfo: 10 blocks and a GUI-update send rate of dynamicGuiTickSendRateOfGUIUpdates = 10 (twice a second), while config/watut-common.toml marks a player idle after ticksToMarkPlayerIdle: 6000 ticks (5 minutes). Privacy toggles exist client-side for players who don’t want their screen or item transfers broadcast (dontSendDetailedGUIInfo, dontSendItemInfo), and server-side settings can hard-override any client that tries to force these features back on. It bundles Forge Config API Port for its config screens and depends on Darkhax’s CoroUtil library.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It’s a social-presence mod that shows what nearby players are doing — an “is typing” indicator, an idle icon, and a small floating view of the actual GUI a nearby player has open, mirroring their mouse and clicks in near-real time.
How close do I have to be to see someone’s GUI? Within 10 blocks (distanceRequiredToShowGUIInfo: 10).
When does a player show as idle? After 6000 ticks (5 minutes) of inactivity.
Can I keep my screen private? Yes — client-side privacy toggles exist (dontSendDetailedGUIInfo, dontSendItemInfo), though server-side settings can hard-override a client that tries to force these features back on.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Xaero's-Mi.title: Xaero's Minimap
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Xaero's-Mi.content:
Xaero’s Minimap
Xaero’s Minimap (xaerominimap, v25.3.10, by xaero96) is the corner minimap — described in its own metadata as “the most vanilla-looking minimap for Minecraft.” It shows nearby terrain, entities (as a radar), waypoints, and the player’s facing/coordinates in a small always-on circular/square overlay, and is the de facto standard navigation mod across the Fabric/Forge modding scene.
This install’s xaerominimap.txt has death points enabled (deathpoints:true, oldDeathpoints:true — a waypoint is automatically dropped where the player last died, useful alongside the grave system from You’re in Grave Danger), cave maps on (caveMaps:2), redstone display on, north-lock enabled (lockNorth:true, map orientation fixed rather than rotating with the player), and radarHideInvisibleEntities:true. It depends on xaerolib (Xaero’s shared library, bundled with both this and World Map) and is built to work directly alongside Open Parties and Claims, which explicitly recommends Xaero’s Minimap/World Map to fully visualize claimed chunks.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods

Open Parties and Claims

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It’s the corner minimap — showing nearby terrain, entities as a radar, waypoints, and the player’s facing/coordinates in a small always-on overlay.
Does it mark where I died? Yes — death points are enabled, so a waypoint is automatically dropped where you last died (useful alongside the grave system from You’re in Grave Danger).
Does the map rotate as I turn? No — north-lock is enabled, so the map orientation stays fixed rather than rotating with the player.
Does it show caves? Yes — cave maps are on.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Xaero's-Wo.title: Xaero's World Map
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/Xaero's-Wo.content:
Xaero’s World Map
Xaero’s World Map (xaeroworldmap, v1.40.11, by xaero96) is the full-screen companion to Xaero’s Minimap (default key M) — a “self-writing” map that fills in as the player explores, showing the whole known world at once rather than just the immediate surroundings. It shares waypoints, death points, and settings with the minimap and requires the same xaerolib base.
This install’s xaeroworldmap.txt has terrain rendering on with slope shading (terrainSlopes:2, terrainDepth:true), footstep and flower detail layers enabled, hovered-biome name display on, and cave map support allowed. Like the minimap, it’s called out by name in Open Parties and Claims’s own mod description as the recommended way to visualize chunk claims and party member locations on the full map rather than just the minimap circle.

Xaero’s Minimap
Open Parties and Claims

What does this mod do? It’s the full-screen companion to Xaero’s Minimap (default key M) — a “self-writing” map that fills in as you explore, showing the whole known world at once rather than just the immediate surroundings.
Does it share data with the minimap? Yes — it shares waypoints, death points, and settings, and requires the same xaerolib base.
What does it help with in this pack? It’s the recommended way (per Open Parties and Claims) to visualize chunk claims and party member locations on the full map rather than just the minimap circle.

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/You're-in-.title: You're in Grave Danger
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/You're-in-.content:
You’re in Grave Danger
You’re in Grave Danger (yigd, v2.0.16, by b1n_ry) replaces vanilla’s scatter-your-items-on-death behavior with a grave: die, and your inventory and XP are collected into a single recoverable grave at (or near) your death location instead of despawning loose items across the ground, with a chat message telling you where it is.
This server’s yigd.json is tuned generously in the player’s favor: item loss on death is fully disabled (itemLoss.enabled = false — nothing is destroyed, the whole inventory goes into the grave), the grave stores both items and XP (storeItems/storeXp = true), XP recovery uses dropBehaviour = "BEST_OF_BOTH" with dropPercentage = 60 / keepPercentage = 15 (some XP stays on death, the rest is recoverable from the grave), and looting is simple — retrieveMethods.onClick = true only (right-click/left-click the grave, no sneak or stand-on requirement), merging retrieved stacks automatically and placing them straight IN_INVENTORY. Grave robbing is enabled (other players can loot your grave), but only after a 1-hour grace period (graveRobbing.afterTime = 1, timeUnit = "HOURS") unless the killer is exempt, and the original owner is notified when it happens (notifyWhenRobbed/tellWhoRobbed = true). Graves respect per-dimension floor limits (minimumGraveYLevel: -60 in the Overworld, 3 in the Nether) and will generate in the void if death happens below the world (generateGraveInVoid = true), while overrideSpawnProtection = true ensures a grave can still form even in spawn-protected areas.
Related

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods
Xaero’s Minimap

Anticipated questions

What does this mod do? It replaces vanilla’s item-scatter-on-death with a grave — your inventory and XP are collected into a single recoverable grave at your death location, with a chat message telling you where it is.
Do I lose items when I die? No — item loss on death is fully disabled, so nothing is destroyed; the whole inventory goes into the grave.
How do I loot my grave? Just click it (right/left-click) — no sneaking or standing-on requirement — and retrieved stacks merge straight back into your inventory.
Can other players rob my grave? Yes, but only after a 1-hour grace period (unless the killer is exempt), and you’re notified when it happens, including who did it.
What if I die in the void? A grave still generates in the void, and graves respect per-dimension floor limits (-60 in the Overworld, 3 in the Nether).

Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/emi-letsdo.title: emi-letsdo-compat
Mods/Quality-of-Life--and--UI/emi-letsdo.content:
emi-letsdo-compat
emi-letsdo-compat (v1.8.1, mod id emi_letsdo_compat) is the EMI recipe-viewer bridge for the “Let’s Do” mod family installed in this pack: Let’s Do Vinery (wine-making), Let’s Do Brewery, and Let’s Do Herbalbrews, all built on the shared letsdo-API. Without this addon, EMI would have no idea how to render the custom station recipes those mods add (wine presses, fermentation barrels, herbal brewing stations) — this plugin teaches EMI those recipe types so they show up as normal searchable/hoverable entries instead of being invisible to the recipe viewer.
It ships no meaningful config (the mod’s own fabric.mod.json doesn’t even set a description string) — it’s a pure glue/compat layer, doing its job entirely in code.
