Mods/Storage--and--Inventory-Mods.title: Storage & Inventory Mods
Mods/Storage--and--Inventory-Mods.content:
Storage & Inventory Mods
For real auto-sorted digital storage, the pack’s actual answer is Applied Energistics 2 — see Tech & Automation Mods. There is no dedicated “auto-categorize into separate physical chests” mod installed (no Sophisticated Storage equivalent); AE2’s Storage Bus + item filters is the closest thing, or a classic vanilla hopper/comparator sorter.
Iron Chests: Restocked
A tiered line of chests bigger than vanilla’s double chest.
Traveler’s Backpack
Wearable, upgradeable backpacks with real customization. Higher tiers unlock more main storage slots plus a dedicated multi-slot weapon/tool rack for quick-swapping gear, and accept Upgrades (e.g. Crafting Upgrade, Void Upgrade with item filters) installed into their own upgrade slots. Genuinely one of the best early storage upgrades available.
Nether Chested
A chest built from Nether materials holding 8x the usual capacity.
Lootr
Makes chest loot personal — every player who opens a loot chest gets their own copy of the contents, so nobody misses out because a friend looted it first.
Carry On
Pick up and carry single-block tile entities (chests, furnaces, etc.) in your empty hands instead of breaking and replacing them.
Inventory Sorter / Visual Workbench
Inventory Sorter adds one-click sorting within a single inventory (not across multiple chests). Visual Workbench keeps items visible inside crafting tables as you work.

Mods/Storage--and--Inventory/Carry-On.title: Carry On
Mods/Storage--and--Inventory/Carry-On.content:
Carry On
Carry On (Tschipp/Purplicious_Cow/cy4n, mod id carryon, v2.1.2.7) lets a player pick up a single-block tile entity — chest, furnace, hopper, spawner-adjacent decor, etc. — with an empty hand and carry it around fully intact (contents, orientation-relevant state, and all) instead of breaking it, losing dropped items to physics, and re-placing it from scratch. This is a genuine workflow change on a multiplayer base: rearranging a shared storage room, moving a loaded chest of loot to a different wall, or relocating a furnace bank next to a newly-built smeltery no longer means emptying it into your inventory first — you just hold it and walk. The server’s config/carryon-common.json sets a 2.5-block max pickup distance, and carrying anything applies a slowness penalty (blockSlownessMultiplier/entitySlownessMultiplier both 1.0, heavyTiles/heavyEntities both true, so bulkier tile entities slow you down more) — active even in creative mode. Small entities can be picked up too, within a 1.5-wide × 2.5-tall survival limit, and even stacked on top of one another when carrying multiple (stackableEntities: true), though hostile mobs, villagers, and a long list of vehicle/large-entity mods are blocked.
The blacklist is heavily tuned for this modpack’s other systems: create:* is entirely off-limits (Create’s kinetic multiblocks can’t be safely relocated by hand), as is lootr:* (see Lootr — per-player loot containers can’t be picked up), waystones:*, refinedstorage:*, ftbquests:*, botania:*, astralsorcery:*, and dozens of other mod-specific tile entities whose state wouldn’t survive a pickup/replace cycle cleanly. A handful of block-state properties are deliberately not preserved on re-placement and instead recalculated fresh — chest orientation (type), sign/creeper-head rotation, vine/glow-lichen face data, and trapdoor half — so a carried block reorients itself sensibly rather than freezing its old facing. Players themselves cannot be picked up (pickupPlayers: false), and hitting a player while carrying something does not make them drop it (dropCarriedWhenHit: false).
How you’ll use it here
Treat Carry On as a base-rearranging tool, not a storage tier of its own: with an empty hand you pick up a single loaded chest, furnace, or hopper and walk it to a new wall, contents intact, instead of emptying it first. It pairs naturally with your Iron Chests: Restocked tiers when you’re relocating a storage room, but note the 2.5-block reach and the carrying slowness (heavier tile entities slow you more). It does nothing to sort or scale items — for auto-sorted digital storage the pack’s real end-game answer is Applied Energistics 2 (see Storage & Applied Energistics — Getting Started). Remember that create:* and lootr:* blocks are blacklisted, so Create multiblocks and per-player loot chests stay where they are.
Anticipated questions
Can I carry a full chest without emptying it first? Yes — that’s the whole point. Pick up a single-block tile entity like a chest or furnace with an empty hand and it moves fully intact (contents and all), so rearranging a shared storage room no longer means dumping everything into your inventory.
Why won’t it pick up my Create machine or a dungeon loot chest? Those are deliberately blacklisted. create:* kinetic multiblocks can’t be safely relocated by hand, and lootr:* containers (see Lootr) hold per-player data, so both are barred from pickup here.
Does carrying something slow me down? Yes, generally — carrying applies a slowness penalty that’s active even in creative mode, and bulkier “heavy” tile entities slow you more than light ones.

Mods/Storage--and--Inventory/Inventory-S.title: Inventory Sorter
Mods/Storage--and--Inventory/Inventory-S.content:
Inventory Sorter
Inventory Sorter (kyrptonaught, mod id inventorysorter, v1.9.0-1.20) is a lightweight quality-of-life mod: it adds a clickable Sort button (plus middle-click and double-click shortcuts) to any open inventory screen, instantly reordering that single inventory’s contents. This server’s config/inventorysorter/config.json5 has it configured to sort by Name (rather than Category or Mod ID), with separate sort buttons shown for both the opened container and the player’s own inventory (seperateBtn: true), though sorting the container does not also sort the player’s inventory (sortPlayer: false). The default keybinding is P. It’s explicitly a single-inventory tool, not a cross-chest auto-organizer — it won’t distribute items between multiple chests in a room the way a Sophisticated Storage-style system would; the pack’s actual answer for that kind of automated, filtered item routing is Applied Energistics 2 (see Tech & Automation Mods).
config/inventorysorter/blacklist.json5 deliberately disables the sort button entirely for a specific set of screens where sorting would break the UI’s meaning: every AE2 terminal and interface (ae2:item_terminal, ae2:drive, ae2:craftingterm, ae2:patternterm, ae2:advanced_inscriber, ae2:crystal_growth), the Spell Engine binding screen, and — notably — all three Traveler’s Backpack screens (backpack_settings, backpack_block, backpack_item), whose non-grid, tiered slot layouts (main storage + tool slots + upgrade slots) aren’t safe to blind-sort. No lang entries define blocks or items since the mod adds none; everything is a client-side interaction layer on top of existing screens.
How you’ll use it here
Reach for the Sort button (or press P) any time a chest or your own inventory gets messy — it reorders that one container by item name in a click, and separate buttons let you tidy the open container and your inventory independently. Think of it as cleanup for the Iron Chests: Restocked chests and vanilla containers you already have, not as an organizer that routes items between them. There is no auto-categorize-into-separate-chests mod on this server, so if you want items automatically filed and searchable, the pack’s real answer is Applied Energistics 2 (see Storage & Applied Energistics — Getting Started); a vanilla hopper/comparator sorter is the low-tech alternative. Don’t expect the button on AE2 terminals or Traveler’s Backpack screens — it’s deliberately disabled there.
Anticipated questions
Will this sort all my chests in a room at once? No. It’s a single-inventory tool — one click sorts the one container you have open, not the whole room. For automated, filtered routing across many containers you want Applied Energistics 2 (see Storage & Applied Energistics — Getting Started).
How does it decide the order, and can I change it? On this server it’s configured to sort by Name. That’s a server-side config choice rather than a per-player toggle, so everyone gets the same name-based ordering.
Why is there no sort button on my backpack or ME terminal? Those screens are blacklisted on purpose. AE2 terminals/interfaces and all three Traveler’s Backpack screens use non-grid, tiered slot layouts that aren’t safe to blind-sort, so the button is hidden there.

Mods/Storage--and--Inventory/Iron-Chests.title: Iron Chests: Restocked
Mods/Storage--and--Inventory/Iron-Chests.content:
Iron Chests: Restocked
Iron Chests: Restocked (ThatGravyBoat/Kekie, mod id ironchests, v5.0.2) is the modern Fabric revival of the classic Iron Chests line — a tier ladder of upgradeable chests and matching barrels, all bigger than a vanilla single chest (27 slots). The server’s actual config/ironchests/chests/*.json tier files give the real numbers rather than rough guesses: Copper is 9×4 = 36 slots (1.3x vanilla), Iron is 9×6 = 54 slots (2x, matching a vanilla double chest), Gold is 11×6 = 66 slots, Diamond and Obsidian are both 12×6 = 72 slots (2.67x), Crystal is also 12×6 = 72 slots but transparent (renders its contents through the block), and Netherite — the top tier — is 13×7 = 91 slots (3.4x vanilla). There’s also a purely cosmetic Dirt Chest (1×1, a joke/troll tier). Obsidian and Netherite chests share the same absurd 1200.0 explosion resistance, making them the only tiers safe to place somewhere that might catch a creeper or TNT blast; Netherite is additionally fire-resistant.
Each tier has a matching barrel variant (same slot counts, no direction-facing GUI quirks) and an upgrade item (e.g. iron_chest_upgrade, diamond_chest_upgrade) that converts a lower chest in place to the next tier without losing contents — recipes are simple, centered around the tier’s associated ingot/gem plus the chest itself. The mod also ships Keys, a Key Ring, and Locks for player-locking a chest to specific keys, plus Dollies (Iron and Diamond) for moving a fully-loaded chest — including its contents — without breaking it, which is a lighter-weight overlap with Carry On’s general tile-entity carrying. No Patchouli guidebook ships with the mod; tiers and recipes are best discovered via JEI/REI.
How you’ll use it here
This is your everyday bulk storage backbone: craft a vanilla chest, then use the upgrade items to climb the ladder in place without unloading — Copper (36), Iron (54, a double chest in one block), Gold (66), Diamond/Obsidian (72), Crystal (72, see-through), up to Netherite at 91 slots. Early game, upgrade a chest or two to Iron or Gold and call it done; save Obsidian or Netherite for anything sitting where a creeper or TNT could reach, since only those two carry the 1200 explosion resistance. It’s more slots per block, not smarter storage — for auto-sorted, searchable digital storage the pack’s real end-game answer is Applied Energistics 2 (see Storage & Applied Energistics — Getting Started), and Nether Chested is the way to pack more quantity per slot rather than more slots. Use the Dollies or Carry On when you need to relocate a loaded chest.
Anticipated questions
Which chest holds the most? On this server the Netherite tier is the top — 91 slots (13×7, 3.4x a vanilla chest) — and it’s additionally fire-resistant on top of its blast resistance.
Which tier is safe next to explosions? Obsidian and Netherite both share the 1200.0 explosion resistance, so they’re the only two tiers safe to place somewhere a creeper or TNT blast might reach. The others will break like normal.
Do I lose my items when I upgrade a chest? No. The upgrade items (e.g. iron_chest_upgrade, diamond_chest_upgrade) convert a lower chest to the next tier in place, contents preserved.
How do I move a full chest? Use an Iron or Diamond Dolly to pick up a fully-loaded chest without breaking it, or Carry On for general tile-entity carrying.

Mods/Storage--and--Inventory/Lootr.title: Lootr
Mods/Storage--and--Inventory/Lootr.content:
Lootr
Lootr (Noobanidus/ZestyBlaze/embeddedt, mod id lootr, v0.7.35.86) rewrites how loot containers work in a way that matters a lot on a shared 10-player server: the first time any player opens a vanilla loot chest, barrel, minecart-with-chest, or loot shulker, the mod converts it into an instanced Lootr container that then generates and remembers a separate, independent set of contents for every player who opens it. In practice this means a dungeon, stronghold, or nether fortress chest a friend already cleaned out is not empty for the next person to find it — they get their own freshly-rolled loot from the same table, so exploration never turns into a race to loot rooms before someone else does. The block itself visually stays a normal chest/barrel/shulker (with vanilla or classic texture toggles available) and can hold a Centennial Trophy advancement track for opening 1/10/25/50/100 instanced containers.
Because each container secretly holds per-player data, Lootr chests cannot be broken normally — this server’s config/lootr.json has breaking.enable_break = false, so the only way to destroy one is sneaking while breaking in creative mode (the in-game warning is explicit: breaking deletes your unique loot and everyone else’s). The config also defines optional decay (a container crumbles to nothing after 6000 ticks/5 min if configured) and refresh (contents reroll after 24000 ticks/20 min) timers per loot table/dimension/mod-id, but both decay_all and refresh_all are left false here, so containers persist indefinitely by default rather than expiring. Notification delay is 600 ticks (30s) between loot-related chat messages. Two Prominence-specific compatibility datapacks ship in config/paxi/datapacks/ — Lootr-BetterNether-Compatibility and Lootr-BetterEnd-Compatibility — extending per-player instancing to those dimension mods’ native structures. Carry On deliberately blacklists lootr:* blocks from being picked up, so a Lootr container has to stay where it spawns.
How you’ll use it here
You don’t build with Lootr — it just changes how loot containers behave out in the world. On this 10-player server it means dungeon, stronghold, and fortress chests give you your own freshly-rolled loot even if a friend already opened them, so exploration never becomes a race. Just don’t try to break a Lootr chest to take it home: breaking is disabled here (only a creative sneak-break works, and it warns you it deletes everyone’s loot), and Carry On blacklists them too, so the container stays put. Whatever you haul out goes into your own base storage — early on a chest or backpack, and eventually an Applied Energistics 2 network for auto-sorted digital storage (see Storage & Applied Energistics — Getting Started). Chase the Centennial Trophy track (1/10/25/50/100 containers) as you explore.
Anticipated questions
A friend already looted this chest — is it empty for me? No. The first open instances the container and every player then gets their own separate, independently-rolled contents from the same loot table, so you still get a full pull.
Why can’t I break this loot chest? Breaking is disabled on this server (enable_break = false). The only way to destroy one is sneaking while breaking in creative mode, and the game warns you that doing so deletes your unique loot and everyone else’s. Carry On also can’t pick it up.
Will these chests disappear or refill over time? Generally not here. Lootr supports optional decay and refresh timers, but both decay_all and refresh_all are left off on this server, so containers persist indefinitely rather than expiring or rerolling.

Mods/Storage--and--Inventory/Nether-Ches.title: Nether Chested
Mods/Storage--and--Inventory/Nether-Ches.content:
Nether Chested
Nether Chested (Fuzs, mod id netherchested, v8.0.4) is a small, focused mod with one block: the Nether Chest, crafted from a vanilla chest ringed with nether bricks and 4 netherite scrap (pattern: netherite scrap in the corners, nether bricks on the edges, the chest in the center). Rather than adding more slots like Iron Chests: Restocked, it works the opposite way — it multiplies the max stack size of every item placed inside it. The server’s config/netherchested-server.toml has this set to stack_size_multiplier = 8, so a 64-stack item like cobblestone stacks to 512 per slot, letting a single 27-slot Nether Chest hold roughly as much raw material as 8 vanilla double chests without the mod needing to touch inventory size or GUI at all.
Two other config values are worth knowing: no_block_above = true means a Nether Chest won’t open if something is placed directly on top of it (same rule as vanilla chests), and explode_in_nether = false — the mod supports an optional “explodes if opened while in the Nether dimension” hazard mode (with a configurable nether_explosion_strength, currently 5), but that risk is turned off on this server, so it behaves as a plain (if very high-capacity) storage block everywhere, Nether included. Already damaged/partially-used items don’t get their stack cap increased, per the mod’s own description. No Patchouli guidebook ships with it.
How you’ll use it here
Reach for a Nether Chest once you have a serious surplus of one bulk material — cobblestone, dirt, netherrack, ores. Where Iron Chests: Restocked gives you more slots, this gives you 8x the stack size per slot (a 64-stack becomes 512), so a single 27-slot Nether Chest holds roughly what 8 vanilla double chests would. It’s mid-game gated: the recipe wants 4 netherite scrap, so it’s not an early build. It’s still a dumb bucket, not sorted storage — you’ll still dig through it by hand. For auto-sorted, searchable digital storage the pack’s real end-game answer is Applied Energistics 2 (see Storage & Applied Energistics — Getting Started); a Nether Chest is best as a high-density holding tank feeding into that.
Anticipated questions
How much more does it actually hold? With stack_size_multiplier = 8 on this server, every item stacks 8x higher — a normal 64-stack goes to 512 per slot — so one 27-slot chest stores about as much raw material as 8 vanilla double chests, without any bigger GUI.
Will it explode in the Nether? No. The mod has an optional “explodes if opened in the Nether” hazard mode, but explode_in_nether = false here, so it behaves as a plain high-capacity storage block everywhere, the Nether included.
Does it boost the stack of anything, like damaged tools? Generally no — already damaged or partially-used items don’t get their stack cap raised. It’s for stackable bulk items, and note it also won’t open with a block placed directly on top.

Mods/Storage--and--Inventory/Traveler's-.title: Traveler's Backpack
Mods/Storage--and--Inventory/Traveler's-.content:
Traveler’s Backpack
Traveler’s Backpack (Tiviacz1337, mod id travelersbackpack, v9.1.50) is a wearable, upgradeable backpack line, and the server’s config/travelersbackpack.json5 gives exact, tuned numbers per tier rather than rough estimates. Five material tiers exist: Leather (27 inventory slots, 2 upgrade slots, 2 tool slots), Iron (45 / 3 / 3), Gold (63 / 4 / 4), Diamond (81 / 5 / 5), and Netherite (99 / 6 / 6) — each step up adds 18 more storage slots and one more upgrade/tool slot. The dedicated tool slots are a separate row from main storage specifically for weapons/tools, with quick-swapping enabled (allowToolSwapping: true) so gear can be pulled straight from the backpack without opening the main grid. Every tier also carries an internal fluid tank sized at 81,000 mB (one bucket) per row of backpack storage.
Upgrades installed into the dedicated upgrade slots add real functionality on top of raw storage: a Crafting Upgrade (portable 3×3 grid), Tank Upgrade, Furnace/Smoker/Blast Furnace Upgrades (passive smelting while worn), a Jukebox Upgrade, and four filter-driven automation upgrades — Pickup (auto-collects matching items), Magnet (pulls matching items from 8 blocks away, tick rate 10), Feeding (auto-eats from a filtered food list, tick rate 100), Refill (keeps the hotbar topped up from backpack stacks, tick rate 5), and Void (deletes filtered junk items outright) — all with 16 filter slots in a 4-per-row grid. Backpacks are invulnerable to lava/fire and void-protected (voidProtection), and a dead player’s backpack drops in place at the death location with its coordinates messaged to them, so losing one to death is recoverable rather than a real loss. This pack has three deliberate blacklist entries beyond the mod’s defaults — prominent:molten_core, prominent:molten_remnant, and zenith:ender_lead — plus beehives/bee nests, all barred from being stored in a backpack. Zombies, skeletons, and endermen (overworld) and wither skeletons/piglins (nether) have a small (0.5%) chance to spawn already wearing a random backpack, and several themed backpacks (bat, dragon, magma cube, squid, quartz, etc.) grant passive status-effect abilities like night vision or fire resistance while worn. Inventory Sorter’s blacklist deliberately excludes the backpack’s own screens (travelersbackpack:backpack_settings, backpack_block, backpack_item) from auto-sort, since its slot layout isn’t a simple grid.
How you’ll use it here
Grab a backpack early — it’s the pack’s recommended first mobile-storage step, and you can search @traveler in REI/EMI to find the recipes. Even a Leather backpack (27 slots + 2 tool slots) turns a mining trip into a one-trip haul, and tool-swapping lets you pull gear without opening the main grid. Climb tiers as materials allow (Iron 45, Gold 63, Diamond 81, Netherite 99, each adding 18 slots and an extra upgrade/tool slot), and spend the upgrade slots on the automation that fits your playstyle — Pickup/Magnet for gathering, Refill to keep the hotbar stocked, a Crafting Upgrade for a portable 3×3. It’s personal carry storage, though: it doesn’t sort your base or route items between chests. That’s still Applied Energistics 2’s job for auto-sorted digital storage (see Storage & Applied Energistics — Getting Started), with a backpack as the thing you fill in the field and empty into the network.
Anticipated questions
Which backpack holds the most? Netherite is the top tier at 99 inventory slots, plus 6 upgrade slots and 6 tool slots — each material step up (Leather→Iron→Gold→Diamond→Netherite) adds 18 storage slots and one more upgrade/tool slot.
Do I lose it when I die? Generally not permanently — a dead player’s backpack drops in place at the death location and its coordinates are messaged to you, and backpacks are also lava/fire-proof and void-protected, so it’s recoverable rather than a real loss.
Why can’t I sort my backpack with the Sort button? Inventory Sorter deliberately excludes all three backpack screens from auto-sort, because the tiered layout (main storage + tool slots + upgrade slots) isn’t a simple grid that’s safe to blind-sort.
Is there anything I can’t store in it? Yes — this pack bars a few items: prominent:molten_core, prominent:molten_remnant, zenith:ender_lead, and beehives/bee nests are all blacklisted from backpack storage.

Mods/Storage--and--Inventory/Visual-Work.title: Visual Workbench
Mods/Storage--and--Inventory/Visual-Work.content:
Visual Workbench
Visual Workbench (Fuzs, mod id visualworkbench, v8.0.1) is a small, purely presentational mod: items placed in a crafting table’s 3×3 grid stay physically visible on top of the table model instead of disappearing into an abstract inventory the moment the GUI closes. It adds no items or blocks of its own (there’s no lang file — nothing to name), just a rendering layer over the vanilla crafting table.
Three toggles in config/visualworkbench-client.toml control the look on this server: rotate_ingredients = true turns the displayed items to always face whichever player is closest, flat_rendering = false means ingredients render standing/floating above the table surface rather than laid flat, and render_result = true also shows the would-be crafted output item sitting on the table alongside the ingredients. It’s a client-side visual mod with no gameplay or balance impact — a nice-to-have that makes a crafting table look “in use” from across a room, pairing well with base-building/decoration work.
How you’ll use it here
There’s nothing to reach for or craft — it’s a client-side visual layer that just makes any crafting table show its 3×3 contents on top of the block. Its value here is purely decorative: leave ingredients in a table to make a workshop look “in use,” which pairs well with base-building. It has no bearing on storage capacity or organization, so for actual storage progression look to Iron Chests: Restocked for bulk and Applied Energistics 2 for auto-sorted digital storage (see Storage & Applied Energistics — Getting Started).
Anticipated questions
Does this change how crafting or storage works? No. It adds no items or blocks and has no gameplay or balance impact — it’s purely a rendering layer over the vanilla crafting table.
Do other players see the items I leave in my table? Generally yes, since it renders the table’s contents on the block itself; on this server the display also rotates to face the nearest player and shows the would-be result item alongside the ingredients.

Mods/Tech--and--Automation-Mods.title: Tech & Automation Mods
Mods/Tech--and--Automation-Mods.content:
Tech & Automation Mods
Several parallel tech trees, each with its own Quest Book chapter. Pick one or two to specialize — see the mid-game stage for when to start.
Create
The showpiece automation mod (6.0.8.1). Everything runs on real, visible mechanical power — shafts, gears, water wheels, contraptions you build by hand and watch turn. Water wheels only spin under genuinely flowing water, not a still pool.
Applied Energistics 2
The endgame storage-and-autocrafting system: one digital ME network that holds, sorts, and auto-crafts from thousands of items instead of a wall of chests. Steep learning curve, enormous payoff — the real answer to “how do I auto-sort my storage.”
Tech Reborn
A complete, self-contained classic tech tree — tools, machines, ore processing — for progressing through “generate power, build bigger machines” instead of Create’s contraptions.
Modern Industrialization
Another full industrial tech tree, heavier on multiblock machines and chemistry-flavored processing chains.
Powah!
The pack’s accessible energy mod — generators, batteries, and cables that wire into whichever tech tree you’re actually playing.
Create addons and companions (grouped)
Create: New Age (bridges kinetic power into electricity), Create Crafts & Additions (Electric Motor/Alternator converting Forge energy ↔ kinetic power), Create: Estrogen (Create-flavored module for the Estrogen mod), Create: Steam ‘n’ Rails (rail/steam expansion), Create: Copycats+ (disguise blocks), Colorwheel (Iris shader + Flywheel compat).
Estrogen
The base mod behind Create: Estrogen — its own fluid handling mechanics and a dash ability.
Other tech trees & AE2 extras (grouped)
Industrial Revolution (another full industrial tech tree) + its EMI Plugin. Alloy Forgery (configurable alloy smelting pre-full-tech-tree). ExtendedAE, MEGA Cells, ME Requester, AE2WTLib (all extend AE2 — QoL content, huge storage cells, auto-restocking, wireless terminals). Applied Botanics (bridges Botania mana into an AE2 network). OnlyExcavators and Just Hammers (3x3-area mining tools). Polymorphic Energistics (AE2 recipes work with the Polymorph system, see Quality-of-Life & UI Mods).

Mods/Tech--and--Automation/AE2WTLib.title: AE2WTLib
Mods/Tech--and--Automation/AE2WTLib.content:
AE2WTLib
AE2WTLib (v15.2.1) is a shared library mod that adds Wireless Terminal support to Applied Energistics 2 with infinite-range capability, and functions partly as plumbing that other AE2 addons in this pack build on rather than a standalone feature mod. Its headline item is the Quantum Bridge Card, which lets a Wireless Terminal attune to a Quantum Bridge for unlimited range instead of AE2’s normal falloff-based wireless distance; a Magnet Card adds an auto-pickup upgrade to the Wireless Crafting Terminal with three modes (off, pickup-to-inventory, pickup-to-ME), toggleable via hotkey. A terminal-cycling hotkey lets players flip between multiple carried wireless terminals without opening an inventory menu.
Anticipated questions
Q: What does AE2WTLib do?
A: It adds Wireless Terminal support to Applied Energistics 2 with infinite-range capability, and serves as plumbing other AE2 addons in the pack build on. See Storage & Applied Energistics — Getting Started.
Q: How do I get unlimited wireless range?
A: The Quantum Bridge Card lets a Wireless Terminal attune to a Quantum Bridge for unlimited range instead of AE2’s normal distance falloff.
Q: Can I auto-pick-up items into my network wirelessly?
A: Yes — the Magnet Card adds an auto-pickup upgrade to the Wireless Crafting Terminal with three modes (off, pickup-to-inventory, pickup-to-ME), toggled via hotkey.
Q: Does it tie into AE2?
A: Entirely — it’s an AE2 addon; it also adds a hotkey to cycle between multiple carried wireless terminals without opening a menu.

Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Alloy-Forgery.title: Alloy Forgery
Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Alloy-Forgery.content:
Alloy Forgery
Alloy Forgery (v2.1.2) adds a configurable, data-driven alloy-smelting multiblock that predates needing a full tech tree: rather than a single dedicated machine block, players build a Forge out of common building materials (bricks, stone bricks, deepslate bricks, end stone bricks, polished blackstone, or prismarine bricks) around a matching Forge Controller. Each material choice acts as a distinct Forge “tier” — recipes can require a minimum controller tier, and the in-game tooltip warns players outright with “This recipe requires a Forge Controller of Tier %d” if they’ve under-built. Fuel capacity scales with the structure, and an “Invalid Multiblock Configuration” message flags builds that don’t match the required shape.
Because it’s purely data-driven, Alloy Forgery is mostly a vehicle other mods and modpacks use to add early-access alloy recipes (bronze, electrum, and similar) that don’t require unlocking an entire industrial mod first — a low-investment way to get basic alloys before committing to Tech Reborn, Modern Industrialization, or Industrial Revolution.
Anticipated questions
Q: What does Alloy Forgery do?
A: It adds a data-driven alloy-smelting multiblock — a Forge built from common materials around a matching Forge Controller — for smelting alloys.
Q: Where does it sit in progression?
A: Early — it’s a low-investment way to get basic alloys (bronze, electrum, and similar) before committing to Tech Reborn, Modern Industrialization, or Industrial Revolution.
Q: Why won’t my recipe work?
A: Recipes can require a minimum controller tier; the tooltip warns “This recipe requires a Forge Controller of Tier %d” if you’ve under-built, and “Invalid Multiblock Configuration” flags a wrong shape.
Q: Do different build materials matter?
A: Yes — each material (bricks, deepslate/end-stone bricks, blackstone, prismarine, etc.) acts as a distinct Forge tier, and fuel capacity scales with the structure.

Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Applied-Botan.title: Applied Botanics
Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Applied-Botan.content:
Applied Botanics
Applied Botanics (v1.5.2) — self-described in its own mod description as “mana through ae2, what could go wrong” — bridges Botania’s mana economy into an Applied Energistics 2 ME network. It adds an ME Mana Cell Housing that accepts dedicated Mana Storage Cells (1k through 256k capacity, plus a Creative variant), Portable Mana Cells for carrying charge outside the network, and a Fluix Mana Pool: an AE2-flavored version of Botania’s Mana Pool that can source and sink mana directly to and from the ME network instead of sitting in isolation.
Unusually, Applied Botanics doesn’t ship its own guidebook — it patches two new entries (covering the Fluix Mana Pool and Mana Drives) directly into Botania’s real in-game Lexica Botania, so the mod’s own mechanics are documented inside the book players already use for vanilla Botania content rather than a separate manual.
Anticipated questions
Q: What does Applied Botanics do?
A: It bridges Botania’s mana economy into an Applied Energistics 2 ME network (“mana through ae2”). See Storage & Applied Energistics — Getting Started.
Q: How do I store mana in my ME network?
A: Via an ME Mana Cell Housing that accepts Mana Storage Cells (1k–256k, plus a Creative variant), Portable Mana Cells for offline carry, and a Fluix Mana Pool that sources and sinks mana to and from the network.
Q: Where’s it documented in-game?
A: It has no separate guidebook — it patches two entries (Fluix Mana Pool and Mana Drives) directly into Botania’s real Lexica Botania.
Q: Does it tie into AE2?
A: Yes, directly — it’s an AE2 addon that extends the ME network to handle Botania mana.

Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Applied-Energ.title: Applied Energistics 2
Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Applied-Energ.content:
Applied Energistics 2
Applied Energistics 2 (v15.4.10) is the pack’s endgame digital storage-and-autocrafting system, built around the ME (Matter Energy) Network: a web of cables carrying both power and “channels” (bandwidth for connected devices) that links Drives full of Storage Cells, Terminals, and processing machines into one searchable, sortable inventory. Instead of a wall of labeled chests, players insert items once and pull any of them from any linked Terminal; a Crafting CPU can be taught multi-step recipes (“patterns”) and then auto-craft entire chains of intermediate materials on demand. Getting started leans on real-world AE2 progression — meteorite hunting for Certus Quartz and Charged Certus Quartz, then Inscribers pressing Silicon/Logic/Calculation/Engineering Processors — reflected directly in the pack’s Quest Book chapter (applied_energistics_2.snbt, 298 quests, icon ae2:controller), whose early quests are literally titled “Preparing to Find Meteorites 1/2”, “Your First Meteorite”, and “Inscriber Presses.” AE2 sits at position 4 of 7 in the Quest Book’s intended order, ahead of Create and Industrial Revolution — the pack expects players to have a functioning ME network before tackling the heavier tech trees.
AE2 ships its own in-game documentation system (a custom Guide book renderer, not the Patchouli framework other guidebook mods use) rather than a lexicon-style item. Under the hood, this server’s config reveals some deliberate tuning: Spatial IO (the pinning/duplication-prevention storage-teleport system) costs scale with spatialPowerExponent = 1.35, meaning larger spatial regions get disproportionately more expensive to store; and — notably — AE2 ships a built-in power-conversion ratio for Tech Reborn (PowerRatios.TechReborn = 2.0), meaning AE2’s own energy storage natively understands and converts Tech Reborn’s power values without needing a separate compat mod.
AE2 is also this pack’s most-extended mod: ExtendedAE, MEGA Cells, ME Requester, AE2WTLib, Applied Botanics, and Polymorphic Energistics all build directly on top of its network, cells, and crafting APIs rather than being standalone systems.
Anticipated questions
Q: What is AE2 for?
A: It’s the pack’s endgame digital storage-and-autocrafting system, built on the ME Network — insert items once and pull any of them from any linked Terminal, with a Crafting CPU auto-crafting multi-step recipes on demand. See Storage & Applied Energistics — Getting Started.
Q: How do I get started?
A: Real AE2 progression — meteorite hunting for Certus Quartz and Charged Certus Quartz, then Inscribers pressing Silicon/Logic/Calculation/Engineering Processors — mirrored in the Quest Book’s early quests (“Preparing to Find Meteorites”, “Your First Meteorite”, “Inscriber Presses”).
Q: Where does it sit in progression?
A: Position 4 of 7 in the Quest Book, ahead of Create and Industrial Revolution — the pack expects a functioning ME network before the heavier tech trees.
Q: Does it tie into the other tech mods?
A: Yes — it has a built-in power ratio for Tech Reborn (PowerRatios.TechReborn = 2.0), and it’s the pack’s most-extended mod: ExtendedAE, MEGA Cells, ME Requester, AE2WTLib, Applied Botanics, and Polymorphic Energistics all build on it.

Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Colorwheel.title: Colorwheel
Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Colorwheel.content:
Colorwheel
Colorwheel (v1.2.5) is a small compatibility shim that lets Iris Shaders render correctly alongside Flywheel, Create’s custom rendering engine for animated kinetic blocks and moving contraptions. Without it, shader packs and Create’s rotating machinery can visually conflict; Colorwheel patches the two systems together so both work at once. Its config is limited to compatibility bookkeeping — toggles for warning the player about incompatible or broken shader packs and an enableFallbackMode switch for degrading gracefully if a pack can’t be reconciled — all left at their defaults on this server.
There isn’t much more to it: it’s glue, not content, and it does its one job quietly in the background whenever a player runs both Iris and Create.

Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Create-Crafts.title: Create Crafts & Additions
Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Create-Crafts.content:
Create Crafts & Additions
Create Crafts & Additions (v1.3.4) is another electricity bridge for Create, focused on two core conversion blocks: the Electric Motor, which generates kinetic rotation from Forge Energy (5,000 FE capacity, up to 5,000 FE/t input, 256 RPM range), and the Alternator, which does the reverse at 75% generator efficiency (generator_efficiency = 0.75) up to 5,000 FE/t output. A Rolling Mill adds a dedicated FE-and-kinetic-stress processing step (100-tick duration, 16 SU stress cost), and a full Wires/Connectors system (Small and Large Connectors, with 16- and 32-block wire ranges respectively) lets FE-based devices network together without item-pipe-style block chains.
Two blocks stand out for their tooltips: the Accumulator (a 2,000,000 FE battery block) is explicitly flagged in its own in-game tooltip as “Deprecated and subject to removal from future releases,” in favor of the newer Modular Accumulator — worth knowing before building storage around it. The mod also adds a defensive Tesla Coil that charges from FE (40,000 FE capacity, 5,000 FE/t charge rate) and zaps nearby mobs and players for 3 and 2 damage respectively on a 20-tick cooldown, functioning as a powered mob-deterrent turret.
Anticipated questions
Q: What does it do?
A: It’s an electricity bridge for Create, centered on the Electric Motor (kinetic rotation from Forge Energy) and the Alternator (rotation back to FE at 75% efficiency).
Q: Where does it sit relative to Create?
A: It’s a Create addon — it connects Create’s kinetic network to FE devices via a Wires/Connectors system (16- and 32-block ranges) so FE devices network without item-pipe-style block chains.
Q: Should I build storage around the Accumulator?
A: Be careful — the Accumulator (2,000,000 FE) is flagged in-game as “Deprecated and subject to removal from future releases,” in favor of the newer Modular Accumulator.
Q: Is there anything for base defense?
A: Yes — the Tesla Coil charges from FE (40,000 FE, 5,000 FE/t) and zaps nearby mobs and players (3 and 2 damage) on a 20-tick cooldown.

Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Create.title: Create
Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Create.content:
Create
Create (v6.0.8.1) is the pack’s showpiece automation mod, built entirely around a real, physically-simulated kinetic power network instead of an abstract “energy” number. Shafts, cogwheels, gearboxes and belts carry rotation (measured in RPM) between machines, and every machine has a Stress rating it draws from the network’s total Stress capacity — go over capacity and the whole network slows to a crawl. On this server the defaults are untouched: max rotation speed is capped at 256 RPM, a Water Wheel supplies 32 Stress Units of capacity while a Windmill Bearing supplies 512 and a Steam Engine 1024, and blocks like the Mechanical Press or Crushing Wheels cost 8 SU to run. As documented server-side, water wheels genuinely only spin under flowing water — a still-water pair reads 0 RPM, a real waterfall column reads a working 8 RPM.
Beyond static machines, Create’s signature feature is Contraptions: pistons, bearings, and minecart assemblies that let players build and move whole structures — elevators, rotating clock towers, driving vehicles — up to a server-configured cap of 2048 blocks per contraption. Trains sit on top of this system, using assembled multi-car contraptions on custom track with their own physics (max 20 bogeys per train, 28 blocks/s top speed unpowered, 40 blocks/s for powered locomotives). The Schematicannon and Schematic system let players blueprint builds and have Create physically construct them block-by-block.
In this pack Create has its own Quest Book chapter (create.snbt, 467 quests, icon create:wrench) placed at position 5 of 7 in the book’s order — meaning it’s intended as a mid-pack tech track once players have some basics down, not the very first system to dive into. Several server-side recipe toggles are notable: bulk cutting/pressing (processing full stacks per swing) are deliberately left off to preserve intended difficulty, while cross-mod recipe bridges (Botania spout-filling, Tinkers’ Construct casting via Spout) are left on.
Anticipated questions
Q: What makes Create different from the other tech mods?
A: It’s built on a real, physically-simulated kinetic power network (RPM + Stress) instead of an abstract energy number — machines draw Stress from the network’s capacity, and exceeding capacity slows everything to a crawl.
Q: Where does it sit in progression?
A: Its Quest Book chapter (467 quests) sits at position 5 of 7 — a mid-pack tech track once players have some basics down, not the very first system to dive into.
Q: Why won’t my water wheel spin?
A: Water wheels only spin under flowing water — a still-water pair reads 0 RPM; a real waterfall column reads a working 8 RPM.
Q: What’s the signature feature?
A: Contraptions — pistons, bearings, and minecart assemblies that move whole structures (elevators, vehicles, trains) up to a 2048-block cap per contraption, plus the Schematicannon for block-by-block builds.

Create: Copycats+
Create: Copycats+ (v3.0.7) is a disguise-block mod purpose-built for Create’s kinetic contraptions: it adds “Copycat” versions of ordinary building shapes — blocks, boards, beams, corner slices, half-layers, half-panels, fences, fence gates, doors (including folding and sliding variants), pressure plates, and panes — that visually take on the texture of any block right-clicked onto them while keeping their own shape and behavior. Create: Estrogen
Create: Estrogen (v1.0.1) is a small integration module that connects the standalone Estrogen mod to Create’s kinetic system. Its centerpiece is the Centrifuge, a machine block with no internal inventory of its own — it has to be fed and drained by placing fluid containers directly around it, taking input from the bottom face and delivering output from the top. The Centrifuge also has a hard kinetic requirement: it only functions at Create’s maximum rotation speed of 256 RPM, meaning it needs the same top-tier gearing (large cogwheel ratios, a windmill, or a well-geared water wheel setup) that any other max-speed Create machine does.
Centrifuging recipes process Estrogen’s fluid items — turning things like Estrogen Pill Packages, Used Filters, and Incomplete Estrogen Patches/“Incomplete UwU” items into their finished forms. The mod also adds one decorative block, the Rosy Maple Seat, matching Estrogen’s moth-themed decoration set.

Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Create:-New-A.title: Create: New Age
Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Create:-New-A.content:
Create: New Age
Create: New Age (v1.1.7f) is an addon that bridges Create’s kinetic power (Stress Units / RPM) into a Forge Energy-based electricity system, letting a base’s rotational machinery power — and be powered by — FE-based mods like Powah!, Tech Reborn, or Modern Industrialization. Motors are the core conversion block, available in Basic, Advanced, and Reinforced tiers that turn stored electricity into rotation: a Basic Motor holds 16,000 FE and drives 512 SU of stress at 128 RPM, scaling up to a Reinforced Motor’s 128,000 FE capacity and 8,192 SU at 256 RPM. The server’s conversion rate between Create’s Stress Units and Forge Energy is set at suToEnergy = 0.029296875, and Energisers (basic/advanced/reinforced) plus Solar Heating Plates and Heat Pumps/Pipes handle the reverse and auxiliary power flows, all connected over a wire network (max wire length 16 blocks, using Copper/overcharged Iron/Golden/Diamond wire blocks).
Its standout system is a genuine nuclear reactor: Reactor Casing, Reactor Rod, Fuel Acceptor, Heat Vent, and Reactor Glass blocks assemble into a multiblock fueled by Thorium Ore, with real meltdown consequences — Corium (and a Solid Corium variant) exist specifically as the molten byproduct of a reactor failure, mirroring real-world reactor meltdown lore. Server-side reactor tuning (ReactorRodHeat = 30, ReactorRodHeatLoss = 25, and multipliers for overheating/passive heat loss/solar panel output) is left at its defaults, so reactor risk and reward play out as the mod author intended.
Anticipated questions
Q: What does Create: New Age do?
A: It bridges Create’s kinetic power (SU/RPM) into a Forge Energy electricity system, letting rotational machinery power — and be powered by — FE mods like Powah!, Tech Reborn, or Modern Industrialization.
Q: How do I convert electricity to rotation?
A: Motors in Basic/Advanced/Reinforced tiers — a Basic Motor holds 16,000 FE and drives 512 SU at 128 RPM, up to a Reinforced Motor’s 128,000 FE and 8,192 SU at 256 RPM; Energisers handle the reverse.
Q: What’s its standout system?
A: A genuine nuclear reactor multiblock fueled by Thorium Ore, with real meltdown consequences — Corium (and a Solid Corium variant) exists specifically as the molten byproduct of a reactor failure.
Q: Where does it sit in progression?
A: It’s a Create addon meant to electrify a kinetic base and interconnect it with the FE-based tech trees, rather than a standalone tech tree of its own.

Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Create:-Steam.content:
Create: Steam ‘n’ Rails
Create: Steam ‘n’ Rails (v1.7.2) is the official expansion to Create’s train and rail system, adding the Track Station (which lets a Deployer holding a Wrench automatically assemble or disassemble a train just by hitting the station — useful for fully automated depots when paired with a hopper feeding the deployer a wrench) and the Big Buffer for handling heavier rolling stock at the end of a line. Train Casings let players press the “Open Bogey Menu” key to pick from different wheel/bogey styles per car, changing how a locomotive looks and handles.
The bulk of the mod, however, is Locometal — an enormous decorative block palette (the mod’s lang file alone runs over 200 KB) covering boilers, smokeboxes, windows, doors, ladders, flywheels, pillars, trapdoors, vents, and hazard-stripe panels, each available in a full set of dyeable colors and material finishes (riveted, plated, slashed, wrapped in brass/copper/iron). In practice this turns Create’s steam trains from a functional system into a genuine model-railroading palette — building a locomotive’s exterior livery is closer to designing a vehicle skin than placing a handful of functional blocks.

Q: Is it mostly functional or decorative?
A: Mostly decorative — the bulk is Locometal, turning Create’s steam trains into a model-railroading palette closer to designing a vehicle skin than placing functional blocks.

A: It’s a Create addon building directly on Create’s existing train/rail system.

Estrogen
Estrogen (v5.0.8) is a standalone whimsical/joke-flavored mod that layers a full item and fluid processing chain onto a “Girl Power” theme, and serves as the base mod that Create: Estrogen hooks into. The fluid side is a small processing chain in its own right: Horse Urine is cauldron-processed into Filtrated Horse Urine, which combines with other inputs toward Liquid Estrogen and Gender Fluid — the same fluids Create: Estrogen’s Centrifuge is built to process.
The mod rounds out with a moth-themed decorative furniture set (Rosy Maple Wool, Bed, and Carpet, plus quilted variants), novelty blocks (Cookie Jar, Dreamcatcher, Dream Block, Bottle of Dreams, a “Block of :3”), and a small permanent-Dash minigame system that’s disabled on this server (minigameEnabled = false, permaDashAmount = 0) — the dash ability itself isn’t part of the enabled feature set here.

ExtendedAE
ExtendedAE (v1.0.2) is a substantial quality-of-life extension for Applied Energistics 2, shipping higher-capacity and more convenient versions of AE2’s core network devices: an Extended Pattern Provider, Extended Interface, Extended Drive, and Extended IO Port that push past AE2’s stock throughput limits, plus an Extended Molecular Assembler, Extended Inscriber, and Extended Charger for beefier crafting and item-charging setups. It also adds a Wireless Connector for linking ME subnetworks without physical cable runs, an Ingredient Buffer for staging crafting inputs, and a Crystal Fixer for automating AE2’s crystal-growth process.
With 147 lang keys, it’s one of the larger AE2 addons in the pack — closer to “AE2, but every device has a bigger sibling” than a narrow single-feature plugin.

Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Industrial-Re.content:
Industrial Revolution EMI Plugin
A small, purely functional addon (v1.0.1) that teaches EMI — the pack’s recipe viewer — how to display Industrial Revolution’s machine and Mining Rig recipes correctly. Without it, IndRev’s custom multi-input/energy-cost recipes either wouldn’t show up in EMI at all or would render with missing items. Every config option is a straightforward on/off toggle, all left enabled on this server: addMachineRecipes, addMiningRigRecipes, addChargedVersions (so charged item variants show correctly), hideNotImplementedItems, and addMissingItems to patch in anything EMI would otherwise render blank.
There isn’t gameplay content here — it’s pure recipe-viewer glue, doing for Industrial Revolution what similar EMI plugins do for other tech mods in the pack.

Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Industrial-Re.title: Industrial Revolution
Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Industrial-Re.content:
Industrial Revolution
Industrial Revolution — tagline “Every other industrial mod ever” — is a third full industrial tech tree in the pack, built around progressive machine tiers (Electric Furnace and Pulverizer each go Mk1 through Mk4, then a top-tier “Factory” variant) and dedicated Mining Rigs that automate resource gathering. The Mk-tier scaling is steep and server-verified: an Mk1 Electric Furnace costs 4 FE per operation and holds 1,000 FE, while the Factory tier costs 64 FE per operation but accepts up to 16,384 FE/t input and holds 100,000 FE — each tier roughly doubling processing speed alongside power draw. Its generator lineup (coal, two solar tiers, heat, gas, biomass, and a steam turbine) tops out at 4,096 FE/t for the Heat Generator and Steam Turbine, giving it genuine late-game power output to match its machine tiers. This server has all of Industrial Revolution’s custom ores enabled in world generation — tin, nikolite, lead, silver, tungsten, plus sulfuric acid lakes and sulfur crystal deposits.
Industrial Revolution has its own Quest Book chapter (industrial_revolution.snbt, 260 quests, icon indrev:mining_rig_mk4) at position 6 of 7, right before Modern Industrialization — placing it as a later-game tech tree alongside Create and MI rather than an early option like Tech Reborn or Powah!. Its own guidebook framing opens with “Welcome to Industrial Revolution!” and walks through Mining Rig drill heads and machine color-coded configuration modules.

Q: Where does it sit in progression?
A: Position 6 of 7 in the Quest Book (260 quests), right before Modern Industrialization — a later-game tree alongside Create and MI, not an early option like Tech Reborn or Powah!.
Q: Does it add ores to the world?

ME Requester
ME Requester (v1.1.4, by Almost Reliable) adds one focused feature to Applied Energistics 2: a Requester block that keeps a chosen stock level of an item or fluid topped up automatically, triggering the network’s autocrafting whenever the count drops below target — effectively a standing “keep X in stock” order rather than a one-off craft request. Requesters are managed from a dedicated ME Requester Terminal, and their configuration can be copied between blocks with an AE2 Memory Card, though it’s explicitly lost if the block itself is broken rather than moved.
Server config sets each Requester to hold 5 simultaneous requests, with a 5.0 AE/t idle energy drain, and requires a working ME channel to function (REQUIRE_CHANNEL = true) — so, like other AE2 devices, a Requester silently stops working if it loses channel allocation on a congested network.

Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Modern-Indust.content:
Modern Industrialization
Modern Industrialization (v1.8.6) is a second full industrial tech tree, distinguishing itself from Tech Reborn and Industrial Revolution by leaning heavily into multiblock machines and chemistry-flavored processing chains — Distillation Towers (server-capped at 9 blocks tall via maxDistillationTowerHeight), Electric Blast Furnaces, and cable/hatch-based multiblock assembly instead of single-block machines. It runs its own EU-style energy tier system with its own cable network, separate from Forge Energy, that other mods bridge into rather than the other way around.
This server explicitly enables Modern Industrialization’s cross-mod hooks: enableAe2Integration = true wires it into Applied Energistics 2’s storage/crafting system, and enableFtbQuestsIntegration = true powers its dedicated Quest Book chapter (modern_industrialization.snbt, 307 quests, icon modern_industrialization:guidebook), positioned last at slot 7 of 7 in the book’s order — the pack treats it as the most involved, latest-game tech tree of the bunch. Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Polymorphic-E.title: Polymorphic Energistics
Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Polymorphic-E.content:
Polymorphic Energistics
Polymorphic Energistics (v0.1.1) is a thin compatibility patch: it adds Polymorph support to Applied Energistics 2’s crafting and pattern system. Polymorph (see Quality-of-Life & UI Mods) normally lets recipe-viewer mods substitute interchangeable ingredients into a recipe on the fly; without a dedicated bridge, AE2’s own autocrafting patterns don’t recognize that flexibility. This mod wires the two together so AE2 patterns can take advantage of Polymorph’s ingredient substitution instead of requiring one rigid pattern per exact-item variant.
It ships no lang file, no config, and no standalone content of its own — it’s pure glue between two systems that are each documented in their own right elsewhere in this vault.
Anticipated questions
Q: What does Polymorphic Energistics do?
A: It’s a thin compat patch adding Polymorph support to Applied Energistics 2’s crafting and pattern system. See Storage & Applied Energistics — Getting Started.
Q: What problem does it solve?
A: Without a bridge, AE2’s autocrafting patterns don’t recognize Polymorph’s interchangeable-ingredient flexibility; this wires the two together so patterns can substitute ingredients instead of needing one rigid pattern per exact-item variant.
Q: Does it add any content?
A: No — no lang file, config, or standalone content; it’s pure glue between two systems each documented in their own right elsewhere in this vault.

Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Powah!.title: Powah!
Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Powah!.content:
Powah!
Powah! (v5.0.11) is the pack’s dedicated power-generation-and-transmission mod, meant to be the accessible “just make FE” option that plugs into whichever tech tree a player is actually running — Tech Reborn, Modern Industrialization, Create, or the AE2 network. Its main generator line is the Furnator (a fuel-burning generator with seven tiers — starter, basic, hardened, blazing, niotic, spirited, nitro — scaling from 1,000 FE capacity and 4 FE/t transfer up to 2,000,000 FE capacity and 3,000 FE/t transfer), alongside a Thermo Generator that produces power from heat-source/coolant pairs placed below and above it (lava gives 1,000 heat, a Magma Block 800, and Powah’s own Blazing Crystal Block a much richer 2,800) and a Magmator burning lava directly. Its endgame Reactor and world-generated Uraninite ore (spawned in poor/normal/dense vein tiers, plus Dry Ice veins) point toward a nuclear power stage past the basic generators.
Powah has its own Quest Book chapter (powah.snbt, 351 quests, icon powah:thermo_generator_nitro) sitting at position 3 of 7 — ahead of both AE2 and Create — with its very first quest handing out Powah’s own in-game guide book and captioned “The book will help you understand the mod if needed.” Early quest titles (“Ready to Power?”, “Electrician’s First Job”, “Electric Glue”, “Initial Parts”, “Electrician’s Right Hand”) frame it explicitly as the pack’s first stop for basic electricity, before players branch into the heavier trees.
Anticipated questions
Q: What is Powah! for?
A: It’s the pack’s dedicated power-generation-and-transmission mod — the accessible “just make FE” option that plugs into whichever tech tree you’re running (Tech Reborn, Modern Industrialization, Create, or the AE2 network). See Storage & Applied Energistics — Getting Started.
Q: What are its main generators?
A: The Furnator (fuel-burning, seven tiers scaling from 1,000 FE / 4 FE/t up to 2,000,000 FE / 3,000 FE/t), a Thermo Generator (heat-source/coolant pairs), and a Magmator burning lava; its endgame points to a Reactor and world-generated Uraninite ore.
Q: Where does it sit in progression?
A: Early — Quest Book position 3 of 7, ahead of both AE2 and Create, framed as the pack’s first stop for basic electricity (“Ready to Power?”, “Electrician’s First Job”) before branching into the heavier trees.
Q: Does it tie into AE2?
A: Yes — it’s built to make FE that plugs into the AE2 network among the other trees.

Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Tech-Reborn.title: Tech Reborn
Mods/Tech--and--Automation/Tech-Reborn.content:
Tech Reborn
Tech Reborn (v5.8.14, built on the shared RebornCore library) is a complete, self-contained classic tech tree in the IC2/GregTech lineage: ore doubling via an Industrial Grinder, tiered generators and dynamos, machine upgrades, and its own Reactor system alongside a craftable Nuke (server-configured to a 40-block radius and 400-tick fuse, though it can be disabled outright via config). Its signature late-game resource is UU-Matter — literally Universal Matter synthesized from raw energy through a Matter Fabricator/Replicator, letting players convert surplus power directly into scarce materials. Machines use the IC2-style “dot side” energy convention (IC2TransformersStyle = true), where the marked face accepts input and the rest of the block outputs.
In this pack’s Quest Book, Tech Reborn is chapter 1 of 7 (tech_reborn.snbt, 456 quests, icon techreborn:uu_matter) — the very first tech tree the book points players toward, with its opening quest subtitled “Welcome to Tech Reborn! A tech mod that provides options for power power generation, power storage, bulk item storage, tools and the creation of materials from energy and scrap.” That ordering, combined with Applied Energistics 2’s built-in PowerRatios.TechReborn = 2.0 energy-conversion setting, suggests Tech Reborn is meant as an accessible on-ramp tech tree that plugs cleanly into an AE2 network once players outgrow it.
Anticipated questions
Q: What is Tech Reborn?
A: A complete, self-contained classic tech tree in the IC2/GregTech lineage — ore doubling via an Industrial Grinder, tiered generators and dynamos, machine upgrades, its own Reactor, and a craftable Nuke (40-block radius, 400-tick fuse, disableable via config).
Q: What’s its signature late-game resource?
A: UU-Matter — Universal Matter synthesized from raw energy via a Matter Fabricator/Replicator, converting surplus power directly into scarce materials.
Q: Where does it sit in progression?
A: Chapter 1 of 7 in the Quest Book (456 quests) — the very first tech tree the book points players toward, an accessible on-ramp.
Q: Does it tie into AE2?
A: Yes — Applied Energistics 2 has a built-in PowerRatios.TechReborn = 2.0 energy-conversion setting, so it plugs cleanly into an AE2 network once players outgrow it. See Storage & Applied Energistics — Getting Started.

Quests/Quest-—-A-Jolly-Christmas.title: Quest — A Jolly Christmas
Quests/Quest-—-A-Jolly-Christmas.content:
A Jolly Christmas!
A seasonal holiday event chapter. It’s short and reward-focused: defeat campaign bosses during the event to claim themed Christmas Presents, capped by a special reward. There’s no new mechanic to learn — it re-uses existing Void’s Invasion bosses as the “unlock” conditions. See Creatures, Bosses & Mobs.
Walkthrough (present unlocks)

Christmas Present — Beginners Hope / First Bossfight — Claimed by defeating one of the first two bosses.
Christmas Present — Merry Magus — Defeat Magus to claim (drops an Ominous Eye reference item as flavor).
Christmas Present — Gu’mas ‘n’ Gingerbread — Defeat Gu’mas to claim.
Christmas Present — Under the Tentacle Twig — Defeat Conjunctivius to claim.
Christmas Molten Star — A capstone reward (“You earned this, bud!”).
Merry Christmas! — Closing note: the Prominence Team thanks you for playing and wishes you a Merry Christmas.

Tips

This is a time-limited holiday event — the presents are a seasonal bonus layered on top of bosses you may already be fighting for the main campaign.
Since the unlocks are tied to existing campaign/side bosses (Magus, Gu’mas, Conjunctivius), progress here comes naturally as you advance the story during the event window.
Watch for a nut-allergy joke — the rewards are gifts, treat them as flavor loot.

Related

Void’s Invasion · Hasturian Era · The Prison · Creatures, Bosses & Mobs

Anticipated questions

Is this chapter always available? No — it’s a seasonal Christmas event.
How do I get the presents? Defeat the referenced bosses (first two bosses, Magus, Gu’mas, Conjunctivius) during the event to unlock each present, plus the Christmas Molten Star capstone.
Are there new bosses here? No — it reuses existing campaign/side bosses as the claim conditions.

Quests/Quest-—-Applied-Energistics-2.title: Quest — Applied Energistics 2
Quests/Quest-—-Applied-Energistics-2.content:
Applied Energistics 2
This chapter walks you through the basics of Applied Energistics 2 — the endgame digital storage-and-autocrafting system covered in Tech & Automation Mods. By the end you should have basic AE power generation and a working ME storage system started. It assumes you can mine Sky Stone (Iron Pickaxe or better) and have a little early-game power on hand (even a Wooden Crank works to start).
Walkthrough
The questline is roughly ordered as: charge crystals → find meteorites → make processors → build a network → set up storage.

Preparing to Find Meteorites — Craft a Charger and use it to make a Meteorite Compass from a normal compass. The compass can be charged very early with a Wooden Crank. It points toward the nearest Meteorite within ~2,700 blocks: spinning rapidly means Sky Stone is in your chunk, spinning slowly means you’re out of range and should explore more.
Your First Meteorite — Bring an Iron Pickaxe or better (Sky Stone is hard). Mine to the center to collect Certus Quartz Crystals, Certus Quartz Blocks, and the Inscriber Presses from the Sky Chest — the presses are the whole reason you came.
Charge Certus & make Fluix — Toss Certus Quartz Crystals into the Charger to make Charged Certus Quartz. Craft Fluix Crystal by dropping Charged Certus, Nether Quartz, and Redstone Dust into water.
Processors — Use the Inscriber (each op needs 1k AE charged) with the presses to make Calculation, Logic, and Engineering Processors. Silicon comes from smelting Certus Quartz Dust.
Power the network — Options in the chapter: the Vibration Chamber (1–10 AE/t from solid fuel), the Energy Acceptor (converts external power, 2 FE = 1 AE), and the novelty Crystal Resonance Chamber. Add Energy Cells (200,000 AE) and Dense Energy Cells (1.6M AE) for buffer storage.
Storage & access — Build Storage Cells (items, fluids, or spatial), an ME Chest for direct access, and eventually an ME Controller (the routing hub — without it only 8 devices work, and you can only have one per network). A Drive Bay holds 10 cells in a tiny footprint. Portable Cells work like a backpack early-game.

Notable rewards & tips

The Crystal Growth Accelerator (consumes 8 AE/t) massively speeds growing Certus/Fluix crystals from seeds in adjacent water — build one early to escape the crafting bottleneck.
Fluix ME Glass Cable is the cheapest cable, carries power + up to 8 channels, and dyes to any of 16 colors.
Grab all the Inscriber Presses on your first meteorite trip; they’re not consumed and you never want to hunt for a second one.

Links

Applied Energistics 2 · Tech & Automation Mods
Storage overview: Storage & Inventory Mods
The Enchanting chapter’s Enchanting Library can be read by an AE2 Storage Bus.

Anticipated questions

Do I need AE2 to beat the pack? No — it’s a parallel long-term goal. Treat it as the answer to “how do I stop drowning in chests.”
Why won’t my network work past 8 devices? You need an ME Controller; without one the network caps at 8 interacting devices.
Where do processors come from? Only the Inscriber + presses, and presses only come from meteorite Sky Chests.
Exact recipes/costs? Check JEI/EMI in-game — this guide is grounded in the quest text, which describes function more than exact recipes.

Quests/Quest-—-Archon.title: Quest — Archon
Quests/Quest-—-Archon.content:
Archon
Archon is a runes-and-mana sorcery mod: you infuse mana into blocks to make magic materials, gear, spell tomes, and summon elemental bosses. This chapter (“Are you ready to become a Sorcerer?”) teaches the full rune workflow. See Magic & Spells Mods. Archon uses its own mana pool, separate from Botania.
Walkthrough

First Magic Steps — Craft the Channeler, a wand that infuses mana into blocks to create magic materials. Hold the Channeler in your off-hand and a block of your chosen metal to work it. Experiment with materials (e.g. Sorcerer’s Metal, Pixie Leaves from leaves, Spry Dust from mana-infused sand).
Boost your mana — Find Ancient Scrolls to raise mana capacity or regen. Build Mana Catalysts — tiered auras that boost nearby players’ mana capacity (+50 mana / 16-block radius, up to +200 / 34-block radius). The Mask of Power helmet gives 4 mana/sec while worn.
Find a Spire — Spires are tall towers in forest/mountain biomes with loot (watch for leeches).
Gather essences — Earth Essence (deep underground), End Essence (End islands), plus you must defeat the four Elementals — Earth, Sky, Fire, Water — to harvest their essences.
Spellcasting — Build the Scripture Table to craft spell tomes (alchemy-style). Each Wand casts only its element’s spells: Fire (Nether), Sky (villages), Water (ocean structures/fishing), End (End Cities/Strongholds), Earth (temples/mineshafts).
Bosses — Use the Pedestal to summon bosses with the right ingredients (from your Grimoire): shift-click removes ingredients; right-click the ingredients on directly (no GUI).

Notable weapons & rewards
The Channeler crafts a suite of magic weapons/armor, each with an ability:

Blade — teleport 8 blocks forward; Scepter — teleport 10 blocks with implosion damage.
Coat — fire resistance + mana-scaling implosion; Sword — slowness cloud; Bow — Ghast fireball; Stave — wither skulls; Mace — ground slam launching mobs (spares pets); Axe — brief resistance + projectile deflection.
Grim Reaper’s Toys — the Crusher converts kills to mana (20/mob, 30/player, 50/boss); the Scythe reaps souls; the Staff of Undead summons minions from a core.
Harvesters (Fire/Breezy/Soaking/Warping/Rocky) increase element-related mob loot; XP Pouches store 550 → 2920 XP.
Magical Farmer boots fertilize crops with mana when you crouch.

Links

Archon · Magic & Spells Mods
Compare with Bewitchment and Spell Books as parallel magic paths.

Anticipated questions

How do I make magic materials? Off-hand the Channeler and hold a metal block, then infuse mana into blocks.
Why won’t my wand cast a spell? Each elemental Wand only casts spells of its own element, found in that element’s structures.
How do I summon a boss? Put the Grimoire’s listed ingredients on a Pedestal by right-clicking them onto it — there’s no GUI.

Quests/Quest-—-Artifact-Reforging.title: Quest — Artifact Reforging
Quests/Quest-—-Artifact-Reforging.content:
Artifact Reforging
This chapter covers the pack’s soulbound artifact weapons — forged at S’kellak’s Forge from the Molten Core, each with a unique ability and its own Upgrade Tree. It’s endgame content: it requires completion of Chapter I of Void’s Invasion (the main story). See Gear Rarity & Reforging and the Simply Swords chapter (whose weapons feed several artifacts).
Getting started — S’kellak’s Forge

The Molten Core is forged from the depths of Cinderstone’s volcano, Vaaz. With it you craft artifact weapons that are bound to your soul — only the forger can use them.
Make a Hardening Catalyst / Hardening Crystal to make artifacts unbreakable, and use Encased Remnants to repair/reforge them.

The artifacts
Each is forged from the Molten Core plus specific components (mostly Simply Swords uniques + essences). Highlights:




























































ArtifactForged fromThemeFrostmourneEssence of Wrath + Awakened LichbladeSoulfrost sword (WoW tribute)Fyr’alathtwo Molten EdgesSoulfire tanking weapon (WoW tribute)A’zharDemonic Essence + SoulrenderTrapped-demon scythe (may betray you)SupernovaEssence of Glory + StarforgeAstral, all-element damageFury of a Thousand FistsEssence of Wrath + Fist of FurySoulfire martial-arts fistsThunderwrath / VaazkarDemonic Essence + ThunderbrandMolten lightning polearmAsh’edarEssence of Glory + Essence of Wrath (+ Essence of Ash’edar to unleash)Astral Sun/Moon twin swordsOrionEssence of Glory + Wizard StaffCosmic bow; evolves to 5 mage variantsGh’aj(eldritch dagger)High haste at the cost of sanityApophis(glory/oath hammer)Paladin protection hammer
There’s also a molten shield (symbol of the Living Statue of Vaaz).
Upgrade Trees

Forging an artifact unlocks its Upgrade Tree — press N and click the Molten Core icon (top-left).
Each tree has up to 7 nodes with branching paths. Unlock nodes by empowering the artifact with Molten Remnants (quest rewards, or craftable from Mythical Essences).
Mastery — beat 10 Mythical Challenges with an artifact to complete its Mastery (an Eternal Challenge per weapon).
Made a mistake in the skill tree? You can reset once for free: /puffish_skills skills reset @s puffish_skills:frostmourne (swap the artifact id).

Endgame reward
Forging all artifact weapons and unlocking their Mastery grants the “Piece of Eternal Knowledge” (Eternal Knowledge: Of the Eternal Forge).
Links

Gear Rarity & Reforging · Reforging · Simply Swords
Core RPG & Combat Mods · Talent Tree & Fate Talents (press N)

Anticipated questions

Why can’t anyone else use my artifact? They’re soulbound to whoever forged them.
How do I make them unbreakable? A Hardening Catalyst/Crystal; repair/reforge with Encased Remnants.
Where do Molten Remnants come from? Quest/campaign rewards, or craft from Mythical Essences, to unlock Upgrade Tree nodes.
I picked the wrong node. Use the free one-time reset command shown above.

Quests/Quest-—-Bewitchment.title: Quest — Bewitchment
Quests/Quest-—-Bewitchment.content:
Bewitchment
Bewitchment is the witchcraft-and-rituals mod: brews, poppets, altars, chalk circles, demon-trading, and vampire mechanics. This chapter (“Witch’s First Steps”) sets you on the witch’s path. See Magic & Spells Mods. The in-game Book of Shadows is the deep reference — read it for details.
Walkthrough

The four magic trees — Gather from Bewitchment’s special trees, each with future uses:

Tree of Blood — bleeds out; found in Nether Fortresses.
Tree of Knowledge — found scattered in forests.
Tree of Death — smells of death; found in taigas and swamps.
Tree of Life — found in savannas.


A Witch’s Knife — essential for rituals and scratching (harvesting) trees; take care of it.
Taglocks & essences — a Taglock binds a target (player) to a ritual; Ghost Essence (ghost goop) is another ritual ingredient.
The Altar — carries the magical energy for rituals. Increase its capacity by decorating it with the right materials and planting more trees around it.
Ritual kit — a Brazier (cursing, incense, rituals), Chalk (draw the activation circle — keep one of each type), Salt (wards off spirits/demons; good for barriers), and Garlic.
Cauldron & brews — the Cauldron brews potions from grown/scraped ingredients (and makes “wine”).

Notable items & rewards

Poppets — curse or protect a target depending on use (multiple types); store them on Poppet Shelves.
Witch outfits — the Besmircher (disguise to trade with demons), the Alchemist clothing (doubles brew durations), the Hedgewitch clothing (increases crop bounty).
Demon materials — Demon Hearts and Demon Parts (from killing demons/demonhounds) craft powerful magical items; Vampire’s Bed (a coffin) lets a player sleep through the day until night.
Utility blocks — mob-spawn blocker (24-block radius), a teleport wall-light (64-block radius), springboard/firewall/blocking brambles, and Witchberry brambles whose fruit restores magical energy.

Links

Bewitchment · Bewitchment Tweaks · Magic & Spells Mods
Compare with Archon and Spell Books as parallel magic systems.

Anticipated questions

Where’s the reference? The Book of Shadows — read it for in-depth mechanics.
How do I raise my altar’s power? Decorate it with appropriate materials and plant more magic trees nearby.
How do I trade with demons? Wear the Besmircher outfit to disguise yourself; demon materials come from killing demons/demonhounds.
What’s a Taglock for? Binding a specific target into a ritual (e.g. curses via poppets).

Quests/Quest-—-Botania.title: Quest — Botania
Quests/Quest-—-Botania.content:
Botania
Botania is the pack’s nature-magic tech tree, built entirely on mana generated and moved by flowers. This chapter takes you from your first Lexica Botanica through mana generation, Runic Altar crafting, Terrasteel gear, and an endgame boss with a hard mode. See Magic & Spells Mods. Tip from the chapter: check the Advancements for extra hints.
Walkthrough

Seedling’s First Steps — Craft the Lexica Botanica (the in-game guide, essential to progress), a Flower Pouch (keeps collected flowers out of your main inventory), and a Petal Apothecary (crafts many early Botania items).
Purification — Use a Pure Daisy to transform logs/stone into more sophisticated crafting materials.
Generate mana — Build the tools of the trade: Wand of the Forest (commands/redirects mana blocks — “You’re a Druid, Harry!”), Mana Pool (stores mana), Mana Spreader (transfers mana wirelessly to nearby mana-holding blocks; aim it with the wand), and a Mana Tablet (portable mana battery, ~half a pool each). Experiment with the different generating flowers.
Functional flowers — Create a flower with a unique function, then branch into rituals and creations using different flora.
Runic Altar & Runes — The Runic Altar (connected to a mana pool) crafts Runes used in many recipes. The Terrestrial Agglomeration Plate infuses three mana-dipped objects into a new ingot, consuming half a mana pool’s capacity — the ritual is wasted if the items aren’t on the plate.
Terrasteel — Craft the expensive Terrasteel Ingot, then work through Manasteel gear before it.

Gear progression & rewards

Manasteel Tools / Armor — better than iron, self-repair using mana.
Manaweave Armor — cheaper mana upkeep than the manasteel set, but weaker defense.
Terrasteel Armor — stronger than manasteel, and passively charges Mana Tablets in your inventory.
Terrasteel weapons (3) — stronger than their manasteel variants; also rank up your Terra Shatterer pickaxe. Its highest rank is the Earthshaker (“drill through the heavens and the earth”).
Upgraded Mana Spreaders — the Elven-tier spreader has higher payout; the best one is slower but pays out the most. Try different lenses on your spreaders.

Boss & hard mode
Defeating the chapter’s boss grants rewards and a chance at an artifact (collect them all). There is a hard mode that re-fights the boss for more rewards — the quest teases doing it without armor / without creative mode.
Links

Botania · Magic & Spells Mods
Bridges into tech: Applied Botanics pipes Botania mana into an Applied Energistics 2 network.

Anticipated questions

Where’s the in-game guide? The Lexica Botanica — craft it first, it explains every block.
My Agglomeration Plate ritual failed. The items must be on the plate, and you need half a mana pool’s worth of mana; otherwise the ritual is wasted.
Manasteel vs Manaweave vs Terrasteel? Manasteel = your first real set; Manaweave = cheaper mana cost, less defense; Terrasteel = strongest and charges tablets passively.

Quests/Quest-—-Collectibles-2.title: Quest — Collectibles 2
Quests/Quest-—-Collectibles-2.content:
Collectibles 2
A Collector’s Journey — the second collection chapter, this one focused on “trinkets and accessories… gathered and admired.” Where Quest — Collectibles is about fish and crops, this chapter is about Artifact trinkets (the “Things”), music discs, and mob heads. It’s optional side content: you find and hoard the items as you explore, fight, and dig, ticking off the display sets. See Quality-of-Life & UI Mods and FTB Quests.
Walkthrough

Get Hoardin’. Open the intro quest (“Welcome, young collector…”) to start the collection lines.
Collect the “Things” (Trinket Artifacts). “You must find the Things and collect them for your own benefit… just refer to them as a Thing, nothing more, nothing less.” These are a large spread of wearable Artifact trinkets, each with a flavor hint in the quest, for example:

Umbrella — “strong enough to be a shield and indestructible.”
Dimensional Bag — “basically an ender chest that you can carry around.”
Owl’s Glasses — a monocle that “enhances the wearer’s vision to even work at night as if they’re in the day.”
Displacement Tome (“A Book of Teleportation”) — charge it with pearls and save a location to teleport to; it needs crafted displacement pages to write down destinations.
Portable Ghast scepter — shoot fireballs like a Ghast, “but remember to carry ammunition.”
Crystallized Hades Fire — makes the wearer “immune to fire and even lava damage.”
Running Shoes — “press B to run,” which makes your sprint faster.
Bedrock Tough — makes an item indestructible (“don’t let it touch cacti though”).
Light as a Rabbit, magnets that “pull in any item,” fall-damage-reducing boots, a mining glove, the Riot Gauntlet, and the joke-tier Whoopee Cushion (“the most legendary artifact”).
Utility items round it out: the Recall Potion / “Milk Tea” (teleports you to your spawnpoint — “a good way to escape or go home quickly”), a chest key for locking/unlocking chests, and an inside-out “flipped” bucket that acts as an infinite water source but can’t pick anything back up.
A Gleaming Compound (“Shiny Red Stone”) is a rare material used to craft the more powerful Things.
