Find the Discs. “These records are almost lost to time… find them and listen to what they have to offer.” Two sets: Minecraft Discs (the classic C418 tracks plus Lena Raine’s Otherside/Pigstep and other vanilla records) and Modded Discs (harder-to-find tracks, including a large block of Prominence OST records by SideralisMusic and others).
Find the Mob Heads. “Finding cool remains is worth showing for display… once you find them and use the brush to dig them out, give your respect.” Get a Brush first, then recover the mob heads for display.
Grab the “Know Your Thing” guide item if you want an in-game reference for where to gather the Things.

Tips

Most of this chapter is passive completion — trinkets drop, discs are found, and heads are brushed up as you play other chapters, so treat it as a long-running checklist.
The Displacement Tome and Recall Potion are genuinely useful travel tools, not just display pieces — the Tome saves named locations (needs displacement pages + pearls), while the Recall Potion is a one-shot trip to your spawnpoint.
Save Gleaming Compound — it’s flagged as rare and is what the stronger Things are crafted from.
Mob heads require a brush (archaeology-style), so get one before hunting remains.

Anticipated questions

What is this chapter collecting? Trinket “Artifacts” (the “Things”), music discs, and mob heads — a display/hoarding chapter rather than a progression one.
What are the “Things”? Wearable Artifact trinkets, each with a joke-y hint in the quest — ranging from useful (Dimensional Bag, Owl’s Glasses, Crystallized Hades Fire, Displacement Tome) to silly (the Whoopee Cushion).
How do I get mob heads for the collection? Find the remains and dig them out with a brush, then the head is yours to display.
What discs are there? Two sets — classic Minecraft records and modded ones, the latter including a big batch of Prominence’s own original soundtrack discs.
What’s the Gleaming Compound for? It’s a rare material used to craft the more powerful Things.
Is this required for the main story? No — it’s optional collection/display content you fill in as you play.

Links

FTB Quests · Quality-of-Life & UI Mods
Quest — Collectibles (the fish/crops collection chapter it pairs with)

Quests/Quest-—-Collectibles.title: Quest — Collectibles
Quests/Quest-—-Collectibles.content:
Collectibles
The Explorer’s Journal chapter — a collection hunt for “items that you wouldn’t actively find.” It’s framed as three god- and captain-themed collecting quests: fishing up specimens for Poseidon, chasing down the drowned Captain Cornelia’s sea loot, and gathering scattered plant life for Demeter. It’s optional side content rather than main-story progression; you fill in the sets as you naturally explore, fish, and farm. See Quality-of-Life & UI Mods and FTB Quests.
Walkthrough

Begin the Hunt. Open the chapter’s intro quest (“Hello young explorer! Welcome to the Explorer’s Journal…”) to unlock the three collection lines.
Poseidon’s Aquarium — go fishing. Poseidon “has lost all of his fish for his personal aquarium,” so find and fish up new specimens for the God of the Sea. This includes a Nether Depths’ Fish sub-set — the fish you catch down in the Nether’s lava seas (lava pufferfish, obsidianfish, searing cod, bonefish, wither bonefish, magmacube fish, glowdine, soulsucker, fortress grouper, eyeball fish, and the long-lava-vision specimen). Complete the collection to earn the Sea God’s Fisher reward (“You have done the God of the Sea a huge favor!”).
Captain Cornelia’s Treasure Hunt. Cornelia “sailed until she fell into the depths of the freezing oceans” — you have to be “daring enough to find her ship and take her treasures.” This line branches into several sets:

Send her to rest — use a special trinket you find to “call the Captain back from the dead” (the quest warns: “Beware the dead”).
Captain Cornelia’s Armor — the set she “wore to survive the freezing depths”; collect the whole set to dive deep yourself.
Armor of a Sea Terror — a pufferfish-like set “for those who love being reckless and fighting underwater.”
Terrors of the Ice Maze — take down the freezing, massive Ice Maze and its ocean depths, and return with the spoils.
Captain Cornelia’s Hideout — once found, search it for her hidden treasure.
Sea Dog Weaponry and Abyssal Sea Weaponry — the crew’s lost weapons (“if you stare at the abyss, the abyss stares back at you”).
Minecraft’s Aquatics — a “classic set of aquatic life, from Minecraft itself.”


Demeter’s Garden — gather crops. Demeter “has left her plant life scattered across the world” and rewards anyone who gathers it. Fill three sub-collections: Croptopia Seeds (a large variety of crops), Croptopia Trees (fruit-tree varieties), and Delight Crops (a smaller set, but “found fairly quickly”).

Tips

This is a fishing/exploration/farming completionist chapter — much of it fills itself in as you play the other chapters, so don’t grind it in isolation.
The Cornelia line is tied to cold-ocean and Ice Maze content, so it pairs naturally with underwater/frost exploration; her armor is themed around surviving “the freezing depths.”
Nether Depths fish are caught in the Nether’s lava, not overworld water — bring the gear to fish and survive down there.
Delight Crops is the quickest of Demeter’s three sets to finish if you want an early completion.

Anticipated questions

What kind of chapter is this? A collection chapter — the “Explorer’s Journal” for gathering items you wouldn’t otherwise seek out, split into Poseidon (fish), Captain Cornelia (sea loot), and Demeter (crops).
Who rewards me? The sea god Poseidon (the “Sea God’s Fisher” reward for finishing his aquarium) and Demeter, the Goddess of Harvest and Agriculture, for gathering her plant life.
Where do the Nether Depths fish come from? They’re fished up in the Nether’s lava seas, not overworld water — a distinct sub-set within Poseidon’s Aquarium.
What is Captain Cornelia? A captain who “fell into the depths of the freezing oceans”; her quest line has you find her ship and hideout and collect her armor, weapons, and treasure.
Is this required for the main story? No — it’s an optional collecting journal you fill in alongside normal exploration, fishing, and farming.

Links

FTB Quests · Quality-of-Life & UI Mods
Quest — Collectibles 2 (its companion trinket/disc/mob-head collection chapter)

Quests/Quest-—-Create.title: Quest — Create
Quests/Quest-—-Create.content:
Create
This chapter introduces Create, the showpiece kinetic-automation mod from Tech & Automation Mods. As the intro itself notes, Create has excellent built-in guides: hover any item in REI/your inventory and hold W to “ponder” it for an animated explanation. Because of that, the chapter is mostly a map of what exists and a rough progression outline rather than step-by-step recipes.
Progression outline
1. Generate kinetic power (SU). Start with the simplest sources and scale up:

Hand Crank — you are the power source; simplest possible.
Water Wheel — same SU at the same RPM as long as one block of flowing water is adjacent (still pools don’t work). Right-click with any wood plank to reskin it.
Large Water Wheel — twice the SU at slower RPM.
Steam Engine — the densest source, but most complex: needs a steady water + heat supply.

2. Read your network. Use the Goggles (essential — shows stress impact and block info), plus the Stressometer and Speedometer.
3. Brass & processing. Heat a Mechanical Mixer over a Blaze Burner (fill an empty burner by right-clicking a blaze or blaze spawner) to mix copper + zinc into brass. The mixer autocrafts shapeless recipes and mixes potions, and needs ≥30 RPM to run.
4. Core machines to build toward:

Encased Fan — extremely versatile: wash, haunt, blast, and smoke items. Add Nozzle for spherical AoE; front-mounted casings (Haunting/Blasting/Smoking/Splashing) set the mode. Notably sand→soul sand (haunt) and soul sand→nether quartz (wash).
Mechanical Press — bonks ingots into plates.
Millstone / Crushing Wheels — grind to dust (keep both around for different recipes).
Mechanical Drill / Saw / Harvester / Plough — for contraption tools, tunnel bores, and farms.
Mechanical Crafter & Mechanical Arm — automatic and oversized crafting, plus advanced item distribution.

5. Contraptions. Super Glue binds blocks; then Mechanical Pistons / Bearings / Gantries / Cart Assemblers move them linearly, rotationally, or along rails. Rope Pulley and the fancier Elevator Pulley handle vertical movement.
6. Trains (endgame). Minimum: 1 Train Casing, 1 Train Station, and enough Train Tracks. Ponder the Train Station to learn assembly. Add Train Signals, Track Switches, Schedules, and a Display Board for a real rail network.
Notable rewards & tips

The chapter’s completion reward is flagged as an Eternal Challenge (“One Cookie to Rule Them All”).
Create: Crafts & Additions content appears here too: Electric Motor (energy→kinetic), Alternator (kinetic→energy, caps at 256 E/t), Rolling Mill, Tesla Coil, and the Modular Accumulator — this is your bridge between Create and electrical tech.
Infinite fluids: a Hose Pulley extracts infinitely from any pool of ≥10,000 source blocks (search $create:bottomless in REI).
Diving kit: Copper Backtank + Diving Helmet/Boots to walk and breathe underwater.

Links

Create · Create Crafts & Additions · Create: Steam ‘n’ Rails · Create: Copycats+
Tech & Automation Mods · Powah! (wire kinetic power into electricity)

Anticipated questions

How do I learn a specific block? Hold W to Ponder it — the mod’s own tutorial is better than any recipe list.
My water wheel won’t spin. It needs genuinely flowing water adjacent, not a still source pool.
Do I need the Goggles? Effectively yes — they show stress capacity/impact, which you need to avoid overstressing your network.

Quests/Quest-—-Deeper-and-Darker.title: Quest — Deeper and Darker
Quests/Quest-—-Deeper-and-Darker.content:
Deeper and Darker — The Otherside
A compact dimension chapter built around the Deeper and Darker mod. It takes you from the Deep Dark and the Warden into a new dimension, The Otherside, with its own sculk-themed mobs and drops. It’s an optional exploration track you can pursue once you’re comfortable in the Deep Dark. See Dimensions & Space Travel Mods and Creatures, Bosses & Mobs.
Walkthrough

Kill a Warden — Found underground in the Overworld’s Deep Dark. Drops the Heart of the Deep, your key to the portal.
Enter The Otherside — Before lighting the portal, remove all Sculk Veins from the inner frame, then right-click the cleared frame with the Heart of the Deep from the Warden.
Otherside mobs (kill quests, each with a themed drop):

Shattered → Soul Dust.
Stalker → Soul Crystal. Rare chance to spawn after breaking an Ancient Vase.
Shriek Worm → Sculk Bone. Appears by stepping on Infested Sculk.


Find a Sculk Snapper — Can be tamed with enchanted Netherite Chestplates; once tamed they occasionally drop enchanted books.

Tips

The Warden is a serious fight — come geared and consider ranged/hit-and-run tactics before attempting the Heart of the Deep.
Don’t try to light the portal until every Sculk Vein is cleared from the inner frame, or it won’t activate.
Keep spare enchanted Netherite Chestplates if you want to tame Sculk Snappers for passive enchanted-book income.

Related

Dimensions & Space Travel Mods · Creatures, Bosses & Mobs · Accessories & Enchanting · Exploration, Dungeons & Structures Mods

Anticipated questions

How do I open the Otherside portal? Kill a Warden for the Heart of the Deep, clear all Sculk Veins from the inner frame, then right-click the frame with the Heart.
How do I get a Stalker to fight? Break Ancient Vases — Stalkers have a rare chance to spawn from them.
Can I tame anything here? Yes — Sculk Snappers are tamed with enchanted Netherite Chestplates and then drop enchanted books.

Quests/Quest-—-Enchanting.title: Quest — Enchanting
Quests/Quest-—-Enchanting.content:
Enchanting
This chapter teaches the pack’s deep enchanting overhaul (built on the Eterna/Quanta/Arcana stat system) — from a basic Enchanting Table up to an Enchanting Library holding every enchant, plus tomes, charms, and infusions. See Accessories & Enchanting and EMI Enchanting.
The Enchanting Table stats
The table shows three bars:

Eterna — the table’s level (and cost). Your required XP level is 2× Eterna (50 Eterna = 100 levels).
Quanta — pure randomness; the more you add, the more chaotic results get. Not recommended to max.
Arcana — rarity and number of enchants. Don’t max it if you want plain enchants like Protection or class enchants like Sunfire — lower Arcana for those.

Bookshelf progression
You build power by surrounding the table with increasingly exotic bookshelves. The rough ladder:

Seashelves / Hellshelves — your first stat shelves; you need ~15 total (a mix is fine) to get started.
Infused shelves — infuse the above with Crystaline/Heartforged Seashelves or Blazing/Glowing Hellshelves (need ≥2 of the higher ones). Following the chapter’s counts gets you to ~30 Eterna.
Echoing / Deep Dark shelves — need Ancient City loot (Echo Shards); make ~8. This is where players “learn to love or hate” the grind.
Draconic Endshelves (Ender Dragon Heads from End ships) and Endshelves (End Rods) — the last mile; make several spares.

Set up an infusion setup to upgrade shelves and infuse Tomes and Charms.
Tomes, charms & the Library

Tomes — scrapping/extraction tomes pull enchants off items; gear-specific tomes get enchants only possible on certain gearsets (e.g. Feather Falling). Read a tome before using it — some destroy the item. Infused tomes work with an Anvil enchanted with Splitting to break a big enchanted book into its components.
Anvil enchants — Obliteration and Splitting (the latter is one of the only ways to extract some enchants from a weapon/book).
Enchanting Library — the payoff: stores all your enchants (and curses) in one block, mineable, and AE2-compatible (face a Storage Bus at it). A bigger/fancier version exists (“Library of Alexandria”).
Charms — crafted from 3 of the same potion for longer effects; they have durability. Make them last with Unbreaking + Mending, a Hardening Catalyst, or Infusion (learned later). The final quests show how to make charms Unbreakable.

Odds & ends flagged in-quest

Special Cobweb removes curses that can’t be removed normally.
Infused Dragon’s Breath — take it from the dragon (bring bottles), buy from Alchemist Villagers (higher-tier trade), or loot dungeons.
Ghast Tears — from Journeyman Alchemist trades or Nether dungeons.
Getting levels — Looting, Scavenger, Soul Devourer, and Knowledge of the Ages (converts items to XP — don’t use on bosses), plus the Bag of Souls armor enchant. Bulk-haunt items with an Encased Fan over soul fire for some materials.

Links

EMI Enchanting · Accessories & Enchanting · Applied Energistics 2 (Library + Storage Bus)

Anticipated questions

Why am I getting bad/random enchants? Too much Quanta (chaos) or Arcana (rarity). Lower Arcana for plain enchants like Protection/Sunfire.
How much XP do I need? 2× your Eterna value in levels.
How do I move an enchant off a bad weapon? An Anvil enchanted with Splitting + extraction tomes.
Best endgame storage for enchants? The Enchanting Library — it holds everything and hooks into an AE2 Storage Bus.

Quests/Quest-—-Gadgets.title: Quest — Gadgets
Quests/Quest-—-Gadgets.content:
Gadgets
A grab-bag chapter about the “unique and quirky items/blocks in Prominence” — many of them useful even for the tech mods. No strict progression; just discover and craft the gadgets you want. See Quality-of-Life & UI Mods and Tech & Automation Mods.
Notable gadgets
Ore & resource tricks

Copper Pan — an early-game alternative to tech-mod ore farms: put sand/gravel below and water above, and it rarely generates ore nuggets, gravel, emeralds, and misc items.

Effect & filter blocks

Blank Plates → Effect Plates — step on an Effect Plate to get its effect. Make plates by striking Blank Plates with lightning.
Damage Plate — hurts mobs down to 1 HP but never kills, perfect for a Looting IV sword (“hurt mobs, but kill them yourself”). Plates don’t apply enchants — your weapon does.
Mob Filters — blocks only certain entities can pass through (more than just player filters).
Cog Blocks (Supplementaries) — act like redstone but can be placed in mid-air.

Movement

Gliders (Kibe) — affordable, one of the best ways to traverse large areas before the End (“not quite flying, not quite falling”).
Levitation Block — a limited zone of creative flight (alternatives: Flügel Tiara, Gravichestplate).
Earthdive Spear — pass through a wall without hurting your head.

Utility & base blocks

Trash Can — deletes unwanted items (“apex predator of an unorganized base”); also a handheld version.
Animal Feeding Trough — auto-feeds your animals.
Waxing Staff — wax blocks without doing it by hand.
Quiver (Supplementaries) — store lots of arrows.
Mob Ward (Bosses of Mass Destruction) — stops hostile spawns in a large area.
Spawn-blocking torches — one stops animal spawns, another stops aquatic spawns (handy for a trident farm).

Links

Quality-of-Life & UI Mods · Supplementaries · Animal Feeding Trough
Tech & Automation Mods (the Copper Pan complements ore automation)

Anticipated questions

Early ore source without a tech mod? The Copper Pan (sand/gravel below, water above) slowly yields nuggets and odds and ends.
How do I make Effect/Damage Plates? Strike Blank Plates with lightning.
Best pre-End travel gadget? A Glider.
Do the damage plates use my sword’s Looting? Plates don’t apply enchants; they just leave mobs at 1 HP so you land the killing blow with your enchanted weapon.

Quests/Quest-—-Getting-Started.title: Quest — Getting Started
Quests/Quest-—-Getting-Started.content:
Getting Started
The very first Quest Book chapter, and the pack’s built-in tutorial. You are a flameborn, created and sent by S’kellak into the Overworld to seek answers. This chapter walks you through the questbook itself and every core system you’ll rely on for the rest of the run. Do it first; most other chapters assume you’ve read it. See also the systems overview in Getting Started (Systems note).
Walkthrough (key quests in order)

First Steps / Enter the Overworld — Introduces the Quest Book. Left side of a quest = tasks to do, right side = rewards. Open it via the book icon at the top-left of your inventory. The Quest Chapters screen is reached by closing a quest and moving your cursor to the left.
Find a fruit or vegetable — Nudges you toward eating early; hunger matters more here than vanilla (Croptopia adds a huge range). See Food, Farming & Cooking Mods.
Craft a Chest — Chests are later upgradeable. Mine copper and use a Blank Chest Upgrade to make a copper upgrade. Storage is its own progression track — see Storage & Inventory Mods.
Backpacks (Traveler’s Backpack) — Equip via the Equip icon, open with B. Upgradeable through tiers; special backpacks appear in loot chests. Search @traveler in the REI/EMI search bar to see variants. Press R / U over any item for its Recipe / Uses.
Use a Waystone — The intended fast-travel system. Waystones generate in villages and are craftable; right-click to bind/teleport.
World Map & claiming — Press M for the World Map. Right-click a chunk and “Claim Selected” to claim it. Watch for server claim limits.
Talent Tree — Press N. You get a talent point every 2 levels. Reset with a Knowledge Scroll (consumed on use, refunds points). This is the main progression method alongside leveling — see Talent Tree & Fate Talents.
Obtain an Anvil / Reforging — All tools roll a random rarity affecting stats. Improve it via the anvil’s second tab using a tool-specific material plus one of the 3 ores. See Gear Rarity & Reforging.
Leveling (Player Level) — Shown top-left of the inventory; grows from combat and boss kills, raises max health, and gates certain boss fights. This is separate from the vanilla XP level on your hotbar. See Progression & Level Caps.
Level caps tied to Campaign — 1–10 unlocked by default; 11–50 unlocked by defeating the first boss of the Void’s Invasion campaign; 51–65 unlocked by starting the Hasturian Era campaign. Level 65 is the current maximum.
The Wiki — Points you to rpg.prominence.wiki for deeper guides (link isn’t clickable in-game).
Tutorial questlines / Eternal Knowledge — Flags the tutorial chapters as essential reading, and hints they are the way to obtain “Eternal Knowledge.”
Parties (Open Parties and Claims) — /openpac-parties create, invite with /openpac-parties member invite [Name], enable PvP with /opacpvp (both players must enable it).

Tips

Rewards in this chapter are mostly cosmetic/quality-of-life (e.g. a music disc, backpack tank) — the real payoff is understanding the systems.
Do the Talent Tree, Reforging, and Leveling reading quests properly; they save a lot of confusion later.

Related

Getting Started · Progression & Level Caps · Talent Tree & Fate Talents · Gear Rarity & Reforging · Storage & Inventory Mods · Quality-of-Life & UI Mods

Anticipated questions

Why can’t I level past 10 (or 50)? Your level cap is tied to campaign progress. Beat the first Void’s Invasion boss for 11–50, and start the Hasturian Era for 51–65.
Player Level vs the number on my hotbar? Player Level (top-left of inventory) is the RPG level that gates bosses and health. The hotbar number is vanilla experience — different thing.
How do I reset my talents? Use a Knowledge Scroll; it’s consumed and refunds all your points.
How do I improve a tool’s rarity? Reforge in the anvil’s second tab with a tool-specific material and one of the 3 ores.

Quests/Quest-—-Hasturian-Era.title: Quest — Hasturian Era
Quests/Quest-—-Hasturian-Era.content:
The Hasturian Era
The expansion campaign that follows Void’s Invasion. You must finish the entire Void’s Invasion campaign to unlock this storyline. Lore: eons ago S’kellak imprisoned the primordial C’thulhu, but its half-brother — a tall hooded, tentacled monster, Hastur, The King in Yellow — broke free. With the realms at their weakest after the Void’s invasion, Hastur returns to claim them. This chapter is partly live and partly coming in v4.0 (the Cinderstone Depths dimension and Kingdom of Vaaz), so expect some quests to be teasers.
Walkthrough

The Hasturian Era (unlock) — Requires finishing the Void’s Invasion campaign, which also unlocks 51–65 leveling. Read the lore intro on Hastur’s escape and return.
Missive from S’kellak — A cinderstone missive confirms the enemy is Hastur, warns the Overworld is unsafe (Hastur twists minds), and tells you to enchant your weapon with Smite because his followers are undead. It directs you to signal a beacon to travel to Vaaz.
Gu’mas, The Fallen Archmage (Required Level ~60–65) — The former Hex leader, killed by the Champions of Vaaz and resurrected by Hastur. He kidnaps/kills anyone trying to reach the Cinderstone Depths. Use Smite to shred his barrier if you lack the required spell power. Defeat the Resurrected Magus, Gu’mas.
Kingdom of Vaaz — Use the Beacon of Hope in the Overworld to travel to Vaaz and meet S’kellak.
Path to Corruption: Infusions — Corruption Infusions add corruption to armor (fuels corruption-scaled active talent abilities). Template drops in End cities; use in a Smithing Table with the item + a material: Aberration Limb (+10), Aberration Heart (+20), X’al the Faceless Eye (+35).
Path to Etyr: Infusions — Etyr Infusions add Corruption Resistance that counteracts your corruption. Negative effects scale off your Total Corruption (which accounts for Etyr). Template in End cities; infuse an Etyr Ingot (+10) via Smithing Table.
Journey to Vaaz — The Beacon of Hope breaks; with no way to reach S’kellak you’ll need another route. This questline is flagged as coming in v4.0, along with the Cinderstone Depths and Kingdom of Vaaz. In the meantime it jokingly tells you to “drink away your sorrows.”
Blog link quest — Points to the official 4.0 development blog (link on the wiki / above the quest).

Tips

This is level 60+ content — max out toward Lv 65 and gear up (artifacts, infusions) before starting.
Smite is essential again here: Hastur’s followers are undead, and it breaks Gu’mas’s barrier.
Balance Corruption (powers your abilities) against Etyr (resistance) — going all-in on corruption without Etyr means heavier negative effects.

Related

Void’s Invasion · Progression & Level Caps · Damage Types & Runes · Accessories & Enchanting · Creatures, Bosses & Mobs

Anticipated questions

Why is this chapter locked? You must complete the whole Void’s Invasion campaign first; doing so also unlocks 51–65 leveling.
Why can’t I finish the Journey to Vaaz? Part of this chapter (Cinderstone Depths, Kingdom of Vaaz) is unreleased content slated for v4.0.
How do I beat Gu’mas if my spell power is too low? Enchant with Smite — it shreds his barrier.
Corruption vs Etyr? Corruption boosts corruption-scaled abilities but its downsides scale with your Total Corruption; Etyr adds resistance that offsets that total.

Quests/Quest-—-Industrial-Revolution.title: Quest — Industrial Revolution
Quests/Quest-—-Industrial-Revolution.content:
Industrial Revolution
Industrial Revolution is another full industrial tech tree — tools, weapons, machines, and ways of generating resources. See Tech & Automation Mods.


                  
                  Industrial Revolution is being removed from Prominence 
                  
                

The chapter itself announces that Indrev is leaving the pack, phased out gradually so players can migrate to Tech Reborn and other tech mods. Reasons given in-quest: the mod was abandoned by its developer, cables don’t transfer at their advertised speed, and machines break unbreakable items / kill things they shouldn’t. Phase one makes all Indrev cables uncraftable and lets you convert them to Tech Reborn cables at any time; other features are unaffected for now. If you’re starting fresh, prefer Tech Reborn instead.


Walkthrough (if you still use it)

Nikolite line — mine for Nikolite Dust (a turquoise dust with useful machine properties). Infuse iron with it for Nikolite-enhanced ingots, and combine with Diamond Dust for Enriched Nikolite. The Solid Infuser is the only machine that can infuse Nikolite — central to the whole tree.
Machine tiers & tools — Machine blocks come in tiers MK1–MK4; Circuit upgrades (MK2/3/4) speed processing and allow more enhancers. Use the Screwdriver to configure machine input/output sides and the energy cube.
Fluid/Item pipes — need a Retriever Servo (pulls into the machine it points at) or an Output Servo to move contents.
Automation machines — Sawmill (more planks + sawdust), Chopper (auto plant + fell trees, needs an axe), Slaughter (kills mobs with a supplied sword), Rancher (auto-breed and kill animals). Each has a top-tier variant.
Mining Rig — generate ores using RF: a Mining Rig Computer + 1–8 Mining Rig Drills + Drill Heads + an Encoded Ore Data Card (encode 64 of an ore in a Data Card Encoder; add Enriched Nikolite, 16 per 1%, to raise richness/yield).
Modular armor — Helmet/Chestplate/Leggings/Boots that accept modules (e.g. Color Modules). The Core of Modularity is charged in a Capsule using Laser Emitter(s) placed 3 blocks away; power with LF and pulse redstone. Warning: pulsing an emitter at an empty capsule destroys the capsule, and pulsing one not facing a capsule makes it explode.

Notable rewards & tips

Enhancers boost machines; the base enhancer adds +25k LF capacity per upgrade.
The chapter openly flags one weapon as a “meme weapon — please don’t use it unironically, it’s bad.”

Links

Industrial Revolution · Industrial Revolution EMI Plugin
Migration target: Tech Reborn · Tech & Automation Mods

Anticipated questions

Should I invest in Industrial Revolution? Not for the long term — it’s being removed. Convert cables to Tech Reborn and build your factory there.
My Indrev cables won’t craft. Intended — phase one made them uncraftable; convert existing ones to Tech Reborn cables.
What replaces it? Tech Reborn is the pack’s recommended alternative, with Modern Industrialization and Create as other options.

Quests/Quest-—-Main-Story.title: Quest — Main Story
Quests/Quest-—-Main-Story.content:
Main Story — Void’s Invasion
The core campaign. S’kellak, the Eternal Flame and creator of all things, has grown weak, and The Void is breaching every dimension, twisting once-serene creatures into aberrations. As the flameborn champion you fight the Void’s heralds across the Overworld, Nether, and End, each a recommended-level boss, then confront the Void’s essence and its faceless herald. Beating the first boss unlocks 11–50 leveling; finishing this campaign is the prerequisite for The Hasturian Era. Bosses have their own level — see the boss-level note below.
Walkthrough (bosses roughly by recommended level)

Gauntlet, First Herald of the Nether (Rec. Lv 15) — Fallen watcher of the Nether, locked in a monolithic prison; shatter its eye to release the corrupted being. Found in the Nether.
The Night Lich, King of All Kings (Rec. Lv 10, ranged-friendly) — Resurrected kings of Ly’rell fused into one. Dwells in colder Overworld biomes atop a broken tower. Use Soul Stars (dropped by undead) to locate it — the quest asks you to obtain and use at least 4. Defeating it unlocks 11–50 Leveling.
The Decaying King (Rec. Lv ~20, melee-friendly) — Cursed Nether king wielding the Darkin Blade. Use a Moonstone Compass to find the Decaying Kingdom; can also be re-summoned via Withered Demon Hearts → Demonite Chunks. (Deep-dive in The Nether.)
Jean, The Fallen Dragon (Rec. Lv 20) — The corrupted Ender Dragon. To open the End portal you need 12 of the 16 unique eyes scattered across Overworld and Nether. (See To The End for the eye hunt.)
The Blackstone Golem (Rec. Lv 25) — Nether’s final Herald, summoned via a ritual: a 9×9 Blackstone platform with Chiseled Polished Blackstone Holders one block out from each side, then a Gilded Blackstone shard on each. Full ritual detail lives in The Nether.
Conjunctivius, Watcher of the Prison (Rec. Lv 30) — Giant eye in its Lair deep in the Prison. Requires a Vine Rune from the Promenade of the Condemned. See The Prison.
The Remains of an Old Champion (Rec. Lv 35) — Possessed skeleton in an underground Overworld grave; alternates shielding stances with attacks.
Obsidilith, Pillar of the Void (Rec. Lv 40) — Living monolith in the End; summon by using an eye of ender atop its floating platform. (Also in To The End.)
The Eldritch Eye (Rec. Lv 50) — The corrupted “Ender Eye.” Build an Eye Shrine (5×5 obsidian base, centered 3×3 crying obsidian, an end rod on each corner) in the End to summon it.

After the heralds fall, S’kellak grants the Molten Core (a vessel needing the essences of ancient beings) and the corruption arc begins:

Essence quests — Defeat side-bosses to charge the Molten Core: Baphomet (Demonic Essence, summoned via the Book of Shadows ritual — progress Bewitchment first), the Fallen Icon (Essence of Glory, via Essence of Eventide on the Old Moon Altar), and the Ghost of Captain Cornelia (Essence of Wrath, summoned with the Shell Horn in the Ice Maze).
End corruption / new dimensions — Visit the Primordial Abyss and the Hasturian Wastes, purge Aberrations (their hits stack corruption on you), and gather Etyr ingots (corruption-resistant metal) from Spire Spikes.
Null, Void’s Essence — Summon in the End’s rift with a pedestal + two End essences (ender pearl, end crystal). Null teleports whenever hit and spawns minions; never stop attacking or it heals. Beating it unlocks Mythic Challenges.
Forge your Artifact — S’kellak tells you to forge a better weapon (the S’kellak’s Forge questline) before trapping a herald.
Magus, the Archmage — Leader of the Hex who made a pact with the Void. Craft a Hexblade offering, kill Magisters for a Hexblade + Prismatic Pearl, use the Hexblade on their portal to reach the Glass Ocean, then a Prismatic Pearl to summon him. His barrier is weak to certain elements and to Smite.
Path to Corruption — Forge The Dreadtide, gather 4 Ominous Eyes from the All-Seeing Eyes (about 1 in 125 Aberrations is mutated and may also drop them), and perform the Ritual of Damnation in the Primordial Abyss.
The Faceless One — The root of corruption, summoned in the Primordial Abyss by breaking an aberration heart at the center of its ritual. Weaken it so S’kellak can trap it in Vaaz. This ends the invasion — and sets up the Hasturian Era.

Mythic Challenges (Req. Lv 50) — Endgame encounters unlocked after Null. Summon with a Void Hourglass; each win grants a higher-level hourglass (stronger nightmare). Dying fails the challenge and drops you to a lower-level hourglass; a fresh Lv 1 hourglass can be re-obtained from Null.
Tips

Match the boss’s level. You deal 10% less damage per level you’re under a boss — at Lv 45 vs a Lv 50 boss you do only 50% damage. Level up before attempting.
Bring Smite for undead heralds and Magus’s barrier.
Many bosses need a summon item/ritual — read each quest’s description before traveling.

Related

The Nether · To The End · The Prison · Hasturian Era · Progression & Level Caps · Creatures, Bosses & Mobs · Magic & Spells Mods

Anticipated questions

Where do I start? The Night Lich (Rec. Lv 10) is the intended first campaign boss — beating it unlocks 11–50 leveling.
Why do I do no damage to a boss? Bosses have their own level; you lose 10% damage per level you’re below them.
How do I unlock the Hasturian Era? Finish the entire Void’s Invasion campaign (through The Faceless One).
What do the essences/Molten Core do? The Molten Core is a vessel; charging it with ancient essences lets you forge artifact weapons.
How do I open the End portal here? Collect 12 of the 16 unique eyes — details in To The End.

Quests/Quest-—-Marium's-Soulslike-Weapon.title: Quest — Marium's Soulslike Weaponry
Quests/Quest-—-Marium's-Soulslike-Weapon.content:
Marium’s Soulslike Weaponry
Marium’s Soulslike Weaponry (“Soul Weaponry”) is a boss-and-gear chapter built on soul materials, a chain of summonable bosses, and an arsenal of themed weapons and firearms. It all starts with a single soul sand. See Core RPG & Combat Mods.
Material base

Lunar Source — mine Moonstone and Verglas in the deepslate layers (uncommon). These are core to soul equipment.
Soul Crafting — smelt Soul Sand into Lost Souls, then craft Soul Infused Ingots — the main soul-equipment ingredient.
Building blocks — Infused Blackstone, Soulfire Stain, Soul Lamp (decorative, seen in the bosses’ structures).

Boss progression (Lord Souls)
Craft a Boss Compass to locate them. Each boss frees/kills a fallen figure and yields a Lord Soul used to awaken gear:

Champion’s Grave — the champion boss.
Accursed Lord (“Fall of a Kingdom”) → Lord Soul Red + Withered Demon Heart.
Draugr Boss (“Fallen Puppet”) → Lord Soul Dark + Essence of Eventide.
Returning Knight / Moonknight (“Retribution”) → Lord Soul White + Essence of Luminescence, via the Altar Block.
The Wither (“The Abyss Stares Back”) → Lord Soul Void + a chaotic shard.
Ender Dragon (“Essence of the Dragon”) → Lord Soul Purple.
Chaos Monarch — summoned from the Blackstone Pedestal with the shard; drops the Chaos Crown and Chaos Robes.

Weapons & gear

Moonlight swords — craft Bluemoon blades (“Imitation Moon”), then insert a powerful soul to awaken them into Moonlight Shortsword/Greatsword.
Firearms (use Silver Bullets): Hunter Pistol (quick reload), Blunderbuss (shotgun blast), Hunter Cannon (10 bullets → one cannonball, long reload), Gatling Gun (rapid fire, eats bullets).
Signature weapons: Soul Reaper (summon the dead), Holy Moonlight Sword (transforms between forms), Lich Bane (true magic damage above ⅓ target HP), Comet Spear, Galeforce bow, Bloodthirster (lifesteal), Darkin Blade / Darkin Scythe (evolves from red/blue souls), Leviathan Axe (freeze + ice explosion), Withered Wabbajack (random gamble effects), Mjolnir (lightning), Freyr Sword (fights on its own).
Armor sets: Soul Robes (dark sorcerer set), Soul Ingot armor (durable), and Forlorn armor (drops only from Evil Forlorns in the Soul Sand Valley).
Moonstone tools (stronger than diamond) and the Moonstone Ring (launch magical waves).
Novelty: kill Chunguses for Chungus Emeralds (9 → the Big Chungus music disc).

Links

Marium’s Soulslike Weaponry · Core RPG & Combat Mods · Creatures, Bosses & Mobs

Anticipated questions

Where do I start? Smelt soul sand into Lost Souls and mine Moonstone/Verglas in the deepslate layers.
How do I awaken the moonlight swords? Craft the Bluemoon versions, then insert a powerful soul (a boss’s Lord Soul).
How do I find the bosses? Craft the Boss Compass.
Where’s Forlorn armor? Only from killing Evil Forlorns in the Soul Sand Valley.

Quests/Quest-—-Mastering-Fate.title: Quest — Mastering Fate
Quests/Quest-—-Mastering-Fate.content:
Mastering Fate
A very small chapter centered on Fate Talents — the powerful capstone choices in the talent system. Its readable quest text in this install is sparse (essentially a single node referencing a “Knowing” essence), so the concrete detail below is drawn from the related systems note rather than invented quest steps. Treat this chapter as a pointer toward the deeper mechanic explained in Talent Tree & Fate Talents.

Note: this chapter’s quest text is too thin to build a full step-by-step walkthrough from. The framing below is general and flagged as such.

What this chapter is about

Fate Talents are the defining, build-shaping talents you fate (commit to) at higher levels — e.g. the archmage/element fates, Shadow Techniques, S’kellak’s Blessing, Warrior’s Devotion, A Bard’s Tale, and the Knowledge of Runes and Stars (Astral) fates referenced throughout the build guides in New Mechanics.
Choosing a Fate steers your class identity (Mage element, Rogue Haste, Tank endurance, etc.). Reset options use the same Knowledge Scroll system as the rest of the talent tree.

Tips

Because this chapter is content-light, use it as a signpost: the actual Fate choices and their effects are documented in Talent Tree & Fate Talents and applied per-build in New Mechanics.
Don’t fate blindly — your Fate should match the stat priorities of the build you’re playing (Archetypes & Builds).

Related

Talent Tree & Fate Talents · Archetypes & Builds · New Mechanics · Combat & Stats

Anticipated questions

What does this chapter actually contain? Very little readable quest text in this install — it’s a thin Fate-themed chapter. The mechanic itself is covered in Talent Tree & Fate Talents.
What is a Fate Talent? A high-tier, build-defining talent you commit to (Shadow Techniques, S’kellak’s Blessing, the element Archmage fates, etc.).
Can I change my Fate? Talents (including fates) are reset with a Knowledge Scroll, as with the rest of the tree.

Quests/Quest-—-Modern-Industrialization.title: Quest — Modern Industrialization
Quests/Quest-—-Modern-Industrialization.content:
Modern Industrialization
Modern Industrialization is the pack’s heavy multiblock tech tree, running from hand tools through steam power, electricity, and finally fusion. The single most important item is the MI Guidebook — the chapter repeatedly insists you read it when you’re lost. See Tech & Automation Mods for context.
Stage 1 — Hand & Steam

Forge Hammer (and Iron Hammer) — blacksmith-style tools that let you triple ores by hand.
Bronze Ingots → Bronze Compressor — build the compressor before the boiler to save many plates on hammering.
Bronze Boiler + Steam — burns fuel to heat water into steam (send it water or the fuel is wasted). Steam machines accept inputs from any side; lock slots to fix an item/fluid type. Bronze machines run recipes up to 2 EU/t (1 mB steam = 1 EU), so a max-temp boiler powers ~4 machines.
Core bronze machines: Macerator (recycle → dust), Mixer, Cutting Machine (uses lubricant), Furnace, Water Pump, plus Fluid/Item Pipes with hatches.
Coke Oven (steam-powered multiblock) → Coke fuel → Steam Blast Furnace → Steel. Always carry a Wrench to view multiblock shapes.

Stage 2 — Steel & first electricity

Steel Upgrade your bronze machines. Build a Steam Quarry (consumes bronze drills to dig below bedrock for ores) — expensive, but one of your best investments; run several SBFs first.
Move off steam: Steam Turbine (LV) turns steam into electricity; Analog Circuit → Electronic Circuit; Assembler + Robot Arm automate machine parts; Polarizer, Wiremill, Electric Blast Furnace (Cupronickel/Kanthal coils), Distillery.

Stage 3 — Chemistry & oil

Chemical Reactor, Distillation Tower (adjustable height via screwdriver), Vacuum Freezer (cool hot ingots like stainless steel back to normal), Electrolyzer, Centrifuge, Heat Exchanger, Pressurizer (water↔HP water, steam↔HP steam).
Oil Drilling Rig — a huge multiblock pulling Crude Oil from under bedrock. Electric Quarry replaces the steam version.
Upgrades: Turbo, Advanced Machine Hull (MV), Advanced/Highly Advanced Upgrades, Processing Unit (“computer brain”).

Stage 4 — Endgame

Stainless Steel → Titanium → Iridium materials; Implosion Compressor (uses Industrial TNT), Blastproof Alloy Plate, Quantum Circuit, Quantum Upgrade (the strongest machine upgrade).
Fusion Reactor — the ultimate power source, fusing Deuterium/Tritium/Helium-3 into Helium Plasma, feeding a Plasma Turbine (100s× diesel EU/t).
Nuclear Reactor — a deep neutron-physics multiblock (fast vs. thermal neutrons, heat management via hatches). It cannot explode or emit radiation and only damages the items inside it, so experiment freely — the guide recommends testing designs in creative first.
UU-Matter via Singularity + Electrolyzer (“the fabric of the universe”).

Notable rewards & tips

Steel Packer / Unpacker automate combining and breaking down machine parts.
Gravichestplate — powered chestplate granting creative flight + fall protection (no other defense).
Tools: Steam Mining Drill, then Diesel Drill/Chainsaw/Jetpack.
Break machines with a pickaxe, not the wrench (wrench is for rotate/config).

Links

Modern Industrialization · Tech & Automation Mods

Anticipated questions

Why is nothing happening in my boiler? No water — the boiler wastes fuel burning dry. Feed it water automatically with a Bronze Pump.
Bronze machine feels too slow. Bronze caps at 2 EU/t by design; upgrade to steel and then electric tiers.
Is the Nuclear Reactor dangerous to my base? No — it can’t explode or irradiate the world, only ruin the items inside if it overheats.
Do I need to understand fusion/nuclear math? No — the guidebook says to experiment with designs in creative until one works.

Quests/Quest-—-New-Mechanics.title: Quest — New Mechanics
Quests/Quest-—-New-Mechanics.content:
New Mechanics
The big tutorial and build-guide chapter (“How does Combat & Gearing Up work?”). It’s mostly reading — the chapter itself says to read carefully, because this is the information you need to understand combat and build your character. Although it’s an early-game tutorial, it extends all the way to end-game builds, and more quests appear as you progress. Treat it as the pack’s manual for Combat & Stats, Damage Types & Runes, and Archetypes & Builds.
Walkthrough
Changed combat & defense

New Combat Mechanics (Better Combat) — Each weapon has its own attack animation/time, consecutive attacks form combos, and you can hold the attack button to keep swinging.
New Defensive Mechanics (Shield Overhaul) — Shields gain new behavior; a shield bash while blocking stuns targets for 1 second (bosses are immune to the stun).

Understanding stats (read these in order)
The chapter explains stats as the numbers everything scales from. Grounded highlights:

Core Stats — used by everyone (e.g. Health by default, Haste/Armor from gear).
Physical Damage — main melee stat. Haste — physical attack speed (Rogue focus). Armor reduces physical damage, Toughness is the “anti one-shot” stat effective on big hits. Health = max damage before death; Stamina reduces passive Energy/hunger loss.
Powers by tier — Elemental (tertiary): Arcane, Fire, Frost (obtain each rune); Lightning for some artifacts/Valkyries. Primordial (secondary): Holy (Priests/Paladins), Soul (hybrids like Soulfire/Soulfrost). Decaying: Blood (Blood DK), Unholy (Unholy DK).
Hybrid stats — Lethality / Magic Penetration (same stat, ignore a % of Armor/Magic Protection), Astral Power (Arcane+Fire+Frost combined, used by Astral Mages/Spellblades), Physical↔Magic conversion stats, Ranged Damage & Draw Speed, Spell Critical & Spell Haste, Movement Speed.
Enchantments — craft an Enchanting Table; enchants heavily boost gear (full guide on the wiki). See Accessories & Enchanting.
Eternal Knowledge: Of Combat & Gear — completing the reading grants a “Piece of Eternal Knowledge.”

Build guides (tiered, Tier I → IV)
The chapter provides gear-direction guides per playstyle. They are guides on what to look for, not fully fleshed builds — check the wiki for complete builds. Difficulty reflects both play and crafting difficulty. Grounded starting points:

Protector / Tank — prioritize Max Health & Armor; Diamond → Netherite → Netherite-Diamond → Sapphire armor (+20 Max Health/piece, reflect passive). Fate: S’kellak’s Blessing. Artifacts: Vaazkar (tank), Fyr’alath (bruiser), Frostmourne (DK sustain).
Warrior — slow but hard-hitting burst melee; Titan’s Shroud (highest Physical Damage), Fate Warrior’s Devotion with the Thunderwrath artifact (or Hero’s Armor for Lightning Power).
Rogue (DPS) — Haste then Physical Damage; fast one-handed weapons to dual-wield. Assassin → Souldancer armor; Fate Shadow Techniques. Monk alt uses fist weapons (Fury of a Thousand Fists).
Mage — pick an element (Arcane burst / Fire high crit / Frost utility); Wizard Staff + Robes → Magus Set → Ekavar (great staff). Astral path via Runic Invocations and Knowledge of Runes and Stars fate.
Ranger — Ranged Damage (+ Draw Speed for fire rate); Ranger Armor, shortbows/rapid crossbows (DPS) or longbows/heavy crossbows (burst); Mutant Skeleton chestplate upgrade; artifact Orion.
Spellblade — hybrid Rogue+Mage; blade of chosen element + Techniques spellbook; artifacts A’zhar/Ash’edar/Frostmourne/Supernova.
Healer — Holy Power + Holy Book; some defense. Paladin path upgrades to the Apophis artifact (oath of Protection or Healing).
Bard — no fixed gear; requires the A Bard’s Tale fated talent and instruments (Immersive Melodies) to buff a party (/openpac-parties).
Death Knight — Runeblades give all three DK powers. Frost (DPS, Frozen Champion set), Unholy (burst/AoE, Plaguebringer set), Blood (tank, under the Protector path). Frostmourne is the standout DK artifact.
Mariums Guns (sidegrade) — Hunter Cannon (highest single-target), Blunderbuss (3 projectiles), Pistol (fast fire).

Tips

Read, don’t skim — the chapter literally gates “Eternal Knowledge” behind reading it.
These are direction guides. Combine with Archetypes & Builds and the wiki for full builds.

Related

Combat & Stats · Damage Types & Runes · Archetypes & Builds · Talent Tree & Fate Talents · Accessories & Enchanting · Core RPG & Combat Mods

Anticipated questions

What’s the difference between Armor and Toughness? Armor reduces physical damage flatly; Toughness scales its reduction on big hits — the “anti one-shot” stat.
What is Astral Power? The combination of Arcane + Fire + Frost, used by Astral Mages/Spellblades and books like Runic Invocations.
Lethality vs Magic Penetration? Same stat, different names — both ignore a percentage of the target’s Armor / Magic Protection.
Are these complete builds? No — they’re guides on what gear/stats to look for. Full builds live on rpg.prominence.wiki.

Quests/Quest-—-Planets-and-Space.title: Quest — Planets and Space
Quests/Quest-—-Planets-and-Space.content:
Planets & Space — The Astral Realm
The space-progression chapter, built on Ad Astra (+ Giselle addon) and tied tightly to tech mods. It’s a long-term parallel goal: build steel and machines, craft rockets tier by tier, and travel from the Moon out to other solar systems. Expect heavy overlap with Tech & Automation Mods — Ad Astra machines run on power from any tech mod. See also Dimensions & Space Travel Mods.
Walkthrough (roughly in order)

Materials base — Craft Steel Plates/Rods (used in nearly every recipe), Iron Plates/Rods, and Gas Tanks. Obtain Steel by smelting Iron in a Blast Furnace; compress iron/steel via the Tech Reborn Compressor (overclockable).
Power — Start with a Coal Generator. Ad Astra machines accept power from any mod; the chapter recommends Tech Reborn Glass Fiber Cables.
Life support — Build an Oxygen Loader to fill Oxygen Tanks/Cans (craft 5 and fill them), and craft a Space Suit (later upgradeable with Jet Propulsion). Make a couple of Fans.
Fuel — Find an Oil Well, build a Fuel Refinery, and add a Fuel Loader to load rockets automatically. Later, the Cryo Freezer makes Cryo Fuel (far more efficient — one bucket launches a rocket).
Rockets (Nasa Workbench) — All rockets share the same recipe layout; only the material tier changes. Each needs 4 Fins and a Steel Engine (built from Engine Frames).

Tier 1 → the Moon / low orbit (Space Stations).
Tier 2 → Mars (needs Desh, found only on the Moon).
Tier 3 → Mercury and Venus (needs Ostrum).
Tier 4 → other solar systems / Glacio (needs Calorite).


The Moon — Visit it; kill Star Crawlers and Corrupted Lunarians (pick them off from range), find Cheese, Lunar Towers, Lunarian Villages, and Moon Dungeons. Mine Desh.
Mars — Ice Caps (“water on Mars?”), Canyon Creek, Martian Raptors, and the Mars Temple. Mine Ostrum.
Mercury & Venus — Venus holds riches; Mercury is mostly uneventful (kill Magma Cubes). Mine Calorite.
Glacio (Tier 4 system) — Kill Pygros, Moglers, and Glacian Rams (milk them), collect Ice Shards; visit Pygro Towers/Villages. Unique sun.
Space Stations — Buildable in any orbit; bring enough Steel / Ostrum / Desh (amount varies by planet). Water freezes there. A Zip Gun (fill with oxygen) propels you in low-gravity orbit.
Infinite oxygen setup — Oxygen Distributor kept running by a Water Pump over an infinite water source, both supplied with power.
Shortcut quest — You can also just craft a Waystone (“No rockets needed!”) for return travel, and craft a Flag to plant on the Moon.

Tips

This chapter is really a tech chapter — get Steel, power, and the Tech Reborn compressor going before chasing rockets.
Each rocket tier is gated by a planet-specific metal: Desh (Moon) → Ostrum (Mars) → Calorite (Venus/Mercury). Plan mining trips accordingly.
Cryo Fuel dramatically cuts fuel needs — build the Cryo Freezer once you can.
Bring a Waystone to any planet/station so you can hop home without a return launch.

Related

Dimensions & Space Travel Mods · Tech & Automation Mods · Creatures, Bosses & Mobs · Quality-of-Life & UI Mods

Anticipated questions

Do Ad Astra machines need Ad Astra power? No — they run on power from any tech mod; Tech Reborn Glass Fiber Cables are recommended.
What gates each rocket tier? Planet-specific metals: Desh (Moon) for Tier 2, Ostrum (Mars) for Tier 3, Calorite for Tier 4.
How do I breathe off-world? Space Suit + filled Oxygen Cans/Tanks (via an Oxygen Loader), or an Oxygen Distributor + Water Pump for a permanent base supply.
Easiest way home? Craft a Waystone and bring it with you — no return rocket needed.

Quests/Quest-—-Powah.title: Quest — Powah
Quests/Quest-—-Powah.content:
Powah!
Powah! is the pack’s accessible energy mod: generators, batteries, and cables that wire into whichever tech tree you’re actually playing (see Tech & Automation Mods). This chapter takes you from crafting the basic electric parts up through the six machinery tiers and the various generators. There’s an in-game book that explains the mod if you get stuck.
Walkthrough

Basic parts — Craft Dielectric Paste (the “glue” for electric parts), Dielectric Rods, and the Wrench (rotate machines, configure cables, link rods to Energizing Orbs).
Secondary parts — Capacitors (combine two for a large one, or cut one into two tiny ones), Thermo Plates, and Dielectric Casing — the last is in every machine recipe and upgrade (“heart of the machine”).
Energizing setup — Energizing Rods energize items held in an Energizing Orb; higher-tier materials need more power. This is Powah’s core crafting mechanic.
Tiers — Machinery upgrades through six tiers via higher-tier capacitors: Basic → Hardened → Blazing → Niotic → Spirited → Nitro (final).

Generators

Furnator — burns fuel (coal/wood); higher tier = more power + efficiency.
Thermo Generator — heat source below, water to cool; higher tier = more power.
Magmator — runs on lava.
Solar Panel — daytime power; needs a Photoelectric Pane, and a Lens of Ender lets it absorb sunlight through blocks.
Reactor — built from Uraninite (needs 36 blocks to form); cooled by water or Dry Ice; the most involved generator.

Storage & transfer

Energy Cells — bulk batteries that buffer and transfer power.
Ender Cells — wireless energy transfer between cells sharing a channel number (each needs an Energy Cell inside).
Energy Hoppers charge items in a chest without an Energizing Orb; Energy Dischargers drain charged machinery and redirect via cables.

Notable rewards & tips

Player Transmitter — charges items in your inventory/armor/trinkets (“walking battery”).
Binding Cards link a Player Transmitter to machinery for wireless charging (same dimension); the cross-dimension version requires using a binding card on an Enderman first.
The Player Aerial Pearl is made by using an Aerial Pearl on a Zombie/Husk.
Fun extra: Charged Snowballs cause a lightning strike on impact.

Links

Powah! · Tech & Automation Mods
Pairs well with Create (via Crafts & Additions) and any machine tree needing Forge Energy.

Anticipated questions

Which tech tree does Powah work with? All of them — it’s a generic energy provider, meant to power Create, Tech Reborn, Modern Industrialization, etc.
Fastest reliable power? A Reactor for scale, or Solar/Thermo/Furnator for simpler setups; upgrade tiers with capacitors as you go.
How do I charge my armor/trinkets on the move? A Player Transmitter + Binding Card wirelessly charges your worn gear.

Quests/Quest-—-Reforging.title: Quest — Reforging
Quests/Quest-—-Reforging.content:
Reforging
This chapter teaches reforging — changing an item’s rarity/quality, a core progression loop. The system note Gear Rarity & Reforging covers the same mechanic in the vault; this guide follows the quest chapter specifically. See also Artifact Reforging for artifact-tier weapons.
What is reforging?
Tools, armor, and weapons have a quality (rarity). Reforging changes it. Do it in the Reforging tab of an Anvil, which has three slots:

Left — Base Material: tied to the item itself (e.g. a Holy Wand needs a Gold Ingot). Hover the reforge button after placing your item to see what it requires.
Middle — Base Item: the item to reforge. Only tools, weapons, and armor are reforgeable.
Right — Reforge Material: determines the quality range you can roll (three tiers below).

Reforge Material tiers





























TierMaterialWhere / howQuality rangeT1Limestone ChunkOverworld — craft from 4× Limestone Blocks (→4) or 4× Diorite Block (→4)up to EpicT2Pyrite ChunkNether — craft from 4× Pyrite Dust (→1, dust from Pyrite Ore) or smelt Ancient Debris (→4)up to LegendaryT3Galena ChunkEnd — craft from 2× Galena Dust + 2× Popped Chorus Fruit (→1); End Stone can substitute for the dust. Galena Dust is found in deep Overworld cavesup to Mythic
Increasing your chances
It’s not all grinding — Luck improves your odds at higher qualities. Stack passive luck items, luck potions, luck trinkets, wine, etc.
The long grind

Become a Mythic Blacksmith — reforge 100 Mythic items (“Eternal Challenge”) to earn the “Piece of Eternal Knowledge” reward (Eternal Knowledge: Of Blacksmithing).

Links

Gear Rarity & Reforging · Artifact Reforging
Rarity system runs on Zenith Renewed / Tierify — see Core RPG & Combat Mods.

Anticipated questions

What can I reforge? Only tools, weapons, and armor.
What decides the quality I get? The Reforge Material tier (Limestone → Pyrite → Galena). The Base Material (left slot) is a per-item ingredient, not the quality driver.
How do I hit Mythic? Use Galena Chunk (T3) and stack Luck to improve the roll.
Practical order? Limestone early, Pyrite mid-game, save Galena for pushing your best gear to Mythic.

Quests/Quest-—-Simply-Swords.title: Quest — Simply Swords
Quests/Quest-—-Simply-Swords.content:
Simply Swords
Simply Swords adds 15+ weapon types plus a Runic Powers system (powers slotted into weapon sockets) and a large roster of Unique weapons. This chapter is mostly about discovering uniques and learning the socket/runic workflow. See Core RPG & Combat Mods.
Runic Powers workflow

Sockets — Uniques and runic gear have sockets that hold Runic Powers.
Empowered Remnant — created by melting down a unique weapon. It’s the key ingredient for the two runic gems (flagged in-quest as “a pain to make”).
Runefused Gem — combine a Runic Tablet + an Empowered Remnant in a Smithing Table, then click to identify the power you rolled.
Netherfused Gem — combine an Empowered Remnant + a Netherite Ingot in a Smithing Table.
Runic Gear — to make socketed runic gear you need a Runic Tablet + a Netherite weapon; also keep a Contained Remnant on you while exploring.

Collecting Uniques
Unique weapons drop from strong enemies. The chapter’s “old book” gives approximate drop chances:

































SourceChanceObsidilith40%Ender Dragon35%Night Lich30%Nether Gauntlet25%Conjunctivius15%Decaying King15%
The Wither and the Ender Dragon are specifically called out as possible sources, and other strong enemies may still carry one.
Notable weapons & rewards

Relic tiers — the questline funnels toward powerful relics: Dormant → Righteous / Tainted, plus Sunfire (pure light), Harbinger (death), and the Brimstone Claymore (“to slay a Dragon”).
Lichblade line — a multi-stage weapon: Slumbering Lichblade → Waking Lichblade → Awakened Lichblade (fed by kills until it reaches full potential). The Awakened Lichblade is a component for the Frostmourne artifact.
Molten Edge — a lava blade used to forge artifact weapons in the Artifact Reforging chapter.
Dozens of flavor-rich uniques (Storm’s Edge, Stormbringer, Soulrender, Soulpyre, Frostfall, Mjolnir, Thunderbrand, Caelestis, etc.), each with distinct abilities — check tooltips/EMI for exact stats.

Links

Simply Swords · Simply Swords Battle Standard Tweaks · Core RPG & Combat Mods
Feeds artifacts in Artifact Reforging; see also Gear Rarity & Reforging.

Anticipated questions

How do I get my first Unique? Kill strong bosses — Obsidilith (40%) and the Ender Dragon (35%) are the best odds. You may already have one from a boss you’ve fought.
What do sockets do? They hold Runic Powers rolled via Runefused/Netherfused Gems for extra weapon effects.
Why melt a unique? To get an Empowered Remnant, the base for both runic gems.
How do I “wake” the Lichblade? Keep killing with it — it progresses Slumbering → Waking → Awakened toward full potential.

Quests/Quest-—-Spell-Books.title: Quest — Spell Books
Quests/Quest-—-Spell-Books.content:
Spell Books
This chapter explains the pack’s spellbook system (built on Spell Engine and the RPG class mods) — how to craft your first books and what every class book does. See Magic & Spells Mods, Accessories & Enchanting, and Archetypes & Builds for how books map to builds.
The Spell Binding Table

The Spell Binding Table creates Tier I spellbooks and attaches spells to books of any tier.
Surround it with Bookshelves like an Enchanting Table — you need 18 bookshelves to unlock all four spells.
Tiers ≠ power. A book’s tier reflects how it’s obtained and its complexity to master, not raw strength. The “difficulty” tag (Easy/Medium/Hard) is about mastery.

Books by tier
Tier I (Easy) — craftable starters:

Warrior’s Codex — bruiser/protector, physical damage (“A Berserking Path”).
Rogue Handbook — stacking damage, teleports, stuns, stealth (“Lethal Shadows”).
Archery Manual — passive shot buffs, crowd control, rapidfire (“The Bullseye”).
Holy Book — healing (“A Holy Healer”).
Elemental Tomes of Arcane / Frost / Fire — ranged casting: Arcane = high crit damage, Frost = quick constant damage + control, Fire = strong hits + high crit chance.

Tier II:

Paladin Libram / Oath of Defiance / Oath of Vengeance (Tank hybrids of Warrior + Priest/Monk) — “A Holy Warrior.”
Death Knight tomes (three): Eternal Winter (Frost, multi-target DPS), Unholy Teachings (single-target DPS, pairs with the Decaying Devotion fate talent), Vampiric Knowledge (Blood, self-sustain tank).
Spellblade Technique books (Frost/Fire/Arcane Battlemage) — melee elemental spells (“The Spellblades,” Tier II Easy).

Tier III:

Astral Magic — combines Arcane, Fire, and Frost; 39 possible spells with an element-shifting ultimate. The hardest book.
The Three Hunters archery books: Mintaka’s Fright (frost/stuns), Alnilam’s Sight (fast rogue archer), Alnitak’s Might (fire/burning/explosions).
Magister’s Knowledge — evolved technique books: Echoes Unleashed (Arcane), Deathchill Tome (Frost), Phoenix Rites (Fire).

Tips

Match your book to your fate talents — e.g. Unholy Death Knight pairs with Decaying Devotion.
Higher tiers aren’t upgrades of lower ones; pick by the element/role you want, not the number.

Links

Spell Engine · Death Knights · Spellblade Next · Archers Expansion
Magic & Spells Mods · Archetypes & Builds · Accessories & Enchanting

Anticipated questions

Is a higher-tier book stronger? No — tier is about how you get it and mastery difficulty, not power.
How do I unlock all spells at the table? Surround the Spell Binding Table with 18 bookshelves.
Which book for a tank? Warrior’s Codex early; Paladin/Oath books (T2) or the Blood Death Knight tome for sustain.
Alternative trophy spellbooks? Yes — the Trophy Collection chapter offers alternate archer/spellblade books, but they aren’t stronger just for being trophy-made.

Quests/Quest-—-Tech-Reborn.title: Quest — Tech Reborn
Quests/Quest-—-Tech-Reborn.content:
Tech Reborn
Tech Reborn is a complete, self-contained classic tech tree (power generation, power storage, bulk item storage, tools, and making materials from energy + scrap). See Tech & Automation Mods for how it sits alongside the pack’s other tech mods. Note: Prominence is migrating Industrial Revolution players onto Tech Reborn (see the Industrial Revolution chapter), so this is the recommended “greener pasture” of the older tech trees.
Early game — basic components

Rubber — right-click a Tree Tap on the orange spots of a rubber tree to extract sap, then smelt into rubber. Later, combine a Treetap + Drain next to a rubber tree to fully automate sap collection into an inventory below.
Refined Iron — the foundation for advanced devices and circuits.
Build the Electric Furnace, Alloy Smelter, Compressor (raw materials under pressure), Recycler (any item → scrap via energy), Wire Mill, and Extractor (efficient rubber use).

Mid game — the Industrial machines

Industrial Centrifuge — the workhorse: extracts many new resources (tungsten from lava/endstone dust, nickel from raw iron/gold/copper ore, lazurite from lapis, and more).
Industrial Blast Furnace — needs cooling; leads into steel/tungsten alloys.
Industrial Grinder — higher ore yields, especially using Mercury instead of water.
Scrap Boxes — craft from 9 scrap for a random loot box; the Scrapboxinator auto-opens them at 32 E/t.
Chemical Reactor, Assembler (cheaper alternate circuit crafts), Vacuum Freezer, Electrolyzer.
Add Overclocker Upgrades (−25% time each), Energy Storage Upgrades, and (optionally) Muffler Upgrades.

Power generation
Many options, scaling up: Solid Fuel Generator, Thermal/Lava Generator (16 E/t), Solar Panels (basic 0–3 E/t up to advanced 32–512 E/t), Semi-Fluid Generator (diesel/nitro diesel, 20 E/t), Water/Wind Mills, Gas Generator (methane/hydrogen, 16 E/t), a Lightning Rod (262 kE per bolt — stack iron fences on top for more strikes), and the endgame Fusion Reactor (16 kE/t) fed by Deuterium/Tritium/Helium-3.
Endgame — UU-Matter
UU-Matter (30 kE + 30 scrap each) can be pattern-replicated into almost any material. Feeds into Iridium, Lapotron Crystals, Data Orbs, and the fusion loop.
Notable rewards & tips

Wrench — instantly break machines (shift+right-click) and rotate them (right-click).
Electric tools — Drill, Chainsaw, Jackhammer, and the Omni-Tool (pick/axe/shovel/sword in one); upgraded versions add 3×3 mining and full-tree felling.
Interdimensional SU — an “ender chest for energy”: all of them share one storage pool across dimensions.
Transformers are cosmetic now — unlike old Minecraft versions, machines/cables no longer explode from a too-high power tier. Transformers only restrict energy flow.

Machine configuration
Click the wrench icon on the left of any supporting machine’s UI, pick a slot, then a side, to cycle input/output/disabled, with auto-input/output checkboxes to push/pull from adjacent inventories.
Links

Tech Reborn · Tech & Automation Mods
Migration target for Industrial Revolution users.

Anticipated questions

Do cables/machines explode from too much power? No — that was old (1.12) behavior. Transformers now only limit flow.
Fastest early power? Solid Fuel or Thermal Generator; scale to Solar/Diesel and eventually Fusion.
What’s scrap good for? Scrap Boxes (random loot) and UU-Matter production.

Quests/Quest-—-The-Art-of-Transmogrifica.title: Quest — The Art of Transmogrification
Quests/Quest-—-The-Art-of-Transmogrifica.content:
The Art of Transmogrification
A short cosmetic chapter covering transmogrification — magic that changes the shape of any item (weapons and armor included) without altering its function. It’s purely cosmetic and gives no stat benefit. See Accessories & Enchanting.
Walkthrough

The Art of Transmogrification — Craft a Transmogrification Table. This magic is powered by Amethyst, so you’ll need some each time you transform an item.
Transmog an item — No items are consumed, but to change an item’s appearance into another you must own the desired item (the one whose look you’re copying).
The Illusion of Nothing — To hide an armor piece or weapon entirely, use a Void Fragment as the transmoggable material.

Tips

Because nothing is consumed, you can freely restyle gear as your look changes — just keep some Amethyst on hand.
Great for keeping a favorite endgame weapon’s stats while showing off a rarer skin (or hiding a slot completely).

Links

Transmog · Accessories & Enchanting
Pairs with trim/appearance mods in Building & Decoration Mods and armor-trim tooling elsewhere.

Anticipated questions

Does transmog change my stats? No — it’s purely cosmetic, no benefit beyond appearance.
What powers it? Amethyst, consumed each time you transform.
Do I lose the item I want to look like? No — you just need to own the desired item; nothing is consumed.
Can I hide a piece entirely? Yes — transmog it using a Void Fragment.

Quests/Quest-—-The-Bumblezone.title: Quest — The Bumblezone
Quests/Quest-—-The-Bumblezone.content:
The Bumblezone
A dimension chapter for The Bumblezone — a self-contained world of bees and honey. It’s a large, exploration-and-collection chapter (find dozens of structures, gear, and essences) rather than a boss gauntlet, and it culminates in earning the favor of the Queen Bee. Mostly optional side content, though its enchanting garden is genuine end-game utility. See Dimensions & Space Travel Mods and Creatures, Bosses & Mobs.
Walkthrough (highlights, in rough order)

World of Bee and Honey — Go to the Bumblezone (the entry quest).
Hive’s Air Pollen-tion — The air is full of pollen; introduces Pollen Puff, Honey Bucket, Bee Bread, Honeycomb Brood.
Bee Weaponry — Craft bee gear from stingers/honey: Stinger Spear, Crystal Cannon, Honey Crystal Shield.
The Bee Armor — Full set (helmet/chestplate/leggings/boots); nice-looking, not very powerful.
Honey Compass & Sempiternal Sanctums — A Honey Compass leads to important sites. Find the six colored Sempiternal Sanctums (Blue, Green, Purple, Red, White, Yellow), each tied to an Essence (Calming, Life, Knowing, Raging, Continuity, Radiance).
Structure hunt — A long list of “Find” quests: Cell Maze, Stinger Spear Shrine, Subway, Queen Bee’s Throne (Throne Pillar), Pollinated Stream, Honitel (honey hotel), Slime Ranch, Pirate Ship, Overgrown Flower, Ice Monolith, Candle Parkour, Bee House, Ancient Hoops, Dance Floor, Hive Temple, Honey Fountain, Cannon Range, Honey Cave Room, Battle Cubes, Ancient Shrine, Cherry Veteran Tree.
One of Us! One of Us! — Meet the Queen Bee at her Throne, trade/do tasks, and earn Essence of the Bees so the bees stop attacking you. (“Now you are one of her kin.“)
The Crystalline Flower (Lv 65) — Endgame enchanting: place a Crystalline Flower on Glistering Honey Crystals in the Hanging Gardens, offer items to grow it, and choose specific enchantments to put into a book. Requires Level 65 to use. See Accessories & Enchanting.
Music discs — A big set of bee-themed discs to collect (“Bee Jams”).

Tips

Grab the Honey Compass early — most of the structure and Sanctum finds key off it.
The real reason to come here late is the Crystalline Flower (Lv 65): targeted, chosen enchantments are extremely valuable — but you can’t use it until level 65.
Earning the Queen’s favor (Essence of the Bees) stops bee aggression, making everything else far easier.

Related

Dimensions & Space Travel Mods · Accessories & Enchanting · Creatures, Bosses & Mobs · Progression & Level Caps

Anticipated questions

Why are the bees attacking me? Until you earn the Queen Bee’s favor (Essence of the Bees) via her Throne, they’re hostile.
What’s the main endgame reward here? The Crystalline Flower in the Hanging Gardens — it lets you pick specific enchantments into a book, but requires Level 65.
How do I navigate this dimension? Use the Honey Compass; it points to the Sanctums and key structures.

Quests/Quest-—-The-Nether.title: Quest — The Nether
Quests/Quest-—-The-Nether.content:
The Nether
A dimension chapter that reworks the Nether via Better Nether and adds new bosses, structures, and ores. You tackle it in parallel with the mid-game Void’s Invasion bosses (the Nether Gauntlet, Blackstone Golem, and Decaying King all live here). It also feeds later progression: Pyrite for reforging, plus materials for tech and Death Knight builds. Structures and mobs here are from Dimensions & Space Travel Mods and Exploration, Dungeons & Structures Mods.
Walkthrough

Enter the Nether — The entry quest.
Lesser bosses / mobs — Kill a Blaze Guardian (near Blaze spawners in fortresses / Nether Wastes), a Necromancer (fortresses), Withered Demons (Crimson Forest — smelt their hearts into Demonite Chunks to re-summon the Decaying King), and the Soul Reaper (Soul Sand Valley, rides The Nightmare).
The Blackstone Golem’s Ritual — Build a 9×9 vanilla Blackstone platform; the Polished Blackstone holders sit one block out from each side, on the same level as the platform. Collect 4 Gilded Blackstone Shards (Piglin Brutes in Bastions are a good source) and place one on each holder to summon it. (This is also a Main Story herald.)
The Decaying King — Spawns in the remnants of the Decaying Kingdom (any Nether biome). Use a Moonstone Compass to locate it. Drops the Darkin Blade, a Lord Soul, and the Withered Demon Heart. Can alternatively be summoned via Demon Chunks on a Moonstone Altar.
Nether Gauntlet — Explore near lava level to find the Gauntlet Arena; shatter its eye. (Main Story herald, Rec. Lv 15.)
Structures to visit — Nether City (in lava lakes; Netherite blocks in chests/drawers — very dangerous), Black Spiral (many Piglins and loot; dig down into the towers), Nether Fortress, Bastion Remnant, Ghast Hive, the Citadel, Nether Pyramid, Wither Tomb, and the Nether Jungle. A “visit all biomes” quest (“A very hot Vacation”) caps the tour.
Mob-kill quests — Piglins, Piglin Brutes, Wither Skeletons, Blazes, plus Bone Llamas / Naga as flavor.
Ores — Pyrite (essential for reforging items up tiers — mine lots), Cinnabar (for engineers/network designers), Lapis (limited here), Nether Ruby (nostalgic warm-to-the-touch material), Sphalerite (zinc + sulfur), Cincinnasite (iron-like with special uses), plus Ruby/Sapphire gems (Sapphire is the tank’s friend — reflect aura).
Blood Trinkets — Found in Bastion Remnants; vital for Blood/tank Death Knights (see New Mechanics).
Endgame tech quests — “Tap the Mantle” for an infinite Lava source, and moving lava to the Overworld via an AE2 Quantum Ring + Hose Pulley + Storage Bus setup (see Tech & Automation Mods).

Tips

Don’t hand-mine for Netherite for hours — the chapter explicitly says to loot Nether Cities and Black Spirals, or use tech (Tech Reborn compressor overclocks, UU Matter) for near-infinite Netherite.
Farm Pyrite heavily; you’ll want it constantly for reforging.
Bastion Piglin Brutes are your reliable source of Gilded Blackstone Shards for the Golem ritual.

Related

Void’s Invasion · Dimensions & Space Travel Mods · Exploration, Dungeons & Structures Mods · Gear Rarity & Reforging · Tech & Automation Mods · Creatures, Bosses & Mobs

Anticipated questions

Best way to get Netherite? Loot Nether Cities and Black Spirals, or use tech multiplication — not hours of hand-mining.
What’s Pyrite for? Reforging items to higher tiers; mine as much as you can.
How do I summon the Blackstone Golem? 9×9 Blackstone platform, Polished Blackstone holders one block out per side, a Gilded Blackstone Shard on each (4 total).
How do I re-fight the Decaying King? Kill Withered Demons, smelt hearts into Demonite/Demon Chunks, and use one on a Moonstone Altar (or find the Decaying Kingdom via Moonstone Compass).

Quests/Quest-—-The-Prison.title: Quest — The Prison
Quests/Quest-—-The-Prison.content:
The Prison
A dimension chapter built on the Mine Cells mod (Dead Cells crossover). You enter a randomly-spawning Prison dungeon, fight the giant eye Conjunctivius, and unlock the Cell Crafter weapon system. Conjunctivius doubles as a Void’s Invasion herald (Rec. Lv 30), so this chapter pairs naturally with the mid-game campaign. See Exploration, Dungeons & Structures Mods and Creatures, Bosses & Mobs.
Walkthrough

Enter the Prison — The entrance spawns randomly throughout the Overworld; find it to enter the Prison dimension.
Defeat Conjunctivius — Spawns in The Lair, found underground within the Prison. To damage it you must first kill its tentacles. (For the Main Story version you first need a Vine Rune from the Promenade — see Void’s Invasion.)
Visit the Promenade — Take the elevator on the last floor of the Prison to reach the Promenade of the Condemned. Bring a Waystone or Pocket Wormhole so you can get home.
Cell Crafter system:

Craft a Cell Crafter — Makes various melee and ranged weapons for the Mine Cells armory.
Loot a Monster Cell — Drops from monsters in the Prison dimension; needed as crafting material.
Craft Cell-Infused Steel — Some Cell Crafter weapons require it.


Quick Healing! (Health Flask) — Cell-crafted from Guts + Monster Cells; heals 10% of max health and grants regeneration for a few seconds — a very useful sustain item.

Tips

Bring fast travel back (Waystone / Pocket Wormhole) before going deep — the Promenade is far from home.
Against Conjunctivius, focus the tentacles first; the body takes no damage until they’re gone.
The Health Flask is worth prioritizing early in the chapter for its cheap, repeatable healing.

Related

Void’s Invasion · Exploration, Dungeons & Structures Mods · Creatures, Bosses & Mobs · Quality-of-Life & UI Mods

Anticipated questions

Where’s the Prison entrance? It spawns randomly around the Overworld — you have to find it.
Why can’t I hurt Conjunctivius? Kill its tentacles first; only then can you damage the eye.
What’s the Cell Crafter for? Making Mine Cells melee/ranged weapons (and the Health Flask) using Monster Cells, Guts, and Cell-Infused Steel.
How do I leave the Promenade? Bring a Waystone or Pocket Wormhole in with you — it’s suggested before you take the elevator.

Quests/Quest-—-The-Scarred-Night.title: Quest — The Scarred Night
Quests/Quest-—-The-Scarred-Night.content:
The Scarred Night
A seasonal Halloween event chapter (available roughly October 20 – mid-November). Framed as “The Crows’ Guide to Destroy the Scarecrows,” it’s a short, story-driven questline that teaches pumpkin-carving mechanics and ends with a boss, Sir Scar Crow — plus a Mythic version for endgame players. See Creatures, Bosses & Mobs.
Walkthrough (Crow’s Guide, page by page)

I feel something in the air… — Play during the Halloween event window to start.
Getting ready to Carve (Page 1) — Get a Pumpkin.
The Tools (Page 2) — Get Shears, then place the pumpkin and use shears on it to carve it.
Carving! / Lights up! (Pages 3–4) — Combine your carved pumpkin with a torch to make a Jack o’ Lantern (light is what brings scarecrows to life).
What We Know (Page 5) — Lore on the leader: it has a metal hook on its left arm; you’ll need to try different face carvings until the right one works.
Work Ain’t Easy (Page 6) — Make a Botanist Workbench to re-cut Jack o’ Lanterns into better designs.
Fancy Carving (Page 7) — Carve a fancy design at the workbench.
Summoning the Bastard (Page 8) — Build the specified structure and try carved Jack o’ Lanterns on it until the leader appears.
Sir Scar Crow (boss) — A cowardly ranged boss that flees and attacks from distance while summoning undead. Defeating him rewards his weapon, The Scarred Night (stolen back from him by the Crows).
Sir Scar Crow (Mythic) — Endgame version. Requires finishing the Void’s Invasion campaign and unlocking Mythic Bosses. Same limited seasonal window. Has a 20% chance to drop the “Pumpmourne” appearance.

Tips

This chapter is time-limited — only playable during the Halloween event window each year.
Expect trial and error on the carving face; that’s intended per the guide (“try all carvings until it works”).
Come back for the Mythic fight only after clearing Void’s Invasion and unlocking Mythic Bosses.

Related

Creatures, Bosses & Mobs · Void’s Invasion · Building & Decoration Mods

Anticipated questions

Why can’t I access this chapter? It’s a seasonal Halloween event (roughly Oct 20 – mid-Nov); outside that window it’s unavailable.
How do I summon Sir Scar Crow? Build the guide’s structure and place carved Jack o’ Lanterns on it, trying different carvings until he appears.
What’s the reward? His weapon, The Scarred Night; the Mythic version can also drop the “Pumpmourne” appearance (20%).
What does the Mythic version require? Finishing Void’s Invasion and unlocking Mythic Bosses, during the event window.

Quests/Quest-—-To-The-End.title: Quest — To The End
Quests/Quest-—-To-The-End.content:
To The End
The dimension chapter for the End, heavily expanded by Better End and Eldritch End. Reaching it is a mini-quest of its own — vanilla eyes of ender don’t work here. Once inside, it’s a huge exploration checklist of biomes, structures, ores, and mobs, plus the Obsidilith boss (also a Void’s Invasion herald). Many of the Void campaign’s late dimensions (Primordial Abyss, Hasturian Wastes) are reached from here. Content is from Dimensions & Space Travel Mods and Exploration, Dungeons & Structures Mods.
Walkthrough

Getting to the End / Entering The End — You need 12 (at most) of the 16 unique eyes — normal Eyes of Ender do not work. Specific eyes are found in structures or traded for at the chapter’s Eye Trading node (no guarantee of the one you want; trades restock after a day). Enter the portal with twelve unique eyes.
