Free the End! (Obsidilith / the Dragon) — “Kill the Dragon and free the End of its reign.” Obsidilith (creature of rock and hate) is summoned at its Arena via an Obsidian Heart. (The corrupted Ender Dragon “Jean” is fought via Main Story.)
Biome tour — Long list of “Visit” quests: Blossoming/Blossoming Spires, Hasturian Wastes, Dark Amaranth Forests, Shadow Forest (bring light; kill Shadow Walkers), Umbrella Jungle, Primordial Abyss (aberration heart region), Crystal Mountains (Aurora Crystals), Chorus Forest (farm Chorus for Galena), Ice Starfield (Ancient Emerald Ice), Amber Lands, Sulphur Springs, Lantern Woods, End Highlands, Glowing Grasslands, Megalake Grove, Umbra Valley, Painted Mountains, and more.
Structures — End City (top priority — best loot), End Gate Fortress, Shipwrecks (End-City-tier loot), End Village (ender pearls, smithing templates, ingots), Eternal Portal (restore it with six Eternal Crystals placed on surrounding pedestals to earn the Eternal Light), Heavenly Rider / Heavenly Challenger, Mega Ship, Phantom Citadel.
Mob quests — End Slimes, Aberrations (stack corruption), Dendlers, Endermen (→ Mutant Enderman), Shulkers, Phantoms.
Materials to collect — Galena Chunks (highest chance of a Mythic roll when reforging — you’ll want a ton; see Gear Rarity & Reforging), Chorus Fruit, Purpur, Aurora Crystals, Tenanea / Helix / Lucernia / Umbrella / Dark Amaranth woods, Umbralith, Lumecorn, Ancient Emerald Ice.
Rewards & gear — Tier 4 Trinkets (kill a Shulker / get any Tier IV trinket), End’s Delights cooking (knife-kill End mobs for powerful foods), Icarus Wings (Elytra-like, go in the cape slot, no durability/fireworks; Nether Star variant costs no hunger — best with no armor), and the Explorer’s Compass (costs Trophies but makes finding structures trivial).

Tips

Stockpile Galena in the Chorus/Chorus Forest areas — it’s the top reforging material for pushing gear to Mythic.
Make End Cities your first priority for gear and templates.
Buy the Explorer’s Compass early in the chapter; it saves hours of hunting the biomes/structures above.
In the Shadow Forest, bring light — something follows you there.

Related

Void’s Invasion · Dimensions & Space Travel Mods · Exploration, Dungeons & Structures Mods · Gear Rarity & Reforging · Accessories & Enchanting · Creatures, Bosses & Mobs

Anticipated questions

Why won’t my eyes of ender open the portal? You need the 12 unique eyes (of 16), found in structures or traded at the Eye Trading node — normal eyes don’t count.
What’s Galena for? It has the highest chance of a Mythic reforge roll — farm it in the Chorus Forest.
What should I look for first in the End? End Cities (best loot) and an Explorer’s Compass to speed up everything else.
Are Icarus Wings better than an Elytra? They have no durability, use the cape slot, and don’t need fireworks — but more armor weighs them down; the Nether Star version also costs no hunger.

Quests/Quest-—-Trophy-Collection.title: Quest — Trophy Collection
Quests/Quest-—-Trophy-Collection.content:
Trophy Collection
The Cinderstone Trophies chapter — a reward-spending chapter rather than a progression one. Trophies “can be obtained from completing Quests in the storyline,” and this chapter is where you cash them in: if you’re reading the first quest, “you have gotten your first one already.” Trophies buy powerful utility items — building wands, exploration compasses, a Pocket Wormhole, and alternate spellbooks — so this chapter is really a shopping list with strong advice about when each purchase is worth it. See FTB Quests and Quality-of-Life & UI Mods.
Walkthrough

Earn Trophies. Trophies come from completing storyline quests, so this chapter fills up naturally as you work through the main progression — you don’t farm them directly.
Building Wands. Spend Trophies on a Stone Wand — “largely a utility item used to only place blocks. It cannot break blocks,” good for filling large holes or building “massive walls.” A second, larger-area wand covers the same job over a bigger region.
Exploration tools. The chapter strongly recommends these:

Explorer’s Compass — flagged as “the best item to make with Trophies,” giving “a lot of utility” and saving “hours of searching.” Massively recommended as soon as you can craft it.
Nature’s Compass — a biome finder (“offers many opportunities”); highly recommended, but noted as best crafted after the End, since you can find most biomes via the Explorer’s Compass and structure knowledge until then.
Pocket Wormhole — “expensive yet useful.” The quest advises not crafting it until you have at least the Explorer’s Compass, one Spell Book, Nature’s Compass, and it warns it’s best made after the End so you don’t miss out on useful early items by relying on it too soon.


Higher Tier Spellbooks. These are Trophy-made alternatives to the spellbooks you’d normally build at the Spell Binding Table — and the quest is explicit that “they aren’t better just because you made them with a Trophy.” Options include:

A do-it-all master book that “has it all” and “scales with Arcane, Fire and Ice depending on the Spell combination” (so flexible you’d “almost need a spreadsheet”).
Archer books — a Fire/explosions archer (“Explosions Explosions Explosions!”), a fast-shooting archer (“shoot like a gun… gone before you know it”), and a Frost archer with a freeze-stack passive and heavy slowing.
Frost- and Fire-scaling books (“as graceful as a Phoenix… scales with Fire Spell Power”).



Tips

Spend Trophies on the Explorer’s Compass first — the chapter itself calls it the best value and a huge time-saver.
Hold off on Nature’s Compass and the Pocket Wormhole until after the End; crafting the Wormhole too early can make you “miss out on incredibly useful items” you’d otherwise pick up while travelling.
Building wands place blocks only — they can’t mine, so they’re for walls and filling, not excavation.
Trophy spellbooks are convenience/alternate options, not upgrades over the Spell Binding Table versions — pick the archery or elemental book that matches how you fight rather than assuming Trophy-made means stronger.

Anticipated questions

What are Cinderstone Trophies and how do I get them? A reward currency earned by completing storyline quests — you’ll have your first one just from progressing the main story.
What’s the single best thing to spend a Trophy on? The Explorer’s Compass — the chapter flags it as the best Trophy item and a major time-saver.
When should I make the Pocket Wormhole? Not early — ideally after the End, and after you already have the Explorer’s Compass, a Spell Book, and Nature’s Compass; relying on it too soon means missing useful items you’d find while travelling.
Do the building wands break blocks? No — they only place blocks (for filling holes or building large walls); one covers a larger area than the other.
Are the Trophy spellbooks better than normal ones? No — they’re alternatives to the Spell Binding Table books, “not better just because you made them with a Trophy”; choose one for its scaling (Arcane/Fire/Ice) or archery style.
Is this chapter part of the main story? No — it’s a place to spend the Trophies the story hands you, not required progression itself.

Links

FTB Quests · Quality-of-Life & UI Mods
Quest — Main Story (Trophies are earned from storyline quests)

Systems/Accessories--and--Enchanting.title: Accessories & Enchanting
Systems/Accessories--and--Enchanting.content:
Accessories & Enchanting
Don’t sleep on these — they carry real passive power on top of your main gear.
Accessories

Jewelry (RPG Series) — rings and necklaces found or crafted from gems mined deep underground, each built to boost a specific archetype (a Mage ring, a Rogue ring, etc.). A real power spike, not just flavor — grab the ring/necklace that matches your build’s Tier guide.
Artifacts — powerful, uncraftable trinkets found only while exploring. Rare drops that change how you play, worth detouring for. (Distinct from artifact weapons, below.)
Accessories / Accessories Trinkets Compat Layer / Trinkets and Things — the invisible slot system Jewelry and Artifacts actually plug into. You interact with the rings and trinkets themselves, never these mods directly.
Charms — craft from 3 of the same Potion for long-lasting potion effects (worn in a trinket/charm slot). They have durability; keep them alive with Unbreaking+Mending, a Hardening Catalyst, or Infusion (learned later in the Enchanting chapter).
Transmog — changes how gear looks without touching its stats, so you’re never stuck choosing between “strong” and “looks good.”

Full mod list: Core RPG & Combat Mods.
Artifact weapons (S’kellak’s Forge)
The endgame weapon system, separate from normal reforging:

Unlock the Molten Core after Void’s Invasion Chapter I; it forges powerful soulbound artifact weapons (only usable by the one who forged them).
Each artifact is forged from special essences/components (e.g. Frostmourne = Essence of Wrath + Awakened Lichblade + Molten Core). Artifacts in this install include Frostmourne, Fyr’alath, A’zhar, Supernova, Fury of a Thousand Fists, Thunderwrath, Ash’edar, Ekavar, Orion, Vaazkar (shield), Gh’aj (dagger) and Apophis (paladin hammer).
Repair/reforge with Encased Remnants; make one unbreakable with a Hardening Catalyst.
Upgrade Trees: press N → click the Molten Core icon (top-left). Each artifact has up to 7 nodes with branching paths, unlocked by empowering it with Molten Remnants (quest rewards or crafted from Mythical Essences). See Talent Tree & Fate Talents and the in-game Artifact Reforging chapter.

Enchanting
A deeper, custom enchanting system layered over vanilla — start with an Enchanting Table, but the table now has three bars you manage:

Eterna — the table’s level. Higher Eterna = better enchants but higher cost. Your XP level needed is 2× Eterna (30 Eterna = 60 levels).
Quanta — randomness/chaos. More = more random results. Don’t max it.
Arcana — rarity and number of enchants. High Arcana can block things like Protection or class enchants (e.g. Sunfire), so lower Arcana when you want those.

Building your enchanting setup (progression)

Surround the table with Seashelves and/or Hellshelves — ~15 infused shelves plus a couple of the higher variants gets you to roughly 30 Eterna.
Move up to Echoing/Draconic Endshelves and finally Endshelves (End City materials, Ender Dragon Heads) to reach the top of the scale.
Filter unwanted stats with a Seashelf of Aquatic Filtration; keep Arcana tuned for the enchants you want.
Endgame: an Enchanting Library block stores all your enchants in one place — it’s even AE2-compatible (point a storage bus at it) so you can pull any enchant on demand. See Storage & Inventory Mods / Tech & Automation Mods.

Tomes, curses & tricks

Tomes manipulate enchants: Scrapping/Extraction tomes pull enchants off items; gear-specific tomes grant enchants only possible on certain gear. Read them first — some destroy the item you use them on.
Anvil enchants: Splitting (split a big enchanted book into its components — a key way to extract just some enchants) and Obliteration.
Curses can’t be removed normally — you need a Special Cobweb to strip them.
Getting XP levels faster (you’ll need a lot): accessories like the Golden Hook and Superstitious Hat, the Lapis Backpack, and enchants Looting / Scavenger / Soul Devourer / Bag of Souls. Knowledge of the Ages converts items to XP — don’t use it on bosses.

Use JEI/EMI (press U on an item) and the in-game Enchanting quest chapter for exact recipes rather than assuming vanilla rules apply.
Spell Books (for casters)
Casters cast from Spell Books (Spell Engine / the RPG-series class mods):

Craft Tier I books at a Spell Binding Table, surrounded by 18 Bookshelves to unlock all four spell slots; the table also attaches spells to books of any tier.
A higher tier doesn’t mean stronger — it means obtained differently and harder to master. Tier I: Warrior’s Codex, Rogue Handbook, Archery Manual, Holy Book, Tomes of Arcane/Frost/Fire. Tier II: Paladin/Oath books, Death Knight tomes, Spellblade Techniques. Tier III: Astral Invocations (39 spells, the hardest), the Three Hunters archery books, and Magister’s Knowledge spellblade evolutions.
Match your book to your archetype and element.

Common mistakes

Maxing Quanta or Arcana. Chaos and over-high Arcana ruin targeted enchanting — lower Arcana for Protection/class enchants.
Under-building shelves. You need ~15 infused shelves before the good enchants appear; overshoot on shelf crafting.
Using a destructive Tome blind. Read the tome; some consume the item.
Trying to scrub a curse in an anvil/grindstone. Only a Special Cobweb removes curses.
Ignoring jewelry/charms. They’re a genuine power spike, not decoration.
Confusing found “Artifacts” (trinkets) with forged “artifact weapons.” Different systems.

Anticipated questions
What do Eterna, Quanta and Arcana mean? Eterna = table level (XP cost is 2× Eterna); Quanta = randomness (keep it low); Arcana = rarity/number of enchants (lower it for Protection or class enchants like Sunfire).
How do I power up my Enchanting Table? Surround it with Seashelves/Hellshelves (~15 for ~30 Eterna), then Draconic Endshelves/Endshelves for the top end.
How do I remove a curse? Use a Special Cobweb — normal methods won’t work.
How do I take an enchant off one item and put it on another? Use Extraction/Scrapping tomes, or an anvil enchanted with Splitting to break an enchanted book into parts.
What’s the best way to store enchants? An Enchanting Library block — holds everything and works with AE2 via a storage bus.
How do I level up fast for enchanting? Golden Hook, Superstitious Hat, Lapis Backpack, and enchants like Looting/Scavenger/Soul Devourer/Bag of Souls. Avoid Knowledge of the Ages on bosses.
How do I get an artifact weapon? Forge one with the Molten Core at S’kellak’s Forge after Void’s Invasion Chapter I; it’s soulbound to you.
How do I upgrade an artifact? Press N, click the Molten Core icon, and spend Molten Remnants on its up-to-7-node upgrade tree.
How do I make a charm or artifact unbreakable? A Hardening Catalyst (or Unbreaking+Mending, or Infusion for charms).
Do I need 18 bookshelves for spell books? Yes — that’s what a Spell Binding Table needs to unlock all four spell slots.

Systems/Archetypes--and--Builds.title: Archetypes & Builds
Systems/Archetypes--and--Builds.content:
Archetypes & Builds
There’s no hard class lock in Prominence II — you build a class out of talents, gear, and weapon type. Pick a rough direction and commit your gear and runes toward it. Nothing is permanent: a Knowledge Scroll respecs you any time.
The New Mechanics quest chapter contains full build guides organized as Tier I → IV, each telling you the next armor set, weapon, stat priority, Fate Talent and endgame artifact for that build. Everything below is grounded in those guides — always open the in-game guide for your build for the exact next step.
How to think about stats
Every build is really a stat priority. Match your gear affixes, runes and talents to the 1–2 stats that matter for you (see Combat & Stats):

Melee DPS (Rogue): Haste, then Physical Damage.
Melee Burst (Warrior): Physical Damage.
Ranged (Ranger): Ranged Damage, then Draw Speed.
Mage: the element’s spell power + Spell Crit/Haste.
Tank: Max Health + Armor/Toughness.
Healer: Holy Power.

Mage (Elemental)
Powered by the Wizards (RPG Series) mod and Spell Engine. A Mage deals ranged damage with spells cast from a Spell Book (see spell books). Start with a Wizard Staff (or an element-specific staff) + Wizard Robes.

Fire (Easy) — high constant damage, no utility. Priority Crit Chance (crits as often as possible), then Crit Damage. Fate: Fire Archmage.
Frost (Easy/Medium) — moderate damage + utility (slows enemies). Priority Spell Haste; Crit Chance/Damage secondary. Fate: Frost Archmage.
Arcane (Easy) — burstiest; slow, hard-hitting spells. Priority Crit Damage, then Crit Chance. Fate: Arcane Archmage.
Elemental Wizard (Hard) — uses all three schools; more versatile but weaker single-target. Path toward Astral.
Runic Invocations / Astral Magic (Hard) — true endgame; blends all three schools via Astral Power. Strongest, hardest to pilot. Fate: Knowledge of Runes and Stars.
Endgame weapon: Ekavar, the Great Cinderstone Staff, which evolves via its upgrade tree into Arcane/Fire/Frost/Holy/Astral versions.

Rogue
Powered by Rogues & Warriors (RPG Series). Fast, one-handed, dual-wieldable weapons; the “DPS” (constant damage) class. Stat priority: Haste, then Physical Damage.

Assassin / Haste Rogue — the Assassin set gives +5% Haste per piece; upgrade later to the Souldancer set (highest Haste of its tier). Fate: Shadow Techniques.
Monk — fist-weapon variant (e.g. Fist of Fury), endgame artifact Fury of a Thousand Fists.
Swordsman Rogue — endgame artifact Ash’edar.

Warrior (melee burst)
Powered by Rogues & Warriors (RPG Series). Swings slow but hard — the “Burst” class (high damage, not constant). Priority: Physical Damage.

Endgame armor Titan’s Shroud (highest Physical Damage stat); endgame artifact Thunderwrath, which synergizes with the Warrior’s Devotion Fate. Alternative Hero’s Armor grants Lightning Power for certain Thunderwrath upgrades.

Ranger (ranged)
Powered by Archers (RPG Series) + Archers Expansion. Priority: Ranged Damage, then Draw Speed. Note rangers are squishier — keep your distance.

DPS route: Shortbows / Rapid Crossbows — low draw speed, high sustained DPS.
Burst route: Longbows / Heavy Crossbows — high per-shot. Veiled Crossbow is the middle ground.
Wear Ranger Armor for the best Ranged Damage. Fate: Sin’dorei Heritage.
Upgrade path: kill a Mutant Skeleton for its chestplate → Crystal Longbow / Ruby Heavy Crossbow → the Orion artifact bow (the only bow artifact), which pairs with the Mintaka’s Fright / Alnilam’s Sight / Alnitak’s Might spell books.

Paladin / Holy & Healer
Powered by Paladins & Priests (RPG Series).

Healer (Medium/Hard) — priority Holy Power; cast heals from the Holy Book. Damage is low; add some Max Health/Movement Speed for survival. Upgrade the Holy Staff, then the Prior set (boosts holy power by a percentage).
Paladin — a Warrior + Priest protector; uses Oaths (Defiance/Vengeance are defensive playstyle choices). Endgame artifact Apophis (the Divine Hand), with an oath of Protection (defensive) or Healing (offensive) branch.
Bard (Medium/Hard) — a support sub-path. Requires the A Bard’s Tale Fate, plays instruments (flute, bagpipe, lute, trumpet, etc.) to buff party members (you must be partied). Bards have no fixed gear — mix with any build (archery, mage, healer).

Spellblade
Powered by Spellblade Next. Hybrid melee + magic — wears Runic armor sets, uses spellblade Techniques spellbooks alongside an elemental blade. Priority: a mix of Physical Damage + your chosen element. Fate: your element’s Archmage, or Shadow Techniques if you attack more than you cast. Endgame armor Magus set (level ~50, from the Magus boss) or Mageseeker Hat for crit; artifacts A’zhar (Soulfire), Ash’edar (Fire & Arcane), Frostmourne (Frost), or Supernova (Astral). Ash’edar path.
Death Knight
A darker, dark-magic-and-melee hybrid inspired by World of Warcraft, added by the Death Knights mod. Weapons are Runeblades (they carry all three DK powers). Three specs:

Frost (DPS) — one-handed Runeblades + Frozen Champion armor.
Unholy (Burst/AoE) — two-handed Great Runeblades + Plaguebringer armor; loves the Decaying Devotion Fate.
Blood (Tank) — self-sustain via the Tome of Vampiric Knowledge + Crimson Knight armor. (Go the Protector’s path if you want pure tanking.)
Shared endgame artifact: Frostmourne, purpose-built for Death Knights.

Tank / Protector
Priority: Max Health + Armor + Toughness; damage is deliberately mediocre. Fate: S’kellak’s Blessing. Taunt with Bone Armor, or take Righteous Hammers for a DPS lean.

Armor ladder: Diamond → Netherite → Netherite-Diamond → Sapphire (less raw armor but +20 Max Health per piece and a damage-reflect passive, ~30% less damage taken).
Endgame artifacts: Vaazkar (tank shield), Fyr’alath (soulfire bruiser), Frostmourne (Death Knight sustain).

Guns (side-grade)
From Marium’s Soulslike Weaponry — a ranged side-grade: Gatling Gun (spins up, decent DPS, slows you), Hunter Cannon (highest single-target, long cooldown), Blunderbuss (3 fast projectiles, high velocity), Hunter Pistol (fast, low commitment).
Common mistakes

Mixing stat priorities. A Rogue stacking Physical Damage over Haste, or a mage ignoring its element’s key stat, underperforms badly.
Wrong Fate for your gear. Follow the table in Talent Tree & Fate Talents.
Skipping the in-game build guide. Each Tier quest hands you the exact next armor/weapon — don’t guess.
Playing Bard without the Fate or a party. Its buffs literally require both.

Anticipated questions
Is there a class system? No hard classes — you build a role from talents + gear + weapon type, and can respec with a Knowledge Scroll.
What’s the easiest build for a new player? Fire Mage, Ranger, or a Tank are all rated Easy in the build guides. Fast Rogue is rewarding but Medium.
Best DPS vs best burst melee? Rogue = constant DPS (stack Haste); Warrior = burst (stack Physical Damage).
Which armor set for my build? Assassin/Souldancer (Rogue), Ranger Armor (Ranger), Titan’s Shroud (Warrior), Sapphire (Tank), Prior (Healer), Magus/Runic (Spellblade), Plaguebringer/Frozen Champion/Crimson (Death Knight). Your Tier guide names the exact next one.
What’s the strongest mage path? Runic/Astral (Knowledge of Runes and Stars + Ekavar), but it’s the hardest to play.
Can I be a hybrid? Yes — Spellblade (melee+magic) and Bard (support+anything) are built-in hybrids.
How do I get an artifact weapon for my build? Forge one at S’kellak’s Forge using the Molten Core (unlocked in Void’s Invasion Chapter I). See Accessories & Enchanting.
Do I have to follow the “recommended” build exactly? No — they’re guides, not rules. But matching stat priority + Fate + armor + rune family is what makes a build actually strong.

Systems/Best-Gear-—-Armor--and--Weapon-R.title: Best Gear — Armor & Weapon Recommendations
Systems/Best-Gear-—-Armor--and--Weapon-R.content:
Best Gear — Armor & Weapon Recommendations
Straight answers to “what’s the best ___?” questions. Short version: there is no single best armor or weapon — the best gear depends on your build and how far you’ve progressed — but there are clear top picks for each goal, and one rule that matters more than the set you pick.

The most important thing: reforging any gear up its rarity ladder (toward Mythic) and matching its affixes/runes to your build matters more than the base set. A Mythic-reforged mid set with the right stats beats a Common top-tier set. See Gear Rarity & Reforging.

What is the best armor for pure protection / tankiness?
For raw survivability, the Tank armor ladder is: Diamond → Netherite → Netherite-Diamond → Sapphire.

Sapphire armor is the top defensive set — it trades a little raw armor for +20 Max Health per piece and a damage-reflect passive (~30% less damage taken). This is the answer to “best protecting armor” if you just want to not die.
Bone Armor is the tank’s utility option — it lets you taunt enemies (pull aggro off squishier friends), which is what you want as the party’s designated tank.
Stat priority for any tank: Max Health + Armor + Toughness. Fate Talent: S’kellak’s Blessing.

See the Tank section of Archetypes & Builds.
What is the best armor for MY build?
“Best” armor is build-specific — each build wants the set that boosts its key stat. Your in-game New Mechanics Tier guide always names the exact next set for you, but here’s the endgame target per build:




























































BuildBest / endgame armorWhyTankSapphire (or Bone Armor to taunt)Max Health + damage reductionRogue (DPS)Assassin → Souldancer+5% Haste per piece; Souldancer = highest Haste of its tierWarrior (Burst)Titan’s ShroudHighest Physical Damage stat (Hero’s Armor for Lightning-Power builds)RangerRanger ArmorBest Ranged DamageHealerPrior setBoosts Holy Power by a percentageSpellbladeMagus set (~lvl 50, from the Magus boss) or Mageseeker Hat for critHybrid physical + magicDeath Knight — FrostFrozen ChampionDPS runeblade setDeath Knight — UnholyPlaguebringerBurst/AoE setDeath Knight — BloodCrimson KnightSelf-sustain / tankyMageElement-appropriate robes + Mageseeker Hat for critStack your element’s key stat
Full details and stat priorities in Archetypes & Builds.
What is the best weapon?
Again, per build — the endgame artifact weapons are the top of each tree, and each has its own skill tree (see Talent Tree & Fate Talents):

Warrior: Thunderwrath (pairs with the Warrior’s Devotion Fate).
Ranger: Orion — the only bow artifact.
Spellblade: A’zhar (Soulfire), Ash’edar (Fire & Arcane), Frostmourne (Frost), or Supernova (Astral).
Astral / Runic Mage: the Ekavar staff — the true endgame, strongest and hardest to pilot.
Other legendary/artifact weapons with their own skill trees include Apophis, Vaazkar, and Fyra’lath.

Getting an artifact and leveling its personal skill tree is a multi-session chase goal.
What’s the “best build” for a new player?
Rated Easy in the in-game build guides: Fire Mage, Ranger, or Tank. Fast Rogue is very rewarding but rated Medium. The strongest mage path is Runic/Astral (Knowledge of Runes and Stars + Ekavar) but it’s the hardest to play. See Archetypes & Builds.
The rule that beats picking the “best” set

Match the set to your build’s key stat (above) — a Rogue in tank armor underperforms.
Reforge it up the rarity ladder toward Mythic, and use Luck to improve rolls — see Gear Rarity & Reforging.
Match your runes and Fate Talent to the same damage family — see Damage Types & Runes and Talent Tree & Fate Talents.
In Hasturian Era, Corruption Infusions (add corruption for corruption-scaled abilities) and Etyr Infusions (add corruption resistance) further tune armor — see Progression & Level Caps.

Do those four and your gear is “the best” for you, whatever the base set.
Anticipated questions
What is the best armor in the modpack? There isn’t one universal best — it depends on your build. For pure defense/tankiness, Sapphire (+20 Max Health per piece, ~30% damage reduction) is the top set. For your specific build, see the table above; your in-game Tier guide names the exact next set.
What’s the best protective / defensive armor? Sapphire armor, the top of the tank ladder (Diamond → Netherite → Netherite-Diamond → Sapphire). Use Bone Armor if you want to taunt as the party tank.
What’s the best armor for a mage / rogue / warrior / ranger? Mage: element robes + Mageseeker Hat; Rogue: Assassin → Souldancer; Warrior: Titan’s Shroud; Ranger: Ranger Armor. See the table.
What’s the best weapon in the pack? The endgame artifact weapons — Thunderwrath (warrior), Orion (ranger bow), A’zhar/Ash’edar/Frostmourne/Supernova (spellblade), Ekavar staff (astral mage). Each has its own skill tree.
Is netherite the best armor? No — netherite is a step on the tank ladder; Netherite-Diamond and then Sapphire are above it, and every build has a better set that boosts its key stat.
Does the armor set matter more than reforging? No — reforging to a higher rarity (up to Mythic) with the right affixes and runes matters more than which base set you wear. A well-reforged set beats a raw top-tier one.
How do I make my armor the best it can be? Match set → your build’s key stat, reforge toward Mythic (use Luck), match runes + Fate to your damage family, and add Corruption/Etyr infusions in Hasturian Era.

Systems/Bosses--and--Recommended-Levels.title: Bosses & Recommended Levels
Systems/Bosses--and--Recommended-Levels.content:
Bosses & Recommended Levels
Prominence II is built around boss fights, and most bosses have a recommended Player Level — walk in under-leveled and you get crushed. This note explains the level-gating and how to prepare. See Progression & Level Caps for how levels work and Creatures, Bosses & Mobs for the mob roster.
Player Level, not vanilla XP
Bosses scale to your Player Level (shown top-left of your inventory), which grows only from combat — not the green vanilla XP bar. Your max level is gated by story progress, so if you’re stuck, advance the Main Story chapter rather than grinding (full detail in Progression & Level Caps). Many boss quest descriptions list a recommended level — treat it as a real warning.
The boss-gating system
The pack wires many bosses into a shared level-definition system (boss_level_definitions.json5) — a structured difficulty curve rather than scattered one-off fights. The gates are soft (a strong recommendation, not a hard lock). Confirmed examples from Bosses of Mass Destruction (BOMD):






























BossRecommended levelNotesNight Lich~10650 HP, summons undead, drops a Soul Star after 50 summon-killsNether Gauntlet~15900 HP, self-heals, drops Ancient DebrisObsidilith~40Tankiest — 2000 HP, 20 armor, heals; End-themedVoid Blossom(optional)1250 HP; sits outside the level-gate list
The same gated roster also includes vanilla’s Ender Dragon, AdventureZ’s Blackstone Golem and The Eye, Souls Weapons’ Accursed Lord/Draugr, Mine Cells’ Conjunctivius, Archon’s Null, Spellblade Next’s Magus, Eldritch End’s The Faceless (X’al), and the pack’s own Hastur Magus finale.
The pack’s boss mods

Bosses of Mass Destruction — four high-threat standalone bosses (above). Built to be fought with real gear, not stumbled into.
Marium’s Soulslike Weaponry — a soulslike arc with its own quest chapter and four named bosses: The Decaying King, Old Champion’s Remains, Fallen Icon → Harbinger of Moonlight, and Monarch of Chaos (pedestal-summoned via a “Shard of Uncertainty”). Beating them yields soul materials for its legendary weapon roster.
Archon — a rune/mana magic tree; bosses are summoned on a Pedestal using ingredients listed in your Grimoire (right-click the ingredients onto the pedestal — there’s no GUI; shift-click to clear). Its gated boss is Null.
Mutant Monsters — oversized, dangerous versions of familiar mobs; a step up from vanilla, good for leveling toward the real bosses.
The Graveyard — the Corrupted Champion, a multiphase fight (400 HP casting → 200 HP hunting phase, summons minions) summoned from staff fragments, plus themed hordes.
Eldritch End — X’al, The Faceless Eye, a summonable End-dimension horror with an area void attack.
Plus dimension/structure bosses: The Bumblezone’s Beehemoth / Queen Beehemoth (“Bee Queen” fight), Mine Cells’ Conjunctivius, and the Main Story’s Hastur Magus finale.

How to prepare for a boss

Check the recommended level in the boss’s quest, and make sure your Player Level clears it (level up via combat — see Progression & Level Caps).
Reforge your gear up a tier first — Limestone early, Pyrite mid, Galena for endgame Mythic gear (see Gear Rarity & Reforging).
Eat a buff meal before the fight — cooked food gives real stat buffs here (see Farming & Food).
Bring the summon ingredients if it’s a summoned boss (Archon Grimoire recipes, Marium’s pedestal Shard, Graveyard staff fragments).
Set a waystone/waypoint nearby so a death doesn’t cost you the trek back (see Fast Travel & Waystones and Death, Graves & Recovery).
Match your archetype gear and talents to the fight.

Anticipated questions
How do I know a boss’s recommended level? It’s written in the boss’s Quest Book entry. Check before engaging.
The gate is “soft” — can I fight above my level anyway? Technically yes, gates are recommendations not hard locks — but bosses scale and hit hard, so under-leveling is how you die fast. Bring the level.
Why am I stuck at a level and can’t get stronger? Your max level is capped by story progress, not grinding. Advance the Main Story / Hasturian Era chapter to raise the cap (see Progression & Level Caps).
How do I summon a boss? Depends on the mod: Archon uses a Pedestal + Grimoire ingredients (right-click, no GUI), Marium’s Monarch of Chaos uses a pedestal + Shard of Uncertainty, The Graveyard’s Corrupted Champion uses staff fragments. Others spawn in the world or their dimension.
Do I keep my stuff if a boss kills me? Yes — your items go into a recoverable grave (item loss is disabled on this server). See Death, Graves & Recovery. But recovering it from a boss arena can be dangerous, so prepare properly.

Systems/Combat--and--Stats.title: Combat & Stats
Systems/Combat--and--Stats.content:
Combat & Stats
Combat uses Better Combat (directional attacks, proper weapon movesets — closer to Minecraft Dungeons than vanilla’s “click and pray”) plus a stamina-based dodge roll from Combat Roll (bind/spam it to i-frame out of attacks). See Core RPG & Combat Mods. The New Mechanics quest chapter is the in-game tutorial for all of this — it’s mostly reading, and it’s essential.
How combat actually plays

Each weapon has its own attack animation and timing (Better Combat) — no more uniform vanilla swing.
Combos: consecutive attacks chain into combos; you can hold the attack button to keep attacking.
Shields are overhauled (Shield Overhaul): bash while blocking to perform a shield bash that stuns the target for 1 second (bosses are immune to the stun).
Dodge roll (Combat Roll) costs stamina and gives i-frames — your main way to survive telegraphed hits. Movement Speed even scales your rolling.

The stat system
Gear and talents grant Diablo/WoW-style stats (“attributes”), not vanilla armor points. Other things scale off them (e.g. Haste defines how fast you attack).
Core stats (everyone uses these):

Physical Damage — increases melee swing/punch damage; the main melee stat, scales all physical weapons/abilities.
Armor & Toughness — Armor reduces incoming physical damage; Toughness reduces it more on big hits (the “anti one-shot” stat). Enemies and bosses have Armor too.
Health & Stamina — Health is your damage buffer; Stamina reduces how fast you lose Energy (hunger), fueling dodging/abilities.
Haste — attack/cast speed (also switch-weapon speed). Huge for almost every build, top priority for Rogues.
Movement Speed — how fast you move; also scales rolling.

Ranged & magic stats:

Ranged Damage — scales projectile weapons (bows/crossbows/guns). From talents, jewelry and the weapons themselves.
Draw Speed — draw rate for bows/crossbows, fire rate for guns.
Spell Critical Chance / Spell Critical Damage / Spell Haste — the caster’s crit and cast-speed stats (Spell Haste shortens casts).

Penetration & hybrid stats:

Lethality (physical) & Magic Penetration — the same stat, different names: they ignore a % of the target’s Armor / Magic Protection. Worked example: 16% Lethality vs an enemy with 100 Armor makes you hit as if they had 84 Armor.
Astral Power — the combination of Arcane + Fire + Frost; fuels the hybrid endgame elemental-mage path and artifacts like Supernova and Ekavar’s Singularity.
Physical-Magic (Hybrid) conversion — “Attack to X” adds spell power as a % of your Physical Damage; “X to Attack” adds Physical Damage as a % of a spell power. For Spellblade-style builds.

Where these numbers come from

Zenith Renewed / Zenith Attributes Renewed — the affix engine behind gear rarity and its bonus stats. See Gear Rarity & Reforging.
Tierify — a separate tier scale (Common/Uncommon/Rare/etc. per item) layered on top.
AttributeFix, Custom Entity Attributes, Custom Item Attributes and friends — the invisible plumbing that widens how high these stats can go without breaking the game.

Full mod list: Core RPG & Combat Mods.
Reading your stats
Your attributes show on the character/inventory screens and on gear tooltips. When comparing two items, compare the stats that matter for your build — a “better rarity” item with the wrong affixes can be a downgrade for you.
Common mistakes

Ignoring Toughness against bursty bosses. Armor alone won’t stop a one-shot; Toughness is the anti-one-shot stat.
Never binding/using the dodge roll. Rolling through attacks is often more valuable than more armor.
Stacking a stat your build doesn’t scale. e.g. Ranged Damage does nothing for a melee build; Spell Haste does nothing for a bow.
Forgetting penetration on tanky targets. Lethality/Magic Pen cut through high-armor enemies far better than raw damage.

Anticipated questions
Why do numbers feel so different from vanilla? The pack replaces vanilla armor points with a full attribute system (Zenith + Tierify + attribute mods). Gear grants stats like Physical Damage, Haste, Crit, etc.
What’s the difference between Armor and Toughness? Armor reduces all physical damage; Toughness scales harder against big hits — it’s your anti-one-shot stat.
What does Haste do? Speeds up attacks, casts and weapon-switching. It’s a top stat for almost every build and the #1 stat for Rogues.
Are Lethality and Magic Penetration different? Same mechanic, different names — each ignores a % of the target’s Armor / Magic Protection.
How do I dodge? Bind and use the Combat Roll — it costs stamina and gives brief invulnerability. Keep Stamina/Energy up.
How do I stun an enemy with a shield? Bash while blocking (Shield Overhaul) — 1-second stun on non-bosses.
What’s Astral Power? Arcane + Fire + Frost combined; the endgame hybrid-mage resource used by Astral builds and artifacts like Supernova.
Do I need crit on everything? No — Fire mages and some builds prioritize Crit Chance, Arcane leans Crit Damage, but Rogues want Haste and Tanks want Health/Armor first. Match crit to your build.

Systems/Common-Problems--and--Fixes.title: Common Problems & Fixes
Systems/Common-Problems--and--Fixes.content:
Common Problems & Fixes
The “why is X not working?” list. Most of these aren’t bugs — they’re a system gating you. Each entry gives the likely cause and the fix, grounded in the pack’s quests and configs. Where a value could vary by server or isn’t published in-quest, it’s flagged as general.
Progression & Leveling
“I can’t level up anymore.”
You’ve hit a campaign level cap, not a bug. 1–10 is unlocked by default; 11–50 unlocks by defeating the first Void’s Invasion boss (Decaying King or Night Lich); 51–65 unlocks by starting the Hasturian Era campaign. Advance the Main Story chapter — grinding won’t help. See Progression & Level Caps.
“I’m killing mobs but getting no character levels.”
Character level comes from combat, but it still can’t pass your current cap (above). Make sure you’re watching the top-left inventory level, not the green hotbar XP bar — those are separate. See Progression & Level Caps.
“I have vanilla XP but I’m still weak.”
Vanilla XP (green bar) only powers enchanting, anvils, and the Waystone teleport cost. Your strength is character level + talents + gear. See Combat & Stats.
Combat & Bosses
“A boss one-shots me / I barely scratch it.”
You’re under its recommended level. Boss fights use level scaling: you deal 10% less damage per level you’re below the boss (5 under = 50% damage), while it hits like an over-leveled enemy. Level up, gear up, and check the level in the boss’s quest before engaging. See Progression & Level Caps.
“I can’t hurt this boss at all.”
Same cause as above, taken to the extreme — plus some bosses resist certain damage. Example: Magus’s barrier is weak to specific elements and the Smite enchant. Read the boss quest for its trick. (Element weaknesses are boss-specific — general.) See Archetypes & Builds.
“My dodge roll won’t fire.”
Combat Roll costs stamina — if your energy/stamina is drained you can’t roll. Keep fed (Stamina stat slows energy loss) and make sure the roll key is bound. See Combat & Stats.
“My shield bash isn’t stunning the boss.”
Working as intended — the Shield Overhaul bash stuns normal enemies for 1 second, but bosses are immune to the stun. See Combat & Stats.
“My attacks feel slow / clunky.”
That’s Better Combat — each weapon has its own attack speed and animation, and combos build over consecutive hits. Stack Haste to attack faster. See Combat & Stats.
Abilities & Spells
“My ability/spell is greyed out or won’t cast.”
Common causes: you’re below the level that unlocks it, you haven’t fated/spent the talent for it, it’s on cooldown, or you lack the resource it needs (e.g. a caster resource, or a rune). (The exact gate depends on the ability — general.) Check the talent tree (N) and the ability’s tooltip. See Talent Tree & Fate Talents.
“My spellbook only has some spells unlocked.”
The Spell Binding Table needs bookshelves around it like an Enchanting Table — you need 18 bookshelves to unlock all four spell slots. See Magic & Spells Mods.
“My spells hit like wet noodles.”
You’re missing the supporting stats: spell power, Spell Haste, spell crit, and the matching elemental runes for your family. Build one damage family, not a mix. See Damage Types & Runes.
“Bard buffs aren’t reaching my friends.”
Bard buffs only apply to party members — create/join a party with /openpac-parties create and invite them, and you need the A Bard’s Tale talent fated. See Archetypes & Builds.
Gear, Reforging & Enchanting
“I can’t reforge this item.”
Only tools, weapons, and armor are reforgable. You also need the correct Base Material (item-specific — hover the reforge button to see it), the item in the middle slot, and a Reforge Material on the right. See Gear Rarity & Reforging.
“Reforging can’t reach Mythic / the rarity I want.”
Your Reforge Material caps the quality range: Limestone → Epic, Pyrite → Legendary, Galena → Mythic. Use a higher-tier chunk. Stacking Luck improves your odds within that range. See Gear Rarity & Reforging.
“My enchants are random / bad.”
Tune the Enchanting Table bars: raise Eterna for level/access, keep Quanta low (it’s pure randomness), and lower Arcana when you want a specific enchant like Protection or a class enchant. Power the table with special shelves (Seashelves/Hellshelves and upgrades), not vanilla ones. See Accessories & Enchanting.
“I can’t get an enchant off a curse / stuck item.”
Curses need a Special Cobweb to remove; extracting enchants uses Tomes (of scrapping/extraction) — and read the Tome first, some consume the item. See Accessories & Enchanting.
Travel & Waystones
“My Waystone won’t teleport me.”
Teleporting costs 1 XP level by default in this install — if you have no vanilla XP, you can’t pay it. Also make sure the destination Waystone has been discovered/bound (right-click it once). (Local void-teleport is free; costs are set in the fwaystones config.) See Getting Started.
“I can’t bind / use a Waystone I found.”
Right-click it to discover and bind it first; you can only teleport to Waystones you’ve visited. See Getting Started.
Claims & Multiplayer
“I can’t claim this chunk.”
Likely causes: you’ve hit the 500-chunk limit (maxPlayerClaims), the chunk is already claimed by someone else, or you’re trying to claim outside your range (maxClaimDistance is 5). Free up claims or move closer. (Limits are the server config defaults and an admin can change them.) See Getting Started.
“I can’t open a chest / break blocks in someone’s claim.”
Claims protect against outsiders by default (doors, chests, blocks, entities all have toggles). Ask the owner to add you to their party or open the relevant protection. See Quality-of-Life & UI Mods.
“Quest progress or teleports aren’t syncing with my friends.”
You need to be in a party together (/openpac-parties), and FTB Teams ties shared quest progress. Form the team early. See Getting Started.
“PvP isn’t working / hurting a friend.”
PvP between party members requires both players to run /opacpvp. Server PvP is on, but claims still protect builds. See Getting Started.
Tech & Machines
“My Create machine/water wheel won’t run.”
Water wheels only generate power under genuinely flowing water, not a still pool. More broadly, most Create machines need enough rotational speed (RPM) and stress capacity — a Mechanical Mixer, for example, needs at least 30 RPM. Use the Stressometer/Speedometer to diagnose, and “ponder” a block (hold W in EMI) to see how it works. See Tech & Automation Mods.
“My machine has no power.”
Check your power source is actually producing and connected — Create runs on visible kinetic power, while Tech Reborn/Modern Industrialization/Powah! run on energy that must be generated and cabled in. See Tech & Automation Mods.
“I can’t auto-sort my items into chests.”
No mod does auto-categorized chests here. Use Applied Energistics 2 (ME network + Storage Bus + filters) for real auto-sorting, or a vanilla hopper sorter. See Storage & Inventory Mods.
Death & Recovery
“I died — where’s my stuff?”
The server isn’t hardcore and keep-inventory is off, so items drop, but You’re in Grave Danger creates a grave at your death spot holding them. Navigate back with the map (M) and reclaim it before the area unloads for good. See Quality-of-Life & UI Mods.
Food & Survival
“My hunger drains way too fast.”
Hunger matters more than vanilla here. Eat proper cooked food (Croptopia/Farmer’s Delight) for its stat buffs, and build Stamina to slow passive energy loss. See Food, Farming & Cooking Mods.
When it really might be a bug
If none of the above fits — the ability truly has resource/level/cooldown all satisfied, or a machine is correctly powered and still dead — check the in-game Quest Book for that system’s chapter, then rpg.prominence.wiki, before assuming it’s broken. Server-side configs (claims, waystone costs, drop rules) can also be adjusted by an admin.

Systems/Damage-Types--and--Runes.title: Damage Types & Runes
Systems/Damage-Types--and--Runes.content:
Damage Types & Runes
Damage in Prominence II comes in three families (“powers”), tied to Rune items you collect as you play. The quest book ranks them by strength: Primordial (secondary/strong), Elemental (tertiary), and Decaying (powers of Death).





























FamilyRunesRoleSource modElemental Powers (tertiary)Arcane, Fire, Frost, LightningMage spell schools; Lightning drives weapons like ThunderwrathRunes (under Magic & Spells Mods)Primordial Powers (secondary)Healing (Holy), SoulHoly heals/supports (Priests, Paladins); Soul combines with elementsRunesDecaying Powers (Death)Unholy, BloodDeath Knight powers (Unholy bruiser/disease, Blood tank/sustain)Death Knights (under Core RPG & Combat Mods) — not the Runes mod
Building around one family — matching runes, gear, and talents together — is generally stronger than spreading thin across all of them.
How the powers combine

Astral Power = Arcane + Fire + Frost together — the endgame hybrid mage/spellblade path (Runic Invocations, Ekavar, Supernova). Take the Knowledge of Runes and Stars Fate.
Soul + element = hybrids: Soulfire and Soulfrost, used mainly by some artifacts (e.g. A’zhar is a Soulfire weapon, Frostmourne is Soulfrost).
Holy is the support element — healing and temporary shields cast from the Holy Book by Healers/Paladins.
Lightning is a specialist elemental power tied to weapons like the Thunderwrath artifact.

These families map directly onto the Mage archetype’s three elemental schools (Fire/Frost/Arcane), while Primordial feeds Healers/Paladins and Decaying feeds Death Knights.
Where runes come from
You obtain runes as drops/rewards while playing (the New Mechanics chapter has quests to obtain an Arcane/Fire/Frost/Healing/Soul rune, and an Unholy/Blood rune). Use the recipe viewer (U on a rune) to see exactly what accepts it. The Runes mod itself ships the six Elemental + Primordial runes (Arcane/Fire/Frost/Lightning/Healing/Soul); the Unholy and Blood runes are separate items from the Death Knights mod (unholy_stone / blood_stone).
Correction from earlier: the Decaying family’s Unholy and Blood runes are added by the separate Death Knights class mod, not by the Runes mod itself.
Common mistakes

Spreading across families. Pick one power family and stack it — mixing Fire spell power with Blood gear helps neither.
Assuming Unholy/Blood come from the Runes mod. They’re Death Knight items.
Ignoring Holy as “just healing.” Holy shields and support are a full role (Healer/Paladin), and Smite-flavored damage matters against the undead Hasturian bosses.

Anticipated questions
How many damage families are there? Three: Elemental, Primordial, Decaying.
What is Astral Power? The fusion of Arcane + Fire + Frost — the endgame hybrid-mage resource. See Combat & Stats.
What are Soulfire and Soulfrost? Hybrid powers made by combining the Soul power with Fire or Frost — used by certain artifacts (A’zhar, Frostmourne).
Which family should my build use? Mage → Elemental (pick one of Fire/Frost/Arcane, or all three for Astral). Healer/Paladin → Primordial (Holy). Death Knight → Decaying (Unholy/Blood).
Where do I get runes? As drops/quest rewards while playing; hover a rune and press U to see what uses it. Elemental/Primordial come from the Runes mod, Unholy/Blood from Death Knights.
Is Lightning its own school? Yes — an Elemental power, mostly relevant to Lightning weapons like Thunderwrath (and thematically to Valkyries).

Systems/Death,-Graves--and--Recovery.title: Death, Graves & Recovery
Systems/Death,-Graves--and--Recovery.content:
Death, Graves & Recovery
Dying in Prominence II is forgiving about your stuff but not about your time — you don’t scatter items on the ground, and you don’t keep everything on the spot either. Instead, You’re in Grave Danger collects your inventory into a recoverable grave. This note covers exactly what happens and how to get your things back.
keepInventory is OFF — but you (almost) never lose items
The server gamerule keepInventory is false (verified in the world’s level.dat). In plain vanilla that would mean dropping everything on death. Here the grave mod intercepts that:

On death, your entire inventory and your XP are gathered into a single grave at (or near) where you died, and a chat message tells you the coordinates.
Item loss is fully disabled (itemLoss.enabled = false) — nothing is destroyed. Every item goes into the grave. You do not keep items in-hand on death (that’s the keepInventory=false part), but you also don’t lose them — they’re in the grave waiting.
A death waypoint is dropped automatically on your Xaero’s map, so you can navigate straight back.

XP: partial keep, partial recover
XP is split, not all-or-nothing (dropBehaviour = BEST_OF_BOTH):

~15% of your XP stays on you through death.
~60% is stored in the grave and recovered when you loot it.
So you lose a little XP on death, but most is recoverable.

Recovering your grave

Right-click (or left-click) the grave — that’s it. No sneaking, no standing on it (retrieveMethods.onClick = true).
Retrieved items go straight back into your inventory, merging with existing stacks automatically.
Graves respect world floors — they won’t drop below Y -60 in the Overworld / Y 3 in the Nether, and if you die in the void a grave still generates so your gear isn’t lost. Graves even form inside spawn-protected areas.

Grave robbing (multiplayer)
Other players can loot your grave — but not immediately:

There’s a 1-hour grace period before anyone else can rob it (unless your killer is exempt).
If someone robs your grave, you’re notified and told who did it.
So on a friendly server you have a comfortable window to walk back; among the group, a rescued-then-returned grave is realistic, and griefing leaves a name.

Recovery routine

Read the death message / check your Xaero death waypoint for the location.
Warp to the nearest waystone, then walk to the waypoint.
Right-click the grave to reclaim everything at once.
If you died to a boss or in a dangerous dungeon, go back prepared — the threat that killed you is still there. Consider bringing backup gear.

Anticipated questions
Do I lose my items when I die? No — item loss is disabled. Everything goes into a recoverable grave. You just have to go get it.
Then why isn’t keepInventory just on? The grave system is used instead of keepInventory so there’s a small stakes/effort element (walk back, minor XP loss, grave-robbing window) without the harshness of losing items. keepInventory is false; the grave mod does the heavy lifting.
How do I open my grave? Just right-click (or left-click) it — no crouching or standing on it required. Items go straight back into your inventory.
Can a friend steal my grave? Not for the first hour (grace period), and if they do rob it afterward you get told who. Your killer may be exempt from the timer.
What if I die in the void or in lava at bedrock? A grave still generates (void deaths included), clamped to a safe Y level, so your gear is recoverable.
Do I lose all my XP? No — about 15% stays with you and ~60% is stored in the grave to reclaim. You lose a slice, not the lot.

Systems/Dimensions--and--How-to-Reach-Th.title: Dimensions & How to Reach Them
Systems/Dimensions--and--How-to-Reach-Th.content:
Dimensions & How to Reach Them
Prominence II keeps the three vanilla dimensions (overhauled) and adds several new ones, each with its own entry requirement. This note lists every dimension and how you get in. Full mod list in Dimensions & Space Travel Mods. Most of these have their own Quest Book chapter — follow it for exact recipes.
Overhauled vanilla dimensions

The Nether (overhauled by Better Nether + Pirate’s Doom + Nether Depths Upgrade) — entry unchanged: build a Nether portal frame from obsidian and light it with flint & steel. The vanilla method still works; only the biomes and content are overhauled. (Entry method is general Minecraft knowledge; the pack changes what’s inside, not the door.)
The End (overhauled by Better End, with Eldritch End and BetterEnd Crashed Ships layered in) — entry is changed by End Remastered. Vanilla eye-of-ender throwing is disabled here. Instead you must collect 17 themed alternate Eyes of Ender, each from a different loot source (desert pyramid, jungle temple, nether bridge, igloo, woodland mansion, buried treasure, mineshaft, wither drop, elder guardian, bastion, pillager outpost, witch drop, etc.), then place them in a stronghold’s End Portal frame by hand. Find the stronghold with Explorer’s Compass (see Finding Structures & Exploration). This is a real scavenger hunt — start collecting eyes early.

New / added dimensions

The Otherside (Deeper and Darker) — reached from the Deep Dark. Steps (per its quest chapter): kill a Warden to get the Heart of the Deep, find the Otherside portal frame (generates underground in the Overworld), remove all Sculk Veins from the inner frame, then right-click the frame with the Heart of the Deep to light it. A sculk/warden-themed dimension with four biomes (Deeplands, Blooming Caverns, Echoing Forest, Overcast Columns).
The Bumblezone (The Bumblezone) — a bee-themed pocket dimension. Entry is advancement-gated — the mod itself points you to “check the advancements for how to play.” It is not a build-a-portal-on-day-one dimension; follow the in-game advancements / quest (Bumblezone chapter) for the exact trigger. (Exact entry item flagged as general knowledge — the vault’s grounded source says advancement-gated; confirm via the in-game advancements.)
Eldritch End biomes (Eldritch End) — the Hasturian Wastes and Primordial Abyss generate within the End dimension (thematically the pack’s namesake). Reach them by getting to the End (above) and exploring — no separate portal.

Space — Ad Astra planets
Ad Astra is a full tech-gated space program (its own “Planets & Space” quest chapter + in-game Astrodux guidebook). You don’t portal to planets — you build and fuel rockets, tiered by material, and need a space suit + oxygen to survive. Progression:






























DestinationRocket tierKey requirementMoonTier 1 (steel)Steel rocket, space suit, ~6 buckets of fuel; yields DeshMarsTier 2 (desh)Desh rocket; yields OstrumVenus & MercuryTier 3 (ostrum)Full Netherite space suit (permanent fire resistance) or you burn instantly; yields CaloriteGlacio (Proxima Centauri)Tier 4 (calorite)Cold but oxygenated; current end of the Ad Astra path
Getting off the ground needs genuine tech progression for power and material processing first (NASA Workbench, Fuel Refinery, Oxygen Loader). Every planet also has an orbit where you can place a Space Station. Off-world survival needs sealed, oxygen-pressurized rooms — breaching the seal triggers a lethal depressurization vortex. See Ad Astra for the full climb.
Quick reference — entry at a glance

Nether: obsidian portal + flint & steel (vanilla).
End: collect 17 alternate Eyes of Ender → stronghold portal (vanilla eye-throwing disabled).
Otherside: kill Warden → Heart of the Deep → clear sculk veins on underground portal frame → right-click with Heart.
Bumblezone: advancement-gated — follow the in-game advancements/quest.
Eldritch End: explore within the End.
Planets (Moon/Mars/Venus/Mercury/Glacio): build & fuel the right rocket tier + space suit; tech progression required.

Anticipated questions
Why won’t my Eye of Ender do anything? Vanilla eye-throwing is disabled here (End Remastered). You need to collect the 17 alternate eyes from loot and place them in a stronghold’s portal frame by hand.
How do I get to the Otherside? Kill a Warden for the Heart of the Deep, find the Otherside portal frame underground, strip the Sculk Veins off the inner frame, then right-click it with the Heart.
How do I enter the Bumblezone? It’s advancement-gated — the exact trigger is spelled out in the in-game advancements and the Bumblezone quest chapter. It’s not a simple portal you can build immediately.
Do I fly to the Moon or use a portal? You build a rocket (Ad Astra). It requires real tech progression for power and materials, a space suit, and fuel — not a portal.
Is the Nether entry different? No — build and light an obsidian portal as usual. Only the biomes/content are overhauled.
Where’s the “Hasturian” content? The Eldritch End’s Hasturian Wastes biome generates inside the End; the Hasturian Era campaign is a Main Story arc (see Progression & Level Caps).

Systems/Economy--and--Trading.title: Economy & Trading
Systems/Economy--and--Trading.content:
Economy & Trading
There’s no central “server shop” currency in Prominence II — the economy runs on villager trading, piglin bartering, and the reforge-material grind that underpins gear progression. This note ties those together. See Gear Rarity & Reforging for the gear side.
Villager trading (the Trading Post)
Villagers are your main renewable source of emeralds, enchanted books, and materials. The pack makes this far less tedious with Trading Post:

Interact with one villager and the Trading Post screen pulls in every trade from every eligible villager nearby — you trade with the whole village at once instead of walking between GUIs.
On this server the range check is effectively not enforced (enforce_range = false), so in practice it pulls trades pack-wide — handy, occasionally surprising if a trade seems to come from “too far away.”
XP from trades teleports to you automatically, and the screen auto-closes a villager’s tab once their trades are used up.

Set up a small village of your own (or move in on an existing one) with varied professions, and the Trading Post turns it into a one-stop market. Note that some farming mods let villagers buy/sell their crops too (see Farming & Food).
Piglin bartering (the Bartering Station)
For Nether-side “currency,” the Bartering Station automates piglin bartering: place the block, keep it stocked with gold ingots, and it feeds gold to nearby piglins and collects whatever they barter back — no more tossing ingots by hand. It searches a small radius and barters roughly every 15 seconds (deliberately slower than manual bartering, but hands-free).
The reforge-material economy (Limestone / Pyrite / Galena)
The most important “economy” in the pack isn’t emeralds — it’s the reforge chunks that let you reroll gear quality. These are a real grind loop, tiered by dimension (full detail in Gear Rarity & Reforging):





























MaterialDimensionRough sourceQuality range it can rollLimestone Chunk (T1)OverworldCraft from 4× Limestone or 4× DioriteCommon → EpicPyrite Chunk (T2)NetherCraft from Pyrite Dust (Pyrite Ore), or 4× Ancient Debris smeltedUncommon → LegendaryGalena Chunk (T3)EndCraft from 2× Galena Dust (deep Overworld caves) + 2× Popped Chorus FruitRare → Mythic
Practical economy rule: stockpile Limestone early (it’s cheap and Overworld-abundant), farm Pyrite through the mid-game, and hoard Galena for pushing your best gear to Mythic — don’t waste T3 chunks on gear you’ll replace. Reforging is done in the Reforging tab of an Anvil; see Gear Rarity & Reforging for the three-slot layout.
Shop mods?
There is no dedicated player-shop or admin-shop currency mod surfaced in the pack’s systems (no “sell chests,” no server currency). The economy is villager trades + bartering + material grinding, plus whatever informal trading your group does. (Flagged as current understanding — if a shop plugin gets added later, this note should be updated.)
Anticipated questions
Is there money / a currency on this server? No formal one. Emeralds (from villagers) are the closest thing to cash; the reforge chunks are the “currency” that actually matters for progression.
Why does the Trading Post show trades from villagers far away? Range enforcement is turned off on this server, so it effectively pulls trades pack-wide. That’s intended-ish — treat it as a feature.
Fastest way to get emeralds? Build/settle a village with varied professions and use the Trading Post to trade the whole population at once. Farming mods also let villagers buy crops.
What’s the single best thing to farm for the economy? Reforge chunks — Limestone early, Pyrite mid, Galena late. They gate your gear quality more than emeralds ever will.
Can I automate bartering? Yes — the Bartering Station does it for you as long as it’s stocked with gold ingots.

Systems/Farming--and--Food.title: Farming & Food
Systems/Farming--and--Food.content:
Farming & Food
Food matters more here than in vanilla — cooked dishes give real stat buffs, not just hunger refill, so it’s worth doing early (see Getting Started). This note covers eating well and brewing drinks. Full mod list in Food, Farming & Cooking Mods.
Read your food — AppleSkin
AppleSkin is turned fully on here: food tooltips show exact hunger + saturation values automatically (no need to hold Shift), and holding a food previews exactly how much it’ll restore before you eat. Use it to compare dishes — a proper cooked meal beats raw ingredients by a wide margin.
Grow more — Croptopia + Farmer’s Delight crops

Croptopia adds a huge range of crops and foods, giving farming real depth beyond wheat-and-carrots.
Farmer’s Delight is the anchor of the whole category — it adds tomato, cabbage, onion, and rice, plus Rich Soil farmland that speeds growth. Six other mods in the pack are add-ons built on top of it (Chef’s, End’s, Expanded, Ocean’s Delight, Farmer’s Knives, Animal Feeding Trough).

Cook well — the Farmer’s Delight kitchen
Farmer’s Delight adds the cooking furniture that turns raw crops into buff food:

Cooking Pot — multi-serving stews and soups, with a recipe-book UI. Your workhorse for hearty meals.
Stove — passive cooking (replaces the furnace+campfire shuffle).
Cutting Board — knife-based butchering/slicing of meats and crops (boosted by Fortune). Turns raw meat into cuts for composed dishes.
Skillet and Basket round it out.
Knives come in Flint → Iron → Golden → Diamond → Netherite tiers, extended further by the add-on mods.

From there you build sandwiches, wraps, rolls, pies, stews and soups from cuts (minced beef, chicken cuts, bacon, fish slices, mutton chops). On this server vanilla soups/stews are also configured to grant Farmer’s-Delight-style buffs, and villagers can trade FD crops.
Brew drinks — the Let’s Do series
Three “Let’s Do” mods add proper drink-crafting (all built on the shared [[[Let’s Do] API]]):

Let’s Do: Brewery — Oktoberfest-themed beer & whiskey. Grow hops and barley, feed them into a Brewingstation (Wooden → Copper → Netherite tiers) with Silos for grain, and brew Wheat/Barley/Hops beers served in Beer Mugs, plus named whiskeys aged in Big Barrels. Also adds pretzels, sausage, pork knuckle and other tavern food, plus tavern furniture.
Let’s Do: Vinery — grapes and wine.
Let’s Do: HerbalBrews — tea.

Drinks are their own little progression: crops → brewing station → aged/served product. Great for a tavern build and for group play.
How to eat well — quick routine

Turn your hunger read-out into a habit: check the AppleSkin tooltip and prefer high-saturation cooked dishes.
Plant a Croptopia + Farmer’s Delight garden early; add Rich Soil for speed.
Build a Cooking Pot and a Cutting Board — that’s 90% of good food.
For drinks, pick a Let’s Do path (Brewery/Vinery/HerbalBrews) and grow its crop.

Anticipated questions
Does food do anything beyond filling the hunger bar here? Yes — cooked dishes give real stat buffs, and saturation (visible via AppleSkin) determines how long a meal lasts. It’s worth cooking properly early.
What’s the single most useful thing to build? A Farmer’s Delight Cooking Pot — multi-serving buff meals from cheap crops.
How do I make beer / wine / tea? Beer & whiskey via Let’s Do: Brewery (Brewingstation + hops/barley), wine via Let’s Do: Vinery (grapes), tea via Let’s Do: HerbalBrews. Each needs its own crop and station.
Can I sell or buy crops from villagers? Yes — Farmer’s Delight is configured so villagers trade FD crops (see Economy & Trading).
Is farming required to progress? Not strictly, but good food is a cheap, permanent combat advantage — under-eating in a combat-focused pack is a real handicap.

Systems/Fast-Travel--and--Waystones.title: Fast Travel & Waystones
Systems/Fast-Travel--and--Waystones.content:
Fast Travel & Waystones
Prominence II is a huge world, and you are not meant to walk everywhere. The intended fast-travel backbone is Fabric Waystones, backed up by the waypoint system in Xaero’s Minimap / Xaero’s World Map. See Getting Started for the first-hour version of this.
Waystones — the main system
A waystone is a tall carved block. You bind to one by walking up to it and right-clicking, which discovers it and adds it to your network. From then on you can open any waystone (or a linked device) and warp to any waystone you’ve already discovered.

Finding them: on this server waystones generate naturally in villages — one per village — wired into dozens of the pack’s custom village variants. So exploring toward any village is a reliable way to grow your network. They’re also craftable if you’d rather place your own at a base.
You must visit a waystone in person to bind it — discovering waystones from a map item is turned off here. No shortcut; go there once, then it’s a warp target forever.
Cost: every jump costs a flat 1 XP level, no matter how far you’re travelling (distance is free; it’s a flat fee). Keep a level or two banked before a long-distance hop.
Anyone can break a waystone on this server, so if you place private ones, put them somewhere claimed (see Getting Started on Open Parties and Claims).

Waypoints — the map layer
Xaero’s Minimap and Xaero’s World Map (default map key M) let you drop waypoints anywhere and see them on both the corner minimap and the full map. These don’t teleport you — they’re navigation markers — but they pair naturally with waystones: mark a dungeon or ore vein you found, warp to the nearest waystone, then walk the last stretch to your waypoint.

Death points are automatic here — a waypoint is dropped where you last died, which works hand-in-hand with your grave (see Death, Graves & Recovery).
Waypoints and death points are shared between the minimap and world map.

Sharing & multiplayer

Waystone networks are per player — you each discover your own. Everyone binding the same village waystones effectively gives the whole group a shared warp hub, so it’s worth agreeing on a few “home” waystones.
Join a party (FTB Teams) early so quest progress and group play line up — see Getting Started.

Practical routine

Every time you pass a village, tag its waystone (right-click) so it’s on your network.
Keep 1–2 XP levels spare for warping home in a hurry.
Drop a waypoint on anything you’ll want to return to.
Build a personal waystone at your base (in claimed land) so you always have a way home.

Anticipated questions
Do I lose the waystone if someone breaks it? Your discovered network is stored on you, but you can only warp to waystones that still exist. Anyone can break waystones on this server, so protect ones you rely on with a land claim.
How much does teleporting cost? A flat 1 XP level per jump, regardless of distance.
Can I teleport straight to a waystone I’ve only seen on the map? No — map-based discovery is disabled here. You have to stand at a waystone and right-click it once to bind it.
Is there any other fast travel? Nether portals still work as the vanilla long-distance shortcut, and some dimensions have their own transit — but for the Overworld, waystones plus waypoints are the system. There’s no /tp for regular players.
Waystones vs. waypoints — what’s the difference? Waystones physically teleport you (for 1 level). Xaero’s waypoints are just map markers you navigate toward; they don’t move you.

Systems/Finding-Structures--and--Explora.title: Finding Structures & Exploration
Systems/Finding-Structures--and--Explora.content:
Finding Structures & Exploration
The world is packed with hand-built dungeons, villages, ruins and structures — and the pack gives you tools so you don’t have to wander blindly. This note covers how to locate things. Full mod list in Exploration, Dungeons & Structures Mods.
The two compasses — your primary tools

Explorer’s Compass — a craftable compass that locates and points to the nearest instance of any structure type (village, stronghold, ocean monument, and all the pack’s added structures). On this server it’s generous: never breaks, zero XP cost per search, a 10,000-block search radius, and no structures blacklisted. Use it before any long trek. (Opped/creative players can even teleport to a found structure.)
Nature’s Compass — the sister mod, but for biomes instead of structures. Genuinely useful given how many biome mods run here (Regions Unexplored, Geophilic, River Redux, Swampier Swamps…). Same generous config: unlimited durability, no XP cost.

Pair either compass with Xaero’s World Map / Xaero’s Minimap: search with the compass, drop a waypoint on the target, then navigate. Warp to the nearest waystone to cut the walk.
The big structure mods worth hunting

When Dungeons Arise — the standout: elegant, dangerous roguelike dungeons and structures scattered worldwide. Reliably “there’s something worth finding over there.”
YUNG’s suite — redesigned, bigger, better-laid-out vanilla structures: Better Dungeons, Desert/Jungle Temples, Mineshafts, Nether Fortresses, Ocean Monuments, Strongholds, Witch Huts, End Island, plus Bridges.
Aquamirae — an ocean ship graveyard with dangerous deep-sea creatures.
Mine Cells — a Dead Cells-style roguelike dungeon (with its own boss, Conjunctivius).
The Lost Castle — a large castle structure to raid.
The Graveyard — graveyard-themed crypts, ruins and a boss (see Bosses & Recommended Levels).
Philip’s Ruins (200+ structures), Sky Villages (villages in the clouds), Moog’s Voyager Structures (80+ hand-built Overworld structures), Towns and Towers, Regions Unexplored (~70 new biomes), plus village overhauls (ChoiceTheorem’s, Integrated Villages, Villagers Plus) and more.

Note: Strongholds matter extra here because the End is entered via a stronghold portal (see Dimensions & How to Reach Them).
Loot is personal — Lootr
Lootr makes loot chests per-player — every player who opens a loot chest gets their own copy of the contents. So exploring a dungeon as a group, nobody misses out because a friend looted first. Explore together freely.
Exploration routine

Open Explorer’s Compass, pick the structure type, and get a bearing (or Nature’s Compass for a biome).
Drop a waypoint on the target in Xaero’s map.
Warp to the nearest waystone, then travel the last stretch — tagging any new village waystones on the way (see Fast Travel & Waystones).
Loot freely — Lootr means your haul is your own.
Watch the threat level: many structures come with their own mobs/bosses. Go in prepared (see Bosses & Recommended Levels, Death, Graves & Recovery).

Anticipated questions
How do I find a specific structure (stronghold, mansion, a modded dungeon)? Craft an Explorer’s Compass, open it, pick the structure — it points you to the nearest one within 10,000 blocks. It never breaks and costs no XP here.
How do I find a specific biome? Use Nature’s Compass — same idea, but for biomes.
If a friend loots the dungeon chest first, do I get nothing? No — Lootr gives every player their own copy of each loot chest. Loot as a group without competing.
Does searching cost anything? No — both compasses are configured with zero XP cost and unlimited durability on this server.
How do I find the stronghold to reach the End? Explorer’s Compass → search “Stronghold.” Note the End portal itself works differently here — see Dimensions & How to Reach Them.

Systems/Gear-Rarity--and--Reforging.title: Gear Rarity & Reforging
Systems/Gear-Rarity--and--Reforging.content:
Gear Rarity & Reforging
Rarity ladder
Weapons, tools, and armor have a quality, ascending:
Common → Uncommon → Rare → Epic → Legendary → Mythic
Higher rarity means better stats and bonus “affix” effects. This system is run by the Zenith Renewed mod (a Fabric port of Apotheosis) — see Core RPG & Combat Mods. A separate mod, Tierify, layers its own per-item tier scale on top, which is why two copies of the “same” sword can feel very different in your hands. When you craft or obtain gear it rolls a random rarity — reforging is how you improve it.
Reforging
Reforging changes an item’s quality and is a core progression loop, done in the Reforging tab of an Anvil, which has three slots:

Left = Base Material — tied to the specific item. Example: a Holy Wand needs a Gold Ingot as its base. Hover the reforge button after placing your item to see exactly which base material it wants.
Middle = the Item to reforge — only tools, weapons and armor are reforgeable (not other items).
Right = Reforge Material — its tier sets the quality range you can roll.

The three reforge materials

























Reforge MaterialWhere / how to get itQuality rangeLimestone Chunk (T1)Overworld — craft from 4× Limestone Block or 4× Diorite Block (yields 4)Common → Uncommon (through Epic)Pyrite Chunk (T2)Nether — craft from 4× Pyrite Dust (mine Pyrite Ore) for 1, or smelt Ancient Debris for 4Uncommon → LegendaryGalena Chunk (T3)End — craft from 2× Galena Dust (deep Overworld caves; End Stone also works) + 2× Popped Chorus FruitLegendary → Mythic
(The in-game Reforging chapter lists each material’s guaranteed range; higher-tier chunks can roll the top rarities but not every roll lands there.)
Increasing your odds — use Luck
Reforging is a roll, and Luck improves your chances at higher qualities. It’s not pure grind: stack passive Luck before reforging your best gear. Sources include luck potions, luck-granting trinkets, and even wine — grab whatever Luck you can, then reforge.
Practical rule: reforge with Limestone early, Pyrite mid-game, and save Galena for pushing your best gear to Mythic. Reforging 100 items to Mythic is even an “Eternal Challenge” (Mythic Blacksmith).
Artifact reforging is separate
Artifact weapons (Frostmourne, Ekavar, etc.) don’t use these chunks — they’re forged and maintained at S’kellak’s Forge with Encased Remnants (repair/reforge) and a Hardening Catalyst to make them unbreakable. See Artifacts and the in-game Artifact Reforging chapter.
Armor sets & tiers
Progression is organized around tiered armor sets tuned to each archetype (Assassin, Souldancer, Ranger, Prior, Runic, Sapphire, Plaguebringer, etc.), obtained by crafting or killing bosses. Each “Tier II/III/IV Guide” quest tells you the next set and weapon for your build — follow it rather than guessing.
Common mistakes

Missing the Base Material. The left slot is item-specific; if reforge won’t proceed, hover the button to read what base it needs.
Trying to reforge non-gear. Only tools, weapons and armor qualify.
Wasting Galena on early gear. Save the End-tier chunk for the gear you’ll actually keep.
Reforging with no Luck. Pop luck potions/trinkets/wine first, especially for Pyrite→Legendary and Galena→Mythic attempts.
Chasing rarity over affixes. A high rarity with the wrong stats for your build can be worse than a lower one with the right ones.

Anticipated questions
How do I improve a weapon’s rarity? Use the Reforging tab of an Anvil: base material (left), the item (middle), a reforge chunk (right).
Where’s the reforging menu? It’s the second/Reforging tab inside a normal Anvil.
Which chunk do I need for Mythic? Galena Chunk (End tier). Pyrite tops out at Legendary; Limestone is the early-game chunk.
What’s the left slot for? An item-specific base material (e.g. Gold Ingot for a Holy Wand). Hover the reforge button to see it.
Reforging keeps giving low rarity — am I unlucky? Partly — it’s a random roll. Stack Luck (potions, trinkets, wine) to bias toward higher qualities, and use a higher-tier chunk.
Can I reforge armor, or just weapons? Both — any tool, weapon or armor. Not other item types.
How do I make gear unbreakable? For artifacts, a Hardening Catalyst at S’kellak’s Forge; for charms/normal gear, Unbreaking+Mending or a Hardening Catalyst via enchanting.
Where do I get Pyrite/Galena Dust? Pyrite Ore is mined in the Nether; Galena Dust is found in deep Overworld caves (or substitute End Stone in the Galena Chunk recipe).
