Systems/Getting-Started.title: Getting Started
Systems/Getting-Started.content:
Getting Started
Prominence II: Hasturian Era is a hardcore-leaning fantasy RPG modpack built on Minecraft 1.20.1 (Fabric). The core loop: quest → level up → pick talents & gear for your build → beat the recommended-level boss → unlock the next campaign tier → repeat, with tech/magic automation as parallel long-term goals.
The quest book calls you a “flameborn” — created and sent by S’kellak into the Overworld with a purpose to uncover. That framing matters later: S’kellak, the Cinderstone city of Vaaz, and the eldritch King in Yellow (Hastur) are the spine of the campaign.
First hour checklist

Eat well early — hunger matters more than vanilla; grab fruits/vegetables (Croptopia adds a huge range). The very first quest literally asks you to find a fruit or vegetable.
Craft a Chest, then upgrade it — chests are upgradeable. Mine copper and combine a Blank Chest Upgrade with it to make a copper upgrade. Storage is a progression track of its own — see Storage & Inventory Mods.
Grab a backpack early — Traveler’s Backpacks equip via the Equip icon in the backpack menu, then open with B. Search @traveler in the REI/EMI search bar (bottom of your inventory) to see every variant; special backpacks hide in loot chests.
Find or craft a Waystone — generates in villages, also craftable. Right-click to bind/teleport. This is the intended fast-travel system.
Open the Quest Book and follow it (FTB Quests) — it’s the pack’s built-in tutorial, gating and explaining every system as you go. Click the book icon at the top-left of your inventory. Left side of a quest = tasks; right side = rewards. See Quality-of-Life & UI Mods.
Multiplayer: claim your land and join/create a Party early so quest progress and teleports work together (details below).

Keybinds & UI you actually need

Quest Book — book icon, top-left of inventory.
N — Talent Tree (the most important build menu; see Talent Tree & Fate Talents).
M — World Map. B — open equipped backpack.
R / U — while hovering any item, show its Recipe / Uses in the recipe viewer.
Player Level shows top-left of the inventory screen; it is not the green vanilla XP bar (see Progression & Level Caps).

Multiplayer setup (do this before you build anything shared)

Claim land: press M, right-click a chunk, choose Claim Selected. Servers can set lower claim limits, so don’t over-claim. Land claims protect against grief and mob damage.
Make a party (so quest/teleport progress lines up): /openpac-parties create, then /openpac-parties member invite <Name>.
PvP inside a party is off by default; every player who wants it runs /opacpvp (it must be enabled by both sides).

A concrete first session

Punch trees, eat a fruit, complete the “First Steps / How To: Questing” quests.
Craft a chest + a backpack; mine copper, make a copper chest upgrade.
Kill a few mobs to reach Player Level 2–3 → you earn your first talent point (1 per 2 levels). Press N, spend it toward a rough archetype.
Craft an Anvil and try the Reforging tab on a tool with a Limestone Chunk (Gear Rarity & Reforging).
Set a Waystone home, claim your base chunks, and start following Main Story.

Common early mistakes

Ignoring the New Mechanics chapter. It’s mostly reading, but it’s the real tutorial for combat, stats, damage families and every build — skimming it is why most new players feel lost. See Combat & Stats.
Grinding for levels too early. You’re hard-capped at level 10 until you clear the first campaign boss — grinding past it is impossible (Progression & Level Caps).
Spreading gear/talents across many builds. Pick a direction early; committed builds crush split ones.
Treating vanilla XP as your “level.” They’re two separate bars.

Quest Book chapters seen in this install
Getting Started, Main Story, Hasturian Era, The Scarred Night, Mastering Fate, New Mechanics (tutorial), Spell Books, Enchanting, Simply Swords, Soulslike Weaponry, Create, Tech Reborn, Modern Industrialization, Powah, Applied Energistics 2, Botania, Bewitchment, Deeper & Darker, The Bumblezone, The Nether, To The End, Planets & Space, Reforging/Artifact Reforging, Transmogrification, Collectibles/Trophies.
Follow Main Story / Hasturian Era for the campaign; the rest are opt-in content tracks.
Where the deepest detail lives
Three things always beat any written guide for exact specifics:

The in-game Quest Book — walks you through everything chapter by chapter.
The official wiki: rpg.prominence.wiki (the quest book flags it as 10+ hours of deeper guides; the in-game link isn’t clickable, type it in a browser).
Recipe viewer (JEI/EMI/REI) — hover any item and press R/U to see how to make/use it.

Anticipated questions
Where’s the quest book? I closed it. Click the small book icon at the top-left of your inventory, or find it in your hotbar/inventory as an item.
How do I fast travel? Waystones — right-click one to bind it, then open any bound Waystone to teleport. They spawn in villages and are craftable.
Why is my “level” stuck / not rising from mining? Player Level only comes from combat, and it’s story-capped. Mining/smelting fill the separate green vanilla XP bar. See Progression & Level Caps.
How do I open my backpack? Press B once it’s equipped (equip it from the Equip icon in the backpack screen).
How do I find a recipe for a weird modded item? Hover it in the recipe viewer and press R (recipe) or U (uses).
Do my friends need anything special to join? They need the same modpack client-side (1.20.1 Fabric) plus Distant Horizons 3.2.0-b if the server shares LOD terrain. Claim land and party up together so quest progress syncs.
Is there a wiki? Yes — rpg.prominence.wiki. It’s the single most detailed source and expands over time.

Systems/New-Player-Roadmap.title: New Player Roadmap
Systems/New-Player-Roadmap.content:
New Player Roadmap
A concrete, ordered checklist for your first ~10 hours, grounded in the Getting Started and New Mechanics quest chapters. The single golden rule underneath all of it: open the Quest Book (book icon, top-left of inventory) and let it lead — this list is the spine, the Quest Book is the detail. You’re capped at level 10 until you beat your first Void’s Invasion boss, so there’s no rush to over-optimize early.
Hour 0–1: Land, eat, orient

Open the Quest Book and read the First Steps / How To: Questing! quests. Left = tasks, right = rewards. (Getting Started chapter.)
Eat something — grab a fruit or vegetable. Hunger drains faster than vanilla and food gives real buffs. See Food, Farming & Cooking Mods.
Learn EMI — click items in the right-hand list, or hover and press R (recipe) / U (uses). This answers almost every “how do I make X” from here on. See Quality-of-Life & UI Mods.
Craft a Chest, then upgrade it: mine copper and use a Blank Chest Upgrade to make a copper upgrade. Storage is its own progression track. See Storage & Inventory Mods.

Hour 1–2: Kit out and secure a base

Get a Traveler’s Backpack — equip it, open with B, and search @traveler in EMI to see variants. Big early inventory boost. See Storage & Inventory Mods.
Claim your base: press M for the world map, right-click a chunk, choose “Claim Selected.” You get up to 500 chunks — claim what your base needs. See Common Problems & Fixes.
Multiplayer: form a party now — /openpac-parties create, then /openpac-parties member invite [Name]. Shared quest progress and teleports depend on it. See Getting Started.

Hour 2–3: Fast travel and the map

Find or craft a Waystone, right-click to bind it. This is your fast-travel anchor — keep a little vanilla XP on hand, since teleports cost 1 XP level. See Common Problems & Fixes.
Set up navigation — Xaero’s minimap is already running; press M for the full map and drop waypoints at your base and each Waystone. See Quality-of-Life & UI Mods.

Hour 3–5: Learn the combat systems

Work through the New Mechanics chapter — it’s the in-game combat tutorial and the most important reading in the pack. Cover:

Better Combat — weapons have movesets, hold to attack, consecutive hits combo. See Combat & Stats.
Combat Roll — bind the dodge; it costs stamina and gives i-frames.
Shield Overhaul — bash while blocking to stun normal enemies for 1 second (not bosses).


Learn the stats from the same chapter: Physical Damage, Armor & Toughness (Toughness is the “anti one-shot” stat), Health & Stamina, and Haste (attack/cast speed — huge for almost everyone). See Combat & Stats.
Open the Talent Tree (N) — you earn 1 point every 2 levels. Spend early points as they come; nothing’s permanent (a Knowledge Scroll fully respecs you). See Talent Tree & Fate Talents.

Hour 5–7: Pick a direction and gear toward it

Choose a rough archetype using the New Mechanics build guides (Tier I): Protector/Tank, Warrior, Rogue, Ranger, Mage, Healer, Spellblade, or Death Knight. Each guide names the gear and stats to chase. See Archetypes & Builds.
Start collecting your damage family’s runes — Elemental (Arcane/Fire/Frost/Lightning), Primordial (Healing/Soul), or Decaying (Blood/Unholy). Commit to one family. See Damage Types & Runes.
If you’re a caster: build a Spell Binding Table and surround it with bookshelves (18 for all four spell slots) to make your first spellbook. See Magic & Spells Mods.

Hour 7–9: Reforge and prepare for the first boss

Get an Anvil and learn Reforging (second tab): Base Material (left) + your item (middle) + Limestone Chunk (right) to roll better rarity. Craft Limestone Chunks from 4× Limestone or Diorite. Reforge your main weapon and armor up. See Gear Rarity & Reforging.
Optionally start enchanting — an Enchanting Table plus special shelves (Seashelves/Hellshelves). Keep Quanta low, manage Arcana. This can wait if you’re eager to fight. See Accessories & Enchanting.
Push toward level 10 by fighting, and read your target boss’s quest for its recommended level and how to find it.

Hour 9–10: Break the first level cap

Beat your first Void’s Invasion boss to unlock levels 11–50 — the two entry bosses are both recommended level 10:

The Decaying King (Nether, melee-friendly) — locate the Decaying Kingdom with a Moonstone Compass.
The Night Lich (Overworld cold biomes, ranged/magic-friendly) — use 4+ Soul Stars (dropped by undead) to find its tower.
Gear up and hit the recommended level first — under-leveling means you deal 10% less damage per level below the boss. See Progression & Level Caps.


From here the game opens up: commit to your Fate Talent, start reforging with Pyrite Chunks, and pick a parallel tech or magic track. Follow the Main Story / Hasturian Era chapters for the campaign. See Progression & Level Caps.

Quick reference — key binds & commands

Quest Book: book icon, top-left of inventory
N — Talent Tree · M — World Map · B — Backpack
R / U (hover item) — Recipe / Uses in EMI
Party: /openpac-parties create · /openpac-parties member invite [Name] · /opacpvp (PvP, both must enable)

Systems/Progression--and--Level-Caps.title: Progression & Level Caps
Systems/Progression--and--Level-Caps.content:
Progression & Level Caps
Player Level ≠ vanilla XP
Two completely separate bars:

Vanilla XP (green bar on the hotbar) — works like normal Minecraft: mining, smelting, enchanting.
Player Level (shown top-left of your inventory screen) — your real RPG level. Grows only from combat (killing enemies and bosses). Each level gives more max health and lets enemies scale up to your level.

Many bosses have a recommended (or required) level shown in their quest description — under-leveled means you get crushed. See Combat & Stats.
Campaigns & Level Caps
Your maximum possible level is gated by story progress, not by how much you grind — this is the single most common point of confusion:





















Level rangeUnlocked by1–10Available from the start11–50Defeating the first boss of the Void’s Invasion campaign (the Night Lich)51–65Starting the Hasturian Era campaign (after finishing all of Void’s Invasion)
Level 65 is the current hard cap. If you feel stuck at a level with nothing giving XP, you haven’t cleared the next story gate yet — advance the Main Story quest chapter, that’s the fix, not more grinding.
The two campaigns, in order

Void’s Invasion — the first campaign (Main Story chapters). Its early bosses include the Night Lich (recommended level 10, ranged-friendly; find him on a broken tower in cold biomes using Soul Stars dropped by undead — killing him unlocks 11–50 leveling), the Nether Gauntlet (rec. level 15), and the Blackstone Golem (rec. level 25, summoned by a Blackstone ritual). Void’s Invasion has multiple chapters (Chapter I unlocks the Molten Core for artifact weapons).
Hasturian Era — unlocked only after finishing every chapter of Void’s Invasion. Story: S’kellak once imprisoned C’thulhu, but his half-brother Hastur, the King in Yellow, broke free and now threatens all realms. You’re summoned by beacon to Vaaz. Its bosses are level 60–65 required and its enemies are undead — enchant weapons with Smite (the questline explicitly tells you this).

The progression stages in order

Stage 0 — First hour. See Getting Started.
Stage 1 — Early game (levels 1–10). Explore, fight, start eyeing an archetype, spend early talent points as they come in. You’re capped at 10 regardless, so there’s no rush.
Stage 2 — Breaking the first cap. Beat the first Void’s Invasion boss (Night Lich). Gear up first via reforging with Limestone Chunks before the fight; bring 4+ Soul Stars and consider a ranged build for this one.
Stage 3 — Mid game (levels 11–50). Commit to an archetype and its Fate Talent, keep reforging with Pyrite Chunks, start a parallel tech/magic track (see Tech & Automation Mods, Magic & Spells Mods), explore overhauled dimensions, and unlock your first Fate Talent for your build.
Stage 4 — Unlocking the final bracket (51–65). Finish all of Void’s Invasion, then simply starting the Hasturian Era chapter unlocks this bracket. Harder fights, better rewards; “The Scarred Night” and “Mastering Fate” chapters open up.
Stage 5 — Endgame. Legendary/artifact weapon skill trees, Mythic-tier gear via Galena Chunks, Ad Astra space travel, Runic/Astral endgame magic, Transmogrification, and the level-60–65 Hasturian bosses culminating against Hastur’s forces.

Common mistakes

“I’m level 10 and can’t level up — the pack is broken.” It isn’t. You must beat the Night Lich to lift the cap. Read his Main Story quest.
Skipping recommended levels. A “recommended level 25” boss at level 15 will delete you. Level and reforge first.
Trying to jump into Hasturian Era early. It stays locked until every Void’s Invasion chapter is done.
Forgetting Smite in the Hasturian Era. Its bosses/mobs are undead and some have barriers you break faster with Smite/spell power.

Anticipated questions
What’s the max level? 65, and it’s the current hard cap.
How do I raise the level cap? By story progress, not grinding: beat the Night Lich (→50), then start Hasturian Era (→65).
Why won’t I gain levels from mining or farming? Player Level is combat-only. Mining fills the separate vanilla XP bar.
Which boss breaks the first cap and how do I find it? The Night Lich. Kill undead to collect Soul Stars, use 4+ of them to be guided to his broken tower in a cold biome, then defeat him.
What order do the campaigns go? Void’s Invasion first (all chapters), then Hasturian Era.
A boss says “Required Level 60” — is that recommended or mandatory? “Required” gates the fight; “Recommended” is advisory but ignoring it usually means death. Both appear in quest descriptions.
Do levels reset if I respec talents? No. A Knowledge Scroll only refunds talent points; your Player Level and campaign progress are untouched. See Talent Tree & Fate Talents.

Systems/Quick-Answers-FAQ.title: Quick Answers FAQ
Systems/Quick-Answers-FAQ.content:
Quick Answers FAQ
Short, direct answers to the questions this group actually asks. Each links to the deep note. When something is a general rule rather than an exact pack value, it says so — for precise numbers always trust the in-game Quest Book, EMI (the recipe viewer), and rpg.prominence.wiki.
Getting Started
What am I supposed to be doing?
You’re a flameborn sent by S’kellak to the Overworld. Follow the Main Story / Hasturian Era quest chapters for the campaign; everything else is opt-in. See Getting Started.
How do I open the Quest Book?
Click the book icon at the top-left of your inventory. Left side of a quest = tasks to do, right side = rewards. See Getting Started.
How do I see a recipe or what an item’s used for?
Open EMI (item list on the right of your inventory), or hover an item and press R for its recipe / U for its uses. See Quality-of-Life & UI Mods.
What should I do in the first hour?
Eat well, craft and upgrade a chest, grab a backpack, find a Waystone, and open the Quest Book. Full ordered list: New Player Roadmap.
How do I use my backpack?
Equip it from its menu, then press B to open it. Search @traveler in EMI to see all variants; better backpacks are found in loot chests. See Storage & Inventory Mods.
Leveling & Caps
How do I level up?
Fight things. Your character level (top-left of inventory) rises from combat. The green vanilla XP bar is separate and mostly matters for enchanting.
I’m capped and can’t level anymore, is that a bug?
No — you’ve hit a campaign level cap. Beat the first Void’s Invasion boss to unlock 11–50, or start the Hasturian Era campaign to unlock 51–65. 65 is the current max. See Progression & Level Caps.
What unlocks each level bracket?
1–10 from the start; 11–50 by defeating the first Void’s Invasion boss (the Decaying King or the Night Lich, both recommended level 10); 51–65 by starting the Hasturian Era campaign. See Progression & Level Caps.
Does the vanilla XP bar make me stronger?
No. It’s only for enchanting, anvil work, and paying the Waystone teleport cost. Your real power comes from character level, talents, and gear. See Combat & Stats.
Builds & Archetypes
How do I even pick a class?
There isn’t one to “pick” formally — you build one out of talents, gear, and weapon type. See Archetypes & Builds.
What are the main builds?
Protector/Tank, Warrior (burst melee), Rogue (fast DPS), Ranger (ranged), Mage (Fire/Frost/Arcane), Healer/Bard, Spellblade, and Death Knight. The New Mechanics quest chapter has a Tier I–IV guide for each. See Archetypes & Builds.
Which build is easiest to start?
The build guides rate Warrior, Fire Mage, Ranger DPS, and Tank as Easy; Rogue and Spellblade lean Medium/Hard. Pick by playstyle, not just difficulty. See Archetypes & Builds.
Can I change my build later?
Yes — a Knowledge Scroll fully respecs you and refunds every talent point, any time. Gear and runes you can just swap. See Talent Tree & Fate Talents.
How do I get talent points?
1 point every 2 character levels. Press N to open the tree and spend them. See Talent Tree & Fate Talents.
What’s a Fate Talent?
A big keystone pick near the top of the tree, unlocked at level thresholds — it defines your build (e.g. Frost Archmage, Shadow Techniques, Sin’dorei Heritage, S’kellak’s Blessing). Take the one matching your archetype. See Talent Tree & Fate Talents.
Combat
Why does combat feel different?
Better Combat gives every weapon its own moveset — consecutive swings combo, and you can hold the attack button to keep attacking. See Combat & Stats.
How do I dodge?
Bind and spam the Combat Roll dodge; it uses stamina and gives you i-frames out of attacks. See Combat & Stats.
What does blocking with a shield do now?
Shields use the Shield Overhaul — a bash attack while blocking stuns the target for 1 second (bosses are immune to the stun). See Combat & Stats.
A boss keeps one-shotting me — what am I doing wrong?
You’re almost certainly under the boss’s recommended level. You deal 10% less damage per level you’re below it (5 levels under = only 50% damage), and it hits far harder than you’re geared for. Level up and gear up first. See Common Problems & Fixes.
How do I heal?
Keep yourself fed for natural regen; drink healing potions; run with a Healer build (Holy Power via the Holy Book/Staff — see Archetypes & Builds); or use life-steal gear/affixes. Tanks survive by stacking Max Health + Armor rather than out-healing. See Combat & Stats.
Gear, Reforging & Enchanting
How do I make my gear better?
Reforge it at an Anvil, and pick up matching rings, necklaces, artifacts, and your archetype’s armor set. See Gear Rarity & Reforging and Accessories & Enchanting.
How does reforging work?
Anvil → Reforging tab, three slots: Base Material (left, item-specific — hover the reforge button to see what it needs), the item (middle), and a Reforge Material (right). See Gear Rarity & Reforging.
Which reforge material do I use?
Limestone Chunk (Overworld, Common→Epic) early, Pyrite Chunk (Nether, Uncommon→Legendary) mid-game, Galena Chunk (End, Rare→Mythic) for your best gear. See Gear Rarity & Reforging.
Can I improve my reforge odds?
Yes — stack Luck (luck trinkets, luck potions, wine) to raise your chance at higher qualities. (Exact percentages aren’t published in-quest — general rule.) See Gear Rarity & Reforging.
What’s the rarity ladder?
Common → Uncommon → Rare → Epic → Legendary → Mythic. Higher rarity = better stats and affixes. See Gear Rarity & Reforging.
How does enchanting work here?
An Enchanting Table shows three bars: Eterna (table level / cost — needed XP is roughly 2× Eterna), Quanta (randomness — don’t max it), Arcana (rarity/number of enchants — lower it if you want specific ones like Protection). Power it with special bookshelves (Seashelves/Hellshelves and their upgrades), not just vanilla shelves. See Accessories & Enchanting.
Why should I bother with accessories?
Rings, necklaces (RPG jewelry), and artifacts add real passive power tuned to your archetype. Artifacts are uncraftable exploration drops worth detouring for. See Accessories & Enchanting.
What are the best enchantments?
For armor, Protection is the staple — note you may need to lower your enchanting table’s Arcana to roll it (high Arcana blocks Protection and class enchants like Sunfire). Match class enchants to your build, and build the Seashelf/Hellshelf/Endshelf setup for high-level enchants. Full method in Accessories & Enchanting.
Magic
How do I cast spells?
Get a spell book or staff (see the Spell Books quest chapter), bind spells to slots, and cast. Build spell power/haste plus the matching elemental runes to hit harder. See Magic & Spells Mods.
How do I make my first spellbook?
Build a Spell Binding Table and surround it with bookshelves like an Enchanting Table — 18 bookshelves unlocks all four spell slots. It also attaches spells to any-tier spellbook. See Magic & Spells Mods.
Does a higher-tier spellbook mean it’s stronger?
No — a higher tier just means it’s obtained a different way and is more complex to master, not automatically more powerful. See Archetypes & Builds.
What are the three magic families?
Elemental (Arcane/Fire/Frost/Lightning), Primordial (Holy/Soul), and Decaying (Blood/Unholy, from Death Knights). Building around one family beats spreading thin. See Damage Types & Runes.
What’s Astral Power?
The endgame hybrid that combines Arcane + Fire + Frost, used by Astral Mages/Spellblades and artifacts like Supernova. Take the Knowledge of Runes and Stars Fate. See Archetypes & Builds.
Tech & Storage
How do I auto-sort my storage?
The pack’s real answer is Applied Energistics 2 (a digital ME network). There’s no auto-sorting-chests mod; AE2’s Storage Bus + filters is the closest. See Tech & Automation Mods and Storage & Inventory Mods.
Which tech mod should I pick?
Any of Create, Tech Reborn, Modern Industrialization, or Powah! — each has its own quest chapter. Specialize in one or two rather than dabbling in all. See Tech & Automation Mods.
My Create water wheel isn’t turning — why?
It only generates power under genuinely flowing water, not a still pool. See Common Problems & Fixes.
When should I start tech?
It’s a parallel mid-game track (levels 11–50), not a first-hour priority. See Progression & Level Caps.
Exploration & Structures
How do I find a specific structure or biome?
Use Explorer’s Compass (structures) or Nature’s Compass (biomes) before a long walk. See Exploration, Dungeons & Structures Mods.
Is loot shared if a friend opens the chest first?
No — Lootr gives every player their own copy of loot-chest contents, so nobody misses out. See Storage & Inventory Mods.
How do I locate a story boss?
Each boss quest tells you exactly how — e.g. Soul Stars point to the Night Lich’s tower, a Moonstone Compass finds the Decaying Kingdom. Read the quest description. See Progression & Level Caps.
Dimensions & Space
How do I get to the Nether / End?
They work like a heavily overhauled vanilla (Better Nether, Better End). The End portal needs 12 of 16 unique eyes scattered across the Overworld and Nether. See Dimensions & Space Travel Mods.
How do I get to space?
Ad Astra rockets need real tech progression first — follow the Planets & Space quest chapter. It’s an endgame goal. See Dimensions & Space Travel Mods.
What are all these other dimensions?
The Otherside (Deeper and Darker), The Bumblezone (bees), Eldritch End, and the story’s Primordial Abyss / Hasturian Wastes. See Dimensions & Space Travel Mods.
Bosses
What are the story bosses and their recommended levels?
Void’s Invasion: Decaying King (10), Night Lich (10), Gauntlet (15), Ender Dragon “Jean” (20), Blackstone Golem (25), Conjunctivius (30), Old Champion’s Remains (35), Obsidilith (40), Eldritch Eye (50). Hasturian Era bosses (Baphomet, Fallen Icon, Ghost of Cornelia, Magus, Null, The Faceless One) are all recommended level 50. See Progression & Level Caps.
What’s the recommended level actually mean?
Bosses have their own level. Being under it means you deal much less damage (−10% per level below) and take more — it’s the difference between a fight and a wall. See Combat & Stats.
What are Mythic Challenges?
Endgame scaling nightmares unlocked after beating Null, summoned with a Void Hourglass. Each win gives a higher-level hourglass; dying fails the challenge and drops you to a lower one. See Progression & Level Caps.
Farming & Food
Does food matter more than vanilla?
Yes — hunger drains faster and cooked food gives real stat buffs, so cook early. Croptopia and Farmer’s Delight add the depth. See Food, Farming & Cooking Mods.
What raises my Stamina/energy?
The Stamina stat reduces how fast you lose energy (hunger) passively; good food keeps it topped up for dodging and abilities. See Combat & Stats.
Travel & Waystones
How do I fast travel?
Waystones. Find one in a village or craft one, right-click to bind it, then teleport back later. See Getting Started.
Does teleporting cost anything?
Yes — Waystone teleports cost 1 XP level by default in this install (local void-teleport is free). Keep a little vanilla XP on hand. See Common Problems & Fixes.
How do I read the map / set waypoints?
Press M for Xaero’s full-screen World Map; the minimap sits in the corner. See Quality-of-Life & UI Mods.
How do I fly?
Flight comes from Icarus wings (worn in a Trinkets back slot — unlimited durability, but flight cuts off once your hunger drops below ~3 food, and heavy armor slows it), a vanilla elytra, or tech jetpacks (Ad Astra / Modern Industrialization / Create-era gear). The server has allow-flight on, so these won’t kick you. See Fast Travel & Waystones and Icarus.
How do I get diamonds or good ores fast?
Mine at deepslate depth, raid YUNG’s Better Mineshafts and dungeon loot, or trade for them. Ore-doubling via tech mods stretches what you find.
Death & Recovery
What happens when I die — do I lose everything?
The server isn’t hardcore and keep-inventory is off, so your items drop — but You’re in Grave Danger marks a grave at your death spot holding your stuff. Go back and reclaim it. See Common Problems & Fixes.
How do I find where I died?
Check your death coordinates / the grave marker, and use the map (M) to navigate back before the area despawns your grave. See Quality-of-Life & UI Mods.
Multiplayer & Server
How do I claim my land?
Press M, right-click a chunk on the map, and choose “Claim Selected.” You can claim up to 500 chunks. See Common Problems & Fixes.
How do I make or join a party?
/openpac-parties create, then /openpac-parties member invite [Name]. For PvP between members, everyone runs /opacpvp. See Getting Started.
Why do I need a party?
So quest progress and teleports work together, Bard buffs reach allies, and claims can be shared. See Getting Started.
Troubleshooting — “Why can’t I…?”
Why do I keep timing out, disconnecting, or getting kicked / lagging out?
It’s almost always our free tunnel, not the server or your internet — it bounces between datacenters every minute or two and each bounce briefly drops the connection (“Lost connection: Timed out”). The server keeps running fine the whole time; just reconnect and you’re back where you were. Full explanation and the other connection fixes: Troubleshooting Connection.
Why is my ability greyed out?
Usually you’re under the required level, out of the resource it needs, or it’s on cooldown. See Common Problems & Fixes.
Why won’t my Waystone bind / teleport?
It may be undiscovered, or you don’t have the 1 XP level for the teleport. See Common Problems & Fixes.
Why can’t I claim this chunk?
You’ve hit the 500-chunk limit, it’s already claimed, or you’re out of claim range. See Common Problems & Fixes.
Why can’t I reforge this item?
Only tools, weapons, and armor are reforgable, and you need the correct base + reforge material. See Common Problems & Fixes.
Where do I go if this vault doesn’t cover something?
The in-game Quest Book first, then rpg.prominence.wiki. Both go far deeper than any written guide. Common issues are collected in Common Problems & Fixes.

Systems/Storage--and--Applied-Energistic.title: Storage & Applied Energistics — Getting Started
Systems/Storage--and--Applied-Energistic.content:
Storage & Applied Energistics — Getting Started
Storage in Prominence II is its own progression track — you climb from a few chests up to a fully auto-sorting digital network. This note lays out that path and the beginner route into Applied Energistics 2 (AE2), the pack’s real answer to “how do I stop drowning in chests.” See Storage & Inventory Mods and Tech & Automation Mods for the full mod lists.
The storage progression (chests → drawers → AE2)
There is no auto-categorize-into-separate-chests mod installed (no Sophisticated Storage equivalent). The real end-state is AE2. The sensible climb:

Chests, upgraded. Start with a Chest and upgrade it via Chest Upgrade items (a Blank Chest Upgrade + copper to begin) — see Getting Started. Iron Chests: Restocked adds a tiered line of much larger chests, and Nether Chested is a single chest holding 8× the usual capacity.
On-the-go storage. Traveler’s Backpack is one of the best early upgrades — wearable, upgradeable packs with a weapon/tool rack and installable Upgrades (Crafting, Void-with-filter, etc.). Carry On lets you pick up and move a full chest or furnace in your empty hands instead of emptying it first.
Bulk single-item storage. If you want mass storage of individual item types before AE2, the Create/tech side and drawer-style blocks bridge the gap. (Note: the pack leans on AE2 rather than a dedicated drawers mod as the mid-tier — flagged as general guidance; check EMI/JEI for what’s craftable.)
Digital storage — AE2. One ME network that holds, sorts, and auto-crafts thousands of item types from a terminal instead of a wall of chests. Steep, but the payoff is the whole reason the other tiers are “temporary.”

The beginner path into AE2
AE2 has its own Quest Book chapter — follow it, it walks the exact recipes. The early arc, grounded in that chapter:

Build a Charger, powered manually with a Wooden Crank to start (no power infrastructure needed yet). It charges crystals and makes a Meteorite Compass from a normal compass.
Craft & charge a Meteorite Compass. It points to the nearest Meteorite within ~2,700 blocks — spinning fast means Sky Stone is in your chunk; spinning slow means keep exploring. Bring an Iron Pickaxe or better (Sky Stone needs it).
Loot the meteorite. Mine to the center for Certus Quartz Crystals/Blocks and, in the central Sky Chest, your Inscriber Presses — you need these presses to make processors, and they only come from meteorites.
Charge Certus Quartz in the Charger, then craft Fluix Crystal (Charged Certus + Nether Quartz + Redstone Dust dropped in water — it reacts on its own). Fluix is the foundation of all ME tech.
Build an Inscriber and make the processors your machines need (each press = one processor type; each operation needs ~1k AE charged up).
Grow into a Controller + ME Drive + cells + terminal, then Import/Export/Storage Buses to automate.

The big caveat: AE2 is hand-assembled
Cables, terminals, and buses are items you attach by hand, not blocks you can place normally. The machine blocks (drive, controller, energy acceptor) place like any block, but the fluix cables, ME/crafting terminal, and import/export/storage buses must be crafted and physically attached to a cable in-world — they cannot be conjured pre-built. A Certus Quartz or Nether Quartz Wrench rotates blocks and removes individual parts from cables. Plan on assembling the network by hand, part by part.
AE2 add-ons in this pack
Once your network runs, these extend it (see Tech & Automation Mods): MEGA Cells (enormous storage cells), ME Requester (auto-restocking), AE2WTLib (wireless terminals), ExtendedAE (QoL content), Applied Botanics (feeds Botania mana into AE2), and Polymorphic Energistics (AE2 recipes play nicely with the Polymorph recipe-conflict system).
Anticipated questions
Is there a mod that auto-sorts items into separate chests for me? No — nothing like Sophisticated Storage is installed. The closest options are AE2’s Storage Bus + item filters, or a classic vanilla hopper/comparator sorter.
Do I need AE2 to enjoy the pack? No. Plenty of players run on Iron Chests + a Traveler’s Backpack for a long time. AE2 is the endgame convenience, not a requirement.
Why can’t I just place the ME cables and terminal down? Because they’re cable parts, not full blocks — you craft them and attach them to a cable in-world by hand. This is a known AE2 quirk, not a bug.
Where do processor presses come from? Only from meteorites — loot the Sky Chest at a meteorite’s center. Use the Meteorite Compass to find one.
Do I need a power plant before starting AE2? No — the first steps (Charger, crystal charging) run off a hand-cranked Wooden Crank. You’ll want real power (see Tech & Automation Mods, Powah!) once the network grows.

Systems/Talent-Tree--and--Fate-Talents.title: Talent Tree & Fate Talents
Systems/Talent-Tree--and--Fate-Talents.content:
Talent Tree & Fate Talents
Press N to open your Talent Tree — the single most important menu in the pack, and the main tool for actually building your character.
Powered by the mods Pufferfish’s Skills and Pufferfish’s Attributes (see Core RPG & Combat Mods).
How it works

You earn 1 talent point every 2 character levels (see Progression & Level Caps). At the level 65 cap that’s roughly 32 points to spend.
Points spend on stat boosts (the stats your build needs) and unlocked abilities throughout the tree.
Fate Talents are big keystone picks unlocked at level thresholds, near the top of the tree — these are what actually define your build. You commit to your build’s Fate once you’re high enough level; the quest build-guides call this “now that you’ve reached enough level to get a Fate Talent, choose X.”
Pick the Fate Talent matching your chosen archetype.

Fate Talents by build (from the in-game build guides)













































BuildFate TalentFire / Frost / Arcane MageFire / Frost / Arcane ArchmageRunic / Astral MageKnowledge of Runes and Stars (grants Astral Power)Haste Rogue / AssassinShadow Techniques (big Haste boost)RangerSin’dorei HeritageTank / ProtectorS’kellak’s BlessingWarrior (burst melee)Warrior’s Devotion (synergizes with the Thunderwrath artifact)Unholy Death KnightDecaying DevotionBardA Bard’s Tale (required to play Bard at all)Spellbladeyour element’s Archmage, or Shadow Techniques if attacking more than casting
These are grounded in the New Mechanics / build-guide quest chapter; verify the exact node names in-game as the tree is periodically tuned.
Respeccing
A Knowledge Scroll is consumed on use and fully resets your tree, refunding every point spent. Nothing here is a permanent choice — experiment freely, especially early on. It does not touch your Player Level or campaign progress, only your talent point allocation.
Beyond the main tree: weapon / artifact skill trees
Several legendary/artifact weapons have their own separate skill trees via Puffish Skills, unlocked by obtaining that specific weapon. Categories present in this install: thunderwrath, apophis, orion, vaazkar, supernova, azhar, fyralath, ekavar_staff, plus the main prom tree.

Open an artifact’s tree the same way: press N, then click the Molten Core icon at the top-left.
Each artifact tree has up to 7 nodes with branching paths; you unlock nodes by empowering the artifact with Molten Remnants (quest rewards, or crafted from Mythical Essences). See Artifacts.
This is a big chunk of true endgame character power, layered on top of the standard Talent Tree.

Common mistakes

Hoarding talent points. Spend them — early points are cheap flexibility and a Knowledge Scroll refunds everything anyway.
Picking a Fate that doesn’t match your gear/runes. Fate + armor set + rune family + stat priority should all point the same way.
Confusing the artifact skill tree with the main tree. They’re separate; the artifact tree lives behind the Molten Core icon and uses Molten Remnants, not talent points.

Anticipated questions
How do I open my talents? Press N.
How many points do I get? One every 2 Player Levels.
How do I reset my talents? Use a Knowledge Scroll — it’s consumed and refunds every point.
Does respeccing cost me levels or progress? No — only talent points are refunded; level and campaign progress stay.
When do I pick a Fate Talent? When you hit its level threshold near the top of the tree. Match it to your archetype (table above).
Can I change my Fate later? Yes — a Knowledge Scroll refunds it along with everything else, so you can re-Fate into a different build.
What are those extra skill trees on my artifact? Weapon-specific trees opened via the Molten Core icon (press N), leveled with Molten Remnants — separate from your normal talent points.
I updated the pack and my artifact tree has a stat I didn’t pick — can I fix it? The Artifact Reforging chapter notes you can reset an artifact skill tree once for free (e.g. /puffish_skills skills reset @s puffish_skills:frostmourne). Check the relevant quest for your artifact.
